## Summary

- Fixes #1470: the calendar's ALL control fired `onSelect([])`, and an empty
  selection is what `FairwayCalendar.tsx` reads as "team events only"
  (`availabilityMode` false, no overlay). Picking a single player instead
  switched to the color-coded availability overlay (their events + classes +
  blocked time). So ALL was showing strictly less than picking any one
  player - not "everyone", but "nobody in particular".
- ALL now selects every roster member id, bypassing the manual 8-selection
  cap. The cap exists to keep `PLAYER_COLORS` (8 entries, same count as
  `AVATAR_TINT_COUNT`) unambiguous per selected player; past it, members
  render identified by initials + their own id-hash tint instead of a
  numbered palette color - the same fallback `FairwayMonthGrid` already uses
  for class-owner chips when color alone would be ambiguous.
- Deselecting back to the plain team calendar is reachable two ways:
  pressing ALL again while everyone is selected, or the existing Clear
  control (both already called `onSelect([])`, so Clear needed no change).
- Also fixes the cap's silent-refusal failure mode one level up: once a
  selection is already past the cap (only reachable via ALL), individual
  toggles stay uncapped too, so deselecting one member and picking them back
  isn't dropped on the floor the way a fresh 9th manual selection still is.

## Known follow-up (out of scope here)

The calendar body's own overlay coloring (`FairwayCalendar.tsx`'s
`overlays` builder, `FairwayMonthGrid`'s `kind === 'overlay'` chip renderer)
still cycles the 8-color palette by index for the schedule blocks
themselves once overlays exceed 8 concurrent players, so two players can
render the same overlay color on a >8 roster. Unambiguous coloring for that
many simultaneous schedules is a separate, larger design problem from the
rail's own chip legibility, which is what #1470 and this fix scope to.

body:
## Goal
A docs/markdown-only PR shouldn't run the unit matrix + Next build + RLS + the flaky BaseballHelm auth smoke. It now doesn't.

## Design
- **`detect-changes` job** classifies the PR diff. `code=false` **only** when *every* changed file is under `docs/` or ends in `.md`. Anything else — config, `ci.yml`, `package.json`, migrations, `*.yml`, `src/` — is code → full suite. Count-based (`grep -cvE`) so it's identical on GNU/BSD grep and testable locally.
- **Fails closed** (e3's criterion): non-PR event, missing base/head sha, failed `git diff`, or empty diff all → `code=true`. A misclassified docs PR wastes one suite; a misclassified code PR ships ungated, so uncertainty always resolves to code.
- **4 heavy jobs gated**: `unit-tests`, `next-build`, `supabase` (RLS), `baseball-auth-smoke` on `code == 'true'`.
- **Change-aware aggregate** (the hunk to review): still fails on any `failure`/`cancelled`; fails on a `skipped` **only when `code=='true'`**. Docs-only skips pass; a code PR with a skipped heavy job still fails.

## Fails closed end-to-end
If the `detect-changes` job itself dies, its result is `failure` → the aggregate's `contains(failure)` catches it → PR blocked. Never a silent skip.

## Verification
- YAML validated.
- Classification unit-tested: `docs-only → code=false`, `code/config/migration → code=true`, `pure .md → code=false`.
- Required contexts unchanged (Smoke checks, CI aggregate, Review Gate aggregate, Analyze×3 all still run and gate).

**Not armed** — handing the aggregate hunk to e3 for review first, since that's the brick-every-PR risk.

## What
`npm run repo:doctor` — a **read-only** repository control-plane integrity command (MVP of the owner's spec). It compares **desired** state (`config/repo/manifest.yml`) against **actual** repo state and reports `PASS / WARN / FAIL / DRIFT / UNKNOWN / BLOCKED`. It never mutates anything.

This is the durable fix for the week's recurring failure shape: *a thing changed, a second representation of it didn't, and the repo kept confidently describing stale state.* Instead of another cleanup doc, the assumptions become executable invariants.

## MVP checks (deterministic, no external access)
| module | checks |
|---|---|
| identity | origin remote == manifest, cwd == top-level, checkout kind |
| workspace | no worktree inside repo root, no nested `.git` |
| scratch | no oversized gitignored dir (search poison), no duplicate `src/app` |
| ai | `CLAUDE.md` imports `@AGENTS.md`, `autoMemoryEnabled` explicit |
| registry | every concrete `memory/registry.yml` doc path resolves |
| ci | each required check name has exactly one producing job |
| config | required npm scripts exist, one Supabase root, deploy model stated |

## Can't-false-green properties (pinned by 13 tests)
- A crashed check → `BLOCKED` → **exit 2**, never silent green.
- External-unavailable → `UNKNOWN` → **exit 3**, never `PASS`.
- Exit codes: `0` clean / `1` hard invariant / `2` crash / `3` external unavailable.
- `--json`, `--summary`, `--verbose`, `--ci`/`--local` modes; structured result model; desired state in a versioned manifest.

Runs clean on current main (17 PASS). eslint clean. Tests wired into the vitest `unit` project.

## Scope
Deliberately **not** wired into `ci.yml` here — that would conflict with in-flight #1524 (also edits ci.yml). CI wiring as `repo:doctor --ci` is the immediate next step once #1524 lands. Follow-on phases (local git/hooks/stashes, GitHub/Vercel/Supabase live-drift, fingerprint ratchets, generated-doc verification) per the spec.

## Goal
Owner: PRs take too long to approve; remove chromium E2E + lighthouse.

## Findings — neither was the bottleneck
- **`Playwright (chromium)`** was already PR-**SKIPPED** (runs on push-to-main only).
- **Lighthouse** has **no active CircleCI job** (`config.yml` = weekly/ios/android). The `lighthouse-preview` check hasn't run; its doc line was stale.
- The real PR-time cost is the unit-test matrix, dominated by the **6 timezone-shifted jobs** (2 tz × 3 shards) that hard-gated every PR through `CI aggregate`.

## Changes
1. **playwright.yml** — chromium `e2e` → `workflow_dispatch`-only (also stops its push-run PRODUCTION fixture seeding).
2. **ci.yml** — `unit-tests-timezone` runs on push-to-**main** only and is removed from the `CI aggregate` `needs`, so it no longer blocks PRs. Cuts 6 jobs off every PR.
3. **branch-protection.md** — dropped the stale `lighthouse-preview` advisory line.

## Tradeoff — reviewers can veto hunk 2
Moving the timezone shards post-merge means #1123-class regressions are caught at **main-time, not PR-time**. Per e3, the enforcement point becomes the **pre-promote check of main's CI** — a red timezone job on `main` blocks the *deploy*, not the merge. Documented in the workflow comment. e3 approved on that condition; owner can override.

No required-check names change; the 6 required contexts are untouched. YAML validated.

## What Prevents the auto-save pile-up that armed the round-destruction incident (docs/audits/ROUND_SUBMIT_TIMEOUT_INVERSION_2026-08-20.md). The 8/19 Guilford team session put eight players' concurrent auto-saves into `save_partial_round_atomic`; each QUEUED on the round row's `FOR UPDATE` lock, then ran its full ~70-shot delete+insert anyway — 15 timeouts across 8 rounds in one evening. - **Migration** `20260820170000`: `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` in `save_partial_round_atomic` — any concurrent writer (another auto-save OR an in-flight submit) → immediate `{success:false, error:'busy'}` instead of queueing. Body is byte-identical to the production definition captured via `pg_get_functiondef` today (not the repo's migration history), except the NOWAIT clause + handler. Dropping a save is safe by construction: every save carries the full round state; the next tick (per shot + 15s interval) covers it. - **"Save for later"** (user-initiated, both clients) retries once after 1.5s instead of failing on a coalescing skip. ## Verified (clean worktree, detached from the shared checkout) - `tsc --noEmit` EXIT 0 - golf actions suite **559/559** - new regression test proven by bug injection: with the `'busy'` branch disabled it fails on both the remapped error and the admin_events write ## Deploy/apply notes for the reviewer - **The migration is NOT applied.** Until someone applies it, the RPC never returns `'busy'` and every code path here is inert — merge order is safe either way. ## The bug A composite insight could be written **`high` or `urgent` on a confidence the generators would have capped at `medium`**. `CompositeRule.priority` is a **static** property typed `'high' | 'urgent'` (`composite/types.ts:135`), so every composite is act-now by construction, while its confidence is produced separately by the rule's own `compose()`. `synthesis.ts:436` wrote `priority: rule.priority`, and nothing compared the two. ## This is the second time `enforcePriorityConfidenceGate` exists because of the first occurrence — its own docblock in `engine/generator-base.ts`: > "a generator that COMPOSES 'high'/'urgent' directly (course_management's > anchoredPriority) bypassed the confidence gate entirely — 7 live > sub-0.5-confidence 'high' rows auto-surfaced in the Alert Center. Every written > priority must clear the same gate regardless of which path produced it." That was closed for generators. The composite path kept the bypass. ## Measured in production (2026-08-18, `golf_coach_insights`) | priority | rows | below 0.5 conf | min conf | |---|---|---|---| | urgent | 13 | 0 | 0.654 | | high | 54 | **5** | **0.333** | All five offenders are `insight_type = 'composite'`, and one was created **2026-08-18 02:49 UTC** — hours before this PR. So this is live behaviour, not residue from before the generator fix. A coach's Alert Center ranks on priority. A 0.333-confidence row sitting at `high` is the engine saying "act on this" about something it barely believes. ## Proven before fixing Against the shipped behaviour: ``` downgrades a high-priority rule that is not confident enough AssertionError: expected 'high' to be 'medium' downgrades an urgent rule that is not confident enough AssertionError: expected 'urgent' to be 'medium' never downgrades below medium AssertionError: expected 'high' to be 'medium' ``` ## The fix `gatedCompositePriority` **delegates** to `enforcePriorityConfidenceGate` rather than re-deriving the rule — one floor, one implementation. Wired at the single write site. Two guards so the paths cannot drift apart: - a fixture guard pinning `MIN_CONF_FOR_HIGH` at 0.5, since composites and generators disagreeing about "confident enough" is the whole bug; - the boundary (exactly 0.5 survives, matching the generators' `<` comparison). ## Not changed The 5 existing rows. They are refreshed by the composite sweep, so they should regrade themselves on the next run rather than needing a data migration — **worth confirming with the query above after this lands.** ## Gates - `npm run typecheck` — **exit 0** - `npm run lint` — **exit 0** - `TZ=UTC npm test` — **exit 0**, 10327 passed / 6 skipped

test(utils): cover the shared display formatters, and pin one landmine 7 of the 9 exports in src/lib/utils.ts had ZERO test coverage — formatNumber, formatMetricLabel, formatDateTime, formatRelativeTime, formatHeight, getFullName, getPipelineStageLabel. They are pure display helpers imported across BOTH products (video cards, journey timeline, college interest, camps, showcase dashboards), so a silent change is visible everywhere at once and nothing would have caught it. This is the untested-live-path shape that hid the Find-a-Time 4-hour offset. NO LIVE BUG WAS FOUND. These are characterization tests: they pin current behavior rather than assert a fix, and the commit claims nothing more. Two edges are documented rather than "fixed", because neither is reachable: 1. LANDMINE — formatRelativeTime returns "Just now" for any FUTURE date. `differenceInMinutes(now, d)` goes NEGATIVE when d is in the future and the first branch is `if (mins < 1) return 'Just now'`, so a scheduled event or a due date would render as "Just now" instead of "in 2 hours". feat(coachhelm): surface the downhill short-putt penalty — the real one The backlog asked to surface "81.8% level vs 30.8% downhill, a 51-point gap nothing surfaces." That headline is a DISTANCE CONFOUND and shipping it would have told coaches something false. Measured against production: slope putts MEAN DISTANCE make% level 4919 4.3 ft 81.9% uphill 2620 16.1 ft 30.8% downhill 2319 16.1 ft 25.3% The "51-point gap" compares 4.3-foot putts against 16.1-foot putts. 74% of all level putts are 0-3 ft tap-ins. The figure was also mislabeled — 30.8% is the UPHILL number; downhill is 25.3%. I then reproduced the same error myself by bucketing at "<=10 ft" and got a nonsense 47-point mean, which is how easy this trap is. The REAL signal, per-player, within single narrow bands (>=8 putts of each slope in the same band): band qualifying players mean penalty 0-3 ft 13 of 42 20.7 pts 4-6 ft 13 of 40 19.9 pts 7-10 ft 8 of 39 -1.6 pts Material inside 6 feet, gone beyond it — physically sensible, since short downhill putts are pace control while longer ones are dominated by distance. PuttSlopeBiasGenerator compares downhill vs level WITHIN one band, bands 0-3 and 4-6 only (7-10+ is excluded outright, not merely gated — there is no signal there and claiming one would be fabrication). Two-proportion z-test, n>=8/side per the measurement above, 12pp effect floor. Picks the single strongest qualifying band. A significant gap in the WRONG direction is rejected, never reframed as a finding. Modeled on PuttBiasGenerator, which already does (distance band x slope) bucketing for break DIRECTION — this adds the slope-vs-slope comparison it never made. The load-bearing test is the confound regression: level skewed to the easy 0-3 band and downhill to the harder 4-6 band, identical within-band rates, both slopes clearing n>=8 in both bands so the sample gate cannot be what rejects it. The fixture's fake 30+ point pooled gap is ASSERTED to exist, so the test cannot pass vacuously; the band-controlled selector must still return null. Deliberate choices worth review: - reuses insight_type 'putt_bias' — the DB CHECK constraint whitelists values, so a new one needs a migration. Signature scope 'putt_slope_bias:' is verified not to be a prefix of 'putt_bias:', so their stale-row sweeps cannot retract each other. - strokes_impact 0. requiresStanding=false means the standing/backfill path never runs, matching putt-bias's own precedent. (Note: I had claimed a symbol ZERO_IMPACT_BY_DESIGN in score.ts — that does not exist. The real mechanism is EXEMPT_FROM_FLOOR/isFloorExemptMetric at score.ts:108.) - returns null when nothing qualifies rather than emitting a "balanced" placeholder row as putt-bias does — most players will not qualify, and a second always-on row would double low-value feed entries. - the pace-control MECHANISM is this generator's inference, not a research-doc claim, and is worded as a hypothesis to match the forced causality_level 'inferred_hypothesis'. twoProportionZTest gained an optional options param so the n>=8 gate reuses its math instead of duplicating it; backward compatible, putt-bias's call site and its 16 existing tests are untouched. Output of a parallel audit run: 8 workers on file-disjoint scopes. Every bug below was **reproduced before it was fixed** — the failing output is quoted in each commit. ## 1. CSV header collisions silently corrupted imported stats `findColumnMapping` matched short aliases (`'r'`,`'h'`,`'hr'`,`'er'`) against headers by **bidirectional substring containment**, first hit wins. So `'hr'` matched a header literally named `"r"`, binding home runs to the runs column. `'r'` matched any header containing the letter r — including `"player"`. Reproduced by *running* the real functions. Standard box score `['name','ab','r','h','2b','3b','hr','rbi','bb','so','sb','cs']` + a hitter row (1 run, 2 hits, **0 HR**) returned `home_runs: 1`, `triples: 1`, `rbis: 1`, `caught_stealing: 2` — with `blockingCount: 0, warningCount: 0`. The bogus non-null pitching fields then trip `hasAny(v, PITCHING_ONLY_FIELDS)` and **fabricate a pitching box-score row for a position player who never pitched**. This is the exact header shape the app's own GameChanger source declares. 9 of 12 new tests failed on the unfixed code. Fix: exact-match tier first; fuzzy only when *both* sides are ≥4 chars (so no canonical short code can ever collide again); plus header-uniqueness tracking so `hits`/`runs` claim `'h'`/`'r'` before `hits_allowed`/`runs_allowed` — which is what kills the phantom row. ## 2. CoachHelm — the coach saw the diagnosis and never the drill This started from the **wrong premise**, and the correction is the useful part. I assumed the evidence was trapped in prose and needed extracting. Measured against the live DB: `sample_n`, `comparison_value`, `strokes_impact` etc. are populated on **100%** of rows and `EvidencePanel` already renders them collapsed *and* expanded. The real defect: `InsightCard` clamped `content` to two lines **unconditionally**, and the expanded block renders the evidence panel and actions — *not* the prose. The tail of every long insight wasn't behind a click, it was **unreachable**. Two lines ≈ 100–140 chars. `approach_miss` averages **377** (117 rows, largest type); `course_management` **427**. And it's the worst two-thirds to lose — these insights close on the prescription. The production example ends *"Work an alignment-stick start line gate…"*. Always the part cut. One line: `!expanded && 'line-clamp-2'`. ## 3. CRM "due today" ended at 8pm Eastern `setHours(23,59,59,999)` on a UTC runtime. A task due at 9pm Eastern was silently excluded from the "Tasks due today" panel — the admin saw "No tasks due today" and could miss a same-day follow-up. Same shape gates the Gmail daily send cap, where the window reset ~8pm Eastern. 4 of 4 assertions failed before the fix, e.g. `expected '2026-08-16T23:59:59.999Z' to be '2026-08-17T03:59:59.999Z'`. Fixed via the existing `wallClockInZone` helper, DST-safe (EST *and* EDT cases). ## 4. Class-conflict detection guessed with the server's timezone `weekdayOf`/`clockMinutesOf` fell back to the server's runtime zone (UTC on Vercel) when no timezone was passed — and the one caller passed **none**. An obligation genuinely at 05:30–06:30 Eastern read as 09:30–10:30 and **fabricated a hard conflict** against a 9am class: precisely the "false high" the file's own header forbids. Fixed to honest degradation — unknown/invalid zone returns `null` and detection early-returns rather than guessing — plus threading the real program timezone through the existing `resolveTeamTimezone` helper. ## 5. Calendar & classes UI/UX **A coach could not pick a date.** `date-picker.tsx` opened at Tailwind's `z-modal` (30) while `ModalShell` paints on the separate `--fw-z-*` ladder at 50 — the date popover rendered *behind* the modal, invisible and unclickable. **A player could not see their own attendance.** `AttendancePanel` was gated `isCoach &&`, despite already having a read-only self-view branch. It was simply never mounted for players. Plus: class sync-failure markers (the page computed which classes failed and discarded it), silent post-mutation refetch (every class edit blanked the page to a skeleton), dark-mode focus rings across 8 call sites, skeleton/first-paint shape matching, token fixes for two colors with no dark-mode override, and 44px touch targets. ## Reported, not fixed — genuine data bugs, out of a presentation pass - `FairwayEventEditor` never reads `event.is_mandatory` and hardcodes `false` on prefill, so **editing a mandatory event's time silently clears the flag**. Root cause is the server SELECT never fetching the column. - Conflict checking is skipped entirely until attendees are selected — a coach filling in a practice before inviting anyone gets no warning. - `strokes_impact` is `0.00` on every `approach_miss` row sampled — the largest insight type carries no impact signal, weakening ranking. - `evidence.diagnosis` is populated structured data (`{drivers:[…]}`) that nothing renders — a real "more root cause" opportunity needing a component. - The surface registry has no entry for `?view=insights` / `?view=deep-dive`, so only 4 of 6 player tabs resolve programmatically. ## Gates | gate | exit | |---|---| | `npm run typecheck` | 0 | | `npm run lint` | 0 | | `TZ=UTC npm test` | 0 — 1028 files, 9644 passed, 6 skipped | | `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati npm test` (+14) | 0 | | `TZ=Pacific/Midway npm test` (−11) | 0 | | `npm run build` | 0 | All three zones because two commits are timezone fixes. No test was weakened, skipped, or deleted; where an existing test pinned old behaviour it was updated deliberately and the reason recorded. Not verified in a browser — the UI work rests on typecheck, lint and the existing unit suite, not a click-through. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Three changes: two aimed at CoachHelm output quality in production, one fixing the unfixed twin of the offline data-loss bug merged in #1464. ## 1. The v1 "Retry sync" was a no-op too (`fix`) #1464 fixed this in the v2 store. A read-only audit of the v1 path found the **identical defect, unfixed**, on the surface a player actually touches mid-round. `useOfflineSync.retryFailedSync` read candidates from `getPendingRounds`/`getPendingShots` — both `index.getAll('pending')`, so every row is `'pending'` by construction — then filtered `syncStatus === 'failed'`. Never true. Nothing was ever requeued. Worse than the v2 case: **v1 had no failed-side reader at all**, so a round whose first sync attempt failed was unreachable by every code path — - the player's "Retry sync" button — this no-op, - the global sync engine's `requeueRetryableFailures` — reads the v2 store only, - the manual "Recover Round" page — also a `'pending'`-only read, despite existing specifically to recover a round that failed to submit. Proven before fixing, against the unfixed code: ``` TypeError: v1.getFailedRounds is not a function TypeError: v1.getFailedShots is not a function ``` with a passing **control** showing `getPendingRounds` returns only `['v1-ok']` and excludes the failed round — the mechanism demonstrated, not asserted. Fix: add `getFailedRounds`/`getFailedShots` (the `'failed'` side of the same `syncStatus` index) and read those. The status check is dropped as redundant; the attempt budget still gates. ## 2. Stop shipping "Monitor this pattern" as an insight (`feat`) **27 of 596 live insights carry the identical content sentence** "Monitor this pattern and discuss with your coach." Next to the approach/composite insights — which cite sample size, a Tour benchmark, a directional diagnosis and a drill — that reads as filler, and it's the concrete reason the pattern feed looks worse in production than the rest of CoachHelm. Cause: `generateRecommendation` handled exactly one condition (`days_since_last >= 7`) and ignored its `_outcome` argument, so everything else fell to a fixed string with no evidence in it. Grounded in the condition vocabulary that **actually occurs** in `golf_patterns_v2`, measured rather than invented: | condition | prod count | before | |---|---|---| | `days_since_last lte 1` — "Back-to-back rounds" | 19 | filler | | `round_type eq tournament` | 10 | filler | | `days_since_last gte 7` | 6 | handled | | `days_since_last gte 5` | 3 | filler | Back-to-back now returns a *recovery* prescription rather than a swing one; tournament-only gaps say why range volume won't close them. When no rule matches, the fallback names the condition back to the reader and is explicit that it's a tendency to confirm, not a diagnosis. The display layer keeps its handling of the old generic string — 27 legacy rows still carry it and nothing regenerates them. One existing test pinned the filler verbatim. Its stated intent is that the miner stays *player-voiced* (the coach rewrite lives in `patternToInsightVocabulary.ts`); that intent is preserved and now asserted directly, rather than by pinning the exact sentence. Five new cases pin each real production condition to a non-filler recommendation. ## 3. Record an outcome when the work is actually done (`feat`) `outcome_status` is NULL on **594 of 596** insights. That's adoption, not a broken writer — `recordFocusAreaOutcome` works and is wired. The likely cause: the capture control only rendered on the *active* card. The moment a coach hit "Mark complete," the card collapsed to a row that would *display* a verdict but offered no way to enter one. The natural closing moment had no affordance. - `FocusAreaCard`: completed branch gains a "How did it go?" row — coach only, only when a handler is wired, only when no verdict exists (the read-only pill still owns that case, so no double control). - `PlayersGridView`: the Completed section now passes `onRecordOutcome`, which it didn't — the prompt would otherwise have been dead. - `GenomeDetailView`: a completed area with no verdict stays visible so the prompt can work; one with a verdict still drops off. - `DevelopmentDrill`: the player's Accept/Decline card now shows `SourceChip`, so a player deciding on a prescribed area can see the review or insight it came from. Previously that evidence appeared only *after* accepting. Presentation layer only — no server action, loader, or data-shape change. **Deliberately not done:** no Reopen-from-declined affordance. `reactivateFocusArea` is only confirmed for `completed → active`; shipping a button the server might silently reject is worse than the honest "Declined" state. ## Gates | gate | exit | |---|---| | `npm run typecheck` | 0 | | `npm run lint` | 0 | | `TZ=UTC npm test` | 0 — 1024 files, 9620 passed, 6 skipped | | `npm run build` | 0 | Build note: on this machine it needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` (heap OOM under concurrent load) and network access for `next/font` Google Fonts. ## The bug `SyncEngine.retryFailed()` is the **only** path that can resurrect an offline item whose sync failed. It read its candidates from `getPendingRounds/Holes/Shots` — each of which queries `index.getAll('pending')`, so every row they return is `'pending'` **by construction** — and then filtered: ```ts if (round._sync_status === 'failed' && shouldRetry(...)) ``` That predicate can never be true. The loop body never ran. Nothing was ever requeued. ## Why it strands player data `markRoundFailed` sets `_sync_status = 'failed'`, and the pending queries exclude `'failed'`. So after **one** failed sync attempt: - the normal sync pass can't see the round (not `'pending'`), - `retryFailed()` can't see it either (its query only returns `'pending'`), - so it sits in IndexedDB permanently. The player-facing control is wired — `continue-round-client.tsx:954` passes `onRetrySync={offlineSyncActions.retryFailedSync}` — so a player mid-round taps "Retry sync", gets no error, and the round never syncs. The **v1 legacy path already guards this exact case**, explicitly: `sync-engine.ts:564` marks an exhausted v1 round failed "rather than leaving it stuck pending forever." The v2 path had neither that guard nor any test. `shot-storage.ts` had **zero** coverage of these functions — the same untested-live-path shape that hid the Find-a-Time 4-hour offset. ## Proven before fixed `retry-failed.test.ts` was written against the **unfixed** code and failed: ``` AssertionError: expected 'failed' not to be 'failed' ❯ src/lib/offline/retry-failed.test.ts:104:34 expect(row._sync_status).not.toBe('failed'); ``` It ships with four cases so the result is unambiguous and the fix can't overreach: - **control** — `getPendingRounds` returns only `['round-ok']`, excluding the failed round. This is the mechanism, demonstrated rather than asserted. - **requeue** — the round reaches the server **in the same call**: asserts `saveRoundDraft` was called once and the row ends `'synced'`, not merely non-`'failed'`. `retryFailed` ends in `syncPendingData()`, and "requeued" is not the same as "recovered" — a round that flipped to `'pending'` and then sat there would satisfy a weaker assertion while the player's data was still stranded. - **shots** — the highest-volume offline entity (one per stroke) requeues too, so the fix is proven on more than the round path. - **guard** — a round at `MAX_RETRY_COUNT` stays `failed`, so the fix cannot become an infinite retry loop. ## The fix Add `getFailedRounds/Holes/Shots`, querying the `'failed'` side of the same `_sync_status` index that `getFailedCount` already uses, and have `retryFailed` read those. The now-redundant status check is dropped — the query guarantees it — leaving only the backoff/budget decision. ## Test scaffolding The in-memory IndexedDB fake is extracted from `db-consolidation.test.ts` into `__fixtures__/fake-indexeddb.ts` so both suites drive the **real** storage functions against it, instead of duplicating ~150 lines. That file is otherwise unchanged and still passes 9/9 — verified before writing anything new. ## Gates | gate | exit | |---|---| | `npm run typecheck` | 0 | | `npm run lint` | 0 | | `TZ=UTC npm test` | 0 | | `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati npm test` (+14) | 0 | | `TZ=Pacific/Midway npm test` (−11) | 0 | 1022 files, **9606 passed** (+4), 6 skipped. All three zones because the test asserts on `_last_retry` / `_created_offline` timestamps. ## Scope note This fixes the requeue path. It does **not** add a "max attempts reached" notification for v2 items — a round that legitimately exhausts 10 retries still stays `failed` silently, where the v1 path surfaces it via `onItemFailed`. That asymmetry is real but is a separate change, and I have no evidence of a user hitting it. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

So I swept the repo rather than trusting the list. ## The sweep, and why the first attempt was useless A naive grep for local date methods feeding a UTC emitter flagged **45 files**. I chased the top candidates and they were all false positives — which is the useful part: - `toDateTimeLocalValue` uses local getters **deliberately**; it feeds ``, which is local by definition. "Fixing" it would reintroduce audit finding #15. - `dayBucketFor` lives under `actions/` but its only caller, `NotificationFeedPanel.tsx`, is `'use client'` — it runs in the **browser**, where the runtime zone *is* the user's zone. Correct as written. - `temporal.ts` does `setDate(getDate() - 90)` — rolling-window arithmetic with no calendar boundary, so it cannot land in the wrong bucket. The three *confirmed* bugs (`detectSemester`, `generateTimeSlots`, event reminders) share a narrower shape: a **wall-clock value** — a specific hour, or a calendar-bucket boundary — crossing into a UTC instant. Encoding that discriminator takes 45 candidates to 7. ## What this PR adds `scripts/audit-ambient-zone.mjs` — the scanner, plus the taxonomy above baked into its header, plus the six sites reviewed-and-left-alone so a re-run surfaces only genuinely new ones. Deliberately **not** a CI gate. Gating needs a checked-in baseline, and a stale baseline is worse than none — it reports and exits 0. ## What this PR does NOT do **No fix.** The 7 remaining candidates are all admin/CRM/analytics day boundaries (`setHours(0,0,0,0)` → `toISOString()`) with no observed user-visible wrong answer. The strongest of them, `insight-management.ts:207`, shifts a *custom* insight date-range filter by the UTC offset — real in principle, but I could not show anyone has hit it, and the correct fix would add a coach→team timezone lookup to a paginated list query. Three fixes for one root cause: over the last 24h I repeatedly drew confident conclusions from sources that could not support them. Each item below closes a specific way that happened. ## 1. `created_at` is not freshness (`memory/glossary.md`) I measured all five golf/CoachHelm tables that looked update-in-place. **All five are** — I had assumed two: | table | rows | `updated_at > created_at` | |---|---|---| | golf_causal_relationships | 5,641 | 5,518 (97.8%) | | golf_coach_insights | 596 | 588 (98.7%) | | golf_patterns_v2 | 538 | 308 (57%) | | golf_insight_effectiveness | 5,587 | 102 | | golf_player_focus_areas | 25 | 10 | Cost so far: two real bugs (#1449 Triage Desk ranking every refreshed insight as oldest, #1460 dedup keeping the wrong survivor) and two false "the engine is dead" alarms — one of which I chased for several cycles before finding `updated_at` was 4 minutes old. The section sits above the AUTOGEN markers. Verified `npm run docs:regen` leaves it alone: **0 deletions**, and `docs:check` passes. ## 2. Every `.claude/rules/*.md` carries a `verified:` stamp Only `coachhelm-review.md` and `design-system.md` were actually re-checked against code, so they get today's date. The other ten say: ``` verified: unverified # never re-checked against code — do not trust without grepping first ``` Deliberately not laundered with today's date. The motivating near-miss: I almost "fixed" `design-system.md` while it was **correct** — its claim is scoped to `fw-*` type roles, which `tailwind.config.ts:326-328` confirms resolve to SF Pro. `autonomy.md` is stamped as guidance rather than unverified — it makes no code claims. ## 3. Production deploys stamp their commit (`scripts/deploy-prod.sh`) `vercel deploy --prod` uploads local source with no git connection, so Vercel never sets `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` and the Sentry `release` tag carries a **stale SHA forward**. That made a perfectly healthy deploy look like "production is running old code" — disproving it took scanning all 55 live client chunks (3.48 MB) for a marker string, and I had already recommended an unnecessary `--force` redeploy. The script stamps `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_RELEASE` from HEAD via `--build-env` (build time is when Next inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`) and `--env` (so server-side agrees), and refuses to run on a dirty tree, off main, or out of sync with origin. Both guards proven to fire, not just written: ``` REFUSING: working tree is dirty. ... (exit 1) REFUSING: on branch 'docs/ground-truth-hygiene', not main. (exit 1) ``` It also pins `core.fsmonitor=false` for its own git calls — this repo's fsmonitor daemon intermittently errors, and the dirty-tree check is the one guard standing between a half-finished edit and production. ## Also: parallel agents share one working tree (`autonomy.md`) Observed yesterday — two agents dispatched in parallel, each told to `git checkout -b`. The second moved `HEAD` out from under the first mid-edit. Nothing errored; the work just landed on the wrong branch, and `git add -A` swept in the other agent's half-finished files. Documented the two valid options (serialize, or `git worktree add`) and the two rules that hold either way. ## Gates | gate | exit | |---|---| | `npm run typecheck` | 0 | | `npm run lint` | 0 | | `TZ=UTC npm test` | 0 — 1021 files, 9602 passed, 6 skipped | | `npm run docs:check` | 0 | | `shellcheck scripts/deploy-prod.sh` | 0 | Docs and one unreferenced script only — no runtime code paths touched. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## The bug `NODE_ENV` is `'production'` in **any** optimized build, so `next build && next start` on a laptop tagged every Sentry event `environment: production`. Caught live: a real `ReferenceError` whose stack path was `/private/tmp/.../wt-qa/.next/server/...`, origin `http://localhost:3210`, `server_name: Mac.lan`, HeadlessChrome — one of our own agent QA worktrees, sitting in Sentry indistinguishable from a live outage. ## The constraint that shaped it Sentry alert rules filter on `environment:production`. Relabelling a **genuine** production event would silence paging — strictly worse than the noise being removed. So both functions are written as *"downgrade ONLY on positive evidence of a local machine"*, never *"upgrade toward production"*. ## Server vs client are not symmetric, and that's the interesting part **Server** gates on `VERCEL`, which is `"1"` on every Vercel build and runtime. Its absence is a much stronger signal than a missing `VERCEL_ENV` (also absent in legitimate Vercel contexts). **Client could not use the same gate.** Two reasons: 1. Next only inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` into the browser bundle, so `process.env.VERCEL` is `undefined` in **every** browser event *including genuine production*. Keying off it would have relabelled all client production errors — the exact failure this guards against. 2. `next.config.mjs:60` bakes `NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_ENV` from `VERCEL_ENV || NODE_ENV` at **build** time, so a local `next build` ships the literal string `"production"` inside the bundle. No client env var can tell the truth; the answer was decided on the build machine. The one signal still evaluated in the browser is `window.location.hostname`. `helmsportslabs.com` and `*.vercel.app` are asserted **NOT**-local in the tests, so a deployed page can never be downgraded. ## Proven before fixing Today's expression was extracted verbatim and run against the matrix, failing exactly twice: ``` × no VERCEL + NODE_ENV=production -> NOT production (the bug) AssertionError: expected 'production' not to be 'production' × production build served from localhost -> downgraded AssertionError: expected 'production' to be 'local-production-build' Tests 2 failed | 29 passed (31) ``` **The other 29 passed under the old logic too** — including every "a real Vercel event is never relabelled" case. That is the evidence this changes nothing on the Vercel path, rather than merely that the new behaviour works. After the fix: 31/31. ## Gates | gate | exit | |---|---| | targeted suite | 0 — 31/31 | | `npm run typecheck` | 0 | | `npm run lint` | 0 | | `TZ=UTC npm test` | 0 — 1019 files, 9597 passed, 6 skipped | The full-suite run was measured while another session's in-flight work was also in the shared checkout, so treat CI on this PR as the clean proof. No errors were attributable to these four files. ## Not included Task 2 (self-hosting fonts to remove the `fonts.gstatic.com` build dependency) was assessed and **deliberately not done**. There are five Google families across four files; converting the one in scope removes one of five load sites while `src/app/layout.tsx` keeps fetching gstatic on every build. Same fragility, three changed surfaces, zero benefit. Full remediation write-up went to the coordinating session. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Two independent recency bugs in the causal layer — one write-path, one read-path. Both were silent: the engine kept running and kept producing rows, so nothing looked broken. ## Write path — the engine analysed the OLDEST 100 rounds `causal-engine.ts` loaded with `.order('round_date', { ascending: true }).limit(100)`. That is the oldest 100. Once a player crosses 100 completed rounds their causal analysis freezes on freshman-year data permanently, while the engine still writes rows on every review. Not biting yet (max ~13 rounds/player) — which is why it is cheap now. **The fix is not just flipping the sort.** `computeDaysSinceLast` reads `rounds[index - 1]` as the previous round and computes `curr - prev`, so a descending array makes every `days_since_last` negative — and that value feeds the causal-strength maths. Flipping the sort alone would trade a visible staleness bug for a silent correctness one. So: fetch newest-first, then reverse back to chronological before computing. ## Read path — relationships ranked by FIRST detection `SELECT_COLUMNS` omitted `updated_at`; both reads ordered by `created_at`. But `saveRelationships` updates in place when a relationship re-fires and only inserts a genuinely new one, so `created_at` is frozen at first detection. Measured in production 2026-08-16: | | | |---|---| | rows | 5,641 | | `updated_at > created_at` | **5,518 (97.8%)** | | newest `created_at` | 2026-07-31 | | newest `updated_at` | 2026-08-16 | **Not display-only.** The table holds physical duplicates per logical relationship (the module header records one `gir→scoring` relationship 1,831×) and `dedupeAndRank` keeps the FIRST row per natural key — so the ordering column chooses the **survivor**. By `created_at` the winner was whichever duplicate was inserted earliest, potentially one the engine stopped confirming weeks ago. Both the player and team reads change together; if they disagreed, a coach and a player would see different rows for the same relationship. `updated_at` is now selected and exposed on the returned row type. **No UI change.** ## Proven before fixed **`causal-engine.recency.test.ts`** — seeds 101 rounds. The stub *simulates Postgres*, applying whatever order/limit the engine actually asks for, so a stub returning a canned array cannot fake a pass. ``` before: expected [ 'round-000', 'round-001', … ] to not include 'round-000' after: 2 passed ``` **`causal-relationships-recency.test.ts`** — two physical rows, one natural key, `created_at` May/June vs `updated_at` Aug-16/Jul-01. ``` before: expected 'rel-stale' to be 'rel-fresh' expected 'created_at' to be 'updated_at' after: 3 passed ``` The second test asserts the dedup **survivor**, not output position. An earlier draft asserted position and was wrong — `dedupeAndRank` re-sorts by `confidence × intervention_potential`, so that draft would have failed against a correct fix. ## Gates - `npx tsc --noEmit` → **exit 0**, 0 errors - `npm run lint` → **exit 0** - targeted suites → **exit 0**, 3 files / 8 tests **Full-suite number deliberately not quoted.** This checkout currently also holds another session's in-flight observability work, so a full local run would span both changes and prove neither. CI on this PR is the clean full-suite proof. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

`buildEvidence` declined to register the enrichment blocks on the stated grounds that *"Composite titles, persona label, and goal display are **non-numeric**"*. Composite titles are emphatically not non-numeric. Sampled from production `golf_coach_insights`: ``` "3-5 ft putting: 47%" "175+ yd approach: 33% greens hit · 25 ft when you do" "Par 4 scoring: 4.24 (+0.24 vs par)" "Double bogey-or-worse rate: 4.5%" "10-15 ft putting: 21%" ``` `buildCompositeBlock` injects them **verbatim** (` - {title}`). So the prompt puts a figure in front of the model, the model uses it, and the citation verifier classifies it as a fabricated cite — then `compose()` discards the **entire review** over that one token. **A false positive by construction: the model is punished for using what it was handed.** ## Registered, not loosened Those figures are not inventions — the insight generators computed them from this player’s own data. So they get registered, exactly as the derived percentages did in #1455. Registration uses **the verifier’s own scanner**: `extractNumericTokens` is now exported from `citations.ts` and `verifyCitations` refactored to call it, so the set we register and the set it judges come from one regex. Two independent copies drifting apart is precisely how a figure becomes registerable-but-unverifiable, or the reverse. **Persona label and goal display are deliberately left unregistered.** The persona is a word, and for goals the prompt already says *"name the metric only; do NOT quote the target number or date"* — so a goal figure **should** still trip the verifier, and it still does. ## Proven failing first ``` AssertionError: expected false to be true > registers figures that appear in the composite-insight titles it injects > registers every figure in a multi-number title ``` A third test keeps the guard honest: a figure from a title that was **not** injected (`91%`) is still rejected. This widens the evidence set to exactly what the prompt contains, and no further. ## Scope, honestly This does **not** prove it fixes the 11 discards seen in the last 36 hours. I checked those against current insight titles and only 2 matched — but insights are upserted, so today’s titles are not the titles those calls saw, which makes that check unsound in both directions. What *is* proven is the mechanism: a number in the prompt that is absent from the evidence set is guaranteed to fail verification. `evidence_offered` (#1457) will show whether this was the source — once deployed. ## Verification | gate | result | |---|---| | typecheck | **exit 0** | | lint (repo, `--max-warnings 0`) | **exit 0** | | LLM suites | **exit 0** — 40 passed | | unit suite under `TZ=UTC` | **exit 0** — 1018 files, 9566 passed, 6 skipped | 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01EbVGD39JBPbGL4gxhq5Rm7

Follow-up to #1455 — **and a correction to it.** ## #1455 recovers about half, not the class #1455 supplied the derived GIR/fairway percentages so the citation verifier stops reading correct arithmetic as fabrication. Validated against the 19 real production discards: - **8 of the 9 decimal tokens** are exactly reproducible as a real round’s GIR% or fairway% — the diagnosis confirmed empirically, not just in a fixture. - But only **10 of 19** discarded calls have *all* their unmatched tokens covered. I claimed more than that in #1455. This corrects it. ## What the other 9 tripped on Integers: `26, 18, 31, 34, 35, 41, 45, 47, 68, 75`. Joined against each caller’s most recent round, they line up exactly with that round’s own numbers: | unmatched | round putts | round score | |---|---|---| | `26` ×2 | **26** | — | | `33` ×2 | **33** | — | | `34,75` | **34** | **75** | | `31,18,28` | **31** | gir_total **18** | | `41,47` | — | **88** (41+47) — a front/back nine split | `total_putts` is a claim when non-null; `total_score` is **unconditional**. So either those inputs were absent for those calls, or the round the model reviewed differs from the one this join found. **The log cannot say.** It stores `unmatched_tokens` and nothing else — no evidence set, no `round_id`. A discard row records what was *rejected* but not what it was checked *against*, which makes a fabricated number indistinguishable from a legitimate one whose claim was missing. That is the actual defect, and it is why the paragraph above ends in a guess after an hour of joins against `golf_rounds`. ## The fix The failure row now carries `evidence_offered` — the field/value pairs the verifier accepted. Fields and values only: no prose, no prompt, no completion. It lands in `golf_coachhelm_llm_calls.citations`, a row that already holds a `player_id`, so it stays the same class of data. ## Deliberately not guessing at a second fix The obvious next move is adding `9` and `18` to the verifier’s SAFE set as structural constants of golf — *"your 18 holes"* is not a claim about a player. It is probably right. **It is not proven**, and I cannot show what `26` or `47` were without the evidence set that did not exist until this commit. The next discard will say, and then it can be fixed on evidence rather than on a plausible story. ## Proven non-vacuous Run with the new field disabled: ``` AssertionError: expected undefined to be truthy > compose() citation grounding (P0-03) > discards LLM text and returns fallback when an unmatched number survives the retry ``` ## Verification | gate | result | |---|---| | typecheck | **exit 0** | | lint (repo, `--max-warnings 0`) | **exit 0** | | LLM suites | **exit 0** — 32 passed | | unit suite under `TZ=UTC` | **exit 0** — 1018 files, 9563 passed, 6 skipped | 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01EbVGD39JBPbGL4gxhq5Rm7

Found via Sentry, then measured against the LLM call log. ## The measurement In `golf_coachhelm_llm_calls`: **19 of 107 round_review compose() calls — 17.8% — were DISCARDED** for failed citation verification. Every discard in the entire table is a round review; no other task has ever failed verification. Those players silently got the deterministic template instead of the conversational round review — the flagship differentiator. ## The unmatched tokens were not hallucinations They were correct arithmetic: ``` 55.6 = 10/18 72.2 = 13/18 27.8 = 5/18 44.4 = 8/18 64.3 = 9/14 71.4 = 10/14 57.1 = 8/14 53.8 = 7/13 ``` `buildEvidence` supplies **counts** (`gir`, `gir_total`, `fairways_hit`, `fairways_total`) and the prompt renders them as `"10/18 greens"`. A good narrative then writes *"you hit 55.6% of greens"* — a derivation, not an invention. The verifier requires every numeric token to appear **verbatim** in the evidence set, so it read that as a fabricated cite and `compose()` threw the whole review away — correctly, given what it believed. ## A detail worth flagging The Sentry message reads `unmatched=26`, which looks like *26 unmatched citations*. It isn't. The log line is `unmatched=${unmatched_tokens.join(',')}` — that is **one token, the number 26**. A single unverifiable figure discards the entire narrative. I nearly filed this as "26 hallucinated citations." ## Fixed by supplying the value, never by loosening the verifier - Both renderings the model uses are registered — `"55.6%"` and `"56%"` are the same true fact, and which one it picks is not worth discarding a review over. - **A percentage that does not follow from the counts is still rejected.** That case is now an explicit test, because a fix here must not blunt the guard that stops a fabricated number reaching a player. - The prompt now states the percentage too (`"9/14 fairways (64.3%)"`), so the model quotes a supplied figure instead of computing one. `pctSuffix` and `pushDerivedPct` share the same 1-dp rounding by construction; if they drifted, the prompt would quote a number the verifier rejects. - Both guard a null or zero denominator — a missing `gir_total` must not register `NaN` or `Infinity` as a citable fact. ## Proven failing first On `BASE_INPUT`, whose own figures (10/18 = 55.6 and 9/14 = 64.3) are two of the exact tokens observed failing in production: ``` expected false to be true // "You hit 55.6% of greens in regulation." expected false to be true // "You hit 56% of greens in regulation." expected false to be true // "You found 64.3% of fairways." ``` ## Verification | gate | result | |---|---| | typecheck | **exit 0** | | lint (repo, `--max-warnings 0`) | **exit 0** | | unit suite under `TZ=UTC` | **exit 0** — 1018 files, 9563 passed, 6 skipped | Citation verification, regenerate-once, and template fallback all remain in place — this changes what counts as *grounded*, not whether grounding is checked. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01EbVGD39JBPbGL4gxhq5Rm7

`long_approach_3putt_cascade` has **never fired in production**, and the reason also put a flattering falsehood in front of coaches. ## Root cause: a conditional measure gated on an unconditional benchmark `proximity_when_hit_feet` is averaged over **green-finding shots only** (`approach-miss.ts` `aggregate()`). The PGA Tour figure it was measured against — research doc §2, *"200+ yds: ~45+ ft"* — is **Proximity to Hole over all approaches** from the range, misses included. The same section quotes 75.4% GIR alongside it, which is only coherent if misses are in the average. Conditioning on hitting the green strips out every long miss. The two quantities differ by construction and cannot be compared. ## Two consequences, both measured against production **1. The rule is dead.** The gate was `> 50` ft ("Tour ~45, +5 = weak"). Across all 29 production `approach_miss:175_plus` insights carrying a proximity: | min | p25 | median | p75 | p90 | max | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 14.0 | 22.7 | 24.8 | 31.0 | 33.3 | **36.3** | **Zero exceeded 50.** It cannot fire. **2. The prose lied — and this is the worse half.** The dial-in sentence rendered: > "When you do reach it you finish **26 ft** from the hole (**Tour ~45 ft**, over N greens)" That tells a D1 coach their player out-dials the PGA Tour from 175+ yards. ## Why CI never caught it Every fixture in `composite.test.ts` used **60 ft** or **42 ft**. Neither value has ever been produced by a player — the observed maximum is 36.3 ft. The tests proved the rule worked on inputs that do not exist. ## Fixes - **`WEAK_ON_GREEN_PROXIMITY_FT = 31`** — the production p75, the worst quartile of long-approach dial-in. Deliberately a **percentile, not a benchmark**: no sourced on-green proximity standard exists for this bucket, and inventing one is what broke the rule the first time. It should become a cohort-relative gate like `isWeakMidPutt` once `approach_miss` carries standing — today **0 of 117** production rows do, against **110/110** for `putt_distance`. - **The Tour comparison is removed from the dial-in sentence.** The reach sentence above it still carries a like-for-like benchmark (green-hit % vs Tour green-hit %), which is where the honest comparison belongs. - **`TOUR_PROXIMITY_FEET` is replaced by a comment**, not silently deleted — recording the numbers, why they are not comparable, and what would make them usable (an *unconditional* proximity, which needs the off-green misses; those are recorded in **yards** and were previously ×3'd into a fake proximity). ## Proven failing first ``` AssertionError: expected null not to be null > long_approach_3putt_cascade > fires at a proximity that actually OCCURS in production ``` Two new cases pin the rule to reality: it fires at the production **p90 (33.3 ft)** and stays silent at the **median (24.8 ft)**, so it flags a worst-quartile leak rather than half the roster. The "good proximity" fixture is re-anchored from 42 ft to the **p25 (22.7 ft)** — 42 sat under the old gate but above the observed maximum, so it tested nothing. ## Verification | gate | result | |---|---| | typecheck | **exit 0** | | lint (repo, `--max-warnings 0`) | **exit 0** | | unit suite under `TZ=UTC` | **exit 0** — 1017 files, 9550 passed, 6 skipped | No migration, policy, or AUTOGEN source touched. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01EbVGD39JBPbGL4gxhq5Rm7

Closes out the ambient-zone-read sweep, and writes up a root-level CoachHelm signal that stops one step short of a production schema change. ## Two latent zone bugs — flagged as latent, not dressed up as live **`trajectory-forecaster.ts`.** `seasonalProjection` built `point.date` as `toISOString().split('T')[0]` (a UTC calendar day) and read it back with `new Date(s).getMonth()` — parses at UTC midnight, answers in the **runtime** zone. Measured: ``` TZ=UTC new Date('2026-05-01').getMonth() = 4 (May) TZ=America/New_York new Date('2026-05-01').getMonth() = 3 (April) TZ=Pacific/Midway new Date('2026-05-01').getMonth() = 3 (April) ``` 1 May, 1 Oct and 1 Nov are all seasonal **bucket boundaries**, so west of UTC each picked up the neighbouring bucket — a 0.3–0.4 stroke swing on the projection. **On Vercel the runtime is UTC, so production was already correct.** Latent, not live. It was wrong on every developer machine and in any non-UTC runtime. The bucket logic is extracted to a pure exported `seasonalAdjustmentFor()` because `seasonalProjection` is private and had **no coverage of any kind**. Eight tests pin the boundaries — including the three first-of-month cases that *are* the bug — and pass identically under UTC, Eastern and Midway. **`ical.ts`.** `convertToICalEvent` has a `setHours` branch feeding `formatDateTime`, which emits `yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ`. Local getter, UTC consumer — a 09:00 event would publish to a subscriber's calendar as 09:00Z = 05:00 Eastern. It is **unreachable today only because its one caller passes `start_time`/`end_time` as null**, so the zone-correct `parseISO` branch always wins. Correctness by accident of a caller, so it gets a comment naming the fix rather than a speculative rewrite of a branch nothing executes. ## A root-level putting signal, specced not built `docs/design/putt-slope-gap-generator.md`. **The obvious version is wrong, and the doc leads with that.** Roster-wide, level putts convert 81.4% and downhill 25.0% — a 56-point gap that is *entirely distance*: level putts average 4.4 ft, downhill 16.2 ft. `PuttBiasGenerator` already learned this exact lesson one column over. Controlled for distance, on real customer data (demo excluded), a real effect survives — and it is **largest at the shortest distances**, which is why nothing surfaces it: | bucket | level | downhill | |---|---|---| | 0–3 ft | 98.6% | **84.4%** | | 3–6 ft | 65.6% | **52.6%** | | 6–10 ft | 36.1% | **25.5%** | | 10 ft+ | — | no signal | A player at 98% level and 84% downhill inside 3 ft blends to ~96% on `puttMakePct0_3` and reads as flawless. **But all 9 real players with n≥10 show a significant gap (z 2.47–11.23)** — so "downhill is hard" is a fact about golf, not an insight about a player, and a significance gate alone fires for the whole roster. The insight is the **spread against the squad**: Gillen's 63.8pp against a squad median near 36.5pp. Compare to cohort, never to zero. Two hazards recorded because they will poison the next analysis too: - **~58% of production putts are demo data.** `Demo University Golf` plus its `Pat Demo` clone outweigh every real customer combined, and the clone copies rounds *across player names* — so per-player aggregates come back byte-identical for unrelated players. Filter `o.name NOT ILIKE '%demo%'` or the numbers are fiction. - **The window must be 365 days, not the v3-usual 90.** All 381 qualifying downhill putts are inside 365 days but only 131 inside 90 — ~5.5 per player against a 15-putt floor, so a 90-day generator would never fire. ## Why it is specced and not built The generator needs a new `MetricId`, and registering one requires a row in `20260606010000_v3_golf_metrics_seed_reproducible.sql` — verified as the **only** migration that has ever inserted a metric, and the file `metric-registry-attribute-parity.test.ts` parses as the DB source of truth. That means either editing an applied historical migration, or adding a new migration **and** extending that guard test. The latter is correct engineering, and it is a schema change against the database serving Golf, Baseball and Lift Lab. CLAUDE.md makes DB changes mandatory-review. That is an owner call, not an unattended 1am one. ## Verification | gate | result | |---|---| | typecheck | **exit 0** | | lint (repo, `--max-warnings 0`) | **exit 0** | | unit suite under `TZ=UTC` | **exit 0** — 1018 files, 9556 passed, 6 skipped | | seasonality tests × 3 zones | **exit 0** — UTC, Eastern, Midway | No migration, policy, or AUTOGEN source touched. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01EbVGD39JBPbGL4gxhq5Rm7

When a coach hits a scheduling conflict, GolfHelm offers alternative times. Those times were being generated **03:00–15:00 Eastern**. ## The bug `workingHours` defaults to `{ start: 7, end: 19 }` in `conflicts.ts` — an explicit **wall-clock** intent, "7am to 7pm". `generateTimeSlots` realised it with `setHours`, which resolves in the **runtime** zone. The whole path is server-side: ``` FairwayEventEditor → checkScheduleConflicts (server action, golf.ts:4363) → checkEventConflicts → findCommonAvailability → generateTimeSlots ``` On Vercel the runtime is UTC, so 07:00 became 07:00Z = 03:00 Eastern. The suggestion feature is reached *precisely* when scheduling has already gone wrong, which is the worst place to be four hours off. Same class as `89fd943d7`, in the **sibling function of the same file**. It surfaced only because a shifted-timezone CI shard failed for an unrelated reason two files away. ## Proven before fixed The test was written against the old signature and run first: ``` AssertionError: expected 3 to be greater than or equal to 7 ``` It asserts **per-slot**, not on the first slot — the bug shifts the whole grid, so a single sample could coincide with a correct hour by luck. `findCommonAvailability`, `generateTimeSlots` and `suggestedTimes` had **zero** test coverage before this. That is why a four-hour offset lived in the suggestion path unseen. ## Changes - **`resolveTeamTimeZone(teamIds, supabase, action)` extracted.** One rule, two callers with different team sets — `getUserBusyPeriods` resolves one user's teams, `checkEventConflicts` every attendee's. It takes `teamIds` rather than deriving them, so the rule cannot diverge. - **`generateTimeSlots` takes the zone** and uses `wallClockInZone`. The working-hours guard is now minute arithmetic instead of `slotEnd.getHours()` — which fixes a second latent bug: a slot running to midnight read as hour `0`, which is `<= 19`, so it was wrongly kept. - **`timeZone` is required, not optional.** An optional zone hands a forgetful caller the runtime zone back — the same null-fallback trap that hid this for months. It earned itself immediately: the compiler caught the second call site (the next-week fallback) that would otherwise have stayed broken. The zone resolves inside the `conflicts.length > 0` branch, so the no-conflict path pays for no extra query. ## Verification | gate | result | |---|---| | typecheck | **exit 0** | | lint (repo, `--max-warnings 0`) | **exit 0** | | unit suite under `TZ=UTC` | **exit 0** — 1017 files, 9548 passed, 6 skipped | | calendar suites × 4 zones | **exit 0** — UTC, Kiritimati (+14), Midway (−11), New York | 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01EbVGD39JBPbGL4gxhq5Rm7

Three defects, one root cause: **`created_at` is the row's insert batch, not when its content was computed.** Insights upsert by `signature`, so a row created in June and recomputed this morning still reports as June. 68% of live rows were born in June. ## 1. The Triage Desk said nothing was new while everything changed `ageDaysFromCreatedAt(row.created_at)` drove four things at once: the rendered `"{n}d ago"`, the "new" filter, the BriefBand counter, and **the ranking** — `recencyBonus()` awarded +3/+2/+1 for ≤1/≤3/≤7 days into `attentionScore`. The consequence was the inverse of the intent: **every genuinely fresh insight scored zero recency bonus**, because its `created_at` is June. The term systematically demoted new content. Observed live: > 2 URGENT · **0 NEW THIS WEEK** · 7 PLAYERS FLAGGED — while 60 rows had been recomputed in the previous hour and 188 in 36 hours. **`updated_at` is not the fix and was deliberately not substituted.** A DB trigger (`update_golf_coach_insights_updated_at`) bumps it on *any* row update, and `insight-management.ts` writes `dismissed`, `acknowledged_at` and `lifecycle_state`. Ranking by it would promote an insight *because a coach dismissed it*. So the false label is removed and the recency term is **neutralised to 0**, not re-pointed. body: Six fixes from a Bridge/Vercel error sweep plus two coach reports from Ben Potter. Four were caused by the same root defect wearing different clothes. ## The AI account mix-up — 3 call sites The Vercel AI Gateway and the Anthropic API are **different accounts**. A bare `'anthropic/…'` model string routes through the gateway on the project's OIDC token (there is no `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`) and bills the **Vercel team** balance; `anthropic(…)` uses `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Three places chose independently and only one chose correctly: | call site | before | effect | |---|---|---| | `chat/stream/route.ts` | had the branch | coach chat kept working | | `v3/llm/compose.ts` | bare string | **every round review served its template since 07-29** | | `golf/schedule-vision.ts` ×2 | bare string | **every class-schedule import failed** | The gateway account is free-tier and answered all three with *"Free tier users do not have access to this model. Upgrade to paid credits."* Because coach chat was healthy the whole time the platform looked fine — and topping up the **Anthropic** console, the obvious response to an out-of-credit message, changed nothing for the two paths actually failing. The choice now lives in one place, `src/lib/ai/model-provider.ts`. `chat/stream` derives from `MODEL_FOR_TASK` instead of naming the model a second time. `model_id` stays gateway-prefixed everywhere it is priced or logged — the cost table keys on it, and an unrecognised key bills at 15× the real rate. ## Class semester was never persisted 26 of 30 synced class series carried a **NULL** semester. Three write paths stored `null` while three read paths fell back to `detectSemester('')` — a pure function of **today's date**. A null column did not mean "no term", it meant "re-guess on every edit", and the guess moves as the calendar does. Edit in September a class added in August and the whole series re-dates. That is the *"individual calendars move all the events around"* report. Four series had also collapsed to **1–2 meetings**: a schedule imported 6 August carried a real start date of 12 August (a Fall class) but the label said "Summer 2026", so `parseSemesterDates` produced `Aug 12 → Aug 15`. A term left with under 21 days by its own start date is now re-derived from that date. ## Per-round stats (Ben's request) > "I can see all 75 or so stats... but that is all their rounds combined. If I try to look at a specific round, it does not give all the stats." No new stats maths was needed. `getDetailedStats` has always taken a `roundId` and honours it in all four internal branches — but the only caller passed the literal `'overall'`, so the parameter was fully built and permanently unreachable. This wires it to a picker on the roster drill-down. Scoping moves the detailed panel and the spray chart **only**. Trend, standing, leak maps and worst-holes are cross-round by construction and stay career-wide, and the UI says so. ## Verified in a browser, not just by gates Every gate was green while the picker's `

body:
CodeQL `js/incomplete-sanitization`, 2 high alerts — both real.

Two message-search call sites did `query.replace(/%/g,'\\%').replace(/_/g,'\\_')`, which escapes the wildcards but never the **escape character**. A user-typed backslash therefore survived into the pattern and changed what the next character meant:

- `a\%b` → `a\\%b` — LIKE reads `\\` as a literal backslash and then `%` as a **live wildcard**, precisely what the escaping exists to prevent.
- `100\` → unchanged — a trailing escape with nothing to escape: a malformed pattern.

Both sites now use a shared `escapeLikePattern()`.

**Notably, the codebase already had this right — twice.** `demo-request.ts` and the gmail-replies cron each carry a correct local copy (`value.replace(/[\\%_]/g, c => `\\${c}`)`), and a comment beside one asks for exactly this shared home. The shared helper matches their single-pass form rather than inventing a third style. Those two are left in place — this change is scoped to the sites that were actually wrong.

Honest on severity: this is a name search, not raw SQL — practical impact is modest. But the behaviour is wrong and it is exactly what the original comment claimed to handle.

Found while triaging the CodeQL failure on #1440. Those alerts were reported as "new in this pull request" but were created at 2026-08-09T00:53Z, hours before it, in a file that PR does not touch — a diff-attribution artifact, not a regression. Fixing them here clears main and unblocks that check.

Verified: the test asserts the OLD expression's wrong output alongside the new one, so it documents the defect rather than only the fix; 4 passed; lint 0; tsc 0; full suite 1002 files / 9321 passed.
title: fix(security): message search escaped wildcards but not the escape character

`saveRoundDraft` looks for the player's existing in-progress round before deciding whether to update it or create a new one. That read discarded its error.

A failure looked like *"this player has no draft"*, so the else-branch **inserted a second in-progress round**. This is the **autosave** path — so a transient blip mid-round creates a duplicate draft, and later saves can land on the wrong one, stranding the shots already entered against the first.

It also **bypassed the `hasTrackedRoundData()` guard entirely** — the very check that exists so the draft writer never overlays a round the tracked-shot flow now owns. That protection only runs inside the `if (existingDraft)` branch a failed read skips. So the failure did not merely create a duplicate; it stepped around the safety net built for exactly this data.

Now refuses and logs. Refusing is right rather than guessing: the caller retries on the next autosave tick, so a refusal costs one tick and a wrong guess costs a split round.

`.maybeSingle()` still reports a genuine "no draft yet" as `{ data: null, error: null }`, so a player's **first** save still creates one.

Found by censusing the existence-guard-before-write shape that produced the four course-library bugs (39 sites repo-wide). This is the round-entry one — the highest-traffic path of the set.

Reads baseline → 1062.

body:
**Reported live:** a Guilford coach clicked "forgot password", got nowhere, and was told to contact the owners. He is not an edge case — **this failed for every user, every time.**

The reset link is minted **server-side** by `admin.generateLink()`, so the recipient's browser never stored a PKCE `code_verifier`. We then emailed Supabase's `action_link`, which bounces through `/auth/v1/verify` and redirects in whichever flow the project uses:

- **PKCE** → `?code=`, which `exchangeCodeForSession()` cannot exchange without the verifier that browser never had;
- **implicit** → tokens in the URL **fragment**, which the reset page cannot see at all, because it reads the query string.

Both fall through to *"This reset link is invalid or has expired."*

The email now links straight to **our own reset page carrying `token_hash`**. A token_hash needs no verifier, and the page's `verifyOtp({ type: 'recovery', token_hash })` branch was **already written and already correct** — it simply never received one. No page changes were needed.

### Measured, not assumed

`public.emails` shows `sslate@guilford.edu` was sent three reset emails (08-07 ×2, 08-09), **opened and clicked every one within seconds** of delivery, `click_count: 2` on the latest — and stayed locked out. The send path was never the problem, which is why a "no email arrived" fix would have changed nothing.

This also closes the one client error I previously said I lacked evidence to diagnose: `sslate@guilford.edu`, `/golf/login`, *"An unexpected response was received from the server"*, 08-07 21:35 — the same minute as his second reset attempt.

Fixes **both sports** — golf and baseball share this sender.

Verified: both link assertions **red** against the old `action_link` and green with the fix, while the `no-account` and `unconfigured` cases pass in **both** directions → 4 passed; lint 0; tsc 0; full suite 1001 files / 9317 passed.

Two guards that gate a **write** on a coach-identity read, found by censusing the shape that produced the four course-library bugs (**39 such sites repo-wide**).

**1. `onboarding.ts` could delete a real coach profile.** `preExistingCoach` decides whether the rollback paths may `DELETE` the coach row — `createdCoachId = preExistingCoach ? null : coach.id`, deleted at three call sites. Its error was discarded, so a failed read looked like "no pre-existing coach" and the code believed it had created a profile it had not. **Any later failure in onboarding would then delete that coach's real profile.**

The comment directly above that read already warns about exactly this — *"deleting a pre-existing coach profile because a later step failed would turn a recoverable error into data loss"* — it just never considered the read itself failing.

**2. `acceptStaffInvite` mints a duplicate coach.** `existingCoach` decides whether to insert. A failed read looked like "this user has no coach row", so the insert created a **second coach profile** for someone who already had one. A duplicate identity row, not a wrong message.

Both now refuse and log. `.maybeSingle()` reports a genuine miss as `{ data: null, error: null }`, so first-time onboarding and a genuinely new coach are unaffected — only the unreadable case changes.

**Course library — four guards that turn a failed read into a bad row:**

1. **`createCourse` minted a duplicate.** The dedup read's error was discarded, so a failure looked exactly like "no such course" and the insert below added a **second copy to the Cloud Course Library every team shares**. Nobody would notice until two Wolf Laurels appeared in the picker. Nothing logged. Now refuses.
2. **`saveTeamCourse` wiped the team's settings.** A failed existing-row read looked like "nothing saved yet", so the upsert overwrote the team's **default tee and pinned state** with defaults and reassigned `created_by_user_id` — silent data loss on choices a coach made. Now refuses.

4. **Tee reuse failed spuriously.** A failed read looked like "no tees here", so the create hit the unique guard and the coach got a hard failure for a tee that already existed.

**Tasks — assigning a task notified nobody.** `createTask` writes the assignment rows, then resolves recipients (`golf_players → user_id`, then `users → email`). Both reads discarded their error; a failure left the list null, the guards fell through, and **no notification went out at all** — while the task was created, so the coach saw success. The surrounding `catch` never fired because supabase-js **resolves** failures rather than throwing. Still fire-and-forget by design; only the silence changes.

body:
`sendPushNotification` ran a per-token loop in which **both** failure paths — an Edge Function rejection and a thrown network error — were swallowed to `console.error`, then returned `{ success: true }` **unconditionally** after the loop. Separately, the device-token read at the top bundled `tokenError` in with "no tokens" and returned success for that too.

So `sendBulkPushNotification` counted `sent++` for every user, including users whose every device rejected the push and users whose token read never ran. **A coach assigning a task, publishing travel, or posting an announcement got a confident "sent" for notifications nobody received** — and because the failures went to `console.error` rather than `logServerError`, none of it reached `admin_events` either, so the Bridge dashboard agreed with the lie.

Now:
- a failed token read returns failure and logs (it is not "no devices");
- delivery is counted, and zero deliveries across N tokens returns failure and logs, naming the type, the user, and how many tokens were tried;
- partial delivery still counts as delivered — the person got it on at least one device, and dead tokens are already pruned by the existing path.

**Honest non-delivery is preserved and tested in both directions:** a user with no registered devices is still a success (nothing was owed), and a user who has turned this notification type **off** is still a success. Neither is a failure.

Also updated the existing push test, which mocked the logger with only `logServerEvent`: the new `logServerError` call was undefined there, threw, and was swallowed by the outer catch — breaking four token-pruning assertions for a reason unrelated to pruning. Three of its `success === true` expectations covered pushes that had actually **failed** and now correctly expect `false`; the preference-gated one still expects `true`.

Verified: 4 assertions red pre-fix **with both honest-case assertions green**; 18 tests passing across both push files; lint 0; tsc 0; full suite 996 files / 9297 passed.

body:
`fetchAllRowsResult` deliberately preserves supabase-js's contract — it resolves to `{ data, error }` and returns `data: null` when the read failed. That makes it exactly as easy to get wrong as a raw query, and **harder to see wrong**, because the wrapper reads like a helper that has already handled things.

`const { data } = await fetchAllRowsResult(...)` therefore turns a failed read into an empty list, and the page downstream states that emptiness as a fact: "no trips", "no rounds", a leaderboard of zeroes.

The unchecked-Supabase-read ratchet cannot see any of it — it matches the supabase query, and here the query is a callback **argument** to the wrapper. Not theoretical: the golf travel itinerary list is one of these, and its baseball twin had already been fixed once as a real customer-facing bug (#1404). Fixing the golf one in #1413 moved the reads baseline by 1 instead of 2, which is what exposed the gap.

Adds `helm/no-unchecked-paginated-read` plus a ratchet, as a **separate baseline** rather than folding newly-visible sites into the reads number — that number should keep meaning what it has meant all week.

**Baseline 23**, concentrated in `stats-data.ts`, `stats-leak-maps.ts`, `shot-analytics.ts` and the CoachHelm mining paths — mostly numbers a coach reads as fact.

Carries the same false-zero guard as its siblings: 0 against a non-zero baseline is treated as a rule that failed to load, not a repo that fixed everything. **Canary-verified** — the rule exits 1 on a synthetic bad shape, so 23 is a real census and not a silent no-op. Two independent detectors agreed on the count before I trusted it.

Two gates in the recruiting privacy path answered a failed read with the permissive value. Both are proven by tests that were red against the pre-fix code.

**1. `isPlayerProfilePrivate` — a private player exposed to recruiters.**
It destructured only `data`, so a failed read returned `false` — which there does not mean "came back empty", it means "this profile is NOT private". `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer` turns that straight into `{ allowed: true }`, so a dropped connection while checking a player who had explicitly opted out returned *allowed* and handed a college coach their contact details. **2. `getDiscoverableTeamPlayerIds` — Discover became an unfiltered cross-tenant listing.**
Discover's core rule is "only players on a discoverable team". Steps 1 and 2 fail closed (`return []` → early return). Step 3 returned `null`, and `null` was consumed as *no constraint*: the early return tested `!== null && length === 0` so it was skipped, and the `.in('id', …)` filter tested `ids && length > 0` so it was skipped too. One failed read removed the rule and returned every recruiting-activated non-college player in the database, cross-tenant — including players from programs that had turned their public profile off. `null` now means refuse at both call sites, matching what it already means in Compare's copy of the same filter.

Three fail-opens shipped in this codebase, and **the unchecked-read ratchet could not see any of them** — because all three bound their error correctly and then answered it permissively:

```js
const { data, error } = await supabase.from('baseball_player_settings')…
if (error) return new Set();          // ← nobody is private
```

The caller applies that as `!privateIds.has(id)`, so an empty set filters **nobody**. The value meaning *"the read failed"* and the value meaning *"allow"* are the same value — indistinguishable to the code and to the reader.

That one is a *decision*, and this rule's job is to make such decisions **visible** rather than accidental. Paying one down means fixing it **or** marking it with an eslint-disable and a reason. Both are wins.

Registered `"off"` in the shared config for the same reason as its sibling (turning it on would fail Lint on every PR), enforced by `scripts/fail-open-audit.mjs`, wired into CI after the existing ratchet. USING decides which rows a coach may *touch*; WITH CHECK decides what the row may **become** — and it said nothing about `team_id`. It discarded its error. So a failed read produced `existing = null`, the dedupe pass was **skipped entirely**, and the row was written as a fresh CREATE. Re-importing a session after a transient failure **duplicated that player’s stats**.
