body:
## What was broken

**Every player join on production was dead**, on both entry points — the `/golf/join/[code]` invite link and the new signup-with-team-code flow. Both funnel through `processGolfTeamInvitation`.

`golf_teams_select` is `USING (is_golf_team_coach(id) OR is_golf_team_player(id))`. A player who is *about to* join is neither yet, so the "does this team exist?" read inside `validateGolfPlayerCanJoinTeam` returned **zero rows for exactly the people the join flow exists to serve**. It reported `Team not found` and abandoned the join before the SECURITY DEFINER insert — which works fine — was ever called.

## How it was proven, not guessed

Role impersonation against production, as a real freshly-signed-up player:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `select … from golf_players where id = <own>` | 1 ✅ |
| `select … from golf_teams where id = <target>` | **0** ❌ |
| `select count(*) from golf_teams` | **0** |
| `golf_team_by_join_code('…')` | 1 ✅ |
| `golf_join_team_with_code('…')` (rolled back) | inserts membership, player active on the team ✅ |

The definer path was never reached.

## The fix

The caller already resolves the team through `golf_team_by_join_code` — the only way to see a team you are not on — so it now passes that resolution down instead of the callee re-reading it under RLS.

**This widens nothing.** The membership INSERT is still performed by `golf_join_team_with_code`, which re-resolves the team from the code server-side and ignores any id handed to it. Validation is a pre-flight for error messaging; authorization lives in the definer function.

## Second defect, same cause

The team lookup feeding the *"<player> has joined <team>"* coach notification runs **before** the insert, so it too came back null and no coach was ever notified of a join. Now uses the resolved team.

## Why no test caught it

The shared Supabase mock returns seeded data for every `from(table)` read, so `golf_teams` was always readable in tests. The failure is a *denial*, and only a mock that can deny expresses it. The new suite models the denial: **against the pre-fix code it fails 6/9 with the exact production symptom, `"Team not found"`**; with the fix, 9/9.

Negative cases are pinned too — wrong code, already on another team, already a member, onboarding incomplete, someone else's player profile, and a definer-insert rejection all still refuse.

## Gates

- typecheck 0 errors
- eslint 0 errors
- **8873/8873** unit tests pass
- `next build` exit 0 (`teams.ts` is `'use server'`; the added `export interface` is type-only and erased — verified by a real build, not assumed)

Recovered from `helmv3-demo-guard`, a git worktree that existed only on the founder's laptop and was never pushed. Rebuilt on current `main` and re-verified there.

Every prospect entering the public golf demo signs into the **same** Supabase account. Without a guard, one visitor's mutation is visible to — and wrecks the tour for — every other concurrent visitor.

BaseballHelm already solves this inside `withBaseballAction` (`demoSafe` opt-in, fail closed). Golf has no equivalent action wrapper, so this adds the same protection as a one-line assertion a mutating action can adopt incrementally:

```ts
const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
if (!user) throw new Error('Unauthorized');
await assertGolfDemoWritable(user.email);
```

Read paths are untouched — this only guards writes. The thrown error is explicitly modelled as expected control flow (not a defect), so callers surface a friendly "the demo is read-only" message and it never reaches Sentry, mirroring `BaseballDemoReadOnlyError`.

**Nothing adopts it yet.** This PR only adds the module and its tests, so merging changes no behaviour — it makes the guard available to wire into golf's mutating actions.

Verified on current main: typecheck ✅ · lint ✅ · 46 tests in `src/lib/demo` ✅

body:
Closes 20 of the 22 issues filed during the overnight audit; the two left open need an account action rather than code (listed at the bottom). Every fix below was reproduced before it was written and re-verified after.

## Security (already applied to production)

Five migrations, each verified against prod with a paired control that could fail:

- **#1258** `golf_coaches` had `USING (true)` on SELECT — 15 coaches' rows (10 emails, 3 phones) readable by any signed-in user. Invisible to the `rls_policy_always_true` advisor, which only inspects INSERT/WITH CHECK.
- **#1257** `golf_teams` was readable via `USING (join_code IS NOT NULL)`. Policies are OR'd, so that exposed **every** team row and **every** join code to any signed-in user. Lookup moved into a definer function that never returns `join_code`; the join itself now re-resolves the team from the code server-side instead of trusting a client-supplied team id.
- **#1267 / #1268** three definer RPCs filtered on a caller-supplied identity rather than `auth.uid()`.
- **#1253** Lift Lab had zero INSERT policy on `helm_lifting_coaches`, dead-ending coach onboarding.
- **#1262** two already-merged migrations had never actually been run.

One judgement call worth flagging: I did **not** `REVOKE EXECUTE` on `user_conversation_ids`, because five RLS policies evaluate it as the querying user — doing so would have killed golf messaging outright. Verified 18 messages / 3 conversations still visible afterwards.

## The one that mattered most — #1270

"Create qualifier" did nothing at all: no POST, no row, no error message.

The cause is in Base UI, not our handler. Every `Checkbox.Root` calls `useField({ enabled: !groupContext })`, so an **ungrouped** checkbox registers itself as a field of the enclosing `<Form>`. Outside a `Field.Root` it inherits the default field context, whose validity is `null`. `Form`'s submit handler then runs `values.filter(f => !f.validityData.state.valid)` — and `!null` is `true`, so all 7 roster checkboxes counted as permanently invalid. Form called `preventDefault()` and never invoked our `onSubmit`. With no `Field.Root` there is also no `<Field.Error>`, which is why it failed in complete silence.

Wrapping the roster in `CheckboxGroup` flips `enabled` to false so nothing registers. Verified live: POST 200, redirect, row created with exactly the 2 selected entries (test row deleted afterwards).

Two earlier diagnostic conclusions on this were wrong and are recorded as such in the commit: `defaultPrevented` proved nothing (the handler calls `preventDefault()` unconditionally on line 1), and the `required`-attribute hypothesis was disproved by the edit form having the same fields and working.

## Everything else

| | |
|---|---|
| **#1251** | React #310 on 100% of coach visits to `/team-hub` and `/settings/notifications`. The framework-level fix used for the bare redirect shims can't apply — the redirect is role-conditional and `next.config.mjs` has no session. Both now render `<FeatureUnavailable>` in place, the pattern every coach-only page already uses for the mirror case. |
| **#1265** | DATE columns parsed as UTC midnight. Reproduced in `TZ=America/New_York`: tasks stored `2026-07-22`/`2026-07-28` rendered "Jul 21"/"Jul 27". Writing the guard surfaced a **worse second symptom the issue missed** — the same files decided *overdue* the same way, flipping true the evening **before** the due date and disagreeing with the canonical rule they claim in their own comments to follow. 7 client sites fixed. |
| **#1266** | A focus-area target could ask the player to get worse and rendered "100% there". Can't be caught at display time (a mistyped target and a legitimate self-heal are numerically identical after the fact), so the guard is at write time. Audited all 12 live rows: exactly one contradiction, the issue's own test row. Removed. |
| **#1249** | Roster per-row actions were 88×20 and 76×24 on a phone. Both deliberately wrap a StatusPill, so `min-height` was the wrong tool — added `.fw-touch-hit`, which grows an invisible `::after`. Measured at 390×844: visual unchanged, hit box now 44px. |
| **#1250** | `completeCoachOnboarding` INSERTed unconditionally against a `UNIQUE (user_id)`, producing an unwinnable retry loop. Now an upsert — which forced a second fix: all three rollback branches deleted the coach row by id, so with an upsert a later failure would have deleted a **pre-existing** profile. |
| **#1263** | The baseball calendar rendered a Documents panel wired entirely to golf tables. Verified the reachability claim independently: the golf route renders `FairwayCalendar`, which imports only *types* from `EventDetailModal`. Gated behind a new capability, default off. |
| **#1260** | Role-denial screens printed their heading and message twice. |
| **#1255 / #1256** | Two integrations that looked functional. `/admin/billing` showed a full invoice form while production has no Stripe vars — the failure only appeared after the admin filled in the entire invoice. CoachHelm was 100% template-fallback for 8 days behind a single amber dot, because the dot grid is an error-*count* with hysteresis and this is a *rate*. Added an availability panel that refuses to fabricate: no traffic reports neutral, never green. |
| **#1264** | 2,808 lines unreachable from any of 667 route entry points — **four of five had green test suites**. Added a route-reachability check; Knip can't express this because a test importing a component makes it "referenced". |

## Corrections to the filed issues

- **#1264 was wrong** that `ShotTrackingComprehensive` had no importer. It exported `calculateHoleStats` with a 42-test suite — testing a *duplicate* of the function that actually ships. That suite was re-pointed at the shipping implementation (all 42 pass unchanged, so no drift) and moved next to it. Coverage kept, false confidence dropped.
- **#1265's site list was incomplete** — see the overdue finding above.

## Verification

- typecheck ✅ · lint ✅ · **934 files / 8,828 unit tests** ✅ · `next build` ✅
- New regression tests, each proven red before green where a before-state existed: qualifier submit (fails on the pre-fix component), date anchoring, directional target guard, touch targets, AI availability, route reachability (fails when a throwaway orphan is added).

## Not done — these are account actions, not code

- Top up the Vercel AI Gateway (the actual repair behind #1256)
- Set Stripe production keys (#1255)
- Rotate the `admin@helmsportslabs.com` password + delete the `create-admin-user` Edge Function (#1271)
- Promote main to production (#1269) — note `git.deploymentEnabled {"*": false}`, so merging does not deploy

## Also worth knowing

Two Next dev servers were sharing one `.next`, which had grown to **30 GB** and was serving stale chunks — a fix verified against it would have been a false positive. Consolidated to one server and reclaimed the space.

Three server-side overdue comparisons were left alone deliberately: they run in UTC, where the question is server-vs-client divergence rather than a parse bug, and that needs a decision rather than a silent rewrite.

## Closes

Closes #1249, closes #1250, closes #1251, closes #1252, closes #1253, closes #1254, closes #1255, closes #1256, closes #1257, closes #1258, closes #1259, closes #1260, closes #1262, closes #1263, closes #1264, closes #1265, closes #1266, closes #1267, closes #1268, closes #1270.

Dependabot's #1191 bundles 16 dev-dependency updates and fails 14 CI checks.
The cause is not flaky — it is a hard ecosystem incompatibility:

    Error: typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0.

#1191 bumps typescript ^5.9.3 -> ^7.0.2, and the pinned typescript-eslint
refuses to run against it. Merging as-is would break ESLint and typecheck for
the whole repo, which is the one failure mode that makes every later PR's green
meaningless. Three other majors ride along in the same PR.

current ranges so each can be upgraded deliberately:

> **Stacked on #1220.** Base is `fix/deepsec-wave1-security`, not `main` — merge #1220 first.
> This branch also inherits three unrelated commits that were on the wave-1 branch
> (`BaseballInviteButton` polish, CoachHelm calibration, a docs report), including the two lint
> warnings they introduced. Those are not from this work.

## What this is

Remediation of the **deepsec wave-2 scan**: the 129 files that use `createAdminClient()` **outside**
`src/app/golf/actions` — cron routes, webhooks, the admin data layer, CoachHelm v2/v3 mining, baseball
actions, and the notification/email libs. Wave 1 (#1220) covered the golf action files.

52 findings. **39 confirmed by adversarial verification, 10 refuted, 1 uncertain.** Refuted findings mean
the code was already correct; changing it would have been the regression. Two further findings were
excluded before any work started: one I disproved by hand (a claimed pagination truncation that keyset
paging handles correctly), and one that was the scanner recording that it had *cleared* some flags.

**56 files changed, +2,466 / −449.**

## Highest-impact fixes

- **`src/lib/notifications/push.ts`** exported `sendPushNotification` and `sendBulkPushNotification` as
  `'use server'` actions with **zero** auth checks anywhere in the file — public POST endpoints letting
  anyone push notifications to arbitrary users and burn the paid quota.
- **`completeCoachOnboarding`** accepted a client-supplied `_preVerifiedUser` and skipped authentication
  entirely when present, passing that attacker-controlled object into service-role writes. Every parameter
  of a `'use server'` export is client-controlled. Introduced 5 weeks ago in `638a14c64` — **already live
  on main**, so this is a fix to shipped code, not a pre-merge catch.
- **Stored blind SSRF** in `api/push-subscriptions` via an unvalidated Web Push `endpoint`. Now validated
  at both the source (route) and the sink (`v3/foundation/push.ts`) — the latter had **no guard at all**,
  despite a comment claiming the two were kept in sync.
- **`CRON_SECRET` compared with a non-constant-time `!==`** in two cron routes.
- **Rate-limit keys derived from the client-controlled leftmost `X-Forwarded-For` hop.**
- **Unsubscribe tokens signed with a source-visible HMAC fallback key** — anyone reading the repo could
  forge a suppression for a known coach id. The batch script signed with the literal too; it now exits 1.
- **Pattern-miner cross-contamination**: the round-level supersede deactivated shot-dispersion patterns
  because it lacked a `pattern_type` scope on a shared table. Found independently from both sides.

## Two regressions this work introduced, then fixed

Both were caught by adversarial review rather than by the gates, and both are worth reading as a pattern —
a correct security instinct implemented so that a *configuration* problem becomes a hard outage.

1. **The SSRF guard rejected all of Chrome.** It tested `h.startsWith('fc')` for IPv6 `fc00::/7` against
   the whole hostname, and `'fcm.googleapis.com'.startsWith('fc')` is `true`. Every Chrome, Chromium, Edge
   and Android subscription got `400 Invalid push endpoint`; Firefox and Apple still worked, which is
   exactly how this reaches production unnoticed. The IPv6 tests are now gated on the host actually being
   a bracketed IPv6 literal. Verified by execution: **28/28 probes on both copies.**
2. **The unsubscribe fix bricked six modules.** It resolved its secret at module scope, and
   `CRM_UNSUB_SECRET` is unset in production — so three API routes, a cron route and two libs threw at
   *import* time, and Next imports route modules at build time. It also made its own legacy-key
   compatibility window unreachable, breaking in-flight unsubscribe links. Signing now fails closed
   lazily; verification still loads and falls back. Verified with the variable genuinely unset: **13/13.**

Separately, the new concurrency claim in `process-sequences` is a *write* that ran ahead of the
paused-sequence *read*, so a paused sequence had its enrollments leased forward on every tick. The read now
runs first; the claim still precedes every send path, so the race it closes stays closed.

## Gates

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `npm run lint` | only the 2 warnings that pre-date this branch (`BaseballInviteButton.tsx:163`, `v3/ranking/score.ts:295`) |
| `npm test -- --run` | **927/927 files, 8,755 tests passing**, 6 skips — **unchanged**, nothing hidden behind a new `.skip` |

## ⚠️ Deploy prerequisite

**`CRM_UNSUB_SECRET` must be set** — in Vercel **and** in whatever environment runs
`scripts/process-sequence-batch.mjs`, byte-identical, or the links each emits won't verify against the
other. Signing now fails closed, so until it is set every CRM outreach send stops (the cron sends 0 and
logs a warning roll-up rather than 5xx-ing). Unsubscribe **verification** is unaffected, so nothing breaks
for recipients.

## Known-open, filed rather than faked

Four fixes are honest app-layer mitigations that need a transactional RPC to be genuinely correct: atomic
LLM-budget reservation, idempotent sequence sends, atomic account deletion, and the baseball `deleteTeam`
TOCTOU. Each carries the SQL it would need. None of them claim atomicity they do not have.

The verify-only legacy unsubscribe key remains accepted until 2026-11-01 (now enforced in code, not just a
TODO) so live links keep working. Until then a repo reader can still forge a suppression for a coach id
they already know — bounded by ids being non-enumerable UUIDs, and nothing signs with it anymore. Say the
word if you'd rather cut that window shorter.

> ### ⚠️ Branch scope — read first
>
> This branch carries **5 commits**, only one of which is the security work:
>
> | commit | what |
> |---|---|
> | `ab5d04efb` | fix(baseball): org + team on OAuth coach signup — *pre-existing, branch was cut from it* |
> | **`c02820e41`** | **fix(golf): the deepsec wave-1 remediation described below** |
> | `184914050` | feat(baseball): BaseballInviteButton polish — *unrelated, added later* |
> | `88fc283b2` | feat(coachhelm): confidence calibration Phase 1.1 — *unrelated, added later* |
> | `2d21031f8` | docs: CoachHelm fix plan progress report — *unrelated, added later* |
>
> The three later commits landed after the security work and are not part of it. If you want a
> security-only PR, `c02820e41` cherry-picks cleanly onto `main` and the rest can go separately.
> The gate results below were measured at `c02820e41` and do **not** cover the three later commits.

## What this is

Remediation of the **deepsec wave-1 scan**: all 113 files under `src/app/golf/actions` plus the direct
service-role-key callers. 77 findings were produced; **52 survived adversarial verification and 25 were
refuted and deliberately left alone** — refuted findings mean the code was already correct, and "fixing"
it would have been the regression.

**48 files changed, +3,733 / −677.**

## Highest-impact fixes

- **`recordInteraction`** (`insights.ts`) was an unauthenticated `'use server'` export writing to the
  CoachHelm learning store through the service-role client. Any user could flood dismissal events against
  another tenant's coach; once `dismissalRate > 0.5` that coach's `alertFrequency` flips to `low` and
  CoachHelm quietly throttles their alert delivery.
- **`suggestGoalTarget`** (`v3/goals.ts`) gated only on "is the caller a coach at all" while the read ran
  through `createAdminClient()`. Coach signup is self-service, so a throwaway account could reconstruct a
  rival program's athlete performance profiles. The in-code comment claimed RLS guarded it — RLS guarded
  the *write*, not the read.
- **`dismissInsight` / `acknowledgeInsight`** had been failing for **every coach in production**. The
  UPDATE named `updated_at`, which the `authenticated` role lacks column privilege on, and Postgres checks
  column privileges for the whole SET clause before RLS — so the statement failed with 42501 every time.
  Confirmed against the production database.
- **`calendar-sync`** generated `golf_events` from an unvalidated semester range via the service-role
  client — `semester='Fall 9999'` built millions of rows; a milder span quietly bloated the table.
- **Signup access code** was enforced only client-side. There was no server-side caller of
  `validateAccessCode` anywhere, so `signupAction` was directly POST-able.
- **Travel expenses** were org-scoped where they needed to be team-scoped, letting a men's-team coach
  reach the women's team's data — on create, update, delete, and CSV export.

## Gates

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `npm run lint` | exit 0 |
| `npm test -- --run` | **923/923 files, 8,681 tests passing**, 6 pre-existing skips |

Baselines were captured *before* any edit (both clean), so these are true comparisons rather than
assertions. Skip count is unchanged — no failure was hidden behind a new `.skip`.

## ⚠️ Deploy prerequisites

1. **`SIGNUP_ACCESS_CODE` must be set in Vercel production.** The committed `'1881'` default is removed
   (it was a secret in git). If the env var was never set — and a committed default is usually *why* it
   wasn't — self-serve signup narrows to coach-invited `join_code` only. It fails loudly rather than
   silently, but confirm it before deploying.
2. **The included migration is NOT applied.** `20260801100000_auth_rate_limits_atomic_rpc.sql` creates
   `check_rate_limit_atomic`, which does not exist in production. **Merging ahead of it is safe**: the
   limiter detects `PGRST202`/`42883` and falls back to the pre-existing non-atomic path, so shipping
   first degrades atomicity to today's production behaviour rather than breaking logins. Apply it after
   db-migration-reviewer sign-off — and note it has never executed anywhere, so validate on a branch DB.

## Known-open, filed rather than faked

- `crm-dedup.mergeCoaches` is **not atomic**. Real atomicity needs a transactional RPC; the file carries
  an explicit in-code disclaimer stating plainly what it does and does not cover, plus the SQL that would
  fix it. No atomicity is claimed that isn't delivered.
- The unvalidated `createGolfConversation` still exported from `@/app/actions/messages` — a barrel wrapper
  adds a safe door without locking the old one.
- **Pre-existing, not from this branch:** the `golf_announcement_recipients` coach policies contain a
  correlated subquery (`team_id IN (SELECT golf_announcements.team_id FROM golf_coaches WHERE ...)`) that
  selects the *outer* row's `team_id`, making the predicate true for any user holding any coach row. That
  is a live cross-tenant read/write and deserves its own reviewed migration.

## Review guidance

The recurring trap in this codebase, which caused three regressions during this work before being caught:
`verifyTeamAccess` and `verifyInsightAccess` route through `coach_id_for_team`, which is **coach-staff-only**
and can never pass for a player. Using either on a player-reachable path denies 100% of legitimate callers —
an availability bug wearing a security costume. Two such instances are corrected here.

## Summary

Promotes 20 of the 40 dead `node --test` guard files in `scripts/__tests__/` to run under vitest's `unit` project. Continues the work started by #1189 (`drawers-mobile`) and #1193 (`icon-only-button-aria-label`) — see #1194 for the tracking issue and the remaining 20 that still need per-file triage.

**Promoted (20):** `baseball-action-integrity`, `baseball-stale-route-links`, `breadcrumb-nav`, `canonical-motion-tokens`, `chartshell-exists`, `check-migration-ledger`, `check-migration-versions`, `check-required-env`, `error-boundary-coverage`, `form-a11y`, `loading-error-pair-coverage`, `no-bare-empty-text`, `no-glasscard-imports`, `no-ios-ease-stats`, `no-legacy-skeleton-imports`, `no-tranwarm-typo`, `radix-dropdown-sonner`, `review-gate-rules`, `single-pageheader`, `token-files-no-conflict`.

**Skipped:** none of the 20 assigned — all 20 converted cleanly and pass. (The other 20 files in the directory are explicitly out of scope for this PR.)

## What the conversion did

For 17 of the 20, this was mechanical: swap `import { test } from 'node:test'` for `import { test } from 'vitest'`, keep `node:assert/strict` as-is, add a one-line "why this exists" comment, and add the file to `vitest.config.ts`'s `unit` project `include` array with a comment naming what it guards.

3 files (`canonical-motion-tokens`, `no-ios-ease-stats`, `review-gate-rules`) turned out to be bare scripts with **no `test()` registration at all** — they were never real `node:test` files, just scripts sitting in the directory that happened to pass when executed (their pass/fail signal was `process.exit()`, and `node --test` treats a whole file with zero explicit tests as one implicit test). `process.exit()` inside a shared vitest worker process would have torn down other tests running in the same process, so each was wrapped in a `test()` (or `test.skipIf()` for the ast-grep-dependent one) with the exit calls replaced by vitest assertions. All underlying check logic — every regex, every file list, every allowlist — is byte-for-byte unchanged; only the pass/fail plumbing changed. Also dropped each file's `process.chdir(repoRoot)` (global, and vitest runs many files in one process) in favor of resolving/passing absolute paths, since none of the check logic actually depended on cwd once traced through.

No assertions were weakened. No NUL bytes found in any of the 20 files.

## What the newly-live guards revealed

Nothing — all 20 pass cleanly against current `main` with their original logic intact. No new defects surfaced (unlike #1193, which found a real a11y bug).

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run --project unit scripts/__tests__/<name>.test.mjs` for each of the 20 — all pass, matching the `node --test` baseline test counts exactly (54 tests across the 20 files)
- [x] `npx vitest run --project unit` — full suite green: 921 test files passed, 8648 tests passed (6 pre-existing, unrelated skips)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean

body:
`scripts/__tests__/icon-only-button-aria-label.test.mjs` was **right, and silent**.

It imports from `node:test`, which only executes under the `node --test` CLI — invoked by nothing in `package.json` or any workflow. So while it ran under nothing, this shipped:

```
src/app/lifting/(dashboard)/dashboard/import/import-client.tsx:361
  <Button variant="ghost" … >   ← icon-only, no accessible name
    <X className="h-4 w-4" />
  </Button>
```

A screen-reader user hears *"button"* with no indication of what it does. It dismisses the action-error banner, so it now says so: `aria-label="Dismiss error"`.

## Why the guard is worth promoting rather than just satisfying

It carries **four self-checks** alongside the repo scan — label-vs-placeholder detection, icon-only-vs-icon+text detection, reserved-subtree exclusion, and an end-to-end *flag-one / pass-one*. So a green run is evidence the detector works, not merely that it found nothing. That is the difference between this and a scanner that silently matches zero.

Proven non-vacuous here too — reverting the `aria-label`:

```
AssertionError: Found 1 icon-only button(s) without an accessible name in product code.
Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)
```

## Also: three raw control bytes removed

`visibleButtonText()` uses a NUL-prefixed `sr-only` sentinel, written as **raw bytes** in all three places it appears. Identical string at runtime — but raw bytes made ripgrep classify the whole file as binary and skip it:

```
$ rg -n "^import" scripts/__tests__/icon-only-button-aria-label.test.mjs
binary file matches (found "\0" byte around offset 7570)
```

A guard that is invisible to the source-text searches used to *audit guards* is a bad shape, and it is part of why this one went unexamined for so long. Now written as explicit unicode escapes; the file is greppable and the string is unchanged.

## How I found it, and what else is there

I ran all 40 unwired `scripts/__tests__` files by hand. The split:

| | |
|---|---|
| **pass today** | 20 — cheap to promote, immediate real coverage |
| **fail today** | 20 — each either rotted, or reporting a real defect nobody has seen |

This is the first confirmed case of the second kind. #1189 is the first of the first kind — `drawers-mobile.test.mjs`, which had rotted in four separate places.

A caution for whoever triages the rest: my first attempt at that sweep reported **40/40 failing**, which was entirely an artifact of `timeout` not existing on macOS — every invocation died on a missing command, not a failing assertion. Worth re-deriving the numbers rather than trusting mine.

`tsc --noEmit` clean.

Updates `playwright` from 1.61.1 to 1.62.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.62.0

🧱 New component testing model

Component testing moves to a stories and galleries model. A story wraps your component in one specific scenario — hard-coded props, mock data, providers — and a gallery page that you serve renders stories on demand. The new fixtures.mount() fixture navigates to the gallery, mounts a story by id, and returns a Locator scoped to the story's root element:

test('click should expand', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount('components/Expandable/Stateful');
  await component.getByRole('button').click();
  await expect(component.getByTestId('expanded')).toHaveValue('true');
});

Pass a story type as a template argument to type-check its props, and use update(props) / unmount() on the returned locator to re-render or tear down within a test.

🛑 Cancel operations with AbortSignal

Most operations and web-first assertions now accept a signal option that takes an AbortSignal, letting you cancel long-running actions, navigations, waits, and assertions:

const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000);

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ signal: controller.signal });

await expect(page.getByText('Done')).toBeVisible({ signal: controller.signal });

Providing a signal does not disable the default timeout; pass timeout: 0 to disable it.

🖼️ WebP screenshots

expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() and expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot() can now store snapshots in the WebP format — just give the snapshot a .webp name:

// Visual comparisons store the golden snapshot as lossless WebP.
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage.webp');

// Standalone screenshots can trade quality for size with lossy WebP.

await page.screenshot({ path: 'homepage.webp', quality: 50 });

page.screenshot() and [locator.screenshot() (https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-screenshot) also accept webp as a type, where quality 100 (the default) is lossless and lower values use lossy compression.

🧩 Custom test filtering with Reporter.preprocess()

New reporter.preprocess() hook runs after the configuration is resolved and before reporter.onBegin(), letting a reporter mark individual tests as skipped, excluded, fixed, or failing through a TestRun object:

`scripts/__tests__/drawers-mobile.test.mjs` imports from `node:test`, which only executes under the `node --test` CLI. Nothing in `package.json` or any workflow invokes that runner, and vitest's unit project globs `src/**` plus a short explicit allowlist — so **this suite has never run under any mechanism.**

`vitest.config.ts` already names the class:

> the other 46 files in `scripts/__tests__/` are written for `node --test` … and are **NOT wired into any CI job or npm script today** — a separate, larger dead-test finding

This is one of those 46, promoted for the same reason its neighbours were: what it guards matters, and #1174 tonight was about exactly this (44px touch targets).

## Running under nothing, it rotted in four places at once

| assertion pointed at | reality |
|---|---|
| `golf/ShotTrackingComprehensive.tsx` | **nothing renders it** — both round clients render `FairwayShotTracking` (`new-round-client.tsx:1841`, `continue-round-client.tsx:979`) |
| `round-review/RoundStripGrid.tsx` | **does not exist in `main`** — the suite would have died on a missing file the instant anything ran it |
| `v3/Chat/ChatDrawer.tsx` | does not exist; chat moved to `coachhelm/chat/` |
| `v3/Chat/ChatComposer.tsx` | does not exist; successor is `PromptComposer` |

The first is the sharpest: it was guarding **dead code** while the surface users actually touch went unguarded.

## Repointed at what actually renders

- **putt pickers** → `FairwayShotEntry` + `FairwayEditShotModal`. The regex accepts `sm:` or `md:` because the two files genuinely differ and both are ≥44pt at 320px (both start 3-up); pinning one literal string would force a cosmetic rewrite of the other.
- **scorecard-height anchor** → `FairwayShotTracking`.
- **composer safe-area** → `chat/PromptComposer.tsx`, which owns the bottom edge of the drawer and applies the inset via `safeArea`, passed as `variant === 'drawer'` from `CoachHelmChat.tsx:108`.

## Two assertions removed, not repointed

Because a replacement would have been *invented* rather than derived:

- **hole-strip scroll+snap** — round review was rebuilt around `FilmstripReview`, which reflows with a responsive grid + `flex-wrap` instead of a scrolling snap strip. That is a legitimate mobile answer, so the rule is obsolete rather than mis-pointed.
- **launcher-FAB safe-area** — the FAB survives at `CoachHelmDrawer.tsx:104`, but it is `hidden … md:flex`, i.e. **desktop-only**. It never renders on a viewport that *has* a home indicator, so a safe-area assertion was the wrong guarantee even before the file moved. Its real constraint is desktop content clearance, which `FairwayDashboardShell` already handles with `role === 'coach' && 'md:pb-28'`.

## This is a coverage fix, not a bug fix

The live components already satisfied every rule kept here — checked while repointing. Nothing about mobile is broken today; the point is that a future regression in the rendered component now fails.

**Proven non-vacuous.** Regressing `FairwayShotEntry`'s putt grid to a bare `grid-cols-6` fails the suite with the intended message:

```
× putt distance pickers stay 3-up on narrow screens (>=44pt targets)
  putt quick-select must drop to 3 columns at 320px so each target is >=44pt
```

and restoring it passes 5/5.

## Follow-up worth its own pass

45 files remain in `scripts/__tests__/` that still run under nothing. Given this one drifted in four separate ways unnoticed, it is reasonable to assume others have too — and a stale test that passes is worse than no test, because it reads as coverage. Related to #1186, which found the same shape on the golf side: a mobile-viewport regression gate that covers zero golf dashboard routes.

The Play Store platform (#1153) landed on `main` a few minutes ago, and `push.ts` now routes by platform:

```ts
const fn = deviceToken.platform === 'android' ? 'send-fcm-push' : 'send-apns-push';
```

So **`main` invokes `send-fcm-push` today, and it is not deployed.** Verified against the live function list rather than inferred — the project has four ACTIVE edge functions (`create-admin-user`, `send-apns-push`, `personalize-email`, `verify-emails`) and that is not one of them.

## Three independent blockers, and fixing one alone changes nothing

| # | blocker | why it is invisible |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | no `google-services.json` | `build.gradle` applies the Google Services plugin only `if (servicesJSON.exists())` and otherwise **logs and carries on** — so the app never registers for FCM and no device token is ever minted |
| 2 | `send-fcm-push` not deployed | edge functions deploy separately from everything else; a merge and a production promote both leave it untouched |
| 3 | `FCM_PROJECT_ID` / `FCM_CLIENT_EMAIL` / `FCM_PRIVATE_KEY` unset | these are **Supabase function secrets, not Vercel env vars**, so `vercel env ls` will never show them — their absence does not look like an absence |

**Order matters.** Deploying the function before the Firebase project exists gives you a function that fails every call with a credentials error, which reads as a code bug and is not one. All three secrets come from the service-account JSON produced in step 1.

## Why this is a doc change and not a fix

Every one of the three is an owner action: creating a Firebase project, deploying an edge function, and setting production secrets. What I can do is make sure the next person does not have to rediscover the shape of it — and that "Android push doesn't work" resolves to a checklist instead of an investigation.

This is the same class the rest of `supabase/functions/README.md` documents — code that assumes infrastructure that is not there. Worth noting it was caught within minutes of the merge that introduced it, **because the README existed to be checked against**. That file is four hours old (#1177).

body:
## The bug

Attaching a file to a golf message fails in production. The bucket it uploads to has never existed.

The path is live and shipped, not dormant code:

```
FairwayMessages.tsx:355  handleSendMessageWithAttachments
  → hooks/golf/use-message-attachments
  → actions/message-attachments.ts  sendGolfMessageWithAttachments
  → lib/storage/attachments.ts:253  .from('golf-attachments').upload(…)
```

`storage.buckets` holds exactly eight rows — `avatars`, `baseball-imports`, `course-images`, `documents`, `helm-bridge-feedback`, `lifting-nutrition`, `logos`, `recruit-documents`. `golf-attachments` is not among them, so every upload returns "Bucket not found".

Found by sweeping every bucket name in `src/` against `storage.buckets`. That turned up **three** misses; see the bottom for why only this one is fixed.

## Every value is read from the code, not chosen

| | value | source |
|---|---|---|
| `public` | `false` | the read path uses `createSignedUrl(path, 3600)` throughout and never `getPublicUrl` |
| `file_size_limit` | 100 MiB | max of `FILE_SIZE_LIMITS` in `lib/storage/attachments.ts` |
| `allowed_mime_types` | 29 types | the keys of `ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES`, verbatim |

## The policies follow the path shape

`generateStoragePath` builds `conversations/<conversationId>/<messageId>/<ts>_<name>`, so `storage.foldername(name)[2]` is the conversation id.

- **SELECT / INSERT** — scoped to conversation membership via the existing `user_conversation_ids()` helper (STABLE SECURITY DEFINER, `SET search_path = public`, reads `golf_conversation_participants`). Reusing it keeps "who is in this conversation" defined once.
- **UPDATE / DELETE** — scoped to `owner`, mirroring the app's sender-only rule at `message-attachments.ts:298`. So a participant reads every attachment in their conversation but removes only their own.

### Why the conversation id is compared as text, not cast to uuid

`name` is attacker-controlled. A path whose second segment isn't a uuid makes `::uuid` **raise** rather than return false, and `AND` does not reliably short-circuit in PostgreSQL, so a guard to its left isn't a guarantee. Verified against the database rather than reasoned about, since the whole point is which one raises:

```
(storage.foldername('conversations/not-a-uuid/x/y.png'))[2] IN (<uuid>::text)
  → false
((storage.foldername('conversations/not-a-uuid/x/y.png'))[2])::uuid
  → ERROR  22P02  invalid input syntax for type uuid: "not-a-uuid"
```

Noted in the migration but **not changed**: the four live `recruit_documents_*` policies cast element `[1]` this way, so a malformed path there raises instead of returning false. It fails *closed* — an error grants nothing — so that's log noise and a 500 where a 403 belongs, not an access hole. Changing a live policy on a bucket holding real recruit files isn't a side errand.

## Not applied

Storage RLS is where "wrong" means a data leak, so this ships as a reviewable migration for a deliberate apply rather than something I ran while you were asleep. The policy expressions were compile-checked read-only against production first.

## The durable half

Adds a static test in the same shape as the realtime-publication test: **every bucket named in `src/` must be created by some migration.** Proven non-vacuous — removing the migration makes it fail with exactly `['golf-attachments']`, and restoring it passes.

`.storage.from('nope')` fails at no build step, no type-check, and no test that mocks storage. It fails in production, and the calling actions flatten it to a generic string ("Failed to upload receipt."), so the real cause never reaches a log anyone reads.

Two buckets stay on an explicit allowlist, each with the issue that owns the decision — plus a second test that fails if an allowlist entry goes stale:

- **`baseball_videos`** (#1173) — note the underscore. No bucket here uses underscores and neither spelling exists, so the intended name is genuinely unknown; guessing would be worse than failing.
- **`expense-receipts`** (#1179) — golf travel receipts, equally broken, but not a bucket-creation problem alone: the code calls `getPublicUrl()` and persists the result to `golf_travel_expenses.receipt_url`, which `FairwayExpenseList` renders later. Private needs the read path to sign on demand; public makes every receipt readable by anyone with the URL. Financial documents — that's a product call.

## Summary

Removes genuinely dead **exports** flagged by `npx knip --no-progress` (the "Unused exports (750)" bucket — not files/dependencies, which a sibling PR (#1164) already handled, and not the separate "Unused exported types" bucket, which is out of scope here).

- **165 exports removed** across 5 batches (53 named + 112 default-export cleanups), all in `src/**`.
- **knip's "Unused exports" count: 750 -> 579** (171 fewer flagged; the delta is larger than 165 because a few barrel re-export chains — e.g. `CalendarSurfaceDefault`/`DatePickerDefault`/`FairwayPlayerDashboardDefault` — were double-counted by knip at each barrel hop, so fixing the root fixed multiple flagged lines at once).
- Gates green after every batch: `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint` (`--max-warnings 0`), `npx vitest run --project unit` (900 files / 8589 tests passing).

## Method

For every candidate, ripgrepped the symbol name across the **entire repo** (`src/`, `scripts/`, `supabase/`, `e2e/`, `.github/`, `docs/`, config files) — not just `src/**`, since that's knip's blind spot. Only removed when the symbol had zero references anywhere outside its own definition (or its own file, for un-exports).

Preferred **un-exporting** (drop the `export` keyword, keep the symbol) over deleting, whenever the symbol was still used inside its own module — lower risk, same dead-surface removal.

For the 112 default-export removals: these are all React page components in `src/components/{fairway,golf,baseball}/**` that follow a consistent scaffolding idiom — `export function X(...) {...}` (the real, used export) plus a trailing standalone `export default X;` that nothing default-imports. Verified per-file that (a) no bare `import X from '.../X'` exists anywhere in the repo, and (b) the named export is present and real. Removing these surfaced two broken barrel re-exports (`export { default as XDefault } from ...`) that `tsc` caught immediately — fixed in the same batch.

## False positives rejected (left untouched, with why)

- `src/components/fairway/index.ts` `CommandGlassSurface` / `src/components/fairway/controls/index.ts` `SEGMENTED_TRACK_SUNKEN_SHADOW` — the barrel's own doc comments say these are **deliberate** disambiguation/shared-recipe re-exports ("so both remain reachable" / "SHARED VISUAL RECIPE (exported)"), not oversights.
- `BROADIE_BENCHMARK` (`coachhelm/v3/chat/provenance.ts`) — explicitly documented as "the one baseline this product is allowed to cite... a single constant so no call site can quietly cite a different one." Currently unused, but clearly a guardrail for future call sites, not dead code.
- `setHapticsEnabled` / `fwScrub` (`lib/fairway/haptics.ts`) and `PIN_VH` / `revealLines` / `prepareBar` / `growBar` / `prepareSettle` / `renderSettled` (`lib/motion/gsap/{tokens,primitives}.ts`) — part of a documented, deliberately-scoped "four verbs" motion primitive system ("these are the only shared utilities... and nothing else") that other scene files partially adopt; not all verbs have a call site yet, but the file's own header commits to keeping the full set.
- `SettingsLinkRow` (`fairway/settings/settings-list.tsx`) — one of "THE PIECES" enumerated in the file's kit-level doc comment; its siblings (`SettingsStack`, `SettingsGroup`, `SettingsRow`, `SettingsToggleRow`) are actively used, this one just hasn't been needed by a settings page yet.
- `getScoringColor` / `getPercentageColor` (`fairway/pages/roster/roster-helpers.ts`) — initially looked internally-used by a naive same-file grep, but the only other hits were doc-comment mentions, not real call sites. Deleted outright instead of un-exporting (un-exporting alone would have left dead local functions and failed the `--max-warnings 0` lint gate).
- `src/components/golf/ShotTrackingComprehensive.tsx` default export — a ~1800-line legacy pre-Fairway component, superseded by `FairwayShotTracking.tsx`/`FairwayShotEntry.tsx` per in-repo comments, genuinely orphaned (only a co-located helper `calculateHoleStats` is still imported). Left alone — too large a deletion to safely verify in a mechanical export-removal pass; flagging for a dedicated follow-up.

## What's left

**~584 exports were not touched** out of the original 750 flagged. The large majority are:
- Named exports only reachable through a barrel re-export chain (`src/components/fairway/index.ts` and friends) — this repo's Fairway design-system barrel is real, actively-consumed API surface (verified real consumers exist for the barrel itself), so pruning individual unused re-exports from it needs case-by-case doc-comment review, which this PR does for a sample but doesn't exhaustively cover.
- The `src/lib/motion/gsap/` "four verbs" motion primitives set, deliberately kept as a complete unit per above.
- Anything I couldn't verify with high confidence in the time budget for this pass — left for a follow-up rather than risk a regression.

- [x] `npm run lint` (`--max-warnings 0`) — 0 warnings (after every batch and after final rebase)

- [x] Rebased onto latest `main` (5 unrelated PRs landed mid-session); gates re-verified green post-rebase

body:
## The trap

`send-apns-push` chose its host with:

```ts
const isProduction = Deno.env.get("APNS_ENVIRONMENT") === "production";
```

That falls back to the **sandbox** host whenever `APNS_ENVIRONMENT` is unset.

The build currently running in production predates #1096 and defaults the other way — `?? "production"`. So deploying this file as it stood, without first setting the variable, would have silently moved every send to the sandbox host. Production device tokens are rejected there outright with `BadDeviceToken`; push would have broken completely, and the only symptom is a 400 per send.

Now defaults to production, with `APNS_ENVIRONMENT=development` to opt into sandbox — which is also the right value for a debug build, since a token is only valid against the host matching the build that minted it.

I found this because I was about to deploy the committed version to fix the two bugs below, and checked the env contract first.

## The bigger finding: #1096 shipped half-done

PR #1096 (2026-07-29) rewrote this function **and** updated its caller in `src/lib/notifications/push.ts` to the new response contract. The function was never redeployed — production still serves the **2026-04-07** build. Two fixes from that PR have never been live:

| fix in the repo since 2026-07-29 | what production actually does |
|---|---|
| absolute `apns-expiration` (24h default) so APNs retries | sends `apns-expiration: 0`, which APNs reads as "deliver once, discard on failure" — **every push to a phone that is off, asleep, or out of signal is silently dropped** |
| `shouldDeactivateToken: true` on 410/400 | never sets it — and `push.ts:212` has a branch that reads this flag to retire a dead token, so **that branch has never executed**; dead tokens accrue `failed_count` forever |

Both are real user-facing iOS push defects, live right now.

## Why this PR does not deploy

## Summary

Fixes an intermittent 5s timeout in `src/test/fairway/settings-coaching-intelligence.test.tsx` > "saves priority reorder through the philosophy hook without issuing a duplicate server-action write" — observed twice tonight, only under the full 899-file unit suite / sharded CI, never in isolation.

**Root cause** (`src/test/fairway/settings-coaching-intelligence.test.tsx:285-321`, pre-fix): the test did its own `await import('@/components/fairway/pages/settings/FairwaySettingsCoachingIntelligence')` inline, inside the timed `it()` body. Because it's the first test in the file, that import pays the one-time cost of transforming + evaluating the page's entire real (un-mocked) dependency graph — every other test in the file paid nothing, since the module is cached afterward.

There is no debounce or logic race in the assertion itself — `handlePriorityChange` in the component under test flushes immediately (`void flushSave(newValues)`, no `setTimeout`), so the mocked `save()` resolves on the very next microtask. Confirmed directly: under artificial CPU pressure (8 busy-loop processes on a 10-core machine, simulating a loaded 3-way-sharded CI runner), that one test jumped from ~150ms to **2.44s** while every other test in the same file stayed under 200ms. Vitest's default 5000ms `testTimeout` has no margin left once shard contention pushes that cold-import cost further.

**Fix**: resolve the dynamic import once in a `beforeAll` (a separately-budgeted hook, given a generous 20s ceiling — appropriate for a one-time cold module transform, not a race being masked) and have every test, including the first, read the already-resolved component reference instead of re-importing. This moves the transform cost out of the assertion's 5s budget rather than widening that budget.

Re-ran the file under the same simulated CPU pressure after the fix: the first test stayed at 289ms.

## Verification

| | isolated (no load) | under simulated CPU pressure (8× busy-loop, 10-core box) |
|---|---|---|
| before | 1.09s (whole file) | first test: **2440ms** (others: 24–190ms) |
| after | 2.49s (whole file, includes beforeAll's one-time cost) | first test: **289ms** (others: 26–139ms) |

Full unit suite (`npx vitest run --project unit`, 898 files / 8582 tests / 6 skipped), run 3 times total (2 before this fix, 1 after): all three runs **100% clean**, identical pass counts every time. No test failed in one run and passed in another — this coaching-intelligence test is the only flake found; no other flaky test was surfaced.

**Nothing in CI has ever touched Android.**

The only mobile job is `ios-compile`, and its branch filter is:

```
main · /release\/.*/ · /ios\/.*/ · /capacitor\/.*/ · /agent\/fix-circleci-ios-.*/
```

No android pattern. And `rg android .github/workflows/*.yml` returns nothing.

So a PR could add — or break — the entire Android platform and every check would stay green. That's exactly the state #1153 is in right now: **all-green while touching zero Android files.**

## What this adds

`android-compile`, mirroring `ios-compile` deliberately rather than inventing a shape — same web-build-then-`cap sync` sequence, same dummy Supabase env, same `store_artifacts` pattern.

Two intentional differences:

| | Why |
|---|---|
| Linux `cimg/android`, not a macOS class | Android needs no Mac. The config already cites macOS rates as the reason the iOS job is gated so tightly; Android can afford to run on every `android/**` change. |
| `assembleDebug`, not a release bundle | Debug uses the auto-generated debug keystore, so **CI never needs the real upload key**. Release signing stays a local/manual concern. |

## This PR proves itself

The branch filter includes `ci/android-*` on purpose, so **this branch triggers the new job**. If the executor image or the Gradle invocation is wrong, this PR goes red and I fix it — rather than merging a job that has never run.

## What this does NOT fix

The other Android blocker: **no `google-services.json` exists anywhere**, so FCM push is silently inert. `android/build.gradle` applies the Google Services plugin only `if (servicesJSON.exists())` and otherwise logs and carries on. That needs a Firebase project for `com.helmsportslabs.golfhelm` — an owner action, not a CI change.

## Base branch

Targets `android/play-store` because `android/` only exists there. Merging #1153 then carries this job to `main` with it.

`process.env.X ?? 'literal'` is fine for a tuning knob. It's a security hole for a credential: **if the var is never set in the deployed environment, the literal IS the production value** — and it's sitting in the repository.

## Two live cases

Both confirmed **absent from Vercel production**, so both fallbacks are what production is using right now.

| Var | What its fallback is | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| `SIGNUP_ACCESS_CODE` | a short numeric literal, also repeated in a source comment | Global signup gate, on a path with no rate limiting I could find |
| `CRM_UNSUB_SECRET` | a fixed string | Unsubscribe-token signing secret — a known secret means tokens can be forged for any recipient |

The values are deliberately **not reproduced here**. Run `npm run check:env-secrets` to see them, and treat that output as sensitive. Team join codes are the other accepted signup path and are unaffected.

Neither of these failed anything. Nothing logged. The app worked exactly as designed — with a published default as the real credential. **It's an absence, not an error**, which is why no amount of error triage would ever have surfaced it.

## Deliberately not wired as a blocking gate, and not "fixed" in code

The safe fix is two steps:
1. Set both vars in Vercel to their **current values** — zero behaviour change
2. Harden the code to `?? ''` so unset means disabled

Step 1 is blocked for me (writing secrets to the production environment), and **step 2 alone would disable the global signup code for real users with no warning**. So this ships as `npm run check:env-secrets`. Flip it to a CI gate in the same change that sets the env vars — then rotate both, since the current values have been in git history for a while.

## Scope is narrow on purpose

`src/` only · secret-shaped names only (`SECRET|_KEY|TOKEN|PASSWORD|_CODE|DSN`) · string-literal fallbacks only · `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` exempt (public by definition) · `?? ''` exempt, because an empty default is the *correct* way to say "unset means disabled".

**Two findings, zero false positives.**

## How this was found

Comparing every `process.env.X` read in `src/` against the actual Vercel production env list — 63 are read but absent. Most are platform-injected (`VERCEL_*`, `NODE_ENV`) or optional flags. Filtering to secret-shaped names with *usable* literal defaults left exactly these two.

body:
The function took `pg_advisory_lock(7777)` — **session** scoped — and only unlocked on the success path, with no exception handler.

```sql
PERFORM pg_advisory_lock(7777);
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY crm_coach_engagement;
PERFORM pg_advisory_unlock(7777);   -- never reached if the REFRESH raises
```

## Why session scope is the bug

PostgREST **pools connections**. A leaked session lock doesn't die with the request — it rides the pooled backend, and every subsequent call blocks on `pg_advisory_lock(7777)` forever. The nightly refresh would then fail silently and indefinitely with the matview quietly going stale.

That's the same failure shape this project has been bitten by repeatedly: a job that looks scheduled and does nothing.

`pg_advisory_xact_lock` releases at `COMMIT` **and** `ROLLBACK`, so the failure path can't strand it. The explicit unlock is removed — a transaction-scoped lock must not be released manually.

## Honest framing

Found while diagnosing `[cron.refresh-engagement] RPC failed: <!DOCTYPE html>` (2026-07-29, a gateway 5xx). Before changing anything I verified **no lock was actually stranded** and the function itself succeeds. So this hardens a latent path — it did not clear a live wedge, and I'd rather say that than claim a save.

## Applied to production and verified

- function now reports `pg_advisory_xact_lock`
- refresh succeeds, 2,318 rows
- `pg_locks` shows **0** advisory locks once the transaction ends — and exactly **1** during it, which is precisely the behaviour change

Audited every other function in `public`: this was the only one using advisory locks at all.

`cron.refresh-engagement` interpolated a raw `error.message` that turned out to be a Cloudflare error page, putting **~6KB of markup into `admin_events`**. I counted **155 call sites** that do the same `logServerError(\`prefix: ${error.message}\`)` interpolation, so any of them can do this.

## Fixed at the sink, not at 155 callers

All three logging entry points funnel into `captureServerTrace`. One change protects every existing call site and every future one.

## Size was the lesser problem

That markup carries a unique **Ray ID, client IP and to-the-second timestamp**, and `admin_events` fingerprints hash the message — so **every occurrence of one outage minted a new incident group**. The existing code comments note this is exactly how a 9.4-hour database wedge stayed invisible as a single event: it looked like dozens of unrelated one-offs.

`collapseEmbeddedHtml` keeps the caller's prefix (which says *which* call failed) and replaces only the HTML with a byte-stable summary, so an outage collapses to one incident with a count.

## Reused, not duplicated

`describeError` already had `collapseHtmlErrorBody`, but it replaces the **whole** string — which would discard the `[cron.refresh-engagement] RPC failed:` prefix when the HTML is embedded mid-message. Exported it and added the embedded-position variant beside it, so there's one definition of what a gateway error page looks like.

## Tests

5 cases, including:
- **byte-stability** across differing Ray ID / IP / timestamp — the property that makes fingerprinting work
- prefix preservation
- a guard that prose merely mentioning "html" does **not** trigger it
- `null` passthrough so non-HTML messages are untouched

Full unit suite green: 899 files / 8,587 tests.

## Incidental finding

While diagnosing, I ran `refresh_crm_coach_engagement()` directly — it succeeds (2,318 rows, no stuck advisory lock), so the 07-29 failure was a transient gateway 5xx rather than a code defect. Worth noting separately: that function takes a **session-level** `pg_advisory_lock(7777)` and only unlocks on the success path, so a mid-refresh exception would leak the lock into a pooled connection. Not changed here — flagging it.

Production shows these repeatedly, from real Android devices, on `/golf/login`:

```
Error: "Keyboard" plugin is not implemented on android
Error: "PushNotifications" plugin is not implemented on android
```

Both packages **are** in `package.json`, so this was never a missing dependency. It's a native-registration gap combined with an unhandled async rejection.

## The mechanism

`addListener()` does **not** throw synchronously — it returns a promise that rejects **asynchronously**. Nothing awaited those promises until unmount, so the rejection reached the global `unhandledrejection` handler and was reported as an incident on every load. A `try/catch` around the call site would never have caught it.

That matches the incident data exactly: both fingerprints arrived via `action: unhandledrejection`.

## Fix

- `Capacitor.isPluginAvailable(...)` before using `Keyboard` / `PushNotifications`, so an unregistered plugin is a no-op instead of a failure
- `.catch()` attached to the returned promises immediately, so nothing is left unattached between mount and unmount — independent of the cleanup handlers, which only run at unmount

## Worth noting

This removes the **cause**, not just the reporting. Those listeners were never working on the affected builds, so keyboard-height CSS and push registration were silently inert there too. Fixing the native registration is the follow-up; this stops the bleeding and makes the failure visible as absence-of-feature rather than a per-load error.

`tsc` clean · `eslint` clean · full unit suite green (899 files / 8,587 tests).

`postgres_changes` only delivers events for tables in the `supabase_realtime` publication. Subscribing to an **unpublished** table still returns `SUBSCRIBED` — it just never fires. No error, no warning, nothing in the console. The feature shows stale data and looks correct in every code review.

## Measured against production, 2026-08-01

The app subscribes to **18 distinct tables. Five were published.**

| Dead subscription | Feature |
|---|---|
| `helm_lifting_sessions`, `helm_lifting_set_results` | **LiveWeightRoomClient** |
| `baseball_messages`, `baseball_conversations`, `baseball_conversation_participants` | baseball messaging |
| `golf_tasks`, `golf_task_assignments` | task live updates |
| `golf_qualifiers`, `golf_qualifier_entries` | live qualifier board |
| `golf_events`, `golf_event_attendance` | calendar + RSVP |
| `golf_rounds` | round status sync |
| `admin_api_perf_log` | Bridge perf feed |

Golf messaging works. Everything else realtime does not.

## Root cause

**The publication has never been populated by a migration.** The only `ALTER PUBLICATION` statements in this repo are the DROPs in the 20260704 graveyard migrations. It was switched on by hand in the dashboard for an early set of tables, and every realtime feature built afterwards was written in code and never enabled. Nothing in CI could see it.

The five "working" tables are in the same position — they exist in the publication only because someone clicked a button, so **a rebuild from migrations would silently lose them**. The migration lists all 18 so the publication is reproducible from source; the guard makes those five a no-op.

## The migration

Additive and idempotent. Each `ADD` is guarded by a `pg_publication_tables` lookup, and a missing table is skipped with a `NOTICE` rather than failing.

**`REPLICA IDENTITY` deliberately unchanged.** All 18 are `d` (primary key), so `UPDATE`/`DELETE` payloads carry only the PK in `old`. Handlers here refetch on notification rather than diffing the payload, so none need `FULL` — and `FULL` materially increases WAL volume, so it belongs in a per-table decision with that cost visible, not a bulk change.

## The guard

A static cross-check of subscriptions in `src/` against tables any migration adds. It cannot see the live database — CI has no production credentials — so it proves intent is *recorded*, not that the migration *ran*. `npm run db:drift:check` covers applied-vs-recorded, and this repo has a documented history of migrations recorded but never run.

Verified non-vacuous: removing one table from the migration fails it, and it asserts both scanners found >10 entries so it can't pass over two empty sets.

## Incidental drift caught

The migration commit's pre-commit hook regenerated `database.ts` (documented behaviour) and surfaced real drift: **7 views → 9, 153 functions → 156**. `glossary.md` derives from it and is regenerated here. `database.ts` is now stable — a second `npm run db:types` produces no further diff — so CI's types-drift job will agree.

## Not yet applied

Unlike a merge, a migration reaches production directly. **Applying this is a separate deliberate act** and hasn't been done.

body:
The PostgREST row-cap class again — this time hidden behind a **constant**, which is exactly the limitation the ast-grep rule in #1158 documents it cannot catch. Found by resolving const values and rescanning.

## Live bug

`fetchShotDriversByCategory` asked for `.limit(SHOT_DRIVERS_FETCH_CAP)` = **25,000**. PostgREST returns at most **1,000** — and the query carried no `ORDER BY`, so for any player past 1,000 shots the shot-driver analysis was built from an **arbitrary subset**.

Measured against production 2026-07-31:

| | |
|---|---|
| max shots for one player | **1,189** |
| players already over 1,000 | **6 of 33** |
| rounds cap (200) | never binds — max rounds is 16 |

So **18% of players were getting truncated shot drivers today**, and every player crosses that line at roughly 14 rounds.

Now paginated with `fetchAllRowsResult`, the ceiling enforced by stopping page accumulation, and the **abort signal carried on every page** so the 5s best-effort budget still bounds the whole walk exactly as before. `.order('id')` added because `fetchAllRowsResult` needs a stable unique sort or page boundaries drift.

## Latent, fixed the same way

Verified as having no current impact, but fixed because they fail silently and corrupt an aggregate the moment they bite:

- **team-detail** team login counts — 300 rows exist vs a 1,000 cap
- **activation-funnel** golf + baseball first-activation maps — 295

Both keep **first-row-per-key**, so a truncation drops whole players/teams out of the funnel rather than merely trimming it. `id` added as a tiebreak — `created_at` isn't unique, and a non-unique sort lets page boundaries drift.

## Judgment call

`causal-relationships` `FETCH_LIMIT` 2500 → **1000**, not paginated. The worst player has **130** active rows, so it has never bitten; the query is built incrementally, so pagination would be a real refactor and isn't justified for 7.7x headroom. Making the number honest *is* justified, since 2500 was always returning 1000.

## Two false positives, recorded

Both from matching code inside **comments**:

- `stats-leak-maps` `.limit(MAX_SHOT_ROWS)` — a comment explaining why they deliberately *don't* do that; they already paginate
- an earlier cron-auth scan matched `CRON_SECRET` in doc comments and reported 13 phantom gaps

Scan scripts in this repo should skip comment lines.

## Verification

`tsc` clean · lint clean (`--max-warnings 0`) · **896 files / 8,576 tests pass** · the const-resolving scan that found this now returns **0**.

body:
Follow-up to #1155. Those were two instances of one class — this stops the third.

## Why a lint rule and not more tests

All three defects in #1155 passed **8,657 tests, 16 CI gates, CodeQL and 11 linters**. More of the same would not have caught them.

Two shared a shape: code PostgREST rejects, against a mock that accepted it. **91 test files mock `createAdminClient`, each rolling its own double, and none model either production limit.** A mock more permissive than production doesn't merely miss bugs — it certifies them.

## The rule

`.limit(N)` with `N > 1000` is an error. PostgREST caps every request at 1,000, so a larger literal is a number that lies — and a *"short page means the backlog is drained"* check against a threshold above 1,000 **can never fire**. That is precisely how Rule C stalled after one batch against an 87,619-row backlog.

- Exactly `1000` is allowed — it's honest about what it returns
- Tests are exempt: a test asserting what the cap *does* has to ask for more
- Wired into `review-gate` as a blocking, source-only rule, with a positive fixture matching the existing `__test__/` convention

## Three live call sites made honest

Every one **verified benign before changing**, so this is behaviourally a no-op:

| Site | Was | Why benign |
|---|---|---|
| `reminder-sweep` | `.limit(5000)` | per-team armed reminders; design already drains across runs |
| `crm-gmail-send` | `.limit(2000)` | priority-ordered pool, ~10 survive dedupe + suppression |
| `operational-signals` | `.limit(2000)` | 21-day window; **worst observed window across all teams is 55 rows** |

The third carries an added comment because `playerIds` derives from those rows — a future truncation would drop *whole players* from the signal set, not just trim data. Worth knowing before someone widens the lookback.

## A test double that fails like production

`src/test/helpers/postgrest-faithful-mock.ts` enforces the ceilings I **measured** against this project's endpoint, not guessed:

- the 1,000-row cap, applied regardless of what `.limit()` asked for
- the 584-value `.in()` limit, returning the literal string `Bad Request` — which is what makes this failure read like a query bug in logs

Any bulk-write test can adopt it in one line and get the real failure with the real confusing message. 4 tests covering both ceilings, plus a chunk-size assertion helper.

## Verification

- Rule flags `5000`/`2000`, passes `1000`/`500`, and correctly does **not** flag a non-literal const — the rule is syntactic, which is why the real defence is still the short-page check comparing against 1000
- Fixture produces exactly 2 errors
- Repo scan clean after the fixes
- `actionlint` clean; `tsc`, `eslint`, and 92 cron + helper tests green

CI's median wall clock is **16.5 min** across the last 7 runs. Job breakdown from run `30674405138`:

| Job | Duration |
|---|---|
| BaseballHelm authenticated smoke | 15.9 min |
| Unit tests | 15.5 min |
| Unit tests (Pacific/Kiritimati) | 15.4 min |
| Unit tests (Pacific/Midway) | 15.2 min |

## The unit suites are runner-bound, not config-bound

Step-level timing shows `npm ci` is only **1.2 min** — installs aren't the lever. The tests themselves take **13.9 min in CI against 2.4 min on a 10-core laptop**. Hosted runners have 4 cores.

Sharded 3 ways, including both timezone legs — unsharded, those would simply inherit the critical path the moment the plain job got faster.

**Three, not four**, keeps total runner minutes roughly flat while cutting each job's wall clock ~15.5 → ~6 min. Move the matrix and the `--shard` denominator together if that trade should change.

**Verified no test loss** — the shards sum exactly to the unsharded run:

```
shard 1/3   299 files   2897 tests
shard 2/3   298 files   2943 tests
shard 3/3   298 files   2728 tests
─────────   895 files   8568 tests
unsharded   895 files   8568 tests   ← exact match
```

Integration tests now run on shard 1 only instead of three times.

## The build was never cached

`next build --webpack` keeps its incremental compilation cache in `.next/cache`, and nothing cached it — the only `actions/cache` entry covered Playwright browsers. Every build was cold. Both build jobs now cache it.

## What I deliberately did *not* do

The smoke job spends **10.2 min building and 1.4 min testing**, and `Next build` does a near-identical build in parallel. Sharing one artifact looks like the obvious win — and it's wrong. The smoke job's own comment says why:

> MUST come after the stack is up: Next.js inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` into the client bundle at build time, so building first would bake in whatever the env held before the local URL existed.

Reusing the artifact would silently bake the wrong Supabase URL into the smoke bundle. The two get **separate cache key prefixes** for the same reason.

## Expected

Critical path **~16.5 → ~10 min**, bounded by the smoke job. `actionlint` clean.

Two problems with one root cause: the reference material the agent is told to trust had rotted, and nothing regenerated it.

## The schema reference covered 30% of the database

`memory/context/golfhelm-database.md` is where `CLAUDE.md` routes **every** database task, billed as *"Every column of every table."*

| | |
|---|---|
| Tables documented | **80** |
| Tables actually live | **266** |
| Missing | all 93 baseball tables, all admin tables |
| Last touched | 2026-04-21 |

It was the last hand-maintained file in `memory/` — and it *reads* as authoritative ("Complete Reference · Total golf tables: 76"), which is worse than being absent. A query written against it during this session failed on a column that doesn't exist.

**Fix:** extended the existing `scripts/regen-docs.mjs` rather than adding a parallel mechanism. It now emits an `AUTOGEN:columns` block — **266 tables, 3,998 columns** — parsed from `src/lib/types/database.ts`, which `npm run db:types` already generates from the live database and `db:types:check` already keeps honest in CI.

- Verified against live `information_schema` (spot-checked `golf_patterns_v2`: types and nullability match)
- Idempotent, verified by hash across repeated runs
- `docs-regen.yml` named its two output files explicitly, so the new one would have rotted identically — added to the diff check and `add-paths`
- Header rewritten to say plainly that the 1,535 lines of narrative above the block are stale and must not be used for column names

## CLAUDE.md: 493 → 184 lines

The documented target is under 200; longer files measurably reduce adherence. Split into `.claude/rules/*` with `paths` frontmatter so detail loads only when the matching files are touched — **308 lines now conditional**.

| Rule | Loads when |
|---|---|
| `golf-feature-ownership` | `src/app/golf/**`, `src/lib/golf/**` |
| `design-system` | any `.tsx` / `.css` |

| `integrations` | `src/app/api/**`, stripe/inngest/email |
| `database` | `supabase/migrations/**`, `**/*.sql` |

**No content lost** — all 400 original content lines were checked for presence across the new files. Zero missing.

## Hooks

Deterministic guards for traps this repo has actually hit. Every one pipe-tested against real payloads, **including negative cases** (`git status` still runs, `git commit -m maintain` isn't caught by the `main` rule, non-`.sql` files ignored, `DELETE … WHERE` allowed).

- `git stash` — `refs/stash` is repo-global and shared across every worktree
- `rm -rf .next` mid-session — Turbopack cold-compile wedge
- **piped gate commands** — `npm test | tail` reports the pipe's status, so a failing suite exits 0. `set -o pipefail` is the escape hatch.
- direct push to `main` / any force push — main is what production serves
- `GRANT TO anon`, `SECURITY DEFINER` without `REVOKE`, `DROP`/`TRUNCATE`, unqualified `DELETE` — on **both** the file-write and MCP paths, since `apply_migration` never touches a file and hits production directly

Three defects from the 07-31 prod incident feed. All three failed silently or looked like they were working.

## 1. Auto-resolve Rule C has never resolved a single row

It selected a page of ids and spent them in **one** `.in('id', ids)` UPDATE. PostgREST puts filters in the query string, so ~1,000 uuids is a ~39 KB request URI, and Supabase's edge answers `400 Bad Request` before Postgres ever sees it.

Measured against this project (read-only probe, random uuids):

| ids | URL | result |
|---|---|---|
| 500 | 19.6 KB | reaches PostgREST |
| **584** | **22.8 KB** | **last size that works** |
| 585+ | 22.9 KB | `400` body `Bad Request` |
| 1700+ | 66 KB | `414`, empty body |

That `400` is exactly the message the cron logged nightly. **87,619 legacy rows were still unresolved** when this was caught. The UPDATE is now chunked at 200 (~7.8 KB, ~3x headroom).

**Companion defect:** `LEGACY_BATCH` was 2000, above PostgREST's own 1,000-row cap — so a *full* page always looked "short" against the threshold and the drain loop returned believing the backlog was empty. Capping it at 1000 makes the short-page check mean what it says.

## 2. log-retention had the identical pair, unfired

Same unchunked `.in('id', ids)`, same oversized `BATCH`. It survived only because so few rows are ever eligible in one night (24 at time of writing). Unlike auto-resolve it has **no try/catch**, so the first night more than ~584 rows aged past 90 days it would have taken the entire retention cron down.

## 3. Sentry fan-out caused its own rate limiting

`fetchSentryFeatureCounts` fired one query per feature in a single `Promise.all`, on a comment reading "37 features → 37 parallel queries". The registry now has **86, none excluded**, and each query can paginate up to `MAX_PAGES`. That burst on every `/admin` load produced **127 rate-limit faults in one 6-hour window**.

It was also self-amplifying: one 429 discarded 85 good responses, and the next page load reissued all 86. Now capped at 6 concurrent, abandons the sweep on first failure (the result is already discarded), and sits out a 60s cooldown.

## Testing

30 tests across 3 files. Each new case was verified to **fail against the old constants** before passing against the fix — no vacuous green.

One test initially passed for the wrong reason: the retention mock keyed rows by table alone, so the second `purgeAdminEvents` call was quietly finishing the first call's backlog. Re-keyed by severity; it now fails correctly against the old code.

Full suite green: 909 files, 8,657 passed.

## Expected effect

Rule C should clear the 87,619-row backlog over ~4 nights. The Bridge incident feed currently treats each null-fingerprint row as its own incident group, so those numbers become meaningful again.

body:
Lynchburg — **$1,500, the largest of the six invoices** — said they won't buy without Android. This adds the platform and documents the organization-account submission path.

## Why this is days, not months

The app is a **server-URL Capacitor wrapper** pointing at `helmsportslabs.com/golf/dashboard`. There's no native UI to port — Android loads the same web app — and all ten Capacitor plugins in use support Android already.

## Three things that would have shipped broken

**1. `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` was missing.** Android 13+ makes notifications a *runtime* permission. Without the declaration the OS drops every notification silently — no prompt, no error, nothing in logcat. The feature would simply not exist. `cap add android` doesn't add it. Notifications are the *specific* thing Lynchburg is asking about, so this one mattered most.

Also added `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` (scheduled reminders surviving a reboot) and `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` (the offline banner).

**2. `appendUserAgent` was iOS-only.** `src/proxy.ts` keys its marketing-route block on the literal string `HelmSportsLabsApp`. Without it on Android, the shell reads as an ordinary browser and renders the landing page, pricing and membership surfaces *inside the app*. Play doesn't enforce Apple's Guideline 3.1.1, but the two platforms shouldn't diverge on what they show.

**3. The body class was hardcoded `capacitor-ios`.** On Android every `body.capacitor-ios` rule would apply anyway, and no Android-specific rule could ever match. Now reads the real platform. Verified nothing in CSS currently keys on it, so this is inert today and correct going forward.

## Push — the one open decision

`@capacitor/push-notifications` uses **FCM** on Android, needing a Firebase project and `google-services.json`.

But the **Web Push stack is already built end-to-end**: `sw.js` push + notificationclick handlers, a VAPID provider on `web-push@3.6.7`, `/api/push-subscriptions`, the `push_subscriptions` table, and **VAPID keys live in Vercel production for 67 days**.

Nothing calls `pushManager.subscribe` — which is exactly why that table has **zero rows**. Wiring that one call gives working Android notifications with no Firebase at all, and fixes desktop/Android-web users too.

**Recommendation: do that first.** It unblocks Lynchburg in hours instead of weeks and needs no store listing.

## Also in here

Supersedes #1137, which was pushed unrebased to measure drift. This is the reconciliation.

## What the drift measurement said

20 of the WIP's 31 files conflicted, and **every conflict resolved the same way: main was newer.** Resolving toward the WIP would have reverted shipped work:

| File | What the WIP would have undone |
|---|---|
