So **every conflicted file keeps main verbatim.** What lands is only what main does not already have.

## Kept — `TeamSignalSummary` (374 lines), wired into `TriageDesk`

Aggregates signal **groups** into per-category pressure: count, high-priority share, freshness, impact, with per-player links. Nothing on that surface does this — `SignalQueue` renders a severity chip per group and trailing filter counts but never the shape of the whole queue at a glance, and main's Team diagnostics panel reads *shot analysis*, which is different data. Rendered above the queue it summarises, so it is reachable rather than orphaned.

## Dropped — `StatCategoryBrief` (145 lines), deleted

**Superseded.** Main shipped the same idea in #1025 and built it better: a pure, unit-tested `buildCategoryInsights` adapter in `buildStatsViewModel.ts` feeding a shared `CategoryInsightStrip` across all five drills. Wiring the WIP's version in would have rendered a *second competing* category-insight block in every drill. All five of its render sites were in conflicted files, so the only options were duplicate UI or a component nothing renders.

It fed a `PlayerHomeBento` prop that no longer exists. A caller for a removed prop is not a feature.

Replaces a `min-w-[420px]` + `overflow-x-auto` row with a 2→4 column labelled metric grid. A real mobile fix main still lacks.

## Rewritten — the read-contract spec, because it asserted the wrong thing

The WIP added `player-coachhelm-dashboard-readonly.test.ts` asserting the read path never calls `coachHelmIntelligence.analyzePlayer` — true of the draft, which had replaced the call with direct table reads. **Main solved the same problem the other way**: it keeps the call and passes `persistPatterns: false`, disabling the `golf_patterns_v2` upsert that raced the coachhelm-* crons and surfaced as a live Postgres deadlock (40P01) failing the whole page load.

Closes #1132.

## The finding

Triaging #1130 / #1131 / #1132 / #1133 turned up **four real Sentry errors and zero code defects to repair.** Three of the four were already fixed on `main`, with regression tests, before or shortly after the events were recorded:

| Issue | Reality |
|---|---|
| **#1130** Stripe webhook 500s | Fixed by **#1116**, merged `2026-07-29T23:45Z` |
| **#1132** RLS refuses conversation INSERT | Fixed `2026-07-26T16:59Z` — **16h *after* its only event**. Locked by `create-conversation-rls.test.ts` |
| **#1133** AI Gateway plan gate | Classified honestly by **#1106**; `provider-fault.test.ts` already asserts the verbatim production string |
| **#1131** Inngest 404 event key | A production **env var**, never a code defect. Already classified, already falls back |

The production deployment serving traffic was built `2026-07-29T18:30Z` — **five hours before #1116 and eleven commits behind `main`.** The errors were genuine. The bugs were not: they were shipped code already repaired in a `main` nobody had promoted.

## So what this PR actually fixes

Not those four features. The defect is that **nothing measured the gap between "fixed" and "shipped".**

`main` deliberately does not auto-deploy (#789, `git.deploymentEnabled {"*": false}`) — a sound policy that silently accrues drift. Triage then keeps rediscovering repaired bugs, which is the most expensive possible way to spend a morning.

- `classifyDeployFreshness` — pure, 10 tests.
- `fetchDeployFreshness` — fail-soft; compares `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` (the sha of the very deployment the cron runs inside, so no token is needed to know what production is) against `main` via GitHub's compare API.
- Cup of Helm gains a **Release** line, and a stale release is pushed to the **front** of the red list — ahead of the errors it reframes.

## Two thresholds, and why neither is redundant

Stale = behind **AND** (≥24h old **OR** ≥10 commits).

`behindBy > 0` alone must not go red: a repo that promotes production deliberately is nearly always a commit or two behind, and a briefing that is red every morning is one nobody reads by week two — the exact failure fixed in #1139.

The 2026-07-30 case was **11 commits at 18 hours**, which the hours test alone would have **missed**. A regression test pins that case and asserts its age is *under* the hours threshold, so neither threshold can later be dropped as redundant.

`unknown` is never `current`: no sha, or an unreachable GitHub, renders as unknown and omits the claim entirely.

## Verification

- Full suite **8,642 passed / 7 skipped across 907 files**
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean on changed paths

## What still needs a human, and is not code

1. **Deploy.** This is what actually closes #1130 — and it ships #1132's and #1133's fixes to users.
2. **Set `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY`** in Vercel production for #1131.
3. **Top up AI Gateway credit** for #1133 — the classifier resolves it as `credit_exhausted / vercel_ai_gateway`, i.e. a spend state, not a plan gate.

`returns error when delete fails` was skipped on `TODO(fake-supabase-migration)`:

> *"with the current single-chain mock, the select-for-existence-check and the delete can't return different shapes. Re-enable after migrating this file to `src/test/fixtures/fake-supabase.ts`, which supports per-operation results."*

**The blocker was real. The remedy was heavier than the requirement.** What the spec needs is *per-operation results* — not that particular fixture. `createChainableMock` now takes an optional `perOperation` map (~15 lines), so one table returns a found row for `select` while `delete` fails.

Migrating 447 lines and 32 specs to a different fixture would have risked the **31 that already pass** in order to enable one.

Implementation detail worth stating: entering an overridden verb switches the *rest* of that chain to the override, because the failing call is `.delete().eq(id)` and the terminal is `eq`, not `delete`. The sub-chain is flat, so an override can't recurse into itself.

## What the test pins beyond "returns an error"

The action must **not leak the raw Postgres text**. It asserts the message contains `Failed to delete` *and* does **not** contain `Delete failed` — the client-facing string, not the driver's.

Plus a paired negative, `reports not-found before attempting a delete`, so the error path is only reachable *after* the existence check succeeds. Without it, the first test would pass against an action that failed for any reason at all.

## Verified non-vacuous — and the third attempt is the interesting one

| injected regression | result |
|---|---|
| swallow the delete error, return success | **fails** |
| leak `error.message` to the client | **fails** |
| remove the existence check | **fails** |

The third took two attempts. My injection used a string replace with `count=1` against a line that appears **twice** in `travel.ts` (267 and 393) — so it patched a *different function* and the suite stayed green.

That reads exactly like *"the test doesn't catch it"* — the same false negative I've been guarding against all night in monitors and probes, this time appearing in my own verification step. Re-ran targeting line 393 explicitly and it fails as it should.

**A verification that silently no-ops is worse than no verification**, because it produces a confident wrong conclusion.

Net: **32 passed + 1 skipped → 34 passed**, zero skipped in this file. typecheck clean · lint clean. `SKIPPED.md`'s "Plan 02 deferred" section closed out with the reasoning.

Continuing the "tests that cannot fail" sweep. Five specs were parked on `TODO(plan-03)` because *"two contradictory docblocks stacked on this function — one says full bar at 16+, the other says 15% of round count."* That was accurate, and **it is still true.**

## I almost un-skipped them as written

The outer docblock reads cleanly and its worked examples look authoritative, so the obvious move was *"the contradiction was resolved, nobody re-enabled the tests."* **Executing the function first is the only reason that didn't ship five failing specs:**

| input | outer docblock says | actually returns |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 4 | **3** |
| 15 | 4 | **3** |
| 16 | 6 (full bar) | **3** |
| 28 | 6 (full bar) | **4** |

Every worked example in that docblock is wrong. The **inner** comment is the accurate one — it documents the deliberate move to 15%-throughout scaling and says so explicitly (*"was a flat 6-round cap above 16"*), citing an investigation that found 18 starvation events across 5 players in 24h. The docblock above it was never updated, so **the file contradicts itself and a reader would trust the wrong half.**

## Measured behaviour, by executing across 0..60 and 100

```
 0..5  -> 2      (below the mining floor entirely)
 6..23 -> 3
24..29 -> 4
30..36 -> 5
37+    -> 6      (full bar, capped at THRESHOLDS.minSampleSize)
```

The full 6-round bar arrives around **37** rounds, not 16 — the sample-size gate is substantially more permissive than documented, which matters because it gates whether CoachHelm emits a pattern at all.

## What I changed, and what I deliberately didn't

**Fixed:** the outer docblock, from verified values, with the retraction left visible rather than silently rewritten.

**Converted:** the four scheme specs into **characterisation** tests — labelled as such — pinning what ships, including the band edges (5/6, 23/24, 29/30, 36/37) so a one-off shift surfaces instead of passing silently. They assert the stale claims are false: 16→3 not 6, no 15→16 jump, trivial inputs return 2 not 3.

**Not decided:** which scheme is canonical. That's Plan 03's call and an insight-quality question, not a by-product of a docs fix. Pinning current behaviour doesn't pre-empt it — it makes a future change show up as a test to update *deliberately*, which is the opposite of a dormant spec.

**Not done:** exporting `THRESHOLDS`. The fifth spec is **still correctly skipped**, and I re-verified why rather than assuming — `const THRESHOLDS = {` at line 96, no `export`, no `export { THRESHOLDS }`, so importing it yields `undefined`. That's also why an earlier probe of mine silently printed nothing for it, which I had briefly misread as *"it's exported now."* Widening a module's production surface to satisfy a test isn't worth it; its comment now records the re-verification so nobody repeats it.

## Verified non-vacuous

Re-injecting the stale scheme (`if (roundCount >= 16) return 6`) fails **3** of the new specs; back to 23 passed / 1 skipped once reverted. The injection also confirmed the formula derived from the transition points — `min(minSampleSize, max(3, round(roundCount * 0.15)))` with `< 6 → 2`.

## 1. `shows loading state` was skipped, and the blocking question was already answered

`src/test/SKIPPED.md:27` parked it pending *"whether children render alongside the spinner."* The component itself is the authority and had already decided — its comment keeps the label **deliberately**, because replacing it with a placeholder *"causes layout shift and loses context for the user."*

Un-skipped with the assertions **inverted** to the decided behaviour: label present, `aria-busy="true"`, a real `svg.animate-spin` in the DOM, `pointer-events-none cursor-wait`.

Plus a paired **negative** test — a merely `disabled` button must *not* be aria-busy and must have no spinner — so the pair can't pass for the wrong reason. A loading assertion that a plain disabled button would also satisfy proves nothing.

## 2. `asChild` had no runtime test at all

I added the prop in #1127 and covered its *source* shape (dom-nesting guard) and the CSP scoping beside it — but **nothing exercised what it renders.** Four tests for the three ways it goes wrong:

- must emit **exactly one** element (the child, no wrapper `<button>`) — a wrapper is precisely the invalid-HTML/hydration bug the prop exists to prevent
- the styling must land on the **child**, including `relative overflow-hidden`, which is what makes the ripple host correct there
- `disabled` must **not** be forwarded (invalid on `<a>`, and it would leave the link clickable) — `aria-disabled` + `pointer-events-none` instead
- icon spans must **not** be injected, since Slot takes exactly one child; they're dropped rather than silently corrupting the tree

## Verified non-vacuous

Three real regressions injected, each restored to 20/20 after:

| injected bug | result |
|---|---|
| forward `disabled` to the child | **1 fails** (the ARIA test) |
| ignore `asChild`, always wrap in `<button>` | **3 fail** (one-element, styling, ARIA) |
| drop the label while loading — *the old behaviour the spec used to assert* | **1 fails** (the un-skipped spec) |

That last row is the point: the previously-skipped test now fails on exactly the behaviour it used to *demand*, which is how you can tell it was inverted rather than deleted.

Closes the gap my own static guard **admits it cannot cover.**

`src/test/schema/no-self-referencing-rls-policy.test.ts` greps migrations for a policy whose predicate joins its *own* table. That catches the single-hop shape cheaply, and it's where a new mistake should get caught. It **cannot see a multi-hop cycle** — A's policy reads B, B's policy reads A — which is precisely the shape `20260729000200`'s own comments describe:

```
baseball_players_select -> baseball_team_members
  -> baseball_team_members_select -> baseball_players
    -> baseball_players_select   ← loop
```

Only *executing* a query catches that, and only against a database built from the migrations. Running the same query against production proves nothing here, because production was patched by hand — **which is the whole reason the recursion survived a month**: prod is healthy, so every behavioural check that ran against it passed.

## What it asserts

Ten assertions across the player and coach halves of `getActiveBaseballContext`'s real query shape.

- **Every `lives_ok` is paired with a count assertion.** A policy can be non-recursive and still wrong — a suite that only proves "no exception" would pass against a policy that silently returns nothing, which is the dangerous RLS failure mode.
- **Both JOINs the app actually issues** are exercised, not just the tables one at a time, since the multi-hop cycle lives in the join.
- Postgres raises SQLSTATE `42P17` for policy recursion, and `lives_ok` fails on any exception *while printing it* — so a cycle surfaces with its own message rather than as a bare count mismatch.

The coach half should already be acyclic (every context policy there calls only definer helpers — verified by comparing the migrations against production's live `qual`, not assumed). Asserted anyway so a future change to one of those helpers can't quietly reintroduce a cycle.

## Convention

`BEGIN;` before `\ir _helpers.sql`, matching `baseball_coaches_org_scope.sql` — the helpers do `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS tests` plus function DDL, and sourcing them outside the transaction would leave that behind after the `ROLLBACK`. Fixture ids use a fresh `…cr1/…cr2` family, verified unused by any other suite so a concurrent run can't collide.

## What is NOT claimed

**This suite has not been executed.** There's no Docker on this machine, so `supabase start` / `supabase test db` can't run here — that's the documented pattern for this repo (*"Database work is verified by CI, not locally"*), and the `Supabase lint + RLS tests` job applying every migration to a fresh Postgres is the proof.

Statically verified: `plan(10)` matches exactly 10 assertions, the scaffolding matches a sibling suite line for line, and the `\ir` line matches the regex CI's harness uses to strip it before prepending the helpers. **If the plan count or a fixture is wrong, that job says so on this PR and only this PR is blocked.**

The follow-up promised in #1140, now that #1125 has landed and `ci.yml` is free.

## This is not hygiene

On 2026-07-29 `main` went red at 8pm EDT because two "today" fixtures were anchored to the UTC date while the code under test used a local/team date (#1123). Sweeping the whole suite found exactly **two** offset-dependent files in 8,514 tests — and the second one is the real argument.

Re-injecting the **original** React #418 hydration bug that `FairwayAgendaView` was hardened against:

| TZ | Result |
|---|---|
| `America/New_York` | **4 passed** — the bug is *invisible* |
| `Pacific/Kiritimati` | 1 failed |
| `Asia/Tokyo` | 1 failed |

**CI runs at UTC**, where midday-ET fixtures land on the same calendar day. So that guard was **dormant** — it could not catch the regression it exists to prevent, and nothing would have told us. This job wakes it up.

## Design choices, and why

- **A matrix of both extremes**, because each caught a different subset: UTC-11 broke one assertion in `stage-history-format`, UTC+14 broke the other two *plus* both agenda cases. One offset detects the class in principle; two is cheap insurance against a fixture that only slips one way.
- **`fail-fast: false`** so a failure at one offset still reports the other — that's how you learn *which* direction slipped.
- **Hard gate, in `all`'s needs.** A timezone-dependent fixture reports a different answer depending on when and where it runs, and one already took main red. Advisory would let the next one land.
- **The step prints the runner's offset and wall clock** before running, so a future failure shows what the runner thought the time was without needing a rerun.

## It blocks nothing that exists today

Verified clean at **both** offsets on `c2ea35695` *before* adding the job — **892 files / 8,514 tests** at `Pacific/Kiritimati`, and again at `Pacific/Midway`, identical to the UTC run.

**Cost is runner minutes, not wall-clock** — GHA runs these in parallel with the other jobs, so a green PR is not slower.

## Rejected alternative

Banning `toISOString().slice(0, 10)`. There are **216** call sites and most are legitimate (formatting an already-stored date, or intentionally UTC), so a blanket rule would be noise that gets ratcheted into irrelevance. A shifted offset catches the class regardless of which API produced the date, and needs no allowlist.

actionlint clean · yamllint clean under the repo's exact review-gate config · the matrix job names collide with none of the three required contexts (`CodeQL`, `all`, `Smoke checks`).

body:
Fixing the Supabase CSP block (#1125) suggested a class worth sweeping: **our own `connect-src` silently refusing an origin the app is wired to talk to.**

Swept every external origin referenced from client-side code — 17 of them. **Sixteen are false positives:** `href` navigation targets (twitter, linkedin, zoom, docs.google, calendar.google, youtube, mail.google, outlook), SVG namespaces (`www.w3.org`), and a test string. Navigation isn't governed by `connect-src`.

**One is real: `us.i.posthog.com`.** `PostHogProvider` is mounted in the **root layout** (`src/app/layout.tsx:126`) and initialises with `api_host` defaulting to that host, which appears nowhere in `connect-src`. Every `posthog.capture()` would be refused by the browser.

## What I am *not* claiming

**That this is why PostHog has no data.** The provider no-ops without `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY`, and that key is commented out in `.env.example`, absent from `.env.local`, and in no CI or deploy config in this repo. Vercel's environment couldn't be read from here, so the key may simply never have been set. **Both explanations are live and the ledger entry picks neither.**

## Why it's worth filing either way

A latent trap with an expensive failure mode: set the key, PostHog initialises, every request is silently refused, and it looks like the integration is just quiet. The equivalent Supabase case cost **three CI rounds** and was only found by reading a Playwright trace's console — the assertion messages could never have pointed at it. And prior notes already record "PostHog is dark" for unrelated reasons, which is exactly the pre-existing conclusion that would stop anyone suspecting the CSP.

## Deliberately not fixed — and the distinction matters

The Supabase fix **provably adds nothing in production**: the origin is emitted only when the target is loopback. Allowing a third-party analytics origin is a decision about **sending user data off-platform** — privacy and security, not mechanical repair — so it's yours to make.

The entry carries the ready-made shape if you want it: mirror `src/lib/security/local-supabase-csp.mjs` and emit the origin **only when the key is also set**, so a deployment not using PostHog keeps a byte-identical CSP.

**Papercut found alongside:** `.env.example:85` suggests `https://app.posthog.com` while the code defaults to `https://us.i.posthog.com`. Whichever is right, an allowlist would have to match the one actually used.

Also adds **N.8** — the Supabase CSP block itself — with its symptom (*a hang on "Opening your command center", never an auth error*) so the next person who sees that string has somewhere to land.

Docs only.

body:
Swept the whole unit suite under `TZ=Pacific/Midway` (UTC-11) and `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` (UTC+14). **Two files out of 8,463 tests** were offset-dependent; this is the second. Two of these four tests failed at UTC+14 and none at UTC-11 — which is why it had never been noticed.

## The component was never wrong

`bucketEvents` derives each bucket from `zonedMidnight(startStr, timezone)`, falling back to `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE` (`America/New_York`). That is **deliberate hardening** — the comment in `FairwayAgendaView.tsx` records that it fixes a real React #418 hydration mismatch, where an event within ~4-5h of midnight ET bucketed differently between the SSR pass (Vercel, UTC) and the visitor's browser.

The **fixtures** didn't respect it. They built instants from *local* wall-clock strings (`new Date('2026-07-16T15:00:00').toISOString()`), so which New York day each event landed on depended on the runner's offset. At UTC+14, local 15:00 on the 16th is 21:00 ET on the **15th** — so the "today" event stopped being today, and the July 20 event bucketed as ET July 19, producing exactly `expected 'Sunday, July 19' to be 'Today'`.

Fixed by **stating the assumption instead of inheriting it**: `timezone` passed explicitly; event instants as explicit UTC (`16:00:00.000Z` = midday EDT) so no offset can slide one across a date boundary; `nowRef` and range bounds stay *local* Dates built from parts, because that's what the component compares them as (`isSameDay` against `new Date(y, m, d)`).

## The finding that matters more than the fix

Re-injecting the **original** bug — `startOfDay(new Date(startStr))`, the calling process's own zone:

| TZ | Result |
|---|---|
| `America/New_York` | **4 passed** — the bug is *invisible* |
| `Pacific/Kiritimati` | 1 failed |
| `Asia/Tokyo` | 1 failed |

**This test cannot catch the regression it exists to prevent unless the suite runs outside the team's timezone.** CI runs at UTC, where midday-ET fixtures also land on the same calendar day — so the guard is **dormant in CI today**. That's the concrete, evidence-backed case for a shifted-offset run, not a hygiene preference.

## What is deliberately not here

- **The CI job.** Adding it means editing `ci.yml`, which #1125 is currently modifying. Handing myself a conflict on the blocked keystone PR to save one commit is a bad trade — follow-up once #1125 lands.
- **A ban on `toISOString().slice(0, 10)`.** 216 call sites, most legitimate (formatting an already-stored date, or intentionally UTC). A blanket rule would be noise; a shifted-offset run catches the class regardless of which API produced the date.

Verified: typecheck clean · lint clean · **44/44** calendar + calendar-lib tests pass identically under America/New_York, Pacific/Midway and Pacific/Kiritimati.

## Stop automated coach email

Owner instruction: cancel the automated emails coaches are getting.

### What was actually happening

Traced through the **Resend send log**, not by reading code:

The daily **"3 things to know about your team this morning"** digest sent **117 times to 7 distinct real coaches** — including `bpotter@guilford.edu`, a paying customer — at 06:30 UTC every day from **2026-05-31 to 2026-07-25**.

It is **already dead.** #1052 deleted `/api/cron/coach-morning-digest` (`30 6 * * *`) on 07-25, which matches the last send to the day. Nothing to fix there.

### What was still armed — what this PR removes

`/api/cron/v3/weekly-coach-email` on `0 23 * * 0` emails **every coach on every golf team**.

It is currently harmless only by accident of data: all **15/15** rows of `golf_coach_philosophy` have `email_digest_enabled = false`, and **0/15** coaches lack an opt-out row, so the route skips everyone. That is a data coincidence one `INSERT` away from sending again — if a new coach's default is ever `true`, the Sunday job mails the whole roster.

This removes the schedule so it **fails closed**. Route, tests and Resend idempotency keys untouched: re-enabling is a four-line revert.

### Deliberately left running

`/api/cron/event-reminders` (hourly) sends "RSVP needed: …" to team members, coaches included. That is **not** unsolicited automation — it fires only for an event a coach created, and goes to players who need to RSVP. Killing it would break the calendar feature, not stop a mailing list. Last send 2026-07-22. Flagging, not deciding.

### Also ruled out

- `cron.job` (pg_cron) holds exactly one job: a telemetry purge. No mail.
- `/api/cron/process-sequences`, the CRM sequence sender, is absent from `vercel.json` by design and documented as intentionally unscheduled.

### Note

`main` does not auto-deploy, so the schedule persists in production until the next deploy. The data-level opt-out above is what is holding the line in the meantime, and it is currently holding for all 15 coaches.

## Cup of Helm

Replaces the "Helm Bridge" ops digest with a 7am founder briefing. Same cron, same dedicated Resend transport, new job description.

**Preview of the rendered email is attached in the review thread.** Five sections, ordered by what you act on: needs-you-today, overnight errors, coaches & CRM, activity (with bars), shipped yesterday.

### Changes

- Rebranded to Cup of Helm; subject states the verdict — "2 things need you" / "nothing needs you", singularised.
- Retimed `10:00 → 11:00 UTC` = **7am ET**. `CRON_REGISTRY` keys off `cadenceMinutes: DAILY`, not a wall-clock time, so nothing else shifts.
- New **Shipped yesterday** section from the GitHub search API.
- Email-safe visuals: activity bars are nested `<table>` cells with inline backgrounds and percentage widths. No external images, no CSS Gmail strips.

### Three honesty rules, each with a test

A briefing that reports zero for a read that *failed* manufactures confidence:

1. Unreachable Sentry → "not reachable", never "0 unresolved".
2. `shippedYesterday` is `undefined` when GitHub could not be asked, `[]` only when GitHub answered and nothing merged. The email says "unknown" vs "nothing merged".
3. An all-zero activity day says "Nobody used the product in the last 24 hours" rather than drawing three empty bars that read as a broken chart.

The GitHub fetch sits outside the existing `Promise.all` so a rate-limited GitHub cannot reject the batch, with a 10s `AbortSignal.timeout`.

### White-on-white regression guard

The CTA is a bold underlined green link, not a coloured button, and a test asserts it. Gmail strips `background` from an `<a>` while keeping `color`, so a "green button with white text" ships invisible. This was hit live on a real invoice email earlier today.

### Deliberately not done

- The ~40 `Helm Bridge` references in `instrumentation.ts` / `proxy.ts` / action wrappers are the **observability architecture** name, not the email. Renaming would be a big diff with no reader-visible gain.
- No automated GitHub **issue creation** yet. An unattended job that opens issues at 7am needs dedupe and a cap designed deliberately, not bolted on overnight — filed as follow-up.

### Before this does anything in production

1. **Deploy.** `main` has `git.deploymentEnabled: {"*": false}`, so a merge does not ship. Production is on-demand.
2. Set **`OPS_DIGEST_TO`** to `admin@helmsportslabs.com,njrini99@gmail.com` (recipients come from env, not code).
3. Confirm **`OPS_DIGEST_RESEND_API_KEY`** is set — unconfigured is a silent skip by design, never a cron failure.
4. Optional: `GITHUB_TOKEN` for the shipped-yesterday section. Without it the unauthenticated search API is used (~10 req/min, fine for one daily call).

### Verification

- 411 tests passing across `src/lib/admin` + `src/app/api/cron`
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean on changed paths
- Email rendered headless at 700px and visually inspected; caught and fixed a double-escaped section title (`COACHES & CRM`)

### DST caveat

Vercel crons are UTC-only. `11:00 UTC` is 7am EDT; it becomes 6am EST in November. Worth a calendar note.

`docs/CI_RUNBOOK.md` exists to answer *"is this check a real blocker?"*, and `.github/branch-protection.md` is the doc the runbook names as its **authoritative source**. Both were wrong about the one thing they exist to state.

## Claimed vs. enforced

```bash
gh api repos/njrini99-code/helmv3/branches/main/protection \
  -q '.required_status_checks | {strict, contexts}'
# => {"strict": true, "contexts": ["CodeQL", "all", "Smoke checks"]}
```

**Three** contexts. The runbook said *four*, including `CodeRabbit`; branch-protection.md still listed `CodeRabbit` as required with its `.coderabbit.yaml` config. CodeRabbit was dropped **2026-07-20** and removed from the required set. Both files now carry the live query, so the next reader checks rather than trusts.

## The part that matters more: `all` is ambiguous

`ci.yml` and `review-gate.yml` **both** define a job named `all`, so both emit a check run named `all` — and the required context is the bare name, which cannot distinguish them. The runbook already listed both jobs as "required context `all`" and drew the conclusion *"so both must pass."* **That conclusion is wrong**, and the difference is not academic:

> On PR #1125, a check-runs query scoped to the head commit returned `all → success` while the `BaseballHelm authenticated smoke` job that CI's `all` explicitly `needs` was still `in_progress`. The green was **Review Gate's**. That smoke job then **failed**, and CI's `all` failed with it.

A name-based readiness check reads green **before** CI has finished, and can read green **while CI is red**. This is very likely how a PR with failing `Unit tests` merged on 2026-07-29 — `Unit tests` is not a required context by name, only transitively through CI's `all`.

Both docs now say never to gate on that name, give the CI-run-scoped query to use instead, and note that a check run's `html_url` identifies which workflow produced it.

**Both also state that fixing it needs the repo owner and must not be done unilaterally:** renaming either job changes its check-run name, so protection would then wait forever for a context named `all` that no longer exists — **blocking every PR**. The rename and the `required_status_checks` update have to land together.

## Also corrected: the fork/Dependabot skip

Both docs described the `baseball-auth-smoke` skip as expected behaviour ("a skip here is expected, not stuck"). #1125 removes it: the skip existed only to tolerate missing repo secrets, and that job no longer uses any. A **required** gate that silently skipped for a whole class of PR was a hole in it, not a kindness. Written as before/after so the doc is accurate whichever order the two PRs land in.

branch-protection.md's Greptile rationale is kept, marked historical, because it generalises to a rule worth having: **a check that structurally cannot report on a class of PR must not be a required context.** That is the same trap the smoke skip was.

## Measured timings

Runbook §2 gains real numbers for that job now that it stands up a stack: **~17 min clean** (`supabase start` ~1m45s, build ~9-10 min under container contention, seed ~1 min, smoke ~1m30s), **~24 min when the smoke fails** because each spec retries twice — close enough to the 30-minute budget to matter, since a JOB timeout cancels outright and the `if: always()` report upload never runs. Exactly how #953 produced three consecutive `cancelled` runs with nothing to diagnose from.

- **Deliberately not fixed either way:** authoring the functions would build out a feature intentionally hidden under the recruiting sunset; deleting the call sites would delete recruiting code. A stale-entry test forces the lines out if either ever changes.

## Why source-text

Same reasoning as its three siblings under `src/test/schema/`: **a database test cannot catch a missing function, because it runs against a database somebody already provisioned** — precisely why the pgTAP suites saw none of the three defects above.

**Verified non-vacuous:** renaming one call site to a function that exists nowhere makes the guard fail, naming both the function and the file it's called from, *and* trips the stale-entry assertion. Restored to 3/3.

body:
`RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` opens with `git branch --show-current  # expect: baseball/overnight-completion` and `git log --oneline main..HEAD`. Both are stale, and the first is actively **dangerous**: the mission's work moved to `main` via PRs, so `main..HEAD` on that branch shows **94 commits** and reads like a large body of unlanded work waiting to be merged.

It is not. It's a squash-merge ancestry artifact.

## Measured, not inferred

`git diff A...B` (three dots) re-counts everything the squash already landed. `git diff A B` (two dots) gives the true delta:

```
git diff --stat main baseball/overnight-completion
  →  -21,617 / +1,070    — every file comes back branch-OLDER-than-main
```

| File | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| `golf/(auth)/login/page.tsx` | `123502e94` 07-29 (#1110, auth resolved server-side) | `8f66b6644` 07-24 — **still carries the client-side check #1110 removed to stop the sign-in flicker** |
| `components/ui/empty-state.tsx` | `9e15b0b71` 07-29 (recruiting sunset) | `5d7f782a9` **06-14** |
| `lifting/.../settings-client.tsx`, `coach/discover/{PlayerCard,FilterPanel}.tsx` | fixed in **#1126** | the pre-fix `<button>`-inside-`<button>` versions |

So the branch's 1,070 "extra" lines are the **old code main has since replaced**. Merging it would revert #1110, #1126 and the recruiting sunset. **Nothing is stranded there.**

A resume doc whose first command sends the next agent to a branch that reverts production is the worst failure mode this file has, so the warning is a stop box at the very top — with the exact re-verification command, because three-dot vs two-dot *is* the whole trap.

## Two hazards added that cost real time tonight

**A green check named `all` does not mean CI passed.** `ci.yml` and `review-gate.yml` **both** define a job called `all`, and `all` is one of only three required contexts. PR #1125 reported `all → success` on its head commit while the `BaseballHelm authenticated smoke` job that CI's `all` *needs* was still `in_progress` — the green was Review Gate's. That smoke job then **failed**. The doc now gives the CI-run-scoped query to use instead.

> Fixing it properly **needs the owner**: renaming a job changes its check-run name, so branch protection would then wait forever for a context named `all` that no longer exists — blocking every PR. The rename and the `required_status_checks` update must land together.

**The seed target guard.** Both baseball seeds now refuse an unnamed non-local target, and `seed:baseball:ci` no longer carries `--allow-prod` — so `REFUSING TO SEED` is the guard working, not a broken script.

Docs only.

The nested-interactive ratchet's remaining 17 entries were all the same shape: `<Link><Button>…</Button></Link>`. That *renders* — which is why it shipped — but it puts a control inside a control: two focusable elements for one action, an ambiguous click target, and a screen reader announcing a button nested in a link.

## The root cause was a missing escape hatch, not 17 independent mistakes

The correct shape is `<Button asChild><Link/></Button>`, which renders **one** `<a>`. But `asChild` existed only on the **Fairway** button — and every one of these 17 sites imports `src/components/ui/button.tsx`, which **did not have it**. There was no correct way to write this, so 17 sites wrote the wrong one.

**Adding the prop is the fix; the sweep is a consequence.**

## `asChild` on ui/button — three deliberate differences from Fairway's

| | Why |
|---|---|
| `disabled` not forwarded | invalid on `<a>`. Becomes `aria-disabled` + `pointer-events-none opacity-50`, so a disabled link-button is neither clickable nor silently still-active |
| icons/spinner not injected | Slot takes exactly one child; they'd have to be siblings. The two `leftIcon` call sites now compose the identical `<span className="flex-shrink-0 -ml-0.5">` inline, so the DOM is unchanged |
| ripple + haptic stay **on** (Fairway skips them) | **behaviour preservation.** Every call site was a `<Link><Button/></Link>` where the Button was the styled element and *did* ripple. This component applies `relative overflow-hidden` to whichever element it styles, so the ripple host is still correct — the migration is invisible to the user |

Where a `<Link>` carried its own layout class (`w-full sm:w-auto`, `shrink-0`, `flex-shrink-0`, `block`) it is hoisted onto the Button, which is now the element rendering those styles. Nothing is dropped.

## One site is not an asChild fix

`components/features/college-card.tsx` is a whole clickable **card** that also holds its own interest toggle — not button-shaped, so asChild doesn't apply, and lifting the toggle into an absolute corner would mean guessing at pixels I can't see. It uses a **stretched link**: the `<Link>` becomes an `absolute inset-0` overlay with an aria-label, so it has **zero layout impact** and the card's geometry is unchanged *by construction*, the whole card stays clickable, and the two controls are siblings.

Two details that matter: the overlay sits **inside** PaperCard so hovering it still fires PaperCard's own `hover:shadow-*` (`:hover` applies to ancestors — a sibling overlay would have broken it), and the interest button is raised to `relative z-20` above the `z-10` overlay or the link would swallow every click on it. Known tradeoff, inherent to stretched links: card text can no longer be mouse-selected.

## Verification

`KNOWN_VIOLATIONS` is now **entirely empty** — both classes closed, **21 sites across 20 files** — and the guard passes 6/6, which proves it two ways at once: the "no new violations" test would report any site still wrapping, and the stale-entry test would fail on anything left behind.

**Proven non-vacuous:** re-wrapping one fixed site makes the guard fail with `app/not-found.tsx:18 — <Button> nested inside <Link>`. The detector is still reading these files and genuinely finding nothing.

Local: typecheck clean · lint clean · **885 files / 8447 tests** green.

## What is NOT claimed

- **None of the 20 surfaces was visually verified in a browser** — several are behind auth, two are sunset recruiting surfaces. The safety argument is structural, not observational: `asChild` moves the same class string onto the same visual element, and the one site that couldn't be done that way uses a zero-layout-impact overlay.
- **The static walk still cannot see runtime nesting** — a component that *renders* a button, placed inside a `<Button>`. That gap is open.

body:
The nested-interactive guard landed in #1122 found **3 SEVERE** violations — interactive controls nested inside a `<button>`. Not a lint nit: a button cannot contain a button, so the parser **closes the outer button at the inner one**. The server DOM and the React tree then disagree and hydration throws (#418/#425). It is the exact shape that shipped in `CalendarView` (#1111) and in `select.tsx`.

All three are the same underlying mistake — a row or card made clickable by wrapping the whole thing in a `<Button>`, then hanging a secondary control off it — so all three take the same fix: **make the inner control a sibling, not a child.**

| File | The nested control | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `lifting/dashboard/settings` TeamPicker — **LIVE, reachable today** | "clear selection" X inside the combobox trigger | sibling, overlaid `absolute right-3 top-1/2`; trigger reserves room with `pr-10` when a value is set, so layout is unchanged |
| `coach/discover/FilterPanel` saved-search rows | delete `IconButton` inside the load `Button` | row is a plain `<div>`; load + delete are siblings |
| `coach/discover/PlayerCard` compact variant | compare checkbox inside the card button | card is a plain `<div>`; checkbox + open-player button are siblings |

## Small improvements that fell out of it

- `e.stopPropagation()` on the clear button is **gone** — siblings don't bubble into each other. The document `mousedown` handler still sees the click as inside `containerRef`, so dropdown behaviour is unchanged.
- The rows/cards gain `focus-within:` equivalents of their hover styling, so a keyboard user sees the highlight a mouse user already saw.
- FilterPanel's delete button gains `focus-visible:opacity-100`. It was `opacity-0` until hover — reachable by Tab but **invisible while focused**.
- PlayerCard's checkbox gains `aria-pressed` (it's a toggle rendered as a button), and its inner `<div>`s became `<span class="block">` — `<div>` inside `<button>` is also outside button's phrasing-content model, just not one the parser splits on.

## Verification

The SEVERE section of `KNOWN_VIOLATIONS` is now **empty** and the guard passes **6/6**, which proves both halves at once: the "no new violations" test would report these files if the nesting were still there, and the stale-entry test would fail if I'd left the entries behind.

**Proven non-vacuous rather than assumed:** re-adding the now-fixed `PlayerCard` entry to `KNOWN_VIOLATIONS` makes the stale-entry test **FAIL** — so the detector is still reading that file and genuinely finding nothing.

Full local run: typecheck clean · lint clean · **885 files / 8447 tests** green.

## What is NOT claimed

- **No runtime/RTL assertion was added.** `TeamPicker` isn't exported and its clear affordance only appears after a server-action-backed dropdown selection, so rendering it needs a harness larger than the fix. The defect class is a *source shape*, and the static walk detects source shape exactly.
- **The static walk still cannot see runtime nesting** — a component that renders a button, placed inside a `<Button>`. That gap is open and not addressed here.
- The two Discover files are **sunset recruiting surfaces**, so their crash was unreachable in the product. Fixed anyway because that code is kept restorable by design; leaving a hydration crash in code we intend to be able to turn back on just defers it. **No recruiting code is deleted.**

body:
`BaseballHelm authenticated smoke` is a **required merge gate**, and it ran `npm run seed:baseball:ci` with the **production** Supabase URL and service-role key in its env, **on every pull request**.

It now stands up a throwaway Supabase stack on the runner and seeds that. `supabase start` was **already** doing exactly this in `ci.yml`'s `Supabase lint + RLS tests` job, so the mechanism was proven; the new `.github/actions/local-supabase-stack` composite wraps it and exports the stack's URL + keys.

---

## What this turned into

Repointing the gate at a fresh database found **five** defects that had each been live for a month or more. They are unrelated in mechanism and **identical in why nothing caught them: CI only ever exercised production, where the missing piece already existed.**

| # | Defect | Why production hid it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **`on_auth_user_created` on `auth.users` is in no tracked migration** — signup never created the `public.users` row on any DB built from migrations | prod already had the trigger |
| 2 | **The demo coach had no `baseball_team_coach_staff` row** — a coach belonging to no team, so *every* authenticated page sat on "Opening your command center" | prod had the row, added **by hand** a day after the coach row |
| 3 | **`avatars` bucket + its 4 storage policies are in no tracked migration** — avatar upload dead on every local stack / preview branch, and it is on the golf onboarding path | prod already had the bucket |
| 4 | **`scripts/seed-baseball-e2e.ts` had no target guard at all** while `playwright.yml` ran it against prod on every push to `main`, creating auth users and DELETEing camp registrations | the rule was ~130 lines *inline* in its sibling |
| 5 | **`golf-attachments` and `expense-receipts` exist nowhere** — golf message attachments and travel expense receipts have never worked | nothing hid it; nobody had looked |
| 6 | **Our own CSP blocked the local stack.** `connect-src` allowed `https://*.supabase.co` and `ws://127.0.0.1:*` (HMR) but **no `http://` loopback origin**, so the browser refused every `supabase-js` call | it only breaks when the app is pointed at a local stack, which nobody had done in a browser |

### #6 is what was actually failing the smoke gate

Two earlier rounds diagnosed it by inference and both were incomplete. This one came from the **Playwright trace's console**:

```
Connecting to 'http://127.0.0.1:54321/auth/v1/user' violates the following
Content Security Policy directive: "connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co …"
```

It presented as a **hang, never an auth error** — the client `getUser()` fetch was refused, so `authLoading` never settled and `DashboardSessionGuard` sat on "Opening your command center" forever. Coach and player failed identically; the three anonymous specs passed because they make no Supabase call. The assertion message (`element(s) not found` on a heading) could never have pointed here.

**A consequence worth more than the CI fix:** `supabase start` + `npm run dev` has *never* been able to authenticate in a browser either. Local-stack development was broken in exactly this silent way — very likely part of why nobody used the local stack, which is the same blind spot that let #1 and #3 survive for months.

**The fix is scoped, and that is the point.** `src/lib/security/local-supabase-csp.mjs` derives the origin from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` at build time and returns it **only** when loopback, so production gets a byte-identical CSP. It deliberately does **not** hardcode `http://127.0.0.1:*`, which is the easy fix and would loosen `connect-src` for every production visitor.

Verified against the real emitted header:

| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | http-loopback in `connect-src` |
|---|---|
| `https://qmnssrrolpinvwjjnufo.supabase.co` | **false** |
| `http://127.0.0.1:54321` | **true** |

21 assertions weighted toward the negative invariant. Host matching is exact: `https://127.0.0.1.evil.com`, `https://localhost.attacker.net`, `https://127.0.0.1@evil.com`, and loopback in a path or query all return nothing. Non-vacuous — hardcoding the literal fails 2 assertions, relaxing the matcher to a substring test fails 3 including both squat cases.

1 and 3 share a structural cause: the baseline `20260527000000_prod_public_baseline.sql` is a **public-schema-only** dump, so nothing in `auth`, `storage`, `cron` or `realtime` could *ever* have been captured by it. 3 was found by deliberately sweeping for the class after 1.

## The gate itself

| | |
|---|---|
| **No secrets needed** | The readiness-check steps and the fork/Dependabot `if:` skip are gone — that skip existed *only* because external PRs get no secrets, and a **required** gate that silently skipped for a whole class of PR was a hole in it. `E2E_BASEBALL_*` are now hardcoded non-secrets: the seed creates those accounts itself, on a database destroyed when the job ends. |
| **Step order changed** | `supabase start` runs **before** `npm run build` — Next.js inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` at build time. |
| **It now tests *this PR's* schema** | `supabase start` applies everything under `supabase/migrations/`, so a migration that breaks a smoke path fails on the PR that introduces it. |
| **`seed:baseball:ci` drops `--allow-prod`** | Against loopback the guard needs no flag, so the flag was pure risk: if prod credentials ever leak back into that env, the seed now **refuses**. |

## Migrations authored, NOT applied

Both are shaped so that applying them to production **cannot change production** — conditional creates and `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, never `DROP`. Production already has both objects; the files exist so databases built from migrations are correct.

**RETRACTED — an earlier version of this description claimed a security hole that does not exist.** It said production's avatar UPDATE policy has `USING` and no `WITH CHECK`, "so a user can move their own row out of their own folder," and raised it for the owner.

That is wrong. **For UPDATE, when `WITH CHECK` is omitted, PostgreSQL applies the `USING` expression to the NEW row as well as the old one.** Production's policy is already owner-scoped on both sides; an explicit `WITH CHECK` would change nothing but the reading.

Settled by execution, not by recalling the docs — a rolled-back transaction on a throwaway table with a USING-only UPDATE policy:

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| move a row **out** of the predicate | `42501 new row violates row-level security policy` |
| **control** — update staying inside the predicate | succeeds |

The control is what makes it evidence rather than coincidence. Left standing, the claim would have sent the owner to harden a policy that is already correct. The migration header records the retraction rather than quietly deleting the sentence.

## Not fixed, with the reason

`golf-attachments` / `expense-receipts` need **new RLS designed** for a shared production database (conversation-membership scoping; team-staff scoping plus `public = true` since the code calls `getPublicUrl`). Hand-written RLS here has already produced two recursion cycles and five anon-callable functions in this run, none visible to reading. Recorded as `KNOWN_MISSING_BUCKETS` with their evidence, and a stale-entry test forces the entries out when fixed.

Verified absent by read-only SQL: neither bucket in `storage.buckets`, zero `storage.objects` rows, both backing tables empty — **broken-and-unused**, not users-hitting-errors.

## One trap caught before it shipped

`baseball_team_coach_staff` has `UNIQUE (team_id, coach_id)` *and* an `id` PK, and production's row carries a **random** id because it was inserted by hand. A deterministic-id upsert conflicting on `id` would have tried to INSERT a second row for the same (team, coach) against production and violated that constraint — which `playwright.yml` would have hit on **every push to main**. Found by checking `pg_constraint` before trusting the upsert, not after.

## Guards

Three new source-text suites under `src/test/schema/`. Source-text on purpose: **a database test cannot catch a missing object, because it runs against the database that is missing it** — precisely why the pgTAP suites never saw any of this. `storage-buckets-tracked` derives its bucket list *from the source* rather than hardcoding production's, so it cannot rot.

The seed's guard rules also moved to `scripts/lib/seed-target-guard.ts` with **21 executable** assertions, replacing a test that only grepped for the string `HELM_PROD_PROJECT_REF`.

**Every guard verified non-vacuous** by breaking the thing it protects and watching it fail, then restoring: 3 historical guard regressions re-injected, the staff upsert removed, the conflict target flipped, the avatars migration removed, a fixed bucket re-added to the known list.

Local: typecheck clean · lint clean · **887 files / 8,458 tests** green · actionlint · yamllint under the repo's exact review-gate config · shellcheck at `--severity=warning`.

## What is NOT claimed

- **`supabase start` and the seed against a fresh schema cannot be verified locally** — no Docker on this machine. **This PR's own gate run is the proof.** Prior runs got progressively further: stack up → seed passing → authenticated renders. If it goes red again, the change is still wrong and only this PR is blocked.
- **`playwright.yml`'s `e2e` job still seeds production**, deliberately: it runs the full chromium suite including golf specs that authenticate against real golf data, and a job has one `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`. Rehoming needs a golf local-stack fixture first. It runs on push to `main` and manual dispatch, **never on a PR**, and its seed steps now carry an explicit `--allow-prod` so the write is stated rather than implied.

**`main` is currently red.** Three tests in two files fail as of #1118, and the failure is **time-of-day dependent** — they pass between 00:00 UTC and 20:00 Eastern, and fail after. #1118's CI ran inside the agreeing window; running the suite at 21:05 EDT broke it.

## #1118's change is correct and stays

It fixed a real bug in both places. `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` is the **UTC** date, so from 8pm Eastern / 5pm Pacific onward "today" resolved to **tomorrow**:

- a player with a session scheduled for the actual current day was told **"No lift today"** — right through the hours they were most likely to be lifting
- the Live Weight Room would start querying tomorrow's sessions **while a lift was in progress in front of the coach**

`PlayerLiftHomeClient` now uses the device's local day; `getLiveWeightRoomData` uses the **team's** day via `todayIsoInTz(resolveTeamTimezone(...))`.

## The tests were left on the old anchor

Each fixture's session now lands on the component's *tomorrow*. Fixed by anchoring each fixture the way its code under test anchors it — **not** by loosening an assertion:

- `live-weight-room-helm-lifting.test.ts` calls the real `todayIsoInTz('America/New_York')`. That literal isn't arbitrary: the fixture's `baseball_teams` row carries no `timezone` column, so `resolveTeamTimezone` returns its `DEFAULT_TZ`, which is America/New_York. Using the production helper rather than a second copy means a future change to day resolution can't silently desynchronise them again.
- `PlayerLiftHomeClient.test.tsx` builds the date from local getters, mirroring the component's own `localYmd()`.

## Worth knowing beyond these three tests

**`Unit tests` is not one of main's three required checks** (`CodeQL`, `all`, `Smoke checks`). So a PR whose unit tests fail can merge on green required gates — which is exactly what happened. Relevant when reading a green tick.

## Verification

Time-independent, not just green-right-now — run under four zones:

| TZ | local | UTC | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14) | 07-30 | 07-30 | 5 passed |
| **Pacific/Midway (UTC−11)** | **07-29** | **07-30** | **5 passed** |
| Asia/Tokyo | 07-30 | 07-30 | 5 passed |
| UTC | 07-30 | 07-30 | 5 passed |

And non-vacuous: the **original** tests fail 3 of 5 under Midway, so the fix is what makes the difference rather than the clock moving on.

Full suite back to green: **885 files, 8445 passed, 0 failed**. typecheck clean, eslint clean.

## The guard missed the bug it was written for

`src/test/dom-nesting/no-nested-interactive.test.ts` exists to catch one thing: interactive content nested inside a button, which makes the HTML parser **split** the outer button so the server DOM and React's tree disagree and hydration throws. CLAUDE.md names it as a known crash class.

It didn't catch the real instance. `INTERACTIVE_COMPONENTS` was `{ 'Link' }` and `INTERACTIVE_INTRINSIC` was `{ 'button', 'a' }` — both case-sensitive, so **`<Button>` matched neither**. `CalendarView`'s month day cell was a `<Button>` wrapping event pills that are also `<Button>`, and this check walked past it. It surfaced only when the component was finally mounted for #1111, by reading the DOM.

A guard that can't see the bug it was written for is worse than no guard — its green tick gets read as evidence.

## Why this isn't a one-line change

Adding `Button` / `IconButton` / `ButtonGroupOption` reported ~35 violations and **most were false**. This repo has two Button components:

- `@/components/fairway/controls/button` → `const Comp = asChild ? Slot : 'button'` (`:157`). So `<Button asChild><Link/></Button>` renders **one** `<a>` — correct. Used at **167 call sites**.
- `@/components/ui/button` → always a real `<button>`.

The walker is now `asChild`-aware: a Slot is neither a violation inside another interactive element nor an ancestor for what it contains. `asChild={false}` still counts as a wrapper; a computed `asChild={expr}` is treated as a Slot — a deliberate false-negative, preferred over flagging valid code.

## What's actually left: 25 real violations, two severities

| | |
|---|---|
| **3 SEVERE** — interactive inside a `<button>`, the parser-splitting hydration class | `lifting/.../settings-client.tsx` (live) · `coach/discover/{FilterPanel,PlayerCard}.tsx` (sunset surfaces) |
| **22 INVALID but non-splitting** — interactive inside an `<a>` | mostly `<Link><Button/></Link>`, where the correct form is `<Button asChild><Link/></Button>`. Renders, but nests two focusable elements. |

Landed as a **ratchet**, not 25 unattended fixes across baseball, lifting, golf and the marketing page — CI already uses this idiom ("Import-cycle ratchet"). New violations fail; the list can only shrink, enforced by a second test that fails on **stale** entries so fixing one forces deleting its line.

## The ratchet key drops the line number, on purpose

Keying on the line was my first attempt and it's unusable. Injecting one violation into `app/not-found.tsx` produced **three** failures — one real, two just known entries shifted down a line. `app/baseball/page.tsx` holds several, so it would have fired on any edit above them, and a guard that cries wolf gets disabled rather than fixed.

Cost: two same-shape violations in one file share a key, so fixing one of a pair won't trip the stale check until both are done. The line-accurate list is still printed on failure.

## Verification

- Added a fixture test that runs the **real** detector. The pre-existing vacuity test inlined its own copy of the walk, so it could not have caught a bug in the `asChild` logic. The new one asserts both directions — Slot suppressed, real wrapper caught, and siblings (how CalendarView was fixed) not flagged.
- Injecting `<Button><Button/></Button>` fails **exactly one** test, line-accurate, no spurious stale failures.
- `npm test` — **8444 passed**, 13 skipped, 0 failed · `typecheck` clean · `eslint` clean.

Docs only. No migration applied, no schema touched, read-only SQL throughout.

## Why this is a small PR

I first wrote these as two commits on `baseball/overnight-completion`. That was the wrong base: **#1092 was squash-merged at 14:23Z**, main moved 21 commits ahead, and main's `DATABASE_STATUS.md` had *already* been reconciled by #1102/#1104/#1105 — with better numbers than mine (cross-org player visibility **35 → 16** for a coach, **35 → 1** for a player) and the "email + phone overstated it" correction already in place.

So most of that work re-derived corrections that already existed. Rather than cherry-pick and clobber the better version, this applies **only what is genuinely new** onto main's current docs. The stale branch keeps its two commits as a record; nothing there needs merging.

## The four findings

**1. `schema_migrations` cannot tell you whether any of this is applied.**
All six recent migrations return **zero rows** from `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` — including A and B, which are demonstrably applied (their helpers exist; the policies they rewrote show the new `qual`). Migrations applied through the Supabase MCP `apply_migration` tool don't record a row the way the CLI does, and most of this project's recent ones went in that way. An empty result there is evidence of nothing. Documented with the object-existence check to use instead.

**2. A pre-apply consequence of `20260729200000` that the diff doesn't show.**
One of the 10 coaches has `organization_id IS NULL`. The new helper opens with `p_org_id IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS(...)`, so that row becomes visible **only to itself**. Fail-closed and fine here — it's an internal `@helmsportslabs.com` account — but a **customer** coach with a NULL org would silently lose sight of their colleagues, and it presents as *"the roster page went blank"*, not as an error. Check the column is populated before applying.

**3. P1.14's `state: dead` is wrong in the direction that breaks production.**
Zero rows holds, re-confirmed by `count(*)`. But **~20 live `.from()` read sites depend on those tables**, so dropping them breaks all of them — and "dead" reads as "safe to remove". It's also **13 tables, not 8**, with two never created in production at all.

The real gap is **ingest**: of pitch / batted-ball / catching / fielding / baserunning / workload events, **not one has a write path** anywhere in `src/`. Only `baseball_video_events` (4) and `baseball_stat_sources` (1) are ever written. The reads were built; the collection never was.

→ The decision is *"build the ingest, or remove the read surfaces too"*, not *"keep or graveyard"*. Deleting the tables alone is the single clearly-wrong option.

**4. The queued "CI seeds PRODUCTION" item is narrower than filed.**
- The `login_attempts` DELETE is **scoped** — `.in('email', [DEMO_COACH_EMAIL, DEMO_PLAYER_EMAIL])` — not a table wipe. Real users' lockout protection is untouched.
- **Fork and Dependabot PRs get no secrets**: both workflows use `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`, with a documented dummy fallback.
- The writes are idempotent upserts into a known demo tenant.

Still a real decision, but rewiring a **required** merge gate to a local stack is how every PR in the repo gets blocked — which already happened once today via #1097/#1098.

Empty-state handling was **spot-checked, not swept**: `buildPitcherWorkload` (`stat-visuals.ts:428`) degrades honestly to `[]` with no fabricated zeros. That's **one of ~20** sites. Whether every consumer shows an honest empty state rather than a confident `0.00` is unverified and flagged in the ledger as worth a sweep.

`read-models/player-snapshot-cards.ts` was carrying another session's uncommitted work and was deliberately not touched.

body:
Twelve defects, one theme: a surface asserting something it does not know. Each shows a coach or player a confident value that came from an absent record, a withheld permission, or a failed read.

## The worst one

`SnapshotHeaderBand` rendered **"Cleared (no flag)"** whenever no availability row existed for a player — turning the *absence* of an availability record into an affirmative clearance, on the coach's player profile. A coach reads that as "somebody checked, and he's fine". Nobody checked.

The same null also absorbs a query error, so a **failed read rendered as a clearance too**. `availability` now carries `readFailed`, and the cell has three states: the status, "Couldn't load", or "Not recorded".

The status chip two rows above already did this correctly — it appends "· assumed" when the row is missing. This was one cell that never got the treatment its own neighbour established.

## The batting game log printed the season average under the OPS heading

The header is 16 columns and each body row emits 16 cells, but the TOTALS row spanned **three** columns after `K` instead of two. That one character swallowed SB + HBP + AVG, pushed the average one cell right, left AVG empty, and made the row 17 cells wide in a 16-column table. **A coach read a .312 average as a .312 OPS.**

The pitching TOTALS row directly below spans 2 correctly, which is what proved this a copy-paste slip rather than a layout choice.

The audit's proposed fix was itself wrong — dropping the trailing empty cell leaves 15 cells in a 16-column table. Only the `colSpan` was wrong.

Added `PlayerGameLog.test.tsx`: asserts every row of both tables occupies the same number of grid columns, and that the average lands in the AVG column **by index** (a text search would have passed while the table lied). **Verified to fail against the original bug** — `expected 17 to be 16` and `expected undefined to be '.500'` — before being kept.

## "Actual load" was the prescribed load

`BaseballWeightRoomBoardRow.actual_main_load` was populated from `session_exercises.prescribed_load` and rendered as "Actual load". A coach reading "Actual load: 225 lb" believed the set was performed at that weight when it had only been assigned — and that is precisely the number they progress load from.

Renamed to `prescribed_main_load` so the type cannot lie, and relabelled. Performed load lives in `set_results` and is not in this payload.

## A "7-day change" measured over 14 days

`bodyweight_delta_7d` took the newest and oldest weigh-in across the whole fetch window — which is 14 days, because it is shared with the readiness feeds. It is rendered as "7-day change" and **alerted on at −3 lb**.

A 3 lb acute loss inside a week is a real strength-and-conditioning flag. The same 3 lb across two weeks is ordinary fluctuation. The window is now narrowed to 7 days; fewer than two weigh-ins inside it yields null rather than a longer-window substitute.

## A body map drawn from data never fetched

Player Inspector rendered `<SorenessBodyMap value={{}} readOnly />`, and the comment above it admitted why the value was empty: region data is not in the board payload.

A body map with no regions highlighted reads as "nothing hurts anywhere", not as "not loaded" — and it could sit directly beneath an "Overall severity: 8/10" badge, contradicting it on the same screen. Removed. The real overall severity stays; region detail is now *named* as absent instead of *drawn* as absent.

## Two surfaces asserting facts from withheld permissions

- **Decision Room** printed "No current availability concerns — all players are ready" when the caller lacks `can_view_readiness`. That is a clean bill of health for an entire roster, assembled from a feed the viewer was never shown. Added `readinessWithheld` (mirroring `PerformanceCommandData`, which already had it), ghosted the KPI, and fixed the **exported text summary** too — it gets pasted into staff notes and read later out of context, where "(none)" is worse.
- **Command Center** printed "ON THE RECORD 0" when the Stats Center envelope came back `unauthorized`. `playersWithData` is now `number | null` so "unknown" cannot be spelled as zero, and the KPI ghosts instead of celebrating.

## Practice Effectiveness turned a failed read into a verdict

On a query error it returned the empty envelope under a comment calling it *"honest empty (authorized but no data)"*. It is not honest: this page exists to tell a coach whether their practice plan moved the needle, and an all-zeros summary reads as **"none of it worked"**. Not leaking the DB error was right; asserting a result instead was not.

## UTC "today" told people they had no lift

UTC rolls over at 8pm Eastern / 5pm Pacific — the exact hours a team is in the weight room. Four surfaces resolved "today" that way:

| Surface | Symptom |
|---|---|
| Player lift home (client) | "No lift today" to a player who has one |
| `getPlayerLiftHome` (server) | Same screen; its one `today` drives both the upcoming filter **and** the readiness `checkin_date` match, so the prompt also reappeared for an athlete who had already checked in |
| Live Weight Room | Started querying tomorrow mid-session, emptying the board in front of the coach running the room |
| Performance Command Center | Dropped the day's sessions from its KPIs and board |

`todayIsoInTz` + `resolveTeamTimezone` already existed and already document this exact failure mode. These four just never used them. The client anchors on the device day, matching the formatter it already renders each date with.

## Not fixed here — naming it rather than leaving it implied

~10 more `toISOString().slice(0,10)` "today" computations remain across the baseball read models. Some are harmless (`since`-window bounds where a day of drift changes nothing); others look like the same bug. They need their own pass with tests rather than a blind sweep inside this one.

## Verification

- 896 test files / **8496 tests pass**, 13 skipped
- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors
- `eslint` on all changed files: 0
- `next build`: clean
- New regression test verified to fail before the fix

Not deployed.

body:
Recruiting was sunset in #1092 behind `isRecruitingEnabled()`. A sweep of the module found the switch was not load-bearing everywhere.

## The headline leak

`/baseball/dashboard/players/[id]/scout-packet` — the surface that mints revocable share links to a player's measurables, video and season line — was **still fully functional**. Not hidden, not degraded: working. Two live coach surfaces linked into it in the present tense ("Mint revocable share links for college scouts").

It sat outside every door at once: not in `MODULE_ROUTE_PREFIXES`, not in the middleware's `RECRUITING_ROUTES`, not in `STAFF_CAPABILITY_ROUTES`, and — alone among its six sibling recruiting pages — carrying no guard of its own.

**Why no prefix could name it.** `MODULE_ROUTE_PREFIXES` is a string-prefix match. The only prefix matching that path is `/baseball/dashboard/players`, and adding it would withdraw the live roster, player-profile, stats and passport routes too. So the registry gained `MODULE_ROUTE_PATTERNS` for module routes with a dynamic segment in the middle — anchored, narrow, with a test asserting the live siblings stay live.

Sealed at four layers, because a page redirect is a sign and not a door:

| Layer | Change |
|---|---|
| Data | All six staff actions call `assertRecruitingShipped()` |
| Route | Both pages call `requireRecruitingCoachRoute()` |
| Middleware | `MODULE_ROUTE_PATTERNS` closes both paths |
| Links | Both inbound links gated at their call sites |

The `requiredCapability: 'can_export_reports'` on those actions never could have done this job — a head coach holds every capability unconditionally, which is precisely why the module registry exists. And they are server actions reachable from any client bundle.

## The middleware module gate was dead code

`checkRouteAuthorization` early-returns `authorized: true` for any path outside its four local lists, and the central module check sits *below* that return — so it never ran for `/colleges`, `/journey`, `/scouting` or `/activate`, the four routes its own comment says it exists to cover. Those doors stayed shut only because each page carries its own guard.

Fixed by adding `moduleClosed` to the early-return condition, deliberately **not** by hoisting the check to its own return as first drafted: refusing before the `baseball_coaches` lookup is cheaper but seat-blind, and `/colleges`, `/journey` and `/activate` are *player* surfaces — a player would have been sent to `COACH_HOME`. Falling through lets the lookup separate the seats first.

## Honest states where a gated feature left copy behind

- **Passport per-field visibility** still offered "Public" and "Scout" — two settings that could never take effect, annotated "only applies once exposure is on", pointing at an exposure tile the same component already withholds. Now disabled-not-removed, so a value persisted *before* the sunset still renders as the selection instead of leaving the control blank.
- **A player whose passport was set to public/scout** was told their fields were "available to anyone with the link". False once the packet route closed. Telling someone their personal data is public when it is not is the worse direction of that error.
- **"View Public Profile"** opens a page only the player and their own staff can see. Relabelled, not removed — the preview is still useful.
- **Camps** got a seat-aware page gate. It is a shared coach+player route, so the middleware's recruiting path bounced players via a `baseball_coaches` lookup that has nothing to do with them.
- **Two `EmptyState` presets** (`watchlist`, `pipeline`) shipped CTAs into `/discover` with zero call sites. Deleted; `camps` kept, since it carries no href.

## Test hardening — which immediately paid for itself

The inbound-link guard's regex excluded `$` and `{`, so a template-literal `href` matched nothing at all. That is exactly why both scout-packet links were never flagged. Capturing only the static head would not have caught them either: `/baseball/dashboard/players/` is a live route and the recruiting part is the **suffix**.

It now rebuilds the whole template with a placeholder per interpolation and tests the real path — and on first run found a **third** leak I had missed, `ScoutPacketRosterList.tsx:133`.

## Corrected a measured claim

The restore note said "expect 54 unit tests to fail, in 7 files". Re-measured by actually flipping the flag across **all** vitest projects: **58 in 8**. The old number was measured with `npm test`, which is the unit project only, so a 3-test integration file asserting the same sunset was invisible to it. Corrected, with the reason recorded so the next re-measure uses the right command.

## Also

Added `BaseballModuleDisabledError` rather than reusing an existing class: `BaseballUnauthorizedError` (401) makes callers bounce to `/baseball/login`, which would send a correctly signed-in head coach to a login screen, and `BaseballCapabilityError` blames a coach's permissions for a product decision.

- 891 test files / **8463 tests pass**, 13 skipped
- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors
- `eslint` on all 20 changed files: 0
- `next build`: clean

Six live invoices totalling **$6,450** are sitting in Stripe right now. Any of them could be paid and **nothing in Supabase would know** — the webhook had four `TODO(persistence)` markers and no table behind them, because the migration that would have created it was never applied.

## The migration (applied to prod, 2026-07-29)

You authorised applying migrations. Since `db-migration-reviewer` isn't available to me, I reviewed it myself and ran pre-apply checks against prod first:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `public.organizations` exists | ✅ both FKs resolve |
| `billing_customers` / `billing_invoices` absent | ✅ clean create |
| `service_role` has `BYPASSRLS` | ✅ `FORCE RLS` can't lock out `createAdminClient` |
| `public.set_updated_at()` exists | ❌ **absent — draft defect** |

**That last check caught a real bug.** The draft wired both `updated_at` triggers to `public.set_updated_at()`, which doesn't exist in this database — inside an `IF to_regprocedure() IS NOT NULL` guard. So the triggers would have been **silently skipped** and `updated_at` frozen at insert time forever, on a table whose entire job is mirroring a *changing* remote status.

The repo's actual convention is `update_updated_at_column()` (24 existing triggers use it). Fixed, and the guard now `RAISE NOTICE`s on a miss instead of passing quietly. Post-apply verification confirms **1 trigger on each table**, not 0.

RLS is deny-by-default with `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and no policies — verified `authenticated` cannot `SELECT` either table.

## The persistence

`syncInvoice()` mirrors each handled event. Two things a webhook receiver has to get right:

**Ordering.** Stripe does *not* guarantee delivery order, and each event carries the invoice as it looked when the event was *created*. A retried `invoice.sent` arriving after `invoice.paid` would flip a settled invoice back to `open` — silently re-opening paid money in reporting and dunning. Terminal statuses (`paid`/`void`/`uncollectible`) are never overwritten by a non-terminal one, which makes the sync order-independent without needing a per-event sequence number.

**Retries.** The upsert keys on the `UNIQUE stripe_invoice_id`, so redelivery is a no-op. A genuinely failed write throws and 500s so Stripe retries, rather than losing the transition silently.

It reads `invoice.status` off the object rather than deriving state from `event.type` — one code path for all six handled events, and no mapping table to drift.

## Tests

9 new, including all four out-of-order cases (no regression from `paid`, terminal→terminal correction allowed, normal forward progress, `uncollectible` treated as terminal), plus bad-signature, missing-header, unhandled-type, and failed-write→500.

## Also

Regenerated `database.ts` (266 tables) and the glossary inventory block so the Database-types-drift and docs-check CI guards stay green.

882 test files / 8412 tests green · typecheck + lint clean.
