body:
## The gap

`updateCrmTask` has been sitting in `crm-foundations.ts:403` fully built — it strips server-managed columns from the patch, revalidates the CRM path, logs exceptions — with **zero callers**:

| Action | Call sites in components |
|---|---|
| `createCrmTask` | 6 |
| `completeCrmTask` | 4 |
| **`updateCrmTask`** | **0** |
| `deleteCrmTask` | doesn't exist |

So a task was **immutable the moment it was saved**. The only verb the UI offered was "complete". A title with a typo, a due date on the wrong day, a priority that turned out to be urgent, a description missing the one detail that mattered — all permanent, and the only way out was to complete the wrong task and create a replacement.

## The fix

Rather than add a second near-identical dialog, `CreateTaskDialog` takes an optional `task` and switches to edit mode — the same shape `ScheduleEventModal` already uses for its `event` prop. Fields prefill, the heading becomes "Edit task", the primary action becomes "Save changes", and submit routes to `updateCrmTask`. `TaskCard` gains an edit affordance; `TasksPanel` owns the one dialog for both modes.

### Three deliberate choices

- **The patch carries exactly five fields** (`title`, `description`, `due_at`, `priority`, `kind`). `status` and `completed_at` stay out: completion is `completeCrmTask`'s job, and letting an edit write those columns would mean two paths fighting over them — saving an edit could silently **reopen a completed task**. A test pins the patch key set so this can't drift.
- **The edit button is always rendered**, not revealed on `group-hover`. Hover doesn't exist on touch, and an affordance only mouse users can find is the same "unreachable on mobile" bug in a smaller package. Low-contrast at rest, strengthens on hover.
- **Completed cards get no edit button** — editing a finished task isn't a workflow worth opening up, and the card already renders read-only there.

## The subtle part: the due date

Prefilling a `datetime-local` input from an ISO string with `slice(0, 16)` or `toISOString().slice(0, 16)` yields **UTC**. So merely *opening* the editor and pressing Save — without touching the due field — would shift the due date by the local offset: 9:00am becoming 4:00pm in UTC+7, or the previous evening in UTC-5. Silent data corruption from a no-op action.

`toLocalDateTimeInput` builds the string from local getters so the round-trip is a no-op, and a test asserts the saved instant equals the original.

## Verification

- 5 new tests: prefill, update-not-create, due-date round-trip, patch key set, failure keeps the dialog open
- `npm test` — 8406 passed, 13 skipped, 0 failed
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `eslint` on all 4 changed files — clean

**Non-vacuity verified twice**, because one check wasn't enough here:

1. All 5 fail with the feature reverted.
2. The round-trip test fails **alone** when only the timezone helper is swapped for the naive UTC version — so it's testing the conversion rather than something incidental.

## Context

Item 6 of the 2026-07-20 CRM wiring audit, verified still open against current code before implementing. `deleteCrmTask` genuinely doesn't exist and is **not** added here — deleting a task is a different decision (soft vs hard, audit trail) and shouldn't ride along with making them editable.

Closes the highest-count Sentry issue (`JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-2K`) — handled, warning-level, 0 users, never crashed, but ~2K events of noise burying any real registry drift.

## What it actually was

The tracked note put this at **~45 unresolved metric ids**, deferred as too much unverifiable domain judgment to land safely.

I re-ran the enumeration against production. **49 distinct ids emitted, 42 already resolved** — earlier alias work had quietly closed most of it. Only **7** were unknown:

```
pattern_detected_{scoring,putting,tee}
bubble_player_{putting,approach}
recurring_weakness_putting
scoring_decline_putting
```

And all 7 are one shape, which makes the classification unambiguous rather than a judgment call: `determineInsightType` (`src/app/golf/actions/insights.ts:167`) returns an `InsightType` union member and the focus area is appended. The id is **`<insight_type>_<focus_area>`**.

So there's no column, cache, or shot table behind *"this insight was categorised as a bubble-player warning"*, and no per-round series to correlate against. A causal-lift number for it would be meaningless. `intentional-null` is the honest answer.

They're **live**, not historical — `bubble_player_putting` was last written 2026-07-25.

## Why prefixes instead of seven entries

The shape is a cross-product of ~13 categories and a growing list of focus areas. Enumerating the 7 observed pairings would let the next one — `bubble_player_tee`, `plateau_approach` — silently reopen the same issue. The family match closes it permanently, and a test asserts unseen pairings resolve.

The reason code is deliberately **distinct** from `v2-mining-needs-shot-level-graduation`. That family is waiting on shot-level data and will one day become attributable; these never will. Monitoring has to be able to tell them apart.

Genuinely unknown ids still return `null` — that's the entire point of silencing the categories, so real drift stays visible. Asserted.

## Safety

Prefix matching runs *after* the canonical registry and the alias table, so it cannot shadow a real metric. There's a test for that too, in case the ordering ever changes and someone adds a canonical id like `streak_length`.

## Tests

The fixture is the **real production enumeration** — all 49 ids, ordered by row count, as of 2026-07-29 — so the next person can re-run the same query and diff it rather than trusting a hand-written list.

body:
## The gap

`getCoachTimeline` unioned **five** sources, and `crm_replies` was not one of them:

| # | Source | What it records |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `crm_contact_log` | what we logged |
| 2 | `email_events` | what our sends did (Resend webhook) |
| 3 | `crm_events` | what we scheduled |
| 4 | `crm_notes` | what we wrote internally |
| 5 | `crm_tasks` | what we assigned ourselves |

Every one is **outbound activity or our own record-keeping**. So a coach's timeline could show a dense history of touches from us and give no indication that they had **written back** — the single event a rep most needs to see was the only one absent, while the reply sat in `crm_replies` with a `coach_id` on it the whole time.

## The fix

`crm_replies` becomes the sixth source, read in the same `Promise.all` and merged into the same DESC sort — so a reply lands in **time order** rather than appended after everything else.

Three deliberate details:

- **`actor_id` is null, not the coach.** `actor_id` resolves against `users` (internal staff). Filling it in would either dangle or, worse, credit a staff member with words a coach wrote.
- **Read state lives in the sub-type** (`'unread'`/`'read'`), not buried in metadata — unread is the actionable state and the UI styles on `type`.
- **`from_address` is surfaced in the footer.** A reply can legitimately arrive from an assistant or a secondary address, and "who actually answered" is part of the signal.

## Why extending the union was the safe move

`TimelineSource` gains `'reply'`, and that forced the rest:

- `TIMELINE_CONFIG` is `Record<TimelineSource, …>` → the compiler required a visual treatment
- `ICON_MAP` is `Record<TimelineIconKey, …>` → the compiler required an icon binding

Neither could be silently forgotten. The reply dot takes the strongest step on the accent ramp (it's the only **inbound** source on the timeline) and uses `IconMessage` rather than `contact_log`'s `IconMessageSquare`, so an inbound reply doesn't read as our own logged outreach at a glance. Still one accent language — no rainbow.

## Verification

- 6 new tests against the **real merge** with a mocked Supabase client — presence, time-ordering among the other sources, actor attribution, read state, thread identifiers, and the config entry
- **Non-vacuity checked**: all 6 fail against the pre-change code
- `npm test` — 8393 passed, 13 skipped, 0 failed
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `eslint` on all 5 changed files — clean

There was no prior test coverage for `crm-timeline.ts`; these are the first, and they exercise the action itself rather than asserting on source text.

## Context

Item 6 of the 2026-07-20 CRM wiring audit. Verified still open against current code before implementing — two other items from that list turned out to have been fixed in the interim.

body:
Third of the three symptoms from the fidgety-navigation report. #1110 covered the login flicker and the stale-service-worker "old CRM on back". This is the welcome/skip one.

## The shape of it

`/golf/welcome` arms its exit sequence **unconditionally at mount** — that was deliberate, it's the fix for the old hang where the sequence waited on something that could fail. But it means three timers are live from the first frame: a fade, a `router.replace` to the dashboard, and a 4.5s failsafe that calls **`window.location.replace`** — a hard browser reload. None of them care whether the component still exists.

## 1. The signed-out bounce never cancelled the sequence

A visitor with no session hitting `/golf/welcome` gets bounced to `/golf/login`. Correct. But all three timers stayed armed.

So: they land on the login form, start typing their password, and a few seconds later get **yanked onto `/golf/dashboard` and hard-reloaded**. Having no session, that bounces them right back to `/golf/login` — with the form cleared.

The Skip handler already carried a comment warning about precisely this hazard. This exit never got the same treatment for a mundane reason: `cancelSequence` was declared *below* the identity effect, so the effect couldn't reference it. The hook call now sits above the effect, and the branch cancels before leaving.

## 2. Skip wasn't idempotent

Dismissing an animation you've seen before means tapping Skip two or three times — that *is* the interaction.

Each extra tap armed another 160ms exit timer while overwriting `skipTimerRef` with the newest handle, orphaning the earlier ones. The unmount cleanup could only clear the last, so the rest still called `router.replace` from a dead component. The existing comment says this class of bug was already fixed — but tracking one handle fixed a *single* timer, not the unbounded set a repeat tap creates. Now guarded with `skippedRef`.

## Tests

`useSequencedNavigation` had **no coverage** — a hook owning three timers and a hard browser reload. Added 8 tests, focused on `cancel()`, since that's the contract both fixes above rest on: cancelled before fade, cancelled after fade, idempotent, safe across unmount, and the failsafe not firing once the soft replace has claimed the navigation.

## Verification

881 test files / 8403 tests green · typecheck + lint clean

## Note on scope

The branch is named `golf/route-transitions` because I started on the shell-level route-transition system. I stopped: my diagnosis there was wrong. Only **3** dashboard pages have their own mount entrance animation, so competing entrances aren't the cause. The real source is that 47 of 51 routes have a `loading.tsx`, so every tab switch unmounts, flashes a skeleton, and remounts — an architectural property of the App Router, not a bug to patch. Speculatively rewriting 47 routes' loading behaviour on a theory I hadn't measured was the wrong call, so it isn't in here.

body:
## The gap

**The CRM had no calendar.** `CalendarView` — the only component that renders `crm_events` as a month/week/day grid — was never mounted anywhere. And neither event modal was reachable in any real sense: `ScheduleEventModal` and `EventDetailModal` sit in the shell (`page.tsx:2009`/`2018`), but on `main` the only code that sets `showScheduleModal` true or `selectedEvent` non-null lives **inside those modals**. A closed circuit with no external opener.

What *did* work, which is why this is a visibility gap and not a dead feature:

| Path | State on `main` |
|---|---|
| Create an event | ✅ `QuickActionsPanel` (reachable from a coach row, `page.tsx:999`) inserts into `crm_events` |
| See events per coach | ✅ `getCoachTimeline` unions them in as `source='crm_event'` |
| See the schedule | ❌ nothing rendered `CalendarView` |
| Open / edit an event | ❌ no external opener for either modal |

The orphan survived audits because its three importers pull the `CRMEvent`/`CRMEventType` **types** out of it, so every "is `CalendarView` used?" grep came back positive:

```
EventDetailModal.tsx:8:    import type { CRMEvent, CRMEventType } from './CalendarView';
ScheduleEventModal.tsx:10: import type { CRMEvent, CRMEventType } from './CalendarView';
EventDetailModal.a11y.test.tsx:13: import type { CRMEvent } from './CalendarView';
```

## The fix

A Calendar destination in the sidebar, reusing the state the modals already own — clicking an event opens `EventDetailModal`, clicking an empty slot opens `ScheduleEventModal` pre-filled with that date. No new data path; this is what makes both modals reachable for the first time.

Shortcut is **`C`**, not `6`: inserting Calendar into the digit run would have meant renumbering Sequences 6→7 and Templates 7→8, silently re-pointing two keys that are already muscle memory — the exact failure the *"shortcuts are bound to ids, not array position"* rule in `page-contracts.ts` exists to prevent.

## Two defects found once it was actually going to render

Neither was reachable while the component was unmounted.

**1. `<button>` inside a `<button>`.** The month day cell was a `<Button>` wrapping the event pills, which are also `<Button>`. Invalid HTML — the parser hoists the inner one, so hydration finds a DOM React didn't render (#418/#423), the crash class CLAUDE.md calls out for exactly this shape. The cell is now a `div` with a full-bleed overlay button at `z-0` and the content layer above it `pointer-events-none`, so empty space still schedules and pills stay clickable: same two behaviours, one flat layer of siblings.

Side benefit — each cell gets its own accessible name (`"Schedule on Tuesday, July 29"`) instead of the day number concatenated with every pill title inside it.

**2. The week view clipped days.** It was `overflow-hidden` around a ~700px grid (64px time gutter + seven columns), so below that width the last weekdays were **unreachable**, not merely small, with no scrollbar to reveal them.

## Mobile

This surface is newly reachable on phones (More sheet) and had **zero** responsive classes in 677 lines:

- Header stacks instead of packing ~620px of controls into one `justify-between` row
- Colour-key legend drops below `lg` — the pills carry their own labels
- Connect Google goes icon-only
- Month grid keeps a 560px floor and scrolls, rather than compressing columns to ~50px where every pill truncates to one character. Day view stays the single-column reading mode for narrow screens.

Scrolling a month grid is a legible trade; a 50px column isn't. I did **not** invent a mobile-only interaction model (tap-day-to-open-agenda), because I can't get a real mobile viewport in this environment to verify one.

## Verification

- `npm test` — **8387 passed**, 13 skipped, 0 failed
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `eslint` on all 5 changed files — clean, zero warnings
- CRM admin suite — 37 files, 215 tests passing

**Non-vacuity checked**, since a structural test that can't fail is worse than none: reverting the source and re-running shows **4 of 5** rendering tests and **all 4** contract tests fail against the pre-change code. The fifth documents behaviour that was already correct (`stopPropagation` already kept pill clicks off the slot handler) — flagged rather than dressed up as a fix.

The nesting test asserts *no interactive element contains another*, structural rather than calendar-specific, so it also catches the next person who wraps a cell in a button.

## Not addressed here

`CalendarView`'s Connect-Google button is the only entry to the (fully built) `/api/crm/google-calendar/*` routes, and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are absent from `.env.example`. That button is now reachable, but the OAuth flow behind it stays unconfigured — an ops task, not a code one.

body:
## What you reported

> If I go into CRM and hit back, it takes me to the old CRM… If I go into login, the animation if I'm already authenticated is buggy. It's fidgety… a lot of fidgety stuff in GolfHelm, not just pieces put together.

Three symptoms, three distinct causes, one theme: **auth and routing were decided per-page, in the browser, after paint.** Every page independently re-derived who you were and where you belonged, then visibly corrected course. That correction is the fidget.

## 1. Login flicker when already signed in

`/golf/login` is a client component. It painted the entire screen — `CourseScene`, brand lockup (0.6s entrance), form card (0.7s entrance) — then ran an async `getUserResilient()` + `users.role` query, and only then `router.replace`d you away.

Signed-**out** users paid as well: `checkingAuth` held the form behind three pulsing dots for a full network round trip, waiting on an answer the form never uses.

`updateSession` now resolves it before any HTML ships. The client check is deleted; the form renders immediately.

## 2. "Back takes me to the old CRM"

Not a routing bug — there's only one CRM route. A **stale service worker** was serving cached pre-migration HTML.

Two compounding causes:
- The SW registered with **no `NODE_ENV` guard** (`use-service-worker.ts`, via `OfflineProvider`).
- `CACHE_VERSION` is only stamped with a real build id by `stamp-sw.mjs` **on Vercel builds** (deliberate — generated-file policy). Locally it stays the literal placeholder `golfhelm-vsource` forever, so the install/activate cache-bust never fires and **a dev cache never invalidates.**

Dev now skips registration *and* tears down any SW a previous session left installed, so existing machines self-heal rather than needing DevTools.

## 3. Five places disagreed about where a signed-in user belongs

`loginAction`, `login/page.tsx`, `welcome/page.tsx`, `NativeRedirect`, and the dashboard layout each carried their own copy of the rules. `resolveAdminPostLoginPath` centralised one ternary; `lib/auth/post-auth-destination.ts` now owns the rest.

## The trap — the first draft of this had the bug

The bounce **must not fire for an idle session.** `isPublicRoute` deliberately marks every `(auth)` route public, so the idle-reauth gate never runs on `/login` — an idle session arrives looking perfectly authenticated. Bounce it to the dashboard and the dashboard's own gate bounces it straight back: an **infinite redirect on the page that exists to recover** (#730).

Two pre-existing idle-timeout tests caught it. Idleness is now a single shared definition (`isIdleExpiredSession`) used by both call sites, and the fresh-vs-idle pair is asserted explicitly so it can't regress.

The bounce set is deliberately **two entries**. `reset-password`, `callback`, `complete-signup` and `welcome` all *require* a session — the recovery link is what signs a user in, so bouncing it would kill password reset outright.

## Verification

- 879 test files / 8385 tests green, 0 failures
- 17 new tests, incl. open-redirect rejection on `returnTo`
- typecheck + lint clean

## Not in this PR

The shell-level route-transition system — one entrance-animation owner instead of every page animating on its own mount. It touches `FairwayDashboardShell` and every dashboard route, which another session is actively editing. Half-building a transition system while the shell moves would produce exactly the incoherence this is meant to remove. Designed, not built — happy to do it as a follow-up once that branch lands.

From the 2026-07-20 CRM wiring audit, **item 5**. Verified still present today before fixing — that audit is nine days old.

## The bug

`COACH_CHILD_TABLES` drives the loop that re-points a merged coach's children onto the survivor. It listed five tables and **not** `crm_stage_transitions` — which the `log_crm_stage_transition` trigger writes on every `crm_coaches.status` change, keyed by `coach_id`.

So merging left pipeline history pointing at the merged coach, who is then soft-archived and therefore invisible. The surviving record showed a stage timeline with a hole in it, and **nothing errored** — the loop succeeded, the merge reported success, the loss was silent.

**Measured in production:** 2,401 stage transitions exist, 83 sit on archived coaches.

⚠️ **What that number does not say.** `crm_coaches` has `is_archived`/`archived_at`/`archived_by` but **no `merged_into`**, so nothing records which archive was a merge. How many of the 83 are merge damage versus ordinary archiving *cannot be determined from the data*. I'm stating it as "sit on archived coaches", not "83 casualties". That missing provenance is its own gap — a merge leaves no trace of what it merged into — noted, not fixed here.

**Existing stranded rows are not backfilled.** That needs a data migration, autonomous execution shouldn't apply one, and without `merged_into` there's no safe way to infer the right destination anyway.

## The test is structural, and says so

`crm-dedup.ts` is `'use server'`, and Next only permits async exports from such a module — so the constant can't be exported for a conventional test without making it a pointless async function. That constraint isn't hypothetical; it broke an earlier attempt to export a pure helper from an actions file in this repo today.

So it asserts against source text and is explicit that it verifies the **list is enrolled**, not that the loop runs. The loop is four lines shared by every entry; enrollment is what regresses.

It strips comment lines before matching, so the long comment naming `crm_stage_transitions` can't satisfy its own assertion.

**Verified non-vacuous:** deleting the one-line fix makes 3 of 4 assertions fail. Restored → 4/4 pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

body:
Reported from the Bridge triage queue — two rows for one event:

```
warning  [submitGolfRoundComprehensive.inngestSendFailed] server trace
warning  [submitGolfRoundComprehensive.inngestSendFailed] Failed to send
         coachhelm/round.submitted to Inngest, falling back to direct
         postRoundTrigger: Inngest API Error: 404 Event key not found
```

## ⚠️ The actual production fault is NOT fixed by this PR — it needs you

`INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` **is** set in Vercel Production (64 days old) and Inngest is rejecting it: a rotated or wrong-environment key. Only someone with the Inngest dashboard can replace it.

**And note:** the call-site comment says Vercel bakes env vars in *at deploy time*, so updating the value also requires a **redeploy** to take effect.

**Impact, measured before touching anything:** rounds are still being analyzed. Every round on the three affected days has `coachhelm_analyzed_at` set and `coachhelm_failed_at` null — the direct `postRoundTrigger` fallback works. What's lost is the **durability guarantee**, not the analysis. Correctly a warning, not data loss.

| day | rounds | analyzed | failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-29 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| 2026-07-28 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| 2026-07-27 | 1 | 1 | 0 |

## What this PR does fix: both rows have one cause

`skipSentry: true` is only set when `classifyProviderFault()` returns a fault. It returned null, so the same failure was **also** captured by Sentry — that's the duplicate "server trace" row. One classification fix removes both.

## Why the classifier missed — and what I could not explain

The stored evidence proves the shape:

```
metadata.extra.stack: "Error: Inngest API Error: 404 Event key not found
                           at a.getResponseError (…/chunks/22064.js:6:6199)"
metadata.errorCode:   null
```

A plain `Error` whose `.message` is exactly the text `invalid_credential` matches. Ruled out **by checking, not reasoning**: the pattern does match (tested in node against the regex extracted from the *deployed* commit); the classifier is in the deployed build; the call site invokes it; and a passing test for `new Error('Inngest API Error: 404 Event key not found')` already existed.

**I could not explain it, so I did not ship a guess at the cause.** Instead `messageOf` stops depending on one extraction being right — it now walks name, message, cause (recursively, including *object* causes), stack, `{response:…}`, `{data:…}`, and a JSON view. Concatenating cannot lose a previously-succeeding match, since the old output is a substring of the new one.

Four shapes verified to have produced an **empty string** before — each classifying as "not a provider fault", exactly the observed symptom — now classify:

```
{ response: { message } }
{ data: { error } }
{ status: 404, body: 'Event key not found' }
Error('Inngest API Error') with cause: { message: '404 Event key not found' }
```

## The bug my own fix introduced, caught by an existing test

Feeding the stack into everything made a **Vercel AI Gateway** credit error report `provider: 'inngest'`. Stacks are full of file paths and this repo has `src/lib/inngest/client.ts`, so `PROVIDER_RULES`' `/inngest/i` — checked first — matched a path segment and would have sent an operator to the wrong dashboard.

Hence the asymmetry, which is the design:

| | matched against |
|---|---|
| **fault kind** | everything, stack included — every rule is a credential/quota phrase that doesn't occur in a path |
| **provider** | message-ish text only — provider names *do* occur in paths, and a wrong provider names the wrong account |

Consequence, asserted rather than hidden: an error whose signature exists only in its stack gets the right kind and tier with `provider: 'unknown'`. Better than silence, worse than a named account, far better than a confident wrong one.

My first version of that test expected `'inngest'` and failed. The code was right and my expectation was wrong — the test now pins the real contract, plus a regression test that a path naming one provider can't override a message naming another.

## Verification

- 12/12 in `provider-fault.test.ts` (4 new tests)
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, 0 errors
- Full unit suite: **877 files, 8,368 passed**, 13 skipped

Finding **#5**, the last unclosed P0. It was deferred as needing *"a product decision + a 75-call-site audit"*. **I did the audit. It doesn't need 75 decisions — it needs zero.**

**Not applied.** See the last section.

## The audit

74 reads of `baseball_coaches` in `src/` (excluding tests), classified by query shape:

| Shape | Count | Effect of org-scoping |
|---|---|---|
| `.eq('user_id', <caller>)` | **66** | none — self-scoped |
| `.eq('id', coachId)`, caller's own id | 3 | none |
| `INSERT` (onboarding ×2) | 2 | none — a SELECT policy can't reach a write |
| service-role client | 1 | none — bypasses RLS |
| same-org by construction | 2 | none — both already degrade gracefully |

**Not one call site requires a cross-organization read.** `documents.ts:62` even documents its own degradation: unknown uploaders *"degrade to `null` rather than failing the whole page load."*

So the product question shrinks to: is a *future* cross-org surface wanted (a recruiting directory letting a college coach contact a HS coach)? None exists, recruiting is sunset, and if one is built it should be a curated view exposing name/program — not a blanket read of the base table including email.

## A correction to the finding itself

It's been described throughout as *"every coach's email **and phone**"*. Measured against production: **10 coach rows, 10 with an email, 0 with a phone.** The live exposure is names, emails, `coach_type`, `organization_id`. Overstating a finding is how the real ones stop being believed — wording fixed in all three places.

Exposure otherwise confirmed: a coach sees **10 coaches across 8 organizations**, only 1 of which is their own.

## The fix, and why it's shaped this way

Self OR same-organization, with the org check in a `SECURITY DEFINER` helper.

**The helper isn't optional.** An inline `organization_id = (SELECT organization_id FROM baseball_coaches WHERE user_id = auth.uid())` is a subquery over the very table the policy guards, which re-enters it — `infinite recursion detected in policy`, i.e. *every* query against the table fails for everyone. That exact bug shipped twice in the tenant-isolation pair and was caught only by executing the SQL.

**`EXISTS` rather than `= (SELECT … LIMIT 1)`.** No user holds more than one coach row today (verified: 0), so `LIMIT 1` would be correct *right now* — but if a coach ever holds rows in two orgs it picks one arbitrarily and silently hides the other. `EXISTS` handles that by construction rather than depending on a fact that happens to be true.

## Measured across all ten coach identities

| coach | now | after | own row |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coach Demo | 10 | 2 | 1 ✓ |
| Demo Strength Coach | 10 | 2 | 1 ✓ |
| admin *(no organization)* | 10 | 1 | 1 ✓ fail-closed |
| …6 more | 10 | 1 | 1 ✓ |

Nobody loses their own row. The Demo University pair still see each other. Everyone else is the sole coach in their org, so seeing only themselves is correct rather than a regression. Both cross-coach call-site patterns were re-run under the new policy and still resolve every row they need.

⚠️ **Honest limit:** production's `baseball_coaches` is 10 rows, mostly test/demo accounts, with 8 single-coach orgs. This shows the policy is correct and locks nobody out; it does **not** exercise a large multi-coach program, because production has none.

## Why this is not applied

The standing rule for autonomous execution is "never apply a database migration". Today's earlier migrations went in under an explicit one-time instruction from the owner while they were awake — that's spent. `CLAUDE.md` also mandates `db-migration-reviewer` for RLS changes, and this has no pgTAP coverage yet.

Merge, let CI build a fresh Postgres from every migration and run the suites, then apply.

## Also refreshed

`RELEASE_READINESS.md` had gone stale in three ways: the *"demo against a demo org until the RLS fix is applied"* caveat is lifted (that leak is closed), the RLS migrations move out of "production-usable but not proven" into verified, and "Blocked, deliberately" now lists what is *actually* still blocked (#1103 and this) rather than a blanket ban that no longer holds.

Corrects a claim I wrote into `CURRENT_PRIORITIES.md` an hour ago that is now false, and records the post-deploy verification honestly.

## The correction

That file asserts **"`main` is still NOT DEPLOYED, and that is deliberate"**, naming `dpl_B9mv3SVZ` / `bd1e625d4` as what production serves. A reader would conclude the offline.html fix and the middleware hotfix are still unshipped and act on that.

Production has been `dpl_GGoaQYjxpJgf2uL3q8ySK7nPLN5U` / **`b18c2a174`** since **18:37:10Z** — READY and aliased to helmsportslabs.com. Confirmed via `/api/health`, which reports its own `deploymentId`, so the cutover was *observed* rather than inferred from the CLI exiting 0.

One deploy carried #1094, #1095, #1096, #1097, #1098, #1099, #1101, #1102.

## Deployed from a clean detached worktree, not the shared tree

`vercel --prod` uploads the local directory, and the shared tree holds another session's uncommitted files — deploying from there would have shipped their in-progress work to production. This document already warns about the shared-tree hazard; the warning now says that deploy is the one path where it reaches users.

## What was NOT verified — the half that matters more

| Confirmed | |
|---|---|
| deployed SHA = main's tip | ✓ |
| `/api/health` healthy, `database: ok`, ~100ms | ✓ |
| `/`, `/baseball`, `/golf/login`, `/baseball/login` | 200 ✓ |
| Vercel runtime errors, 1h spanning the deploy | **none** ✓ |
| postgres ERRORs | 6, all my own probes ✓ |

**Not confirmed:**

- **The mobile hamburger was not visually re-verified in production.** Chrome won't resize below ~500px; Playwright's MCP profile is locked by another session; and the site correctly refuses to be framed, killing the iframe workaround. It rests on 5 passing unit tests (lock on `documentElement` not `body`, Lenis scroller stopped/restarted) plus SHA confirmation.
- **Join-by-code was not exercised through the UI.** A logged-out visitor cannot resolve a code by design — anon EXECUTE is revoked on the resolver — so the page requires sign-in, and entering credentials is out of scope. The resolver is verified at the database layer (1 row for an authenticated non-member).

## A trap I walked into, documented so nobody repeats it

Curling `/baseball/join/<code>` *looks* like it renders "not found" for **valid** codes. It does not. `not found` / `notFound` are framework identifiers in the JS chunks of every response — including the invalid-code response, which is why both matched identically. I reported it as concerning before checking whether the string was page content.

body:
Applies the baseball tenant-isolation migration pair plus the Lift Lab identity sync to production, on the owner's explicit instruction, and records the verification so the claims are checkable rather than asserted.

**No new SQL is authored here.** These migration files were written and reviewed earlier (#1092); this PR applies them and replaces their stale `⚠️ NOT APPLIED` banners with what actually happened.

## What was closed

Live since the 2026-05-27 baseline: any authenticated user on any team could read every other program's full roster (email, phone, GPA, SAT/ACT), every team's secret `join_code`, and — through three policies comparing a column to itself — every private coach↔player message in the database, with INSERT and UPDATE as well as SELECT.

Five of the six P0s in `DATABASE_STATUS.md` are now closed. **#5 (`baseball_coaches` email/phone) is untouched and is now the only unclosed one** — it has no authored fix because tightening it is a product decision plus a 75-call-site audit, not a policy swap.

## What made it safe

Migration B's own precondition was *"verify by EXERCISING each flow, not by reading the diff"*, and I had recorded that I could not satisfy it. That was wrong. Postgres lets you assume the `authenticated` role and set `request.jwt.claims` inside a transaction, which runs the policies exactly as a named real user, and `ROLLBACK` makes it free:

```sql
BEGIN;
  SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated;
  SET LOCAL request.jwt.claims = '{"sub":"<uuid>","role":"authenticated"}';
  -- every query here is filtered by RLS as that user
ROLLBACK;
```

Measured before and after, as three real users:

| | player (non-member) | coach, 8-player roster | owner, 14-player roster |
|---|---|---|---|
| teams visible | 13 → **1** | 13 → **1** | 13 → **1** |
| join codes visible | 13 → **1** | 13 → **1** | 13 → **1** |
| players visible | 35 → **1** | 35 → **16** | 35 → **22** |
| own roster / self row | 1 → **1** ✓ | 8 → **8** ✓ | 14 → **14** ✓ |
| messages visible | 9 → 9 ✓ | 9 → 9 ✓ | 73 → 73 ✓ |

Cross-org visibility does not fall to zero because the recruiting backstop admits players who **opted in** (`recruiting_activated = true` — 9 of 35; all 26 college players correctly excluded). Consent model working, not leak persisting.

I also dry-ran B's new `USING` clauses as a plain SELECT *before* applying, which is how I know the coach's roster survived rather than finding out afterwards.

## Flows exercised after applying

| Flow | Result |
|---|---|
| `resolve_baseball_team_by_join_code` as a non-member | 1 row ✓ |
| `get_baseball_team_join_context` as a non-member | 1 row ✓ |
| roster search, full cross-org email | 1 row ✓ |
| roster search, `'sm'` | **0 rows** ✓ |
| `baseball_teams_public_profile` as `anon` | 13 rows, no `join_code` ✓ |

That `'sm'` probe is the leak itself — the old search was an unscoped ILIKE over name **and** email, so two characters returned strangers' addresses from every program.

## Also in here

- **Lift Lab sync (`20260729000300`).** Production still had `DO NOTHING`, so `helm_lifting_athletes.user_id` was write-once: **21 of 22 athletes had it NULL and active — every one permanently unable to open `/lifting/dashboard`.** Applying the file only makes the repair possible; a coach clicking "Sync Athletes" performs it, so I ran it (14 + 8 rows). After: 0 unlinked, 22 active *unchanged*, every `user_id` matching its source player across 22 distinct accounts. Verified in a rolled-back transaction first that a deactivated athlete stays deactivated.

- **`unresolve_admin_event` was anon-EXECUTEable** — mine, from earlier today. Not exploitable (it self-gates; an anon call returns `42501 Forbidden`, exercised) but closed. `log_crm_stage_transition` needed `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC`, not `FROM anon`, because its grant came through PUBLIC and revoking from anon was a silent no-op.

- **Regenerated `database.ts`.** `check:types-drift` diffs it against production, so the eight new functions would have turned it red. Note it **removes `graphql_public`**, which a fresh generation does not emit — meaning that check could only ever have passed by skipping (it exits 0 when `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` is unset). Also inherits `crm_unmatched_inbound`, a table another session created in production without regenerating types.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` — exit 0, zero errors
- `npm test` — **877 files, 8359 passed**, 13 skipped, 0 failed
- `regen-docs` — 264 tables / 7 views / 153 functions (non-empty, so removing `graphql_public` did not break its parser)

## Honest limits

Every measurement is a row count at the data layer. No browser walked these screens, and production carries little traffic right now, so "no errors since applying" is weak evidence. The residual risk is a rendering bug in the app, not a policy denying too much — the policies themselves have been executed.

body:
Triaged every error in production for the last 7 days. **Almost everything real was already fixed and deployed** — this PR carries the one code bug that wasn't.

## The one code fix

`describeError` — the module whose entire purpose is eliminating `[object Object]` from telemetry — had it inside its own fallback:

```ts
try { return JSON.stringify(err); }
catch { return String(err); }   // <- [object Object]
```

Found via production, 2026-07-27: `[recurring_events.editRecurringEvent] [editRecurringEvent Error]: [object Object]`, logged twice while a coach failed to edit a recurring event, **from a call site that does use describeError**.

Three reachable paths, verified in node:

| input | JSON.stringify | old result |
|---|---|---|
| circular reference | throws | `[object Object]` |
| BigInt anywhere | throws | `[object Object]` |
| function/symbol value | returns `undefined` | `"undefined"` |

The third never reached the catch, so hardening the catch alone would have missed it. Now falls back to naming the value — constructor, own keys, surviving `message`.

## Triage of the week — everything else

**Already fixed and deployed** (verified by dating each fix against each error):

| error | fix | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `golf_players_1.jersey_number does not exist` (attendance) | `b177ea047`, 2026-07-28 | error was 07-23, 5 days earlier ✅ |
| `golf_conversations` RLS insert denial (coach→player DMs) | `8d78b56d4`, 2026-07-26 16:59Z | error was 00:49Z same day ✅ |
| `editRecurringEvent` missing error context | `b177ea047`, 2026-07-28 | error was 07-27 ✅ |

**Explained, not bugs:** the 07-29 cron failures (`refresh-engagement`, `coachhelm-safety-net`) are collateral from the 9.4h database wedge — the RPC error body is literally the Cloudflare 522 HTML page. `No active team membership for player` / `No completed rounds in 90 days` are expected empty-data conditions logged at `error` severity.

**React #310** — 9 rows / 3 users, but spread across a dozen unrelated routes (`/hub`, `/stats`, `/my-standing`, `/rounds/new`, `/coachhelm`, `/whats-new`). That breadth is stale-bundle, not a component bug, and it's corroborated by concurrent `Loading chunk NNNNN failed` errors. Matches the prior audit (44 files, 0 hook violations). None since 07-27.

## Still open — flagged, not fixed

- **`editRecurringEvent`'s actual failure cause is unknown.** Logged with no code, details, hint, or `extra`. Nothing can reconstruct it; a recurrence will now be diagnosable.
- **`fetchShotDriversByCategory` aborting 34× in 7 days** (30 `AbortError`, 4 statement timeout). Insights are being generated *without* shot drivers, silently — degraded quality, not a crash.
- **Two billing-driven AI outages** (operational, not code): 11× `chat/stream: model error — Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API` and 3× `compose() LLM call failed for task=round_review: Free tier users do not have access to this model`, both in the last 3 days.
- **`budget: 2 settings rows for team_id=…`** ×10 — duplicate rows where the code expects one.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` 0 errors · eslint clean · unit suite **877 files / 8,364 passed / 13 skipped / 0 failed**

body:
Three things, all from this morning.

## 1. The hamburger menu opened 2,000px above the viewport

Reported as *"when I click the hamburger, if I'm scrolled, it still does not drop down. Only if I'm at the top."*

The menu was opening every time — **where** was the bug. Measured on production at `scrollY 2200`:

| | value |
|---|---|
| header bounding box | `y = -2200` |
| open menu | `y = -2014` |
| menu `display` | `block`, `hidden` removed, opacity 1 |

Cause: the scroll lock from the 2026-07-24 audit, `document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden'`. The `overflow` **shorthand** also sets `overflow-x`, and `globals.css:173-188` already documents what that does here — *"`overflow-x: hidden` forces overflow-y to compute to `auto`, turning `<html>`/`<body>` into a scroll container — which defeats `position: sticky`"*. Those rules deliberately use `clip`; this line undid it at runtime.

`position: sticky` resolves against its nearest scrolling ancestor, so promoting `<body>` moved the header's scrollport from the viewport to the document. **At `scrollY 0` those are the same point** — which is exactly why it worked at the top and nowhere else.

Fix, both parts measured:

| lock, at scrollY 2200 | header `y` |
|---|---|
| none (control) | `0` |
| `html { overflow: hidden }` | `0` ✅ |
| `body { overflow: hidden }` (shipped today) | `-2200` ❌ |

Plus `scroller.stop()` — `overflow:hidden` is *not* a lock while Lenis is mounted; it scrolls programmatically. Measured: with the document element locked, a wheel gesture still went `2200 → 2499`.

5 new tests. Verified the guard bites: reverting the fix fails 4 of 5, while *"the menu does open"* stays green — correct, that part was never broken.

## 2. Bridge user-detail page unreadable on a phone

- Header put the identity block and the wide "View as (read-only, 15 min)" button on one row → identity column collapsed to ~150px, meta line broke into **four** lines, email truncated to `kcentenoglen…`. Now stacks below `sm`.
- Activity/error rows used `truncate` (⇒ `white-space: nowrap`) on **log lines**. The label already gets its own line via `basis-full`, so nowrap bought nothing and cost the whole message — clipped mid-word by `overflow-x: clip`, with no ellipsis to signal it. Now `break-words sm:truncate`.

`md`+ unchanged in both.

**Honest limit:** I could not get an authenticated Bridge session to re-measure the fixed page, so unlike (1) there is no before/after geometry. If it still scrolls sideways after this, there is a second cause this commit did not find.

## 3. The six RLS exposures verified against production, not migration source

The database was unreachable all night, so every security claim in the overnight mission was inferred from migration files. It came back at 13:43Z; I read it (read-only — `pg_policies`, `information_schema`, `count(*)`).

**All six are live and match source exactly.** Nothing had drifted, nothing had been quietly hotfixed. The three `baseball_messages` policies really do compare `cp.conversation_id` to itself in production, and their correctly-correlated twins really are present alongside them — which is the load-bearing assumption behind "apply the three `DROP POLICY` statements first" and had never been checked against the running database.

Two corrections the live read forced:

- **Nothing is exposed to `anon`.** All `authenticated`-only, so the bar is "any registered user", not "anyone on the internet". Still a real cross-tenant failure; the earlier write-up didn't distinguish them and a buyer's security reviewer would.
- `baseball_player_percentiles` has a second policy reading `FOR ALL USING (true)`. I nearly filed it as a write hole. It's `service_role`-only, which bypasses RLS anyway.

Measured blast radius: **80** messages, **35** players with email/phone/GPA/SAT/ACT, **13** join codes, **10** coach records — and **0** rows behind both the invitation and percentile policies, which drops those two from red to yellow.

Also closes the one item marked BLOCKED-on-reachability: `public_profile_mode`'s live default is `'unlisted'`, not the `'private'` the DDL declares, and all 13 teams are `unlisted` — so cross-org discovery is not zeroed. The feared impact was nil.

**No migration applied.** Read-only throughout.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` 0 errors · eslint clean · unit suite **876 files / 8,343 passed / 13 skipped / 0 failed**

body:
## Production impact

helmsportslabs.com stopped serving on 2026-07-29 — errors on **every route**, including the marketing pages and the login screen, which need no auth at all.

Vercel runtime errors for the window:

```
292x  Error [AuthRetryableFetchError]: The operation was aborted due to timeout
      route=/middleware   first=04:16Z  last=13:16Z   (nine hours)

926x  Error [TimeoutError]: The operation was aborted due to timeout
      routes=/middleware, /api/admin/log-event, /api/health
```

## Root cause

The **trigger** is upstream: the Supabase project has been returning Cloudflare **522** ("Connection timed out" — the edge reaches the origin, the origin never finishes) in flapping windows. Supabase's status page reports all systems operational, so this is project-specific, not a platform incident.

But a degraded auth server should not be able to take the site down — that is precisely what `getUserResilient` exists to prevent. It had a hole in its last line:

```ts
const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
```

`getSession()` is documented as a local cookie read, but supabase-js attempts a token **refresh** when the stored access token has expired — and a refresh is a network call to the very auth server we've already established is unreachable. That call was not wrapped, so **the final step of the degraded fallback could throw the precise error the fallback exists to absorb.**

Middleware runs in front of every request, so the escaping `AuthRetryableFetchError` became a 500 on everything. The safety net shared the failure mode of the thing it was protecting. The Vercel stack shows it escaping through two frames of `getUserResilient` straight out of the middleware entry point.

## Fix

Wrap the fallback `getSession()` and treat an unreadable session as "no session".

Strictly better than a total outage, and not a security relaxation: returning null only ever **denies** access. `degraded: false` is deliberate — we could not read a session at all, so there is no local identity to carry forward and callers must not be told there is one.

The site now serves public routes normally during an auth outage, and authenticated routes fail closed instead of failing the entire origin.

## Tests

Two regression cases covering the fallback throwing both an `AuthRetryableFetchError` and a plain `TypeError`.

**Both were verified to fail against the pre-fix code** — 18 passed / 2 failed before, 20/20 after. A test that passes either way would be worthless here.

`tsc --noEmit` 0 errors, `eslint` clean, `src/lib/auth` suite 29/29.

## Still outstanding

This stops the hard failure; **it does not make Supabase healthy.** While the project 522s, authenticated surfaces cannot read data and users will be treated as signed out. The Supabase project itself needs attention — the flapping pattern (healthy for minutes, then ~20s timeouts across every endpoint including static ones) points at compute or connection saturation rather than a network issue.

Note CI cannot go green on this PR while Supabase is down, because the required `all` check depends on a Supabase-seeded smoke — see #1097, which hardens that path separately.

title: hotfix(auth): stop the degraded-auth fallback from taking the whole site down

body:
## What happened

On 2026-07-29 Supabase returned Cloudflare **522** ("Connection timed out" — the edge reached the origin, the origin never finished) three times inside half an hour:

| Time (UTC) | Where |
|---|---|
| 12:17 | **main** |
| 12:23 | PR #1095 |
| 12:41 | #1095 again, after a rerun |

Every run died in the same place: `Seed BaseballHelm CI accounts` → `scripts/seed-baseball-demo.ts` → the first `supabase.auth.admin.createUser`, which throws on its first error **with no retry of any kind**.

That step gates the BaseballHelm authenticated smoke, which feeds the `all` aggregate — one of main's three required status checks. So a ten-second upstream hiccup became a **repo-wide merge freeze**, and main stayed red long after the outage had passed. Supabase measured healthy again by 12:52 (12/12 requests, 100–250ms, zero timeouts).

It was also undiagnosable. A 522 body is Cloudflare's HTML, not JSON, so supabase-js surfaced an error with no usable message and the log read literally:

```
createUser failed for demo-coach@baseballhelmdemo.com: {}
```

## The fix

`scripts/lib/retrying-fetch.ts` — a drop-in `fetch` wrapper passed to `createClient` via `global.fetch`.

Retrying at the **fetch layer** rather than at the six call sites is deliberate: one wrapper covers every request the client makes (auth admin, PostgREST, storage), including any added later, and it can't be forgotten at a new call site.

- retries `408/425/429/5xx` and the whole Cloudflare `52x` family
- 750ms → 1.5s → 3s → 6s over 5 attempts, ~11s of cover
- **does not retry 4xx.** "Already registered", a bad service key, a schema violation — these are real answers, and retrying them only makes a genuine failure take four times as long to surface
- on exhaustion returns the transient **response**, not a synthetic error, so the log reports the true status
- `describeFetchError` renders the contentless `{}` case, so the next occurrence says what happened

`ensureAuthUser` is now idempotent against its own retry. A 522 fails the *response*, not necessarily the write — the origin can create the user and then time out answering. The replay then comes back "already registered", which for a seed is success wearing a failure's clothes, so it re-resolves the row rather than failing a required check over our own retry.

## Tests

`scripts/lib/__tests__/retrying-fetch.test.ts` — 9 cases covering the exact incident:

- two 522s then recovery → asserts 3 calls and 750/1500 backoff
- 4xx returned immediately, zero sleeps
- network throws (`socket hang up`, `ECONNRESET`) retried
- exhaustion returns the true status (503), not an invented error
- rethrow of the original error when every attempt throws
- the full transient / non-transient status split

Sleeps are injected so the suite doesn't spend the real ~11s.

Wired into the `unit` project **explicitly**, matching the existing precedent in `vitest.config.ts` — there's deliberately no `scripts/**` glob, because the 46 legacy files under `scripts/__tests__/` are written for `node --test`.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` 0 errors, `eslint` clean, **9/9 new tests passing**.

Note this PR can't prove itself green until Supabase is stable, since it rides the same required check it's hardening. The reruns I triggered on main and #1095 after Supabase recovered are the immediate un-redding; this is the durable fix so the next blip doesn't do it again.

body:
Two of the findings from the sign-in → dashboard audit, both dashboard-side.

## 1. The layout blocked on a closed drawer

`(dashboard)/dashboard/layout.tsx` awaited the CoachHelm chat drawer's data in its body, directly in front of `{children}`:

```ts
const ctx = await resolveCoachChatContext(sb);
const pulse = await getProgramPulse(sb, ctx).catch(() => null);
```

`resolveCoachChatContext` is **six serial round trips** — `auth.getUser()` → `golf_coaches` → `resolveCoachTeamIdWithCookie` → `golf_teams` → `golf_team_members` → `golf_players`. `getProgramPulse` adds its own query wave on top, including a `golf_rounds` read capped at 400 rows.

A layout can't return until its own awaits settle, so the real dashboard couldn't render behind any of it — on **every** `/golf/dashboard/*` navigation, not just the one after sign-in.

None of it is first-paint content. `CoachHelmDrawer` mounts **closed** (`useState(false)`) — this is the data behind a button nobody has pressed.

It now streams in its own `<Suspense>` boundary, so the dashboard paints on its own schedule and the launcher appears when its data lands. `fallback={null}` because the drawer is a floating corner affordance, not a reserved region — a skeleton there would reserve a shape that never settles anywhere.

The only await left in the layout is `getGolfSessionProfile()`, which is `React.cache()`-wrapped and already called by the parent layout this request. A cache hit, not a query.

## 2. The same chain ran twice per request

`/golf/dashboard/intelligence` and `/golf/dashboard/coachhelm/chat` each resolved the chat context (and the pulse) **again** in the page, after the layout had already resolved it for the drawer. Two callers, one request, same answer, double the latency.

Adds request-scoped getters in a new `chat/request-cache.ts`. Note the shape — they take **no arguments** and build their own client:

> `cache(resolveCoachChatContext)` does not work. `React.cache` keys on arguments, that function takes a Supabase client, and `createClient()` is not itself cached — so every call site constructs a fresh client identity and misses the cache every time. A zero-arg `cache()` is a guaranteed hit for the rest of the render pass: deduplicated within one request, never shared across requests or users.

Behavior is preserved at every call site. `getCoachChatContext` still throws `CoachContextError` (the chat page's redirect is unchanged); `getCoachProgramPulse` returns `null` on failure, matching the existing degrade-don't-fail contract, and the intelligence page converts that `null` back into its existing `command = null` path.

## On the third finding — the prefetch

The audit flagged `router.prefetch(href)` as `AUTO`-kind (warming only to the loading boundary) and called a `PrefetchKind.FULL` upgrade a one-line omission. **The fetch-strategy half is right; the conclusion isn't**, and I did not ship it:

- the golf dashboard is `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`
- Next's `experimental.staleTimes.dynamic` defaults to **0** (`node_modules/next/dist/server/config-shared.js:242`), and `next.config.mjs` does not override it

So a full prefetch would be cached with a stale time of zero, be stale the instant it landed, and be re-fetched from scratch on navigation anyway. The only thing purchased would be a second complete server render of the dashboard — roughly a dozen extra DB round trips per sign-in — thrown away.

Making it pay off means raising `staleTimes.dynamic` app-wide, trading data freshness on every dynamic route in every product for this one hand-off. That's a product call, not a hook detail. It's documented at the call site (on #1093) so it doesn't get "fixed" into a regression.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors, `eslint` clean
- **Full unit suite: 870 files / 8237 tests passing**
- Changed routes compile and respond

**Not verified end-to-end in a browser**: the demo coach account is sitting in the shared `login_attempts` lockout and the Supabase MCP was timing out, so I couldn't hold a session to confirm the drawer still mounts on a live dashboard. The change is structural rather than logical, but that check is genuinely outstanding.

title: perf(golf): stop the chat drawer's data gating the dashboard render

body:
## The bug

A user on **full LTE bars** was served `offline.html` on helmsportslabs.com
and could not get past it. Every tap in the mobile menu appeared to do
nothing — they were all the same failure.

The service worker is registered `scope: '/'` from the **golf dashboard**
(`OfflineProvider`), so it controls the entire origin: marketing site,
BaseballHelm, auth pages. Only the golf dashboard ever asked for offline
support. Every other navigation fell through to `handleDynamicRequest`,
whose `catch` turned **any** single `fetch` rejection into a full-page
"No Connection" — no retry, no check of whether the device was actually
online, and a "Try Again" button that re-entered the same handler.

One transient blip and the site was gone until the user cleared Safari's
website data.

## The fix

1. **Navigations outside the golf dashboard are no longer intercepted at
   all.** A browser's own network-error page is recoverable and honest;
   ours asserted a false fact and dead-ended. Not intercepting beats
   intercepting and guessing wrong.
2. **`offline.html` is served only when `navigator.onLine === false`.**
   Online with a failed fetch is a transient error → rethrow and let the
   browser handle it. A cached copy of the requested page still wins over
   both.
3. **No fabricated responses.** The synthetic empty `404` for assets and
   the `503` for subresources are gone — an empty body reads as a
   *successful empty script*, a weaker signal than a network error, which
   gives `StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript` less to catch. Cross-origin
   requests are now skipped entirely.

**Golf's offline support is deliberately untouched** — `/golf/dashboard`
navigations still route through `handlePageRequest`, still cache, still
fall back when genuinely offline. A test asserts this so "stop
intercepting" cannot quietly become "delete the feature".

## Evidence

The worker had **no tests**, and it is the most dangerous file in the repo:
a bad one pins every client permanently, and you cannot push a fix to a
client that will not fetch. It has 10 now, driving the real handlers in a
`vm` context with a synthetic `self`.

Verified against the **shipped** worker rather than asserted — stashing this
change and re-running the new suite produces **5 failures** (marketing

body:
The screen between "Sign in" and the dashboard — `/golf/welcome`, the one that says **"Good morning, Coach ___"**.

## It could hang forever

The identity load was an un-caught async IIFE:

```ts
const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();  // throws
...
setReady(true);                                            // never runs
```

On a slow or flaky connection that rejects (`AuthRetryableFetchError: signal timed out`), so `ready` stayed false. **Both** the greeting and the Skip button were gated on `ready`, as was `useSequencedNavigation`'s `armed` — and every timer in that hook, including the 6s "failsafe" that exists for exactly this, is created inside `if (!armed) return`. So the failsafe could not fire either. A rejected promise is not a render error, so `error.tsx` never caught it.

**Stranded on an empty gradient with no text, no button, and no way out.** I hit this live.

Fixed by anchoring the navigation deadline to **mount** rather than identity resolution. That's safe because the destination is already known at mount in every real flow: `golf-sign-in-form.tsx` always passes `?next=`, and the sign-in action already resolved the role to build it. Identity now only supplies the *name* (cosmetic) and, in the no-`next` fallback, an admin destination — itself belt-and-braces, since `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` redirects admins anyway. The fetch can fail, time out, or never return and the user still lands on time. It's wrapped in try/catch regardless, and Skip renders from the first frame.

## It showed nothing while it waited

The greeting rendered only after three Supabase round-trips. The time-of-day word comes off the **local clock** and needs no network — the screen was blank for no reason. It's now in the first painted byte (verified in the SSR HTML).

The `users.role` query was also a wasted serial hop: its only consumer is dead whenever `?next=` is present, which is every real sign-in. Now conditional.

## It was a design orphan

A hardcoded `#FFFEFA → #FFF7E0 → #FDEAC0` gradient, an inline `"DM Sans"` stack for a font this repo no longer loads, `#1c1917` ink, and a Skip button on retired `cream-100` / `stone-700` / `primary-600` tokens using the legacy `ui/button`.

Now `bg-canvas` + `bg-canvas-gradient` — the same wash AppShell paints — so the hand-off to the dashboard no longer changes the background at all. The greeting uses the same `font-fw-display` treatment as the dashboard's opener, so the sentence read here is the sentence waiting at the top of the dashboard.

Layout is **left-anchored on purpose**: the name arrives after the greeting does, and centred text would visibly slide when it lands. Line 2's height is reserved from first paint so the block never grows.

## Dark mode

The page had zero theme-aware values — a dark-mode user got a full-screen light-orange flash on every sign-in.

Switching to tokens isn't sufficient alone: `ThemeScript`'s path guard covered only `/golf/dashboard*`, so the tokens would have resolved **light** anyway and merely moved the flash. `/golf/welcome` is now in the guard. Verified: `main` resolves to `oklab(0.188 …)`, the dark `--fw-color-canvas`.

Because `router.replace` is a soft navigation, the `.dark` class would then survive onto `/golf/login` (only partly dark-capable — dark inputs on its light illustrated scene) in the signed-out bounce. That one exit cleans up after itself.

## loading.tsx

Rendered `FormPageSkeleton` — a 4-field form silhouette — before a screen that is one sentence and has no form. Same "different skeleton, then it switches back" class of flash. Now the page's own wash.

## Also fixed

- **Skip didn't disarm the sequence.** Harmless while arming was gated behind a slow fetch; not harmless once it arms at mount — the failsafe's hard `window.location.replace` would fire seconds later on whatever page the user had since reached. The hook now returns `cancel()` and Skip calls it.
- **Skip's exit timer had no handle** and fired after unmount.
- **The "Coach Coach" guard failed in exactly the case its own comment named**: a single-word `full_name` of `"Coach"` (last === first === "Coach"). Re-testing the chosen suffix catches both shapes. A `full_name` that sanitises to nothing now falls through to a complete sentence instead of the bare title — the literal **"Coach blank"**.
- **Reduced motion had the shortest escape window** (900ms), handing the users most likely to need Skip the least time to find it. Now 1400ms, legible from frame one since there's no fade to wait through.
- **The entrance ate the screen's life**: 140ms delay + 700ms fade on a screen that only lives 1900ms left ~800ms of fully-legible text. Now 60/450 → ~1.1s legible.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` 0 errors, `eslint` clean on all four files. Verified in-browser at 1440×900 and 402×874 in both themes, with **zero page errors**: greeting present in SSR HTML and on first paint, one line at both sizes, dark canvas resolving to the correct token, and the `.dark` cleanup confirmed on the signed-out bounce.

Not verified: the *named* state ("Good morning," / "Coach Edwards.") — the demo account tripped the shared `login_attempts` lockout during testing and the Supabase MCP was timing out, so I couldn't hold a session. The name path is covered by the logic above but hasn't been photographed.

Findings came from a 58-agent audit of the sign-in → welcome → dashboard chain; 65 defects surfaced, and the ones this PR doesn't address (the dashboard layout's ~7 serial chat-context round-trips, and `router.prefetch` only warming to the loading boundary) are dashboard-side and left for a separate change.

**Draft.** Opened primarily so CI executes SQL that has never been run — see "The one thing to do first" below.

## The headline

Two live cross-tenant data exposures in production, confirmed from migration source and unreplaced by any later migration:

```sql
-- supabase/migrations/20260527000000_prod_public_baseline.sql:18179
CREATE POLICY "baseball_players_select" ON public.baseball_players
  FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true);
-- :18377
CREATE POLICY "baseball_teams_select" ON public.baseball_teams
  FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true);
```

Any authenticated user on any team can read every other program's full roster — email, phone, GPA, SAT/ACT — and every team's `join_code`, the secret that gates membership. Live since 2026-05-27.

**Nothing in this PR has been applied to any database.** The fix is authored as files, in a sequence a human applies deliberately.

## The one thing to do first

The SQL in this PR has never been parsed by any Postgres. Everything here is static review.

CI's `supabase` job builds a fresh local stack from all migrations and runs every pgTAP suite in `supabase/tests/rls/`. **That is the first real correctness gate — read it before reading the diff.** It will catch plpgsql syntax errors, function-overload ambiguity, and RLS evaluation-order surprises that no amount of reading will.

## Applying the RLS fix (do not skip a step)

| Step | What | Blast radius |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Apply `20260729000100_..._a_additive.sql` | **None.** Five `CREATE FUNCTION`s + `GRANT EXECUTE`. No policy, no revoke, no `ALTER`. Cannot change the result of any existing query. |
| 2 | Deploy this branch | Works under both the old and new policies. |
| 3 | Apply `20260729000200_..._b_policies.sql` | Swaps the two policies. **The leak closes here.** |

Step 3 before step 2 is an outage: join-by-code, cross-org browse, and roster "Add existing player" all fail as **empty results, not errors**, so the symptom is "the product quietly stopped working."

Verify step 2 by **exercising** the flows, not by reading the diff — a merged-but-undeployed change looks identical in git and fails identically to no change at all:
- Join a team by code as a non-member, and confirm the pending-approval screen still names the team.
- Search a transfer's full email in roster "Add existing player" and confirm the exact-email result appears.

`db-migration-reviewer` is mandated by CLAUDE.md for this. It is the shared Golf + Baseball production database.

## Recruiting is sunset

Preserved, not deleted. `src/lib/baseball/product-modules.ts` is a one-line switch, and every test that asserted pre-sunset behaviour was **kept** and re-run under a mock-enabled module rather than flipped — so restoration has live coverage instead of being an archaeology project.

Closed at every layer: navigation, hub resolution, server route guards, middleware, and the one surface reachable with no session at all — the public `/baseball/packet/<token>` share link, which was still serving a high-school player's measurables and video to anyone holding an old URL.

`/team/[id]`, `/program/[id]` and `/player/[id]` stay public. A player's own profile is not a recruiting artifact the way a scout packet is; gating it removes a feature we still sell.

## Also fixed

- **"Sync Athletes" reported success while inserting nothing** — every call passed `p_org_id`, a parameter the RPC does not have, and the error was never read. Assigning a team now also seeds its athletes, which the doc comment had claimed for months without it being true.
- **Cutting a player never deactivated their Lift Lab athlete row.** Nothing was going to converge: the sync RPC is `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so it can add an athlete but never deactivate one. Deactivate, never delete — their lifting history is the program's record of work done.
- **Three bottom bars silently rendered 3 tabs instead of 4** after the sunset, because an unresolvable nav key is dropped by `.filter(Boolean)`.

## One P0 retracted

Recon reported the staff-invite accept RPC had no email-ownership check. **It was wrong** — the check is present at three layers and always has been. Recorded as a retraction rather than deleted, and pinned by a test: a P0 that turns out not to exist means the recon pass produced at least one false positive at the highest severity, so its other findings deserve the same read-the-source treatment.

## Known and not fixed

- `baseball_teams_public_profile` filters `public_profile_mode <> 'private'`. The column's DDL default is `'private'` (`20260624000091:23`) while a 2026-07-09 live read recorded `'unlisted'`. If the DDL is what is live, that filter is default-**deny**. Recruiting is sunset so impact today is zero. Settle with `select public_profile_mode, count(*) from baseball_teams group by 1` before recruiting returns — Supabase MCP timed out on every attempt.
- Postgres RLS is row-level. Once the recruiting predicate admits a row, every column is readable, including PII the UI never shows.
- `baseball_team_invitations` has the same unaudited `.eq('code', code)` shape.

Full state, including what is complete versus improved-but-incomplete, is in `docs/baseballhelm-overnight/`.

## The shell/skeleton flip — root cause

`src/app/golf/loading.tsx` rendered the legacy `GenericPageSkeleton`.

A `loading.tsx` inside a segment sits **inside** that segment's own layout (layout → Suspense → page), so it cannot cover its own layout's `await`. The boundary that covers an async layout is the one in the **parent** segment. `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` is async and does real work before it renders anything — `getGolfSessionProfile()`, the active-team cookie, `resolveCoachActiveTeamId`, `getCoachTeamSwitchContext`, plus a deliberate 300ms sleep on the post-onboarding path. For that entire window the only boundary above it was `golf/loading.tsx`.

So one load of `/golf/dashboard` painted three different frames:

1. legacy generic skeleton — no rail, no top bar, `max-w-5xl`, retired `surface-matte` / `cream-100` / `warm-200` tokens
2. the real Fairway shell + `FairwayDashboardSkeleton`
3. the real dashboard

Step 1 → 2 is the reported *"it renders a different shell and then switches back"*. Both files inside `(dashboard)/` were already correct — which is why this kept getting missed. The offending file neither lives in nor looks like it belongs to the dashboard.

### Fix

Adds `FairwayShellSkeleton`: the app-shell silhouette (dark rail with the real brand lockup, glass top bar, `md:pl-[260px]` content column). Every number is read from the live chrome, not eyeballed — 260px matches AppShell's expanded `railOffset`, which is also what the real shell first paints, since it seeds `collapsed` to `false` and only reads localStorage in an effect.

`golf/loading.tsx` now renders that around the same `FairwayDashboardSkeleton` the next boundary shows, so the hand-off changes what is *inside* the chrome and never the chrome itself.

**Verified on an authenticated load.** The streamed document contains the silhouette (`bg-nav-surface/70` ×14 — its 7 rail rows) and **zero** occurrences of `skeleton-shimmer`, `surface-matte`, or `max-w-5xl`.

## The `<h1>` rewriting itself after paint

Both dashboards derived the greeting in a `useEffect` seeded with a time-neutral "Welcome back", on the stated grounds that SSR would have to guess the coach's clock. It does not have to: the payload already carries the team timezone (`golf_team_settings.timezone`, defaulted by `dashboard-data.ts`, so always a real zone) — the same value the effect was reaching for. The largest text on the page rewrote itself a beat after first paint, on every single load.

The phrase and the date label are now resolved server-side in `resolveOpener()` and passed down. The effects remain as fallbacks for callers that don't wire the props, and no longer write state when the server has settled it.

## The opener

- **eyebrow** was the literal string "Coach Dashboard" — a label the top bar already carries. It now carries the date, in the team's timezone.
- **description** was a `·`-joined dump of team name and two counts. The name is the description; the counts are `meta` chips with icons and tabular figures.
- The opener sits on the warm `surface-tint` **plinth** (DESIGN-SYSTEM §4.1, one per large-title page) instead of floating as one more flat text block. Applied to both dashboards — they share one pre-role skeleton, so their mastheads have to agree on geometry.
- The founder's **green rule is preserved exactly**, as the `border-t` of the window row it was introducing rather than a free-floating `h-px` sibling. One fewer stacked band before any content.
- **`disableAnimation`**: ViewHeader's default entrance is opacity-0 → 1 / y-8 → 0. A shape-matched skeleton paints that silhouette immediately before it, so animating in from nothing drops settled text 8px away from where the placeholder just sat. That *is* the flicker.

`FairwayDashboardSkeleton`'s masthead is rebuilt against the plinth's real classes, so the resolved header lands on those pixels rather than near them.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors
- `eslint` on all changed files: clean
- Dashboard + Fairway unit tests: 9/10 files pass. The one failure (`settings-coaching-intelligence`, a 5s timeout under parallel load) **reproduces identically on baseline with these changes fully removed** — pre-existing flake, not from this PR.
- Rendered and screenshotted at 1440×900 and 402×874, signed in as a real coach account.

body:
## Why

The Bridge had two axes for an incident — `event_type` and `severity` — and neither answers the question `/admin/errors` exists to answer: **is this a bug I have to do something about?**

Measured against production: **2,321 of 2,728 July error rows (85%) are not bugs.** The top "unresolved incident" was `insights.triggerPlayerInsightsAfterRound.gateMetrics` at 575 unresolved — routine threshold telemetry. Another 129 rows were `Integrity PASS`: checks that *passed*, filed as errors and left open forever. Real defects (`documents.handleError … [object Object]`, React #310, a `column … does not exist` query failure) ranked below all of it.

## What

**A kind axis, orthogonal to severity** (`src/lib/admin/incident-classification.ts`).

Computed at **read time**: no migration, no backfill, applies retroactively to ~93k historical rows, and a wrong rule changes only a derived view rather than destructively rewriting anything. The Errors tab defaults to actionable, with a notice stating exactly what is held back, per class, each a link, plus "Show everything". Noise is defaulted out of view, never deleted.

Rules are pinned to real production titles. Running the classifier over the full corpus — not a sample — caught three misclassifications in the first draft: `Invalid email or password` as degradation, `Free tier users do not have access to this model` as access (it's a *billing* fault), and `ResizeObserver loop` noise as a defect. All three are now regression tests.

Unmatched errors default to a **visible defect** — new failures fail loud, never silent.

**Depth**
- `requestId` existed in schema and Sentry tagging for months with **zero** call sites passing it. Per-call-site was the design that already failed, so one AsyncLocalStorage scope opens in `withAdminObserved` — one edit, ~129 actions correlate every log line they emit.
- `error.cause` is now walked into the persisted stack. V8 stacks exclude the cause, so wrapped Supabase errors dropped their root cause from the Bridge's own tables. Sentry chained it natively, which is why this was invisible.
- Fingerprint detail: `firstSeen` was the oldest of a `.limit(100)` page, so any incident over 100 occurrences reported a recent timestamp as "first seen" **and fed that wrong start time into deploy attribution**.
- `savePartialRound` wrote 3–4 rows per failure (confirmed in prod: the same Lifting Lab error under two sources). Also fixes pre-existing over-logging of the conflict/already-completed returns the code's own comments say should stay silent.
- **Regression detection** for app-origin incidents. Compares against `firstSeen`, not `lastSeen` — the latter would flag an incident that has simply been open across a stale resolution. Two fingerprints currently qualify, one resolved at 07:31 and firing again by 21:23 the same day.
- **Dead integrations** now leave a durable trace. A Sentry 429 or expired `VERCEL_API_TOKEN` previously produced zero signal — only whoever was looking at that card during that render ever knew.
- **Sentry duplicate** removed: every boundary through `logError` produced two issues per crash. Suppression is scoped to console-origin events so the deliberate capture survives regardless of React's logging order.

**UI**
- Status banner tested `sentry.status === 'error'`, but `AdminFetchStatus` is tri-state — an *unconfigured* Sentry rendered "All systems nominal" while the Bridge was blind to it.
- Bulk resolve gets a confirm step: `resolve_admin_event` is the only writable mutation and there is no `unresolve` RPC anywhere.
- Fingerprint detail renders the rollup the data layer already computed then discarded, with honest labels (`lower bound`, `47 of 312`).

**Copy report** leads with classification, and warns explicitly when a message was degraded on capture so a reader does not try to debug from `[object Object]`.

## Verification

Typecheck 0 errors · lint clean · **847 test files / 8,053 tests passing** · production build succeeds · `actionlint` clean.

## Reviewer notes

- **`bridge-env` is not a required check.** New jobs aren't added to branch protection automatically, so it won't gate merges until you add it in repo settings — deliberately left to you. It runs in `--drift` mode: a no-op while none of the six secrets are provisioned (CI today), a hard failure the moment some are set and a sibling goes missing. Both branches verified.
- **Regression detection won't visibly fire yet.** Both currently-qualifying fingerprints are `access`-class, so the default filter still holds them back. Correct by design — a recurring expected-denial isn't a failed fix — but the badge stays invisible until a real defect regresses.
- **The incident signature was deliberately left alone.** It includes `severity`, which splits one bug across severities. Changing it would churn a durable key that is also the `[fingerprint]` route param, splitting every existing group at deploy — for a benefit the classifier already absorbs.
- **`~462 describeError() sites` remain.** Several live errors still log `[object Object]`; the report now flags them rather than fixing the call sites, which is separate work.
