## What

Players can now upload a **screenshot or photo** of their class schedule — previously the importer was PDF/TXT/paste only. The image is read by Claude vision through the Vercel AI Gateway, mapped into the existing `ParsedClass` shape, reviewed in the same ConfirmClassesModal, and auto-synced to the calendar through the existing save pipeline. Both surfaces get it (the Fairway classes page delegates modals to the legacy page, so there is one flow).

## How it reads "a variety of" real schedules

The extraction prompt was built from a survey of real SIS renderings (Workday, Banner 8/9, PeopleSoft classic + Fluid, Colleague/Student Planning, Populi/Jenzabar, schedule-builder apps, calendar-app week views), including the failure modes that actually cause misreads:

- **Day-pill trap**: portals that print all seven day letters for every class with only meeting days highlighted — read the highlighted state, never the letters.
- `R`/`H` = Thursday, `TR`/`TTh`/`TuTh` = Tue+Thu, `MoWeFr` compounds, spelled-out and slash-joined day names.
- Times: `9:05a`, `1400-1515`, legacy `905A`/`1215P`, `to`/en-dash separators; bare `12:00` = noon with lowered confidence; credit hours (`3.000`, `1.00-4.00`) and 5-digit CRNs are never times.
- Lecture + linked lab/recitation = separate entries; A/B half-term duplicates kept distinct; cross-listed codes = one entry; busy-blocks and final-exam-only blocks excluded; `Staff`/`TBA` instructor and ARR/online day-less rows preserved as valid.
- Weekly grids: same course's blocks merged into one entry; truncated titles transcribed verbatim.
- Non-schedule uploads (tuition bill, degree audit…) are refused with a message saying what the image actually is.

## Client behavior

- Accepts PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF; iOS transcodes HEIC at pick time (accept list excludes it), Safari-dragged HEIC decodes via canvas.
- Downscales/re-encodes client-side (bakes EXIF rotation, keeps payloads small).
- **Tall scrolling captures** (aspect > 2.4) are sliced into ≤6 overlapping segments the model is told to merge/dedupe.
- Extraction warnings (cropped rows, low-confidence times, half-term notes) surface as toasts going into the confirm step; malformed times degrade to blank fields the player fills in rather than dropped classes.

## Safety / plumbing

- Server action is auth-first with media-type and size backstops, and logs failures to Helm Bridge (`academics_classes`) — observability coverage-contract test passes.
- ConfirmClassesModal gains Sat/Sun chips so weekend classes are visible during review; `calendar-sync getDayOfWeek` now maps `Sa`/`Su` (`in` check because Sunday is 0).
- `src/types/ai-shim.d.ts` now declares `generateObject` (the ambient shim replaces the `ai` package types and must cover every surface used).
- Model: `anthropic/claude-opus-4.8` (gateway slug uses a dot, per Vercel's changelog); `SCHEDULE_VISION_MODEL` env var is the override hatch.

## Gates

- typecheck ✅ · eslint + lint:ratchet ✅ · unit tests ✅ (new schedule-vision suite + observability contract) · production build ✅

## What

Two audit findings from the Full Product Audit Swarm, integrated together.

### 1. One canonical coach "needs you" attention count (the deepest finding)

The coach dashboard told three different stories about what needed the coach:

- the hero counted `actionItems.length` (tasks **+ announcements**) and its copy claimed "approvals" it never counted;
- pending roster join-request approvals were counted by nothing;
- announcements (which have no accept/resolve step) inflated the "waiting on you" total as if they were backlog.

New pure `attention-queue.ts` derives **one** honest count from data the dashboard already holds (no new query, no RLS change): `total = actionable tasks + pending approvals`, announcements excluded. Wired through every surface:

- **Hero** (`coach-signal.ts`): the number is the canonical total — approvals are finally counted, so the "approvals" copy is now true — and the body names only the parts that exist ("3 tasks and 2 approvals flagged from your roster this week.").
- **Action Items panel**: badge counts actionable work only; announcements move to a clearly labelled, separately counted strip and never inflate the backlog. Row markup extracted to a shared `ActionItemRow`.
- Approvals keep their dedicated banner (the act-now affordance); Signals and Team Pulse keep their own genuinely-different metrics.

### 2. Course-scoping: hide create/edit/delete controls from players (owner decision: "keep library open, hide player edit")

Players could browse the shared course library (intended) but four mutation controls leaked to player sessions: the library "+ Add course" button and empty-state CTA, plus (on non-library courses) "Edit course", photo upload/replace/remove, "Add tee", and the per-tee "Edit" button. All now gate on the existing `canManageTeam` boolean the server page already resolves from session role. Pure UI role-gate, no RLS/server-action change; same conditional path serves desktop and mobile.

body:
Fixes the five phone screenshots from the owner report (2026-07-18): unreadable "Who's contributing" drill-down, Action Items running past the screen edge, Signals toolbar bleed-through + clipped pills, evidence labels wrapping one word per line, and the full-viewport dashboard hero.

## The real bug behind the screenshots

**Every ModalShell dialog was collapsed on iPhone.** The panel is `h-fit`; its body was `flex-1` (percentage flex-basis). iOS Safari resolves that percentage against the intrinsic-keyword height as **0**, so the body rendered ~0px tall — title + a clipped sliver of content + footer. Desktop engines size it from content, which is why QA never saw it. The screenshots' clipped chip strip is exactly this. Fixed at the primitive (`flex-auto min-h-0`) in **both** `ModalShell.Body` and `Sheet.Body` — so the drill-down's Sheet conversion doesn't re-ship the same collapse, and every other dialog (create task, event editor, invite player, penalty, travel, focus area…) is unbroken on iOS in one edit.

## Per-surface

## Context

Full CRM + Bridge wiring audit (37 parallel auditors, every non-wired finding adversarially verified). Most integrations are correctly wired; this PR fixes the three findings that are **code bugs** (env-var gaps are listed at the bottom for Nick — they need dashboard access).

## Fixes

**1. Demo-request → CRM coach row silently never created** (`src/app/actions/demo-request.ts`)
The landing-page action inserted into `crm_coaches` under the *anonymous visitor session*, but that table's only INSERT policy is admin-only — the insert RLS-failed on every genuine submission and the error was never checked. The promised "admin can follow up from the CRM" row never existed. Now: service-role client, error-checked, Bridge-logged, and never fails the visitor flow.

**2. Zero notification on new demo requests**
A hot lead sat invisible until someone opened the CRM Inbound Leads tab. Now:
- Instant ops alert email on each submission via the dedicated `OPS_DIGEST_*` transport (production-only, fail-soft skip when unconfigured) — new `sendOpsAlert()` in `src/lib/admin/digest/transport.ts`, with `sendOpsDigest` delegating to it.
- Daily admin digest gains a demo-requests section + a **red item** while any request is `pending` — it nags until the lead is moved out of pending in the CRM.

**3. Root `middleware.ts` was dead code — prod failed OPEN on Supabase misconfig**
With `appDir` at `src/app`, Next's middleware/proxy detection scans `src/` only, so repo-root `middleware.ts` (fail-closed 500 + Sentry fatal on missing `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_*`) was never compiled; the live `src/proxy.ts` failed open on *every* error. The fail-closed contract + transient-error Sentry capture are now ported into `src/proxy.ts`; the dead file is deleted; the lock-in test moved to `src/test/proxy-middleware.test.ts` (with an added stale-refresh-token no-capture case). Native-UA redirect, dev bypass, refresh-token downgrade, and the INTERNAL_LOG_KEY Bridge relay are all unchanged.

Three narrowly-scoped inline `nosemgrep` waivers on the intentionally-anonymous public action (with justifications) — the file-level rule stays armed; verified with a must-fire canary.

## Gates
typecheck ✓ · eslint ✓ · semgrep + canary ✓ · 5401 unit tests ✓ · prod build ✓

## Needs Nick (not in this PR — Vercel dashboard)
- `RESEND_API_KEY` absent in prod → **all** transactional email dark (coach digest, task/event reminders, weekly email, 8 notification types, CRM sends, lifting invites). Setting it turns real user email ON — deliberate decision.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` absent in prod → Sentry SDK is a silent no-op in production (value exists in `.env.production.local`).
- `DEMO_COACH_EMAIL=demo@golfhelmdemo.com` absent → public golf demo gate tells every visitor the demo is unavailable.

## Lane 12 — team-ops-today + colleges-catalog + devplans

Part of the visual-audit fix fleet (see `scratchpad/fix-spec.md`). Three
independently-verified fixes; one finding deferred due to file-ownership
conflict with another lane.

### 1. Calendar "N upcoming events" — timezone bug [BROKEN]
**Note:** `coach-team-ops.md`

`calendar/page.tsx` computed `startOfToday` from
`new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate())` — the SERVER
RUNTIME's own local date. Vercel serverless functions run in UTC, so in the
evening Eastern hours (after ~8pm ET) this silently promoted tomorrow (UTC)
to "today," excluding the team's own still-today events from both the
headline count and the per-type badges. Reproduced exactly in the audit
screenshots (captured ~10:42pm ET, app showed "Today NOW · July 16" when the
real day was July 15).

**Fix:** extracted the boundary computation into a pure, unit-tested
`computeUpcomingEventsSummary()` (`src/lib/baseball/calendar/upcoming-events.ts`)
and wired it through the existing Daily Contract
`resolveTeamTimezone()`/`todayIsoInTz()`/`localDayBoundsUtc()` utilities
(`src/lib/baseball/daily-contract/contract-day.ts`) instead of the runtime's
own clock — the same Gap-1 fix already applied to lifting.

**Evidence:** `src/lib/baseball/calendar/__tests__/upcoming-events.test.ts`
reproduces the exact repro instant (`2026-07-16T02:42:00.000Z` = 10:42pm ET
July 15) and asserts a team-local evening event now counts as "upcoming"
instead of being silently dropped.

**Note on scope:** the audit also flagged a client-side manifestation in
`CalendarDayViewSwipeable.tsx` ("Today NOW" badge / "Your {weekday} is free").
That component's `currentDate` state is owned entirely by
`PremiumCalendarClient.tsx` (Lane 10's file — `useState(() => new Date())`),
so wiring a team-tz-aware "today" into it would require editing a file Lane
10 owns. Left untouched per the disjoint-file-ownership rule; flagging for
the orchestrator to route to Lane 10 or a follow-up. (This is also a browser-
local-clock-vs-team-tz question, not purely a bug — a real coach's own
device clock is normally correct; the observed symptom is amplified by the
CI screenshot runner's UTC system clock.)

### 2. Discover Colleges catalog — seed/E2E/QA fixture data [DISHONEST]
**Note:** `player-journey-colleges.md`

`useColleges()`'s query filtered `organizations` only to `type = 'college'`,
with no exclusion of non-production rows — a real player's catalog was
majority (12 of 21 observed) test fixtures: "Codex Demo College", "Codex
Test College", "Demo University Golf" (and a near-duplicate), "E2E Test
University", "QA Test University", "UI Test College 179805…", and a college
literally named "Yes" located in "Yes, YA" ("YA" isn't a real US state).

**Fix:** `organizations` has no `is_test`/`source` column, so
`src/hooks/use-colleges.ts` now combines two independently-defensible
signals — (1) name/conference matches a known seed/E2E/QA naming convention,
(2) `location_state` isn't a real US state/DC/territory code (catches "Yes,
YA", the one fixture with an otherwise-unremarkable name) — applied
consistently across `useColleges`/`useStates`/`useConferences` so the filter
dropdowns never offer a fixture-only option either. Zero DB writes; fully
reversible; exported predicates (`isNonProductionOrgName`,
`isInvalidUsStateCode`, `isNonProductionOrg`) for testability.

**Evidence:** `src/hooks/__tests__/use-colleges.test.ts` — unit tests every
fixture name/state from the audit plus every real program named in the note
(Denison, Guilford, Hampden-Sydney, Lenoir-Rhyne, Methodist, Piedmont,
University of Lynchburg, Rini University), plus an integration test against
`useColleges()` itself with a mixed fixture+real result set.

**Note on scope:** the note also flagged (a) no `player_type` gate on the
Recruiting hub and (b) the Journey KPI strip's missing `researching`/
`committed` buckets — both explicitly owned by Lane 6
(`use-journey.ts`/`JourneyClient.tsx`/the player_type gate file) per the
fix-spec. Not touched here.

### 3. Development Plans card — badge/button layout [DESIGN]
**Note:** `coach-devplans-performance-videos.md` (§005)

Two reproducible mobile-composition defects on the "in progress" plan card:
- A long title wrapping to 4 lines centered the status badge against the
  whole block (`items-center`), so it visually landed beside a middle line
  instead of labeling the card.
- The "View Plan" link had no `shrink-0` guard; the sibling title/badge
  column could squeeze it below its own text's intrinsic width, and
  `Button`'s base classes (`whitespace-nowrap overflow-hidden`) hard-clipped
  the label to "View" with no ellipsis — real content loss, not just a
  visual nit.

**Fix:** `items-start` (badge now pins to the title's first line regardless
of wrap count) + `shrink-0` on the action `Link`.

**Evidence:** `DevPlansClient.test.tsx` — jsdom has no real layout engine, so
this asserts the specific Tailwind classes that produce the correct
behavior in a real browser (matches the repo's existing `toHaveClass` idiom
in `src/components/ui/select.test.tsx`), documented inline in the test file.

**Deferred (file-ownership conflict, noted for orchestrator):** the note's
[BROKEN]/[DISHONEST] Performance Command Center findings — `due_date` never
compared against "today" for an overdue sweep, and "Today's lift"/"Upcoming"
batch titles reading 11-14 days stale — require editing
`PerformanceDashboardClient.tsx`'s Recent Assignments render, which Lane 3
owns (for its ClimbArc/TrendChart caller-prop work). Not touched here; the
Videos page (§016) had no issues to fix ("[OK]").

## Lane 10 — player-affordance-leaks

Two BROKEN role/data-safety findings from the visual-audit fix spec (`player-player-comms-docs.md`).

### (a) Player sees a live "+ Add Event" CTA on the desktop calendar

**Evidence**: `PremiumCalendarClient.tsx:1153` built the desktop `CalendarHeader` with `onAddEvent={handleAddEvent}` **unconditionally**. Every other call site in the same file already gates on role — mobile day view (`:1249` `onAddEvent={isCoach ? handleAddEvent : undefined}`) and the mobile FAB (`:1444` `{showMobileUI && isCoach && (...)}`) — only the desktop header didn't. `CalendarHeader`'s underlying `PageHeader` (`variant="calendar"`) renders the "Add Event" pill whenever `onAddEvent` is truthy and `!isMobile`, so on desktop every viewer — including players — saw a live, primary-styled "create event" button. The server action is correctly capability-gated (`createBaseballEvent`/`createGolfEvent` → `requireBaseballCapability(..., 'can_manage_calendar')`), so this was never a privilege-escalation bug, but it's exactly the "coach-only affordance leaking to a player" failure mode: a player who fills out the modal hits a capability error after already investing the effort.

**Fix**: `onAddEvent={isCoach ? handleAddEvent : undefined}` — matches the pattern already used everywhere else in the file.

**Test**: `src/components/golf/calendar/__tests__/PremiumCalendarClient.player-add-event-gating.test.tsx` renders the **real** `PremiumCalendarClient` → real `CalendarHeader` → real `PageHeader` (only the heavy neighbors — `NotificationCenter`, `CalendarAvatarSidebar`, dynamic view chunks, range-fetch/RSVP hooks — are stubbed), and asserts the "Add Event" button is present for `isCoach=true` and **absent** for `isCoach=false`. Verified the test fails (8/8 assertions) when the fix is reverted.

### (b) CollegeProfileEditor: blank First/Last Name inputs — real data-loss risk, not a paint artifact

**Evidence**: the audit flagged First/Last Name inputs rendering empty despite the completion-checklist arithmetic on the *same render* proving those fields are populated (62% = 8/13, and City/State — not First/Last — are the first two "missing" fields listed). I traced the actual mechanism rather than guessing:

- `formData` is seeded **once** at mount via `useState<Partial<Player>>(player)` (`CollegeProfileEditor.tsx:133`), with no effect to resync it if `player` later becomes more complete.
- `use-baseball-auth.ts`'s `reconcileStore()` (a separate, lightweight route-guard reconciliation shared via the same Zustand auth store `useAuth()` reads from) can write a **partial** player object — `{id, onboarding_completed, player_type}` only — into the store ahead of `useAuth()`'s own full-row (`select('*')`) fetch resolving.
- If `CollegeProfileEditor` first mounts against that partial snapshot, `formData.first_name`/`last_name` are `undefined` forever after — even once the store is later replaced with the complete row — because nothing ever re-seeds `formData`. The Inputs (bound to `formData.first_name || ''`) render empty while `{...player, ...formData}` (used only for the completion calculation, where `player` is the CURRENT, now-complete prop) correctly shows the name as filled — exactly reproducing the audit's observation.
- **Real risk**: `handleSave` sends the whole `formData` object to `onUpdate()` → `updatePlayer()` (`use-auth.ts`), and `first_name`/`last_name` are **not** in `PLAYER_UPDATE_DENYLIST`. A player who opens this tab and hits Save without retyping their name risks the update either omitting the name entirely or — in an adjacent code path — sending an explicit empty string.

**Fix (defense in depth, both ends)**:
1. `CollegeProfileEditor.tsx` — added a resync effect that backfills any `formData` field still strictly `undefined` whenever a fresher `player` prop arrives. It can never overwrite a field the player has already touched (even cleared to `''`), only fill in fields that were never set.
2. `use-auth.ts` `updatePlayer()` — defensive guard: if an incoming update would set `first_name`/`last_name` to `''` while the player's on-record name is already non-empty, that specific field is dropped from the write rather than applied. Belt-and-suspenders against this whole class of bug, not just this one call site.

**use-baseball-auth.ts** (the actual source of the partial player object written into the shared store) is **not in this lane's assigned file set** — flagging for the orchestrator as a systemic root cause. The two hardening fixes above make the *symptom* (blank inputs, possible name-loss) unreachable, but the underlying partial-object-into-shared-store pattern in `reconcileStore()` could resurface elsewhere with a different field.

**Tests**:
- `src/components/baseball/profile/__tests__/CollegeProfileEditor.formdata-resync.test.tsx` — renders with a partial player, asserts inputs are (honestly) empty, then rerenders with the full player and asserts the inputs backfill; a second test proves an in-progress edit is never clobbered by the resync. Verified all 3 tests fail without the effect.
- `src/hooks/__tests__/use-auth-update-player-denylist.test.ts` — new `describe` block: drops an empty-string name overwrite when the player has a real name on file, still allows a genuine name edit through, and still allows clearing a name that was already empty/null. Verified the first two assertions fail without the guard.

## Gates
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npx eslint --max-warnings 0 <touched files>` — clean
- `npx vitest run <affected + new>` — 48/48 passing (all 4 test projects: unit/rls/business/integration), plus 56/56 on other `PremiumCalendarClient` consumers (`BaseballCalendarWrapper.rsvp-routing`, `CalendarFairway.shell-height`) to confirm no regression there
- `node scripts/check-cycles.mjs` — OK, 33 known cycles, none new

6 files touched (well under the 15-file cap): `PremiumCalendarClient.tsx`, `CollegeProfileEditor.tsx`, `use-auth.ts`, `use-auth-update-player-denylist.test.ts`, plus 2 new test files.

## Lane 2 — roster-mobile

Source: `scratchpad/notes/coach-roster-academics.md` (`/baseball/dashboard/roster` section), verified against `db-truth.json` and code before changing anything.

### (a) [BROKEN] Player name invisible on the 390px roster wall

**Root cause (verified in code, not just screenshots):** `PlayerRowPlate.tsx`'s name span used Tailwind's `truncate` (`overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis`) with no `min-width`. Per the CSS Flexbox spec, a flex item's "automatic minimum size" resolves to `0` once its computed `overflow` is anything but `visible` — so the name span's floor was 0, while its siblings (the jersey-number span and `PositionChip`, neither of which set `overflow`) kept their full content-based minimum. Under the width pressure of a 390px row (jersey + 2× fixed 80px stat columns + kebab menu), **all** the squeeze fell on the name, collapsing it to 0-1 characters — exactly the pattern the audit screenshots show (rows with a 2-char position chip render 0 chars of the name; rows with a 1-char chip render exactly 1).

**Fix:**
1. `PlayerRowPlate.tsx` — give the name span an explicit `min-w-[64px]` floor.
2. `RosterFairway.tsx` — the phone roster wall now hands `PlayerRowPlate` **one** stat column (OPS — the same column the desktop wall already crowns a team leader in) instead of two (AVG + OPS). Math check: with 2 full-width 80px stat columns retained, the ~390px row simply doesn't have 64px to spare for the name floor even after the CSS fix — it would either still collapse or overflow. Dropping to one column reliably leaves ~100px+ for the name across 360-390px viewports. AVG/OBP/SLG remain one tap away on the player detail page this row already opens (unchanged existing behavior).

### (b) [DISHONEST] Desktop "SESS" column

`agg.total_sessions` (`Math.max(legacy.total_sessions, boxScore.g)`, `legacy-stat-adapters.ts:219-220`) showed 14-22 per player sitting undisclosed beside four columns (AVG/OBP/SLG/OPS) that reconcile exactly with the team's real current-season box-score stats — but the team played only 8 games all season (`db-truth.json`). The legacy row-count virtually always wins the `Math.max`, so "SESS" reads as "games this season" and isn't.

Per the note's own guidance ("either drop SESS or relabel... pick the honest one"), I dropped the column rather than relabel — an honest caveat ("legacy lifetime count, not this season's games") doesn't fit legibly in a 4-letter, 80px header, and the column isn't part of the roster's core "identify + triage" job (AVG/OPS already are). Also removed the now-orphaned "Sessions" sort option (`RosterFairway.tsx`'s `SORT_OPTIONS`) so a coach can't sort by a figure nothing on screen shows anymore. `legacy-stat-adapters.ts` itself is untouched — its `Math.max` "honest floor" contract is legitimately documented and used elsewhere; the dishonesty was purely in this wall's presentation of it.

### Refactor (test seam)

Extracted `WALL_COLUMNS`/`buildWallStats`/`buildWallStatsMobile` out of `RosterFairway.tsx` into a new `roster-wall-stats.ts`, mirroring the existing `roster-constants.ts` split (same file, same stated rationale: avoid an import-cycle risk and make the pure logic directly unit-testable without pulling in `RosterFairway`'s much heavier component graph — `LineupBuilder`, `InviteModal`, `RosterMemberActions`, etc.).

### Not touched

- `PositionChip.tsx` — listed as an owned file but no change was needed; the fix addresses the actual root cause (the name span's automatic-min-size collapse) rather than the chip's sizing.
- `legacy-stat-adapters.ts` — read and verified as the source of the SESS figure per the note, but the honest fix is the presentation-layer change in `RosterFairway.tsx`; the adapter's own documented contract is unchanged and still covered by its existing test suite (`legacy-stat-adapters.test.ts`, re-run below, unaffected).

### Files changed (5, within the 15-file cap)

- `src/components/baseball/living-annual/molecules/PlayerRowPlate.tsx` — min-width fix
- `src/components/baseball/living-annual/molecules/PlayerRowPlate.test.tsx` — new
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/roster/RosterFairway.tsx` — mobile 1-stat, SESS drop, imports from new module
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/roster/roster-wall-stats.ts` — new (extracted)
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/roster/roster-wall-stats.test.ts` — new

Fixes for `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/discover` (coach recruiting
Discover page), scoped to `DiscoverView.tsx` and `SmartEmptyState.tsx` per
the fix spec. `DiscoverClient.tsx` was read for context but needed no
changes — its own curated `activeFilterCount` (lines 385-396) was already
correct; the bug was in the two downstream consumers duplicating that logic
incorrectly.

### (a) [BROKEN] dead stateCounts

`DiscoverView.tsx:610` (pre-fix) passed a hardcoded `stateCounts={{}}`
literal into `SmartEmptyState` instead of the real `playerStateCounts` prop
already in scope (declared `:92`, defaulted `:123`, and correctly used for
the map at `:285`). Every branch of `SmartEmptyState` that depends on
`stateCounts` — "suggest neighboring states" and "Top states for
{position}" — was permanently dead, independent of how much real recruit
data exists.

**Fix:** pass `playerStateCounts` (the correct prop for the players-mode
empty state; matches the `stateData` computation just above it in the same
file).

### (b) [DISHONEST] drifted filter count

`SmartEmptyState.tsx:103` (pre-fix) computed `activeFilterCount` via
`Object.values(filters).filter(v => v !== undefined && v !== '').length`
over the *whole* filters object it receives. That object, at runtime, also
carries `mode: 'players' | 'teams'` (always a non-empty string, never a
user-set filter) — so this count was always at least 1 higher than
`DiscoverClient.tsx`'s own curated `activeFilterCount` (the number on the
"Filters" button badge/mobile Sheet description). The audited screenshot
shows the drift directly: the Filters button shows no badge (0 real
filters) while the empty-state copy two inches below claims "You have 2
filters active."

**Fix:** compute `activeFilterCount` from the same curated field list
`DiscoverClient.tsx` uses (gradYear/position/states.length/minVelo/maxVelo/
minExit/maxExit/hasVideo/search/teamType), explicitly excluding `mode`.

### Two more bugs found while verifying (a)/(b), in the same owned files, also fixed

- `SmartEmptyState`'s neighboring-state suggestion block keyed off
  `filters.state` (singular) — a field that has **never existed** on the
  real filters object (which has always used `states`, a multi-select
  array, per `DiscoverClient.tsx:113/121`). That branch was permanently
  dead for a second, independent reason — fixing only the `stateCounts`
  wiring in (a) would not have made it reachable. Now derives
  `singleSelectedState` from `filters.states` (only offers neighbor
  suggestions when exactly one state is selected; multi-state selections
  fall through to the "top states for position" block instead).
- `DiscoverView`'s own `hasActiveFilters` (used to show/hide the plain "N
  players/teams found" count line) had the *identical*
  `Object.values(filters).some(...)` + `mode`-inflation bug as (b) — making
  it permanently `true`, which silently hides that count line any time zero
  filters are genuinely set. Rewritten to the same curated-field check.

### Not touched (out of scope for this lane's file list)

`coach-recruiting-suite.md` also flags a P0-class privacy gap in
`src/app/baseball/actions/player-peek.ts` (Player Peek panel skips the
`recruiting_activated`/`profile_visibility`/team-relationship checks that
`discover.ts`'s list/map endpoints already enforce). That file isn't in
this lane's assigned set — flagging for the orchestrator to route to
whichever lane owns `player-peek.ts` / `PlayerPeekPanel`.

## Lane 11 — passport-masthead

Fixes two findings from the detailed visual audit (`player-today-passport-timeline.md`), confined to
`PlayerPassportFairway.tsx` and `Masthead.tsx`. `PlayerTodayClient.tsx` was read for context (it's where
both bugs surface, in the compact Passport widget on the Today desktop right rail) but needed no changes —
both root causes live entirely in the two touched files.

### (a) [DISHONEST] Compact "Verified Measurables" header carried the wrong percentage

`PlayerPassportFairway.tsx:523` — the compact (Player Today) widget's header read
`Verified Measurables — 38% on the record`, but `model.completeness.percent` is the **whole-passport**
completeness figure (identity + positions + measurables + stats + story + media + academic + exposure),
not a measurables-specific number. The read model's own comment for the measurables signal says it is
*always* `complete: false` until a value is verified — and all five measurable rows directly below the
header render as honest ghost dashes (0% true measurables completion). A reader saw a non-zero percentage
sitting directly above five "—" rows, reading as a contradiction.

The full (non-compact) Passport page already gets this right — its equivalent header (`:588`) carries no
meta at all; the percentage appears, correctly, only on the page-level "On the Record" footer (`:631`).

**Fix:** removed the `meta` prop from the compact header so it now matches the full page's header exactly.

**Evidence (code):**
```diff
- <SubSectionHeader title="Verified Measurables" meta={`${model.completeness.percent}% on the record`} />
+ <SubSectionHeader title="Verified Measurables" />
```

### (b) [BROKEN] Surname clips mid-character in the narrow Today desktop right rail

`Masthead.tsx` set the surname to a fixed `text-5xl md:text-7xl` with no wrap or shrink handling. The
compact Passport widget renders inside `PlayerTodayClient.tsx`'s desktop right rail
(`grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-3` → rail is 1-of-3 columns, ~1/3 width), inside a `PaperCard` that sets
`overflow-hidden`. As a flex item (`flex flex-wrap items-start justify-between`, Masthead + InkBadge),
the surname `<div>` had the default `min-width: auto` floor — an unbreakable word like "RODRIGUEZ" can't
soft-wrap, so its min-content width *is* its full-size rendered width, and a flex item can never shrink
below that floor by default. Once the rail was narrower than that, the text bled past the flex item's
box and got clipped by the ancestor `PaperCard`'s `overflow-hidden`. Confirmed absent on the dedicated
full-width Passport page (same `Masthead`) and on mobile (single column, wraps cleanly) — this is a
narrow-embed-specific regression, matching the note's own diagnosis.

**Fix:** added `min-w-0` to the Masthead root (lets the flex item actually shrink instead of holding the
intrinsic-width floor) and `break-words` to the given-name/surname lines (lets the now-narrower box wrap
the unbreakable word onto a second line instead of overflowing). `Masthead.tsx` is not the frozen barrel
(`living-annual/index.ts`) — only the barrel itself was left untouched, per the lane note.

**Evidence (code):**
```diff
- className={cn('relative', className)}
+ className={cn('relative min-w-0', className)}
...
- className="font-annual text-5xl font-medium uppercase leading-[0.9] tracking-tight text-text-primary md:text-7xl"
+ className="break-words font-annual text-5xl font-medium uppercase leading-[0.9] tracking-tight text-text-primary md:text-7xl"
```

- `src/components/baseball/passport/PlayerPassportFairway.test.tsx` (new) — renders the component in both
  compact and full mode with a fixture whose whole-passport `completeness.percent` is a nonzero 38%;

  the real 38% still surfaces on the "On the Record" footer in full mode (regression guard against the

- `src/components/baseball/living-annual/Masthead.test.tsx` (new) — asserts both name lines render, the

## Lane 5 — mystats-mobile-strips

Fixes from `player-my-stats-analytics.md` (My Stats route, phone 390px).

### (b) [FIXED] "2026 Season" 8-stat block: only 2 chips visible, zero swipe cue

`MySeasonStats.tsx` passes 8 items (G/AB/R/H/HR/RBI/BB/SB) to `KPIContentsStrip`,
which crosses `StatStrip`'s `STAT_STRIP_RAIL_THRESHOLD` (5) into the snap-rail
branch. The rail hides its native scrollbar (`[scrollbar-width:none]`) by
design, but at 390px two chips (G, AB) fill the card's content width almost to
the pixel — leaving **zero** visual cue that H/HR/RBI/R/BB/SB exist past the
edge. Confirmed the exact chip-width math (`basis-[9.25rem]` × 2 + `gap-4`
≈ card content width at 390px) reproduces the reported "2 chips, no
affordance" symptom.

**Fix**: added a static trailing `mask-image` fade to `StatStrip`'s
`RAIL_BASE` shell (`src/components/fairway/charts/StatStrip.tsx`) — this is
the ONE shared phone-shape primitive behind every KPI/stat rail app-wide
(baseball My Stats, golf admin, Bridge `/admin/*`), so the fix applies
everywhere a ≥5-item strip renders on phone, not just this one card. Reset to
`none` at `sm` (rail dissolves into an `overflow-visible` grid there —
nothing to fade) and in `forced-colors` mode (never fade the one outline
high-contrast mode relies on for the band's edge). No hooks were added —
`StatStrip` stays hook-free / RSC-safe per its own doc contract (verified: no
`'use client'` needed, pure Tailwind arbitrary-property classes).

Left chip width (`9.25rem`) and `StatTile`'s internal layout (fixed
88px `Sparkline`) untouched — narrowing chips to force a bigger literal peek
risked squeezing `StatTile`'s sparkline on the other ~6 rail consumers grepped
below; the edge-fade alone directly resolves "no swipe cue," the literal
defect reported.

**Grepped every other rail-mode (`count>=5`) `StatStrip` consumer** to confirm
the fix helps without hurting anything else (all get the same fade, all keep
their `sm:` desktop grid untouched):
`src/app/admin/golf/tracer/page.tsx`, `src/app/admin/page.tsx`,
`src/app/admin/golf/page.tsx`, `src/app/admin/users/page.tsx`,
`src/app/admin/errors/page.tsx`.

**Evidence the mask actually compiles** (not just a class name that looks
right): ran the project's real `tailwind.config.ts` + `postcss.config.mjs`
against its actual `src/**` content glob and confirmed the generated CSS
(`grep`-verified, not npm build/dev — CLI CSS extraction only):
```css
.\[mask-image\:linear-gradient\(to_right\2c black_calc\(100\%_-_2rem\)\2c transparent\)\] {
  -webkit-mask-image: linear-gradient(to right,black calc(100% - 2rem),transparent);
          mask-image: linear-gradient(to right,black calc(100% - 2rem),transparent);
}
@media (min-width:640px) { .sm\:\[mask-image\:none\] { mask-image: none; } }
@media (forced-colors:active) { .forced-colors\:\[mask-image\:none\] { mask-image: none; } }
```

### (a) [NOT REPRODUCED — no code change] "Last 5 AVG" 3rd KPI invisible on phone

The note reports the 3rd item of a 3-item `KPIContentsStrip`
(Sessions/Trend/Last 5 AVG in `MyStatsClient.tsx`) vanishing on phone with
"no reserved space, no partial row," attributing it to
`StatStrip`'s `GRID_LAST_SPAN_3` branch.

Verified this end-to-end and could not reproduce a defect:
- `StatStrip.tsx`'s `count === 3` branch applies
  `[&>*:last-child]:col-span-2 sm:[&>*:last-child]:col-span-2
  lg:[&>*:last-child]:col-span-1` to the grid container. Compiled this exact
  class list through the real project tailwind config (same method as above)
  — it emits `grid-column: span 2 / span 2` targeting the container's last
  DOM child, i.e. standard CSS Grid auto-placement guarantees a 2nd row for
  the trailing item. No accidental class-drop from `tailwind-merge` either
  (verified the merged class string with the project's actual `cn()`/
  `twMerge` — nothing conflicts or gets stripped).
- `KPIContentsStrip.test.tsx:42-49` and `StatStrip.test.tsx:42-50` both
  already assert the exact classes/DOM structure for the count===3 case, and
  pass.
- `RuledStatLine`/`StatReadout` (the atoms rendered inside each cell) have no
  viewport-conditional `hidden` classes and no data-dependent conditional
  rendering that would drop the 3rd item.

Given the audit note's own aside — a `position: fixed` bottom tab bar
"appears to float mid-page in both screenshots, directly under the
Sessions/Trend row" and was flagged as a probable screenshot-stitching
artifact — that overlay sits at exactly the vertical position the 2nd grid
row would render. Most likely explanation: the same capture artifact, not a
layout bug. Not forcing a change to layout code that checks out correctly
under direct compilation. Flagging for the orchestrator rather than silently
dropping it.

## Lane 6 — journey

Fixes both BROKEN findings from `scratchpad/notes/player-journey-colleges.md` (orchestrator-verified).

### (a) Journey KPI strip silently drops `researching`

`useJourney`'s `JourneyStats` (`use-journey.ts:200-208`, pre-fix) only bucketed `interested/contacted/visited/offered` (+ a separate `committed` boolean). `'researching'` is a fully valid, selectable status (`JourneyClient.tsx` `statusOptions`, `RecruitingSchemas.updateStatus`) with **no bucket at all** — a school marked "Researching" counted toward `total_interests` but vanished from every displayed column, so the KPI strip's numbers never summed to "Total Schools" once any school used that status. Not visible on the live screenshot only because the demo account has 0 interests (latent, not currently firing).

**Fix:** added `schools_researching` to `JourneyStats`, computed it the same way as the other buckets, and added a "Researching" item to `JourneyClient`'s `KPIContentsStrip` (bumped `columns` 5→6 to match the new 6-item strip).

Evidence: `src/hooks/use-journey.ts:37,208` (bucket), `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/journey/JourneyClient.tsx:254-264` (render).

### (b) Player recruiting hub (Journey / Colleges / Analytics) has no `player_type` gate

`requireBaseballPlayerRoute` only checks `role === 'player'` — it never checked `player_type`. Per the codebase's own Recruiting Activation Model, a **college** player's recruiting status is "Never" — team features only — yet a college player could reach and fully use the school-interest tracker (`/dashboard/journey`), college search (`/dashboard/colleges`), and recruiting-analytics (`/dashboard/analytics`). `nav-registry.ts` is FROZEN and was left untouched — the existing `/dashboard/activate` route already solves this identical problem at the page level (checks `session.player.player_type === 'college'` and renders an honest "not available" `EditorsLetter` instead of a silent redirect), so this PR mirrors that established, already-approved pattern rather than inventing something new.

**Fix:** added `requireRecruitingPlayerRoute` to `src/lib/baseball/server-route-guards.ts` (thin wrapper around `requireBaseballPlayerRoute` that also resolves `isCollegePlayer`), and wired it into all three page.tsx entries. A college player now sees an honest "isn't for college players" letter; every other player type (`high_school`/`juco`/`showcase`) is unaffected, and the pre-existing coach redirects (including `analytics/page.tsx`'s distinct `command-center` target) are preserved exactly.

## Lane 3 — climbarc-shared

Fixes both BROKEN findings from the visual audit for the shared `ClimbArc` viz
(`src/components/baseball/living-annual/viz/ClimbArc.tsx`), which backs the
My Stats batting-average trend, the recruiting Analytics/Passport "Profile
views" chart, and the strength-coach Performance dashboard's lift trend.

### (a) Decimal-precision heuristic destroyed the AVG trend

`ClimbArc.tsx:139` was `values.some((v) => !Number.isInteger(v)) ? 1 : 0` —
any non-integer series got capped to 1 decimal. For a batting-average series
(0–1 range, where `.250` vs `.300` is the whole point) this is destructive:
the screen's "NOW `0.3`" was actually `.250` rounded, and "PR `0.7`" was
actually `.667`.

Fix:
- Added an optional `decimals` prop to `ClimbArcProps`; `TrendChart.tsx`
  (My Stats AVG chart) now passes `decimals={3}` explicitly.
- When omitted, derive from the series: non-integer + magnitude < 10 → 3
  decimals; non-integer + magnitude ≥ 10 → 1; all-integer → 0 (unchanged
  for the Lift Trend / Profile Views callers).
- Also aligned with the kit's `formatRate` leading-zero-drop house style
  (every other rate stat on these screens shows `.244`, not `0.244`) — the
  "Now" readout, PR caption, and Goal caption now all drop the leading zero
  for sub-1 rates. Gated on `decimals > 0` so it can never trip
  `formatRate`'s own decimals=0 edge case (which collapses `0` to an empty
  string) — verified with a dedicated regression test.

### (b) Hardcoded `signoff="— My Development"` on the empty state

`ClimbArc.tsx:101` hardcoded this copy in the `<2 points` "not enough data
yet" branch with no override. It's wrong on **both** actual current callers:
the recruiting Analytics/Passport page (about coach engagement, not "My
Development") and the strength-coach Performance dashboard's Lift Trend
(coach-facing, not first-person).

Fix: added an optional `signoff` prop, defaulting to none. No caller
currently has a confirmed-correct string to supply (the note itself couldn't
confirm which of the other two features the copy actually belonged to), so
per the "or default to none" guidance this is the conservative fix — no new
guessed copy introduced anywhere.

## Lane 7 — decision-room-datelabel (DISHONEST)

### Finding (orchestrator-verified, scratchpad/notes/coach-decision-settings.md)
`loadGameResults` (`src/lib/baseball/read-models/decision-room/games.ts:96-148`) applies **no date-range filter** — it returns the most-recent `MAX_ROWS` (100) *completed* games regardless of age. But the "Wins since last meeting" rail on the Staff Decision Room hardcoded a caption of **"Last 14 days"** (`StaffDecisionRoomFairway.tsx:570`, plus the empty-state text at `:574`), and the Export Summary text repeated the same claim (`StaffDecisionRoomClient.tsx:128`).

Verified prod case from the audit: the team's games actually shown ran **May 28 → Jun 17**, roughly a month before the audit's "today" (Jul 15). A coach reading "Last 14 days" over that list would believe these were this fortnight's results — they are not. This is a pure mislabeling bug, not a data-fabrication bug: the game data itself reconciles correctly against db-truth, only the time-window claim is false.

### Fix (picked the safer, non-behavior-changing option per the lane spec)
Relabeled the section to **"Most recent completed games"** (masthead eyebrow + Export Summary text) and the empty state to **"No completed games yet."** — text that accurately describes what the (unfiltered) query already does, rather than bolting on a real `gte('game_date', ...)` window, which would have silently emptied this section for any team on a bye week (the spec's own guidance: "Pick the honest one; if unsure, relabel (safer, no data-window behavior change)").

Also added a doc comment to `loadGameResults` itself flagging the "no date filter" behavior so a future change doesn't silently reintroduce a window-specific label without a matching window-specific query.

### Files touched (4, all in-lane)
- `src/lib/baseball/read-models/decision-room/games.ts` — doc comment only, no behavior change
- `src/components/baseball/staff-decision-room/StaffDecisionRoomFairway.tsx` — eyebrow + empty-state copy

- `src/lib/baseball/read-models/decision-room/__tests__/games-wins-label-honesty.test.ts` — new regression test

### Test
New file pins both halves so this can't silently regress:
1. `loadGameResults` still returns a completed game 40 days old, untouched (the behavior the honest label now describes) — proves the loader is a "most recent" feed, not a "last 14 days" feed.
2. Non-completed (`scheduled`) games are still excluded — the gate is status, not date.
3. Source-content assertions: `StaffDecisionRoomFairway.tsx` no longer contains `"Last 14 days"` / `"No completed games in the last 14 days"` and does contain the honest replacements; `StaffDecisionRoomClient.tsx`'s export text likewise.

### Finding (verified in code, orchestrator note `coach-stats-suite.md`)
`StatVisualsSection.tsx:211`'s `FamilyEmptyState` hardcoded `href="/baseball/dashboard/import"` on its per-family "Import stats" CTA. `StatVisualsSectionProps` had no capability/href field, and `StatsCenterClient`'s `<StatVisualsSection>` call (~line 931) passed nothing. This bypasses the capability-aware routing the same page's other two import CTAs (header "Import Center" button, "Import a box score" empty-state CTA) already use: `can_manage_imports` → `/baseball/dashboard/import`, else `can_manage_stats` → `/baseball/dashboard/stats/upload`. `/baseball/dashboard/import/page.tsx` redirects anyone lacking `can_manage_imports` straight to the command center with no error — so a staffer holding `can_manage_stats` but not `can_manage_imports` (assistant/pitching/hitting/catching/defensive/strength coach tiers) got silently bounced. Same lockout class as the #863 finding.

### Fix
- Added optional `importHref?: string` to `StatVisualsSectionProps` (doc comment explains the parent-resolved contract: omit → hide the CTA, never a hardcoded fallback route).
- `FamilyEmptyState` now renders the "Import stats" link only when `scope === 'team' && importHref` is truthy, using the passed href instead of a literal string.
- `StatsCenterClient.tsx`'s `<StatVisualsSection>` call now passes `importHref={canShowImportEntry ? importEntryHref : undefined}` — reusing the exact `canManageImports`/`canManageStats` resolution already in scope for the page's other two import CTAs.
- Checked for other `<StatVisualsSection scope="player">` render sites before changing the prop contract (per the lane instruction) — grepped the whole repo, confirmed **none exist yet** (only the `StatsCenterClient` team-scope call site and a forward-looking code comment referencing a not-yet-built player-profile mount). So this prop-contract change has exactly one call site to update, which is done.

### Evidence
- Before: `FamilyEmptyState` action always linked to the hardcoded `/baseball/dashboard/import`, dead-ending `can_manage_stats`-only viewers.
- After: the link's `href` comes from the capability-resolved `importHref`; when omitted (viewer holds neither capability) the CTA doesn't render at all — matches the "no dead button" contract of the page's other two import entry points.
- New test `src/components/baseball/stat-visuals/__tests__/StatVisualsSection.import-href.test.tsx` covers: (1) team scope renders the link with the passed `importHref`, (2) team scope with no `importHref` renders no link (no hardcoded fallback), (3) player scope never shows the CTA even if `importHref` is supplied.

## Summary

`getPlayerPeekDataImpl` (src/app/baseball/actions/player-peek.ts) selected full player PII — name, high school, city/state, height/weight, gpa, velocities — for **any** `playerId`, gated only by an auth check inside `withAdminObserved` (telemetry only). No capability gate, no `recruiting_activated` filter, no `profile_visibility` filter, and it never called `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer`. The P0 Discover privacy enforcement (`discover.ts:178-251` — `recruiting_activated=true`, exclude `profile_visibility='private'`, exclude own-team handled separately) was never extended to this surface.

This restores the existing policy (not a new one) for the peek panel:

- **(a) own-roster peek** — the viewer is a coach on a team the player is a member of → allowed, regardless of `recruiting_activated` / `profile_visibility`.
- **(b) everything else goes through `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer`** — `recruiting_activated = true`, not a `college` player, coach_type/player_type compatible (a JUCO coach may not recruit another JUCO player), `baseball_player_settings.profile_visibility` is not `'private'`, and the player is on a discoverable (HS/showcase/JUCO) team roster — the exact predicate Discover's browse query and the watchlist write path already enforce.
- A viewer with **no `baseball_coaches` row at all** (e.g. a player-role session) is denied outright, mirroring Discover's own "no coachProfile → nothing" behavior.
- Every denial returns the same generic `'Player not found'`, so a denied request is indistinguishable from a truly-missing row.
- The gate runs **before** the engagement-event insert and the profile-view email, so a denied peek fires neither.

## Round 2 (review fix)

The first version of this PR re-derived only half of `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer`'s policy inline (`recruiting_activated` + `profile_visibility`) instead of calling it, and that partial copy missed two of Discover's restrictions with **no DB-level backstop** (`baseball_players` RLS is `USING (true)` — the app gate is the only guard):

1. **coach_type vs player_type** — `discover.ts:192` hides JUCO players from JUCO coaches' browse results (`if (serverCoachType === 'juco') query.in('player_type', ['high_school','showcase'])`); the peek gate didn't fetch `coach_type` at all and never consulted it, so a JUCO coach could peek a rival JUCO player's full PII by UUID even though that player is invisible to them in Discover.
2. **discoverable-team membership** — `discover.ts:144-151/197-198` (`getDiscoverableTeamPlayerIds`) excludes players with no current team assignment from Discover; no write path resets `recruiting_activated` to `false` on roster removal, so a player removed from every roster stayed fully peekable by UUID even though Discover would never surface them.

Fixed by routing the non-own-roster branch through `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer` (`src/lib/baseball/recruitability.ts`) directly instead of re-deriving a partial copy — the same single source of truth Discover's browse query and the watchlist/engagement write paths already rely on, so this surface cannot fork from that policy again. `player-peek.ts`'s coach lookup now also selects `coach_type` so the gate can pass it through. Own-roster is still checked locally first (peek's own-roster rule is the *inverse* of `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer`'s — a coach always sees their own roster player regardless of activation/visibility, whereas that function denies own-roster players with reason `on_own_roster` since you don't "recruit" a player you already have).

`player-peek-privacy.test.ts` gained two new cases: a JUCO coach peeking a JUCO player (deny) and an activated+public player removed from every roster (deny) — both previously unguarded, both now green, alongside all five original allow/deny cases. `player-peek-engagement-events.test.ts`'s fixture was extended with a discoverable-team-membership mock so it keeps testing only the engagement-event insert mechanics under the now-complete gate.

## Trace: who calls the peek panel

`PlayerPeekPanel` is mounted from `PipelineClient`, `DiscoverClient`, and `WatchlistClient` — all pass IDs of prospects the coach is tracking/browsing (pipeline/watchlist entries, discover results), never a roster surface today. The own-roster bypass is still implemented per the explicit policy spec (and covered by a test) as defense-in-depth for any future roster-mounted caller, and because "you may always see your own players" is the established rule everywhere else in this codebase (recruitability.ts's `on_own_roster` reason, discover.ts's own-roster exclusion).

## De-duplication

`profile_visibility` and own-roster-player-id lookups were previously **forked verbatim** between `discover.ts` and `recruitability.ts`. Extracted both into a new shared module, `src/lib/baseball/player-visibility.ts`:

- `getPrivatePlayerIds` / `formatIdListForNotIn` — bulk form (discover.ts's listings/counts).
- `isPlayerProfilePrivate` — single-player form (recruitability.ts; player-peek.ts now gets this transitively via `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer`).
- `getCoachRosterPlayerIds` — own-roster player IDs, shared by discover.ts, recruitability.ts, and player-peek.ts's own-roster bypass.

`discover.ts` and `recruitability.ts` now both import from this module instead of each carrying their own copy, and `player-peek.ts`'s recruitability check is now `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer` itself rather than a fourth partial copy — no drift risk between the call sites.

## Wrapper

Replaced the telemetry-only `withAdminObserved` wrapper with `withBaseballAction` (`requireActiveContext: false, demoSafe: true`), matching discover.ts's own idiom for cross-team browse/peek reads: peek is reached from Discover/Watchlist/Pipeline, all cross-team by nature, so there's no single "target team" to resolve a capability against; identity is derived inside the impl from the coach's own `baseball_coaches` row (unchanged), not an active-team context. `withBaseballAction` already performs the same `observeActionSoftFailure` telemetry `withAdminObserved` did (plus Sentry scope, RLS-denial capture, and the demo read-only guard), so nesting both would be redundant — no existing call site in this codebase composes them.

`demoSafe: true` preserves this action's **pre-existing** (previously totally unguarded) behavior for the shared demo coach session. Flagged as a separate, out-of-scope concern below — this PR's job is the authorization gate, not the demo-write question.

## Sibling audit

Audited player-peek.ts's only other export (there is none besides `getPlayerPeekData`) and sibling peek/preview surfaces for the same hole:

- `scout-packet.ts`'s `getScoutPacketPreview` / `getScoutPacketRoster` — already gated via `withBaseballAction({ requiredCapability: 'can_export_reports' })` + `ctx.targetTeamId`, and `assembleScoutPacket` keys the exposure gate on `(player_id, team_id)` in `baseball_player_passport_settings`, so a foreign player + your own team resolves to `not_exposed` (fails closed). No hole found.
- `interests.ts` — player-side interest-in-organization actions, not opposing-player PII. Not applicable.
- `player-actions.ts` — self-only (`assignee_player_id` pinned to the resolved player), not applicable.
- `watchlist.ts` — already calls `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer` before writes. Not applicable.

No further fixes needed in this PR's scope.

## Tests

Authorization matrix (`player-peek-privacy.test.ts`, style matches `imports-capability-shape-gate.test.ts` / `discover-privacy.test.ts` — mocks only the session/table seam, leaves the real `withBaseballAction` wiring in place):

- non-activated player + unrelated coach → denied, **and** the engagement-event insert does not fire.
- private-visibility player + unrelated coach → denied (even though `recruiting_activated=true`), insert does not fire.
- activated + public player + any coach → allowed, insert fires exactly once.
- own-roster player + own coach → allowed regardless of `recruiting_activated`, insert fires exactly once.
- player-role viewer (no `baseball_coaches` row) → denied regardless of target player.
- **JUCO coach + JUCO player** (activated, public, on a discoverable team) → denied.
- JUCO player + college coach → allowed (only JUCO-on-JUCO is restricted).
- **activated + public player removed from every roster** (not on a discoverable team) → denied.

Updated `player-peek-engagement-events.test.ts`'s fixture (`recruiting_activated: true`, plus a discoverable-team-membership mock for the new `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer` call path) so it continues to test only the engagement-event insert mechanics under the now-complete gate.

## Deferred

- **Demo write-pollution** (found during audit, out of this P0's scope): `getPlayerPeekData` performs two real writes — an `engagement_events` insert and a `notifyProfileView` email to the target player — that were, and with `demoSafe: true` remain, reachable from the **shared** Baseball demo coach session. Every demo visitor who peeks a real recruiting-activated player triggers a real "a coach viewed your profile" email and pollutes `baseball_player_engagement_events` with the shared demo coach's id. This is a data-hygiene/demo-isolation issue, not a privacy/authorization one (the peeked player already opted into public recruiting visibility) — flagging for a follow-up decision on whether to flip `demoSafe: false` (blocks demo peek entirely) or suppress just the two writes when the session is the shared demo coach.
- **Pre-existing `getDiscoverableTeamPlayerIds` duplication** between `discover.ts` and `recruitability.ts` (different return shapes — `string[] | null` vs. `Set<string>`) was left as-is; the peek gate now calls `recruitability.ts`'s copy (via `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer`), so this is unchanged pre-existing duplication between those two files, not a new fork — out of scope for this PR, lower risk than the predicates already consolidated in `player-visibility.ts`.

~~**Coach-type vs. player-type recruiting eligibility**~~ — **retracted, this was factually wrong.** The original text claimed "Discover's own browse query... do[es] not additionally restrict by coach-type/player-type." That's incorrect: `discover.ts:192` (`getDiscoverPlayersImpl`) explicitly does `if (serverCoachType === 'juco') query.in('player_type', ['high_school','showcase'])`, and `getStateCountsImpl` applies the same restriction to map counts. This was a real gap in the original peek gate (a JUCO coach could peek a JUCO player Discover would never show them), not a "matches Discover's existing behavior" scope cut — now fixed per "Round 2" above.

## Evidence

```
$ npm run typecheck                                    → exit 0, no errors
$ npx eslint --max-warnings 0 <3 touched files>         → exit 0, no warnings
$ npx vitest run --project unit --project business --project integration --project rls
    (player-peek-privacy.test.ts: 8 cases, player-peek-engagement-events.test.ts: 2 cases,
     plus the full unit + business suites since this PR touches auth/authorization)
                                                        → unit 5298/5298, business 5374/5374, all green
$ node scripts/check-cycles.mjs                         → OK — 33 known cycles, none new
```

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
title: fix(baseball): P0 privacy — gate player-peek behind Discover's authorization policy

## Bug

`updateSession()`'s idle-timeout gate (`src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts:~438`) was keyed on `sport` (truthy for **any** `/baseball*`, `/golf*`, `/lifting*` path) instead of the middleware's own protected/dashboard route predicate. Result: a signed-in-but-idle (>5 min) session got bounced to `/login?message=session_expired` when visiting **PUBLIC** pages — marketing roots, the login pages themselves, and public player/team/program/packet profiles, across all three sports. Verified against live prod behavior twice; it also bounced our own production crawl.

## Fix

Changed the gate condition from:

```ts
if (user && (sport || onAdminPath)) {
```

to:

```ts
if (user && (isProtectedRoute || onAdminPath)) {
```

`isProtectedRoute` (= `isDashboardRoute`, already computed a few lines above) and `onAdminPath` are the middleware's existing "this route actually requires a live session" predicates — reused as-is, no new logic.

Behavior:
- **Public marketing roots, login/signup pages, and `(public)` route-group profiles** (`/baseball`, `/golf`, `/baseball/login`, `/baseball/player/[id]`, `/baseball/team/[id]`, `/baseball/program/[id]`, `/baseball/packet/[token]`, etc.) — idle sessions are **never bounced**. The real Supabase auth session still refreshes silently via `supabase.auth.getUser()` above this block on every request regardless of route, so nothing about token refresh changes — we only skip the extra app-level "bounce with `session_expired` banner + explicit cookie cleanup" step, which these routes never needed.
- **Dashboard routes** (`/baseball/dashboard/*`, `/golf/dashboard/*`, `/lifting/dashboard/*`) and **`/admin`** — idle-bounce + local signOut + explicit auth-cookie/activity-marker cleanup is **unchanged** (#730 preserved exactly).

Comment above the block rewritten to state the new scoping explicitly and explain why (avoids this regressing again).

## Tests

New file `src/lib/supabase/__tests__/middleware-idle-timeout-public-routes.test.ts`, matching the existing `middleware-admin-idle-timeout.test.ts` harness idiom exactly (same `@supabase/ssr` mock, same `buildRequest` helper):

- idle session + `/baseball` (marketing root) → no redirect, page serves
- idle session + `/golf` (marketing root) → no redirect, page serves
- idle session + `/baseball/player/<id>` (public profile) → no redirect
- idle session + `/baseball/login` itself → no redirect
- idle session + `/baseball/dashboard/roster` → `session_expired` redirect **preserved**
- idle session + `/admin/errors` → `session_expired` redirect **preserved**
- fresh visit (no activity cookie) to `/baseball` → no idle-marker bootstrap (out of scope entirely for public routes)

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npx eslint --max-warnings 0` on both touched files — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run --project unit` on the new test file + all existing middleware/session tests that exercise `updateSession` (`middleware-admin-idle-timeout.test.ts`, `root-middleware.test.ts`, `nav-capability-gating.test.ts`, `log-auth-failure.test.ts`) — 26/26 passed
- [x] `node scripts/check-cycles.mjs` — OK, 33 known cycles, none new

## Summary
- New `e2e/visual-audit.spec.ts`: for each of the `baseball-coach`/`baseball-player` Playwright projects, discovers every visible nav route from the LIVE rendered DOM (mirrors `e2e/baseball-route-crawler.spec.ts`'s proven pattern — `FairwaySidebar` aria-label="Main navigation" rail + hub-sub-nav strip, both real `<Link>`s inside `<nav>` elements, never nav-registry source) and captures full-page screenshots at phone (390x844) and desktop (1440x900) viewports for every route, plus signed-out publics (`/baseball`, `/baseball/login`, up to 3 best-effort public player/team/program links discovered from the authenticated crawl) in a fresh unauthenticated context. Writes a per-role `manifest.json` (route → files, HTTP status, load ms, console error count).
- **Screenshots are data capture, not assertions** — the spec never fails on a broken/near-blank/erroring route; it only fails on a login failure (auth storageState didn't hold, or the session bounced to `/login` mid-crawl) or a total navigation failure (entry route unreachable, zero nav links discovered, or 0/N routes produced a screenshot).
- Gated behind `VISUAL_AUDIT=1` (`test.skip` otherwise). Updated `playwright.config.ts`: the plain `chromium` project now ignores this spec, and `baseball-coach`/`baseball-player` now match it (alongside the existing smoke/route-crawler specs). Verified `playwright.yml` and `ci.yml` never pick it up — both invoke Playwright with explicit spec-file arguments that don't name this file, and `chromium`'s testIgnore now excludes it outright.
- New `.github/workflows/visual-audit.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` with a `base_url` input (default `https://helmsportslabs.com`), runs `npx playwright test e2e/visual-audit.spec.ts --project=baseball-coach --project=baseball-player`. Verified against the installed Playwright runner source (`collectProjectsAndTestFiles` in `lib/runner/index.js`) that this also runs the `setup` project (`playwright/baseball-auth.setup.ts`, both coach + player) as a dependency with its own full/unfiltered file set — no `--project=setup` needed, and Golf's `playwright/auth.setup.ts` is never pulled in since `setup`'s `testMatch` is scoped to `baseball-auth.setup.ts` specifically. `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL` from the input makes `playwright.config.ts`'s `webServer` block a no-op (only defined when unset), so there's no local build/dev-server/seed step at all. `PLAYWRIGHT_BASEBALL_REQUIRED=1` + existing `E2E_BASEBALL_COACH_EMAIL/PASSWORD` + `E2E_BASEBALL_PLAYER_EMAIL/PASSWORD` repo secrets (no new secret names). Uploads `test-results/visual-audit` as `visual-audit-<run_number>`, retention 7 days, `if: always()`. `timeout-minutes: 30`. Concurrency group cancels a superseded re-dispatch.

## Test plan

## Summary

`team/[id]`, `player/[id]`, `program/[id]`, and `packet/[token]` all sit under `src/app/baseball/(public)/` — the (public) route group's `layout.tsx` was a bare `<>{children}</>`, no `LazyMotion` anywhere upstream.

`team/[id]/page.tsx` and `player/[id]/PlayerProfileClient.tsx` render Living Annual `m`-based atoms directly (`Masthead`, `RuledStatLine`, `HairlineRule`). Their entrance variants (`inkSettles` / `rulesDraw` in `living-annual/motion.ts`) start at `hidden` — `opacity: 0`, `scaleX: 0` — and only animate to `visible` once framer-motion's animation feature bundle is loaded via a `LazyMotion` ancestor. Without one, an `m.*` component's `AnimationFeature` never mounts, so `hidden` is terminal for any visitor without `prefers-reduced-motion` on. **Player and team names, and stat numerals, were invisible on these live public recruiting pages** — the exact same class of bug already fixed once for `/admin` (`AdminMotionProvider`) and documented in `(dashboard)/dashboard/template.tsx`.

## Verification performed (before writing any fix)

- Confirmed `(public)/layout.tsx` had no motion provider — `return <>{children}</>;`.
- Confirmed no `LazyMotion` anywhere in `src/app/baseball/(public)/**`.
- Confirmed `team/[id]/page.tsx` and `PlayerProfileClient.tsx` import `Masthead` / `RuledStatLine` / `HairlineRule` from `@/components/baseball/living-annual` and render them directly (no local `LazyMotion` wrapper of their own).
- Confirmed `living-annual/motion.ts`'s `inkSettles(reduced=false)` hidden variant is `{ opacity: 0, y: 6, filter: 'blur(2px)' }` — i.e. genuinely invisible, not just dim.
- Read `(dashboard)/dashboard/template.tsx`'s self-documenting comment (the exact prior instance of this bug class) and reused its `loadFeatures` import (`@/lib/motion/load-features`) — the real code-split loader, not a bare `domAnimation` import.
- **Correction to the initial framing**: `program/[id]/page.tsx` does **not** currently render any Living Annual `m` atom directly — its children (`ProgramTabs`, `ProgramRoster`) are plain UI (`Card`/`Badge`/`Avatar`), and `GradeStamp` (also named in the original bug report) isn't used anywhere under `(public)/` today — it's dashboard-only (`PipelineClient`, `WatchlistClient` via `RecruitCard`). `packet/[token]/page.tsx` renders `ScoutPacketView`, which **already** wraps itself in its own `<LazyMotion features={loadFeatures} strict>` — it was not actually broken. So the confirmed, currently-live bug is on `team/[id]` and `player/[id]` only; `program/[id]` and `packet/[token]` get the fix defensively (either page could add a Living Annual atom in the future and inherit visibility for free, and `packet`'s inner `LazyMotion` nests harmlessly under the outer one).

## Fix

- **`src/app/baseball/(public)/PublicMotionScope.tsx`** (new) — `'use client'`, `<LazyMotion features={loadFeatures} strict>{children}</LazyMotion>`. Mirrors the existing `AdminMotionProvider` (`src/app/admin/_motion-provider.tsx` / `src/app/golf/admin/_motion-provider.tsx`) pattern already established in this repo for exactly this problem. `strict` is safe here — verified no descendant in this route's component tree (checked `PlayerProfileClient`, `ScoutPacketView`, `ProgramTabs`, `ProgramRoster`, and the shared `ui`/`icons` components they pull in) renders a full `motion.*` component, only `m.*`.
- **`src/app/baseball/(public)/layout.tsx`** — now mounts `<PublicMotionScope>{children}</PublicMotionScope>`. Stays a Server Component (`export const metadata` untouched) — the client boundary lives entirely in `PublicMotionScope`.

## Test

**`src/app/baseball/(public)/PublicMotionScope.test.tsx`** (new) — no existing test asserts a motion provider directly (`(dashboard)/dashboard/template.tsx` has none), so per the task's fallback: a render test under jsdom, deliberately **not** mocking `framer-motion` (unlike `Reveal.test.tsx` / `HoverReveal.test.tsx`), because the bug IS framer-motion's real `m`-without-`LazyMotion` behavior — a mock Proxy would render everything visible regardless and catch nothing.

- Test 1 reproduces the bug: `<Masthead>` with no `LazyMotion` ancestor → `toBeVisible()` fails forever (computed `opacity` stays `'0'`).
- Test 2 proves the fix: same `<Masthead>` wrapped in `<PublicMotionScope>` → `waitFor(() => expect(...).toBeVisible())` passes once the async `loadFeatures` bundle resolves and the real entrance transition starts (confirmed via manual spike logging: opacity climbs from `0` → `0.256` → ... across real jsdom animation frames, not a mocked jump to 1).
- Test 3 pins `(public)/layout.tsx` itself so a future revert to `<>{children}</>` fails this test.

## Gate evidence

```
$ npm run typecheck
> tsc --noEmit
(clean, no output)

$ npx eslint --max-warnings 0 "src/app/baseball/(public)/PublicMotionScope.tsx" \
    "src/app/baseball/(public)/layout.tsx" "src/app/baseball/(public)/PublicMotionScope.test.tsx"
(clean, no output)

$ npx vitest run --project unit "src/app/baseball/(public)/PublicMotionScope.test.tsx"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)

$ npx vitest run --project unit src/components/baseball/living-annual "src/app/baseball/(public)"
 Test Files  6 passed (6)
      Tests  40 passed (40)

$ node scripts/check-cycles.mjs
check-cycles: OK — 33 known cycles, none new
```

## Relationship to PR #865

#865 (open, same base `batch/allofit-0715`) adds `src/components/baseball/marketing/BaseballMarketingMotionScope.tsx` — a near-identical `'use client'` `<LazyMotion features={loadFeatures}>` wrapper, but scoped to the separate `/baseball` marketing root page, not this `(public)` route group. Its PR body explicitly flags this exact gap as out of its scope:

> "Found (not fixed here...): the `(public)` baseball profile pages ... render the same Living Annual `m`-based atoms without any `LazyMotion` ancestor anywhere in their tree — flagged separately to the orchestrator..."

This PR is that flagged fix. **Did not touch any of #865's files.** The two wrappers (`BaseballMarketingMotionScope` and this PR's `PublicMotionScope`) are functionally identical (`LazyMotion` + `loadFeatures`, differing only in `strict`) and could reasonably be consolidated into one shared `src/components/baseball/motion/BaseballMotionScope.tsx` if both land — leaving that call to whoever merges both, rather than editing #865's file from this branch.

Not merging — base is `batch/allofit-0715` per fleet instructions.

## Summary

Closes the #852 residual velocity coverage gap: box-score-migrated players had **no velocity metrics** in the CoachHelm engine. Their legacy `exit_velocity`/`pitch_velocity` scalar is dropped alongside superseded legacy GAME rows (`engine-stat-rows.ts` precedence rule 1), and the canonical box-score tables (`baseball_box_score_batting`/`_pitching`) carry no velocity columns at all. `loaders.ts`'s `eventDerived` hook (#851) already threaded a per-field event-layer override into `loadPlayerMetrics`/`loadAllPlayerMetrics`, but nothing ever called it — so those players' `avg_exit_velocity` / `max_exit_velocity` / `avg_pitch_velocity` / `max_pitch_velocity` metrics silently went dark.

## Changes

**New: `src/lib/baseball/coachhelm/engine-event-derived.ts`**
- `loadEngineEventRows(db, teamId)` — team-scoped, paginated (`fetchAllRowsResult`, PostgREST 1000-row cap) read of `baseball_pitch_events` / `baseball_batted_ball_events`, filtered to the **#813 current (non-superseded) rows only** (`superseded_by_run_id IS NULL`). **All-or-nothing**: either table failing returns `data: null`, mirroring `loadEngineStatRows`'s own honesty rule.
- `eventDerivedVelocityForPlayer` / `buildEventDerivedByPlayer` — pure per-player reducers that reuse `elite-stat-events.ts`'s real `buildHitterMetrics` / `buildPitcherMetrics` + `loaders.ts`'s `eventDerivedVelocityFromMetrics`, so the honesty-gated average here is byte-identical to what the Stats Center already shows — never a second, drifting "average exit velocity" implementation.

**Wired into all three engine callers:**
- `engine-run.ts` — full-history event pool → `loadAllPlayerMetrics`'s new `eventDerivedByPlayer` param.
- `outcome-sweep.ts` — event rows filtered to the **same per-action after-window** as the box-score read (`measured_at > created_at`), so a pre-action event can never count toward "did it move" measurement.
- `action-baseline.ts` — full-history event pool → the baseline capture (a baseline is "current value at conversion time", matching the box-score read's own no-date-filter semantics).

**Manifest:** extended `stat-layer-manifest.ts`'s `GRANDFATHERED_CONSUMERS` allowlist for the 3 new wiring-test fixture files (they seed fake `baseball_player_stats` rows as the legacy-fallback pin, not staleness) — required by the existing `stat-layer-contract.test.ts` enforcement.

**Test fixtures:** added a real (not no-op) `.is()` passthrough to the existing custom fake-client builders in `outcome-sweep-insight-resolve.test.ts` and `action-baseline.test.ts`, since both callers now query with `.is('superseded_by_run_id', null)`.

## Tests

- `engine-event-derived.test.ts` — pure aggregation: hitter-side/pitcher-side isolation (no cross-player leak), two-way player gets both independently, zero-event honest absence, #813 supersede filter, all-or-nothing degrade on read failure.
- `engine-run-event-velocity.test.ts` — event-derived avg exit velocity **wins** over the legacy scalar for the same player; a zero-event player **keeps** their legacy scalar; event-read failure degrades **every** player back to legacy (fixed clock).
- `outcome-sweep-event-velocity.test.ts` — same win/fallback pattern, scoped to the per-action after-window (a pre-action event is proven excluded).
- `action-baseline-event-velocity.test.ts` — same win/fallback pattern for baseline capture.

Not merging — leaving for review per batch process.

Task: `wizard-consolidation`. Audited both parallel stats-upload wizards end-to-end and consolidated per the orchestrator's decision — **Import Center is canonical**.

### Audit findings (before touching anything)

- `/baseball/dashboard/import` (`ImportWizardClient`) already covers the "lighter wizard"'s core write path: it calls the **same atomic `save_baseball_full_box_score` RPC**, already dual-writes to legacy `baseball_player_stats` (issue #379), and additionally has provenance (raw file preserved + hashed), dedup/duplicate verdicts, rollback, and required-review — none of which the legacy wizard had.
- The legacy wizard's "corrections path" (`resolveUnmatchedPlayers` / `reprocessUpload` in `actions/stats.ts`) is **already dead code with no UI call site** — both actions were changed in a prior pass (W5a) to honestly refuse and point the coach at Import Center's re-open-run + re-commit flow instead, which is strictly better (audited, reversible).
- The two capabilities the legacy wizard genuinely had that Import Center's flow didn't: **drag-and-drop file upload**, and a **visible sample-values preview** of the parsed CSV before committing to a column mapping. Ported both below. Everything else was already superseded — no other capability to port.

### Changes

1. **Import-mode port** (`ImportWizardClient.tsx`, no server-action signature changes):

Removed Stats Center's now-redundant standalone "Upload" button (it sat right next to an "Import Center" button pointing at the exact same eventual destination — keeping both was a duplicate).

## Summary

Writes (does **not** apply) the one-time #379 legacy-stats backfill migration: `supabase/migrations/20260715141727_baseball_legacy_stats_backfill.sql`. Pure data file, no code changes, no schema DDL beyond session-local `TEMP TABLE`s that drop themselves at commit.

## What it does

- Finds teams with a `stat_type = 'game'` row in `baseball_player_stats` and **zero** rows in both `baseball_box_score_batting`/`_pitching` ("zero box-score data"). Teams already on the box-score path (even one row) are completely excluded — those are maintained live by the adapter precedence in `imports.ts`/`games.ts`.
- For those teams only, groups legacy `'game'` rows by `(team_id, session_date)` into **one shared** `baseball_games` row per team-date (never per-player — mirrors #827's `buildBoxScoreRowsForSessions` fix), skipping any date where a `baseball_games` row already exists (defensive: never risks a duplicate).
- Copies each attending player's legacy row into a `baseball_box_score_batting` row (always) and a `baseball_box_score_pitching` row (only when `innings_pitched > 0`), computing avg/obp/slg/ops and era/whip/k9/bb9 with the **same formulas** `games.ts`'s `computeBattingRates`/`computePitchingRates` use — including outs-based innings-pitched conversion (`src/lib/baseball/innings.ts`; the `X.1`/`X.2` notation is thirds of an inning, not a decimal fraction).
- `practice`/`other` rows are never read. Legacy rows are never mutated (copy-only).
- Every id is deterministic (SHA-1, RFC4122-v5-shaped bytes, own namespace `baseball-legacy-backfill-379` — distinct from #827's seed-script namespace), and every insert is `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` — re-applying is always a no-op.
- **Deliberately does not** call `recalculate_baseball_season_stats()` / touch `baseball_player_season_stats` — that table can already hold an independent `season_totals`-imported baseline for a zero-box-score team, and the recalc RPC's `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` would silently overwrite it. Documented in the migration + runbook as an opt-in, per-team follow-up instead.

No new database function is created (id derivation is inlined CTEs using `pgcrypto.digest` + `get_byte`/`set_byte`, already-installed extension) — nothing new to REVOKE from anon or pin a search_path on.

## Also included

`docs/baseball/legacy-backfill-runbook.md` — what it does, how the orchestrator applies it via `mcp__supabase__apply_migration`, pre/post-check queries, and the rollback story (copy-only ⇒ rollback recomputes the same deterministic ids from current `baseball_player_stats` and deletes exact matches — spelled out as a runnable 3-statement `DELETE`, no bookkeeping table needed).

## Verification (gate evidence)

- `npm run typecheck` — clean, exit 0 (no `.ts`/`.tsx` touched; ran repo-wide as a no-op confirmation).
- `npx eslint --max-warnings 0 <touched>` — N/A, touched files are `.sql`/`.md` only (outside the lint glob `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`).
- `npx vitest run <affected>` — N/A, no test files affected (no code changed).
- `node scripts/check-cycles.mjs` — `OK — 33 known cycles, none new`.
- **End-to-end exercised** against a disposable local Postgres 16 instance (schema mirrored from the real prod-baseline + drift migrations; never any shared/Supabase project) with fixtures covering: a normal batter, a two-way partial-innings pitcher (`6.2`/`4.1` IP, confirmed exact era/whip/k9/bb9 by hand), a duplicate same-player-same-date legacy row (dedupe picked one deterministic winner), a team already on box-score (fully untouched), and a team with a pre-existing scheduled game on a legacy date (that date correctly skipped). Confirmed a second run inserts zero additional rows anywhere (idempotent), and a dry-run rollback recompute+delete matched exactly the rows created and nothing else.

## Status

Written, **not applied**. Do not `apply_migration` without Nick's explicit go — see the runbook.
