`docs/audits/BASEBALL_REGRESSION_PACK_2026-07-03.md` has the full table, but the headline: **#406 (staff player-scope RLS) is enforcement 100% in Postgres RLS** (`can_view_baseball_player`) with no TypeScript mirror — a vitest mock would only prove the mock's own behavior, not the real policy. True atomic-capacity-under-concurrency for #442 has the same limitation. While building the drift guard, found that PR #736 fixed the *symptom* of the admin-panel outage (restored the admin row, added `admin_allowlist`/`is_super_admin()`) but never migrated the RPC layer off the bug that caused it:

- All 11 `get_admin_*_rollup` SECURITY DEFINER functions (6 directly, 5 via the shared `__admin_rollup_b_gate()` helper) still gated solely on `users.role = 'admin'`. Bridge's app-layer gate (`requireSuperAdmin()`) only checks `SUPER_ADMIN_USER_IDS` + `admin_allowlist` and never looks at `users.role` — so the original failure ("`requireSuperAdmin()` still passed, but admin panel RPCs died with 42501") was still fully reproducible by *anything* that flips `users.role`, not just the specific baseball-onboarding path already patched.
- `guard_users_role_self_change()` blocked self-*escalation* to a role outside player/coach, but explicitly allowed `'coach'`/`'player'` as `NEW.role` — i.e. it did nothing to stop a super admin's own onboarding/profile-update flow from silently self-demoting `admin` → `coach`, which is the literal #736 incident. That specific transition was never actually blocked.

**Migration `admin_rollup_consistent_super_admin_gate`** (applied to production, verified live via `pg_get_functiondef`):
- Every rollup gate now accepts EITHER `public.is_super_admin()` OR the legacy `users.role = 'admin'` check — additive only; verified pre-change that `admin_allowlist` and `users.role='admin'` are the same single user, so no currently authorized caller loses access.
- `guard_users_role_self_change()` now also blocks `OLD.role = 'admin'` → `NEW.role IN (coach, player)` for allowlisted super admins.

**New:** `scripts/db/check-supabase-drift.mjs` (`npm run db:drift:check`) — read-only guard covering #651 columns, golf drift shape, #728 function body, #772 linked-lint functions, #732 rate_limits, admin rollup RPC existence + consistent gating, and the role-demotion guard. Queries `information_schema`/`pg_proc` directly rather than `schema_migrations`, per the drift report's finding that the migration ledger can't be trusted alone here.

### Also surfaced (documented, not fixed in this PR)

- `npm run test:rls` (`vitest --project rls`) matches **zero** files under its own `*.rls.test.{ts,tsx}` glob — there are no RLS-specific test files anywhere in the repo, so that CI lane silently runs generic unit tests under the "rls" label instead of testing RLS policies. Same "safety net that never actually runs" pattern as the dead `scripts/__tests__/` secrets guard fixed in #774.

## What this PR does NOT do

- No `supabase db push`, `migration repair`, or `db reset`.
- No issues closed (recommendations only).
- Does not fix the `test:rls` gap or the migration-ledger mismatch — both documented for a dedicated follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] Migration applied to production via Supabase MCP `apply_migration`, approved via the native approval card (sensitive admin-RPC mutation).
- [x] Verified live: all 8 functions (`__admin_rollup_b_gate` + 6 rollups + `guard_users_role_self_change`) now reference `is_super_admin()`.
- [x] `npm run test:rls` (4472 passed / 39 skipped) and `npm run test:run` (4398 passed / 39 skipped) — both green post-migration.
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean.
- [x] `src/lib/types/database.ts` regenerated by the pre-commit hook — diff was empty (function body changes don't affect generated types).

## Related

- #774 — P0 fix for the still-live hardcoded service-role secrets (shipped first, per the brief's priority order).

## Summary

Issue #516 ("P0: production service_role key hardcoded in 9 tracked scripts") is marked **closed**, but a 2026-07-03 re-verification pass found the closure was incomplete:

- All 9 scripts named in #516 (`check-policies.ts`, `check-rls.ts`, `db-health-check.ts`, `debug-player-insert.mjs`, `diagnose-rls.ts`, `fix-auth.mjs`, `import-via-api.mjs`, `list-orphan-players.ts`, `run-sql.mjs`) **still had the literal production `service_role` JWT** hardcoded in tracked source, confirmed via `gitleaks` + manual read of every file.
- One additional script not named in #516, `scripts/run-migration.mjs`, had the same hardcoded prod URL.
- Two of those scripts (`check-rls.ts`, `diagnose-rls.ts`) additionally hardcoded the `anon` JWT **and** a real plaintext account password used to sign in during RLS diagnostics.
- The JWT's `iat` claim decodes to 2026-01-13 and the files were last touched 2026-02-14 — consistent with the key having been rotated around 2026-01-13 and then immediately re-committed into these scripts, meaning this is very likely still the **live** production key.
- The regression guard meant to catch this (`scripts/__tests__/scripts-no-committed-secrets.test.mjs`) only scanned `seed-baseball-*.{mjs,ts}` (added for a different issue, #391) — none of the 10 offending files matched.
- That guard was **also never executed by anything**: it imported from `node:test`, but nothing in `package.json` or `.github/workflows/**` ever ran `node --test` against it, and vitest only globs `src/**`. It has never run, in CI or locally, since it was added.
- CI's `gitleaks` job scans new commits per push/PR by default, not the full existing tree, so a rule added after a secret is already committed doesn't retroactively catch it — which is why this sat green in CI the whole time.

## Changes

- Refactor all 10 scripts to read `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` / `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` from env vars, failing fast with a clear error if missing.
- Replace the hardcoded RLS-diagnostic login with `RLS_DIAGNOSTIC_TEST_EMAIL` / `RLS_DIAGNOSTIC_TEST_PASSWORD`.
- Replace `seed-rini-baseball-demo.ts`'s hardcoded demo passwords with required `RINI_DEMO_*_PASSWORD` env vars (this script sets real auth passwords, so hardcoded literals are worse than typical test fixtures).
- Broaden `scripts-no-committed-secrets.test.mjs` to scan every file in `scripts/`, not just `seed-baseball-*`, and add a regression check for the specific leaked password string.
- Port that guard to vitest and wire it into the `unit` project (`vitest.config.ts`) so `npm test` / CI's `Unit tests` job actually execute it.
- Document new env vars in `.env.example`.
- Add `docs/operations/2026-07-03-p0-service-role-key-rotation-runbook.md` — the maintainer-only follow-up (rotate the live key, rotate the demo password, decide on git-history scrubbing) that no tool available to this session can perform.

## What this PR does NOT do

- **Does not rotate the live key.** That requires Supabase dashboard access to regenerate the JWT secret, then updating Vercel (prod/preview/dev) + any CI secrets + local `.env.local` files. See the runbook doc for the exact checklist — please treat this as urgent.
- Does not scrub git history (the old key/password remain visible in past commits). The runbook recommends deciding this only after rotation, consistent with how a prior P0 (`docs/operations/2026-05-17-p0-runbook.md`) handled the same trade-off.
- Does not touch the other ~46 files in `scripts/__tests__/` that are also not wired into any CI job — that's a separate, larger finding called out in the runbook for its own pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `gitleaks detect --no-git -c .gitleaks.toml --source scripts` — 0 findings (previously 12 across 8 files; the one remaining hit before/after is a `'your-password'` placeholder in a comment, not a real secret).
- [x] `git grep --cached` for the leaked JWT prefix and demo password across the whole tracked tree — no hits outside `.env.example` (placeholder) and `.gitleaks.toml` (the rule itself).
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- [x] `npm run test:run` — 429 passed / 1 skipped (was 428/1; +1 for the newly-wired secrets guard), 4399 passed / 39 skipped.
- [x] `npm run build` — succeeds.
- [ ] Maintainer: complete `docs/operations/2026-07-03-p0-service-role-key-rotation-runbook.md` (rotate key, rotate demo password, update Vercel/CI/local envs).

# Lift Lab unification: program-builder → helm, CRM fixes, admin badge, e2e stabilization

One train, one deploy. Four workstreams:

## 1. Program-builder → helm_lifting_* (completes the Lift Lab schema split)
The last writers of the 16 legacy `baseball_lift_*` / `baseball_strength_*` / bodyweight / availability tables move to `helm_lifting_*` (all legacy tables verified **0 rows** in prod; 15/16 had exact helm mirrors, the 16th — `helm_lifting_group_audit` — was created + RLS'd in prod ahead of this PR):
- All program CRUD (`createLiftProgram`/`addLiftWeek`/`addLiftDay`/`addLiftSection`/`addLiftPrescription`, update/delete/reorder/duplicate/template) now writes helm tables with the family renames (`player_id→athlete_id`, org+sport scoping, `baseball_context→sport_context`).
- `publishLiftDay` no longer materializes legacy rows and bridges — it writes `helm_lifting_program_assignments`/`sessions`/`session_exercises` directly. The legacy dual-space session resolver is deleted.
- Strength groups/members/audit, maxes, PRs, bodyweight, availability → helm equivalents. Upserts target the real prod uniques (weeks `program_id,week_number`; days `week_id,day_number`; members `group_id,athlete_id`; sessions `program_assignment_id,athlete_id`; bodyweight `athlete_id,entry_date`).
- Residual legacy reads in 10 read-model/loader files swapped; dead `createLiftExercise` + `getStrengthGroupDetail` deleted.
- **After this deploys**: phase-3 graveyard migration (`20260704090000`, staged in this PR) moves all 16 legacy tables out of `public` — every FK edge stays inside `graveyard` (verified against `pg_constraint`).

## 2. CRM fixes (RLS already applied to prod; code here)
- `demo_requests` had no SELECT/UPDATE policy → the admin Inbound Leads list showed 0 while the dashboard badge counted 3 (a real Heidelberg lead sat invisible since June 11). Admin-gated policies applied + mirrored.
- Inbound Leads view used status values the CHECK constraint rejects (`new`/`converted`) — now mapped to the real domain (`pending`/`completed`); Add-to-CRM no longer silently fails.
- `get_crm_events_in_range` + `get_crm_time_to_open` were EXECUTE-able by any authenticated user → admin-gated (applied + mirrored).

## 3. /admin/teams/[id] health badge
Detail page fed `classifyTeamHealth` only completed rounds by current roster members; /admin/golf uses unfiltered team activity. Detail now exposes `teamLastActivity` (unfiltered, one cheap query) for the badge; per-player roster columns unchanged.

## 4. e2e stabilization (root causes from CI-log forensics — no local browser runs)
- **The recurring red gate**: `seed-baseball-demo.ts` never reset existing CI demo passwords, so secret drift + Playwright retries fed the 10-attempt DB lockout every run. Seed now force-sets the two synthetic CI identities' passwords and clears lockout state.
- Fail-fast secrets verification step in `playwright.yml` (missing secret now fails in seconds, not after build+seed).
- Fixed wrong post-login URL patterns (`auth.spec.ts`, `helpers/auth.ts`), tolerant `waitForPageLoad`, 18 hard sleeps → web-first assertions, golf specs migrated to env-gated fixtures, dead placeholder specs deleted.
- Note: the main suite step remains soft-failed (advisory) — flipping it to a hard gate is a follow-up once a few honest green runs establish ground truth.

## Verification
- tsc 0 / eslint 0 (max-warnings 0 baseline) / full unit suite green — exit codes captured explicitly, no piped gates
- pgTAP RLS suites updated (group-audit → helm table; v11 visibility → helm)
- Bridge integration tests rewritten against direct-helm behavior (same protective properties: no session loss on republish, snapshot correctness)

## DB sequencing (for the record)
Applied to prod pre-merge (all additive/verified-safe with live code): `demo_requests_admin_read_update`, `crm_rpcs_admin_gate`, `helm_lifting_group_audit`. Applied post-deploy: `graveyard_legacy_liftlab_tables_phase3` (16 tables, public 275→259, graveyard 16→32).

v10.0.0

DayPicker v10 removes the public APIs deprecated in v9 and introduces a new @daypicker/react package name. Non-Gregorian calendars are now published as standalone @daypicker/* packages.

If your app already uses the current v9 API, the upgrade should be relatively small. If your app still relies on deprecated v9 APIs, those usages should be updated before upgrading.

See the full v10 changelog, the upgrade guide, and the v10 announcement for questions and upgrade feedback.

Install

npm install react-day-picker@latest

For new projects, prefer the scoped package name:

npm install @daypicker/react@latest

import { DayPicker } from "@daypicker/react";
import "@daypicker/react/style.css";

The react-day-picker package remains available in v10 for compatibility.

Breaking Changes

Deprecated navigation props removed

Removed prop Use instead
fromMonth startMonth
fromYear startMonth={new Date(year, 0)}
toMonth endMonth
toYear endMonth={new Date(year, 11)}
fromDate hidden={{ before: date }} and optionally startMonth
toDate hidden={{ after: date }} and optionally endMonth

Deprecated focus and event props removed

Changelog

Sourced from react-day-picker's changelog.

v10.0.1

Release date: 2026-05-12

This patch release fixes inline styles for component slots and adds @types/react as an optional peer dependency for strict package managers.

What's Changed

  • fix: apply inline styles to all component slots by @​gpbl in #2995
  • fix: add @types/react as an optional peer dependency by @​mrmckeb in #2997

v10.0.0

Release date: 2026-05-08

This major release introduces the @daypicker/react package name, publishes calendar add-on packages under the @daypicker/* scope, and removes public APIs that were deprecated in v9.

Upgrading to v10

Upgrading from v9 should be straightforward if your app does not use any deprecated APIs. See the upgrading guide for details. If you use one of the non-Gregorian calendars, such as Persian, Hebrew, Buddhist, Ethiopic, or Hijri, install the corresponding calendar add-on package alongside DayPicker.

Package Name

For new projects, prefer the @daypicker/react package:

import { DayPicker } from "@daypicker/react";
import "@daypicker/react/style.css";

The react-day-picker package remains available for compatibility and exposes the same DayPicker API in v10.

Calendar Packages

Calendar add-on packages are now published under the @daypicker/* scope. Install the add-on package for the calendar you need alongside @daypicker/react. For example, to use the Persian calendar:

npm install @daypicker/react @daypicker/persian

Breaking Changes

  • Removed deprecated props: fromDate, toDate, fromMonth, toMonth, fromYear, toYear, initialFocus.
  • Removed deprecated event props: onWeekNumberClick, onDayKeyUp, onDayKeyPress, onDayPointerEnter, onDayPointerLeave, onDayTouchCancel, onDayTouchEnd, onDayTouchMove, onDayTouchStart.

  • Removed deprecated DeprecatedUI compatibility typing for classNames and styles.
  • Removed deprecated DateLib exports: FormatOptions, LabelOptions, dateLib, and DateLib.Date.

Release notes

v1.61.1

Bug Fixes

  • #41365 [Bug]: Expect.Extend matcher with same name as default matcher in same expect instance overrides default matchers implementation to custom matcher
  • #41351 [Bug]: Playwright UI mode: apiRequestContext._wrapApiCall reports unexpected number of bytes (same test passes in headed mode)

  • #41311 [Bug]: [Regression]: Sync loader throws "context.conditions?.includes is not a function" on Node 22.15
  • #41371 [Regression]: Sync ESM loader (registerHooks) fails to resolve extensionless .ts subpath imports across pnpm workspace symlinks

v1.61.0

🔑 WebAuthn passkeys

New Credentials virtual authenticator, available via browserContext.credentials, lets tests register passkeys and answer navigator.credentials.create() / navigator.credentials.get() ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers:

const context = await browser.newContext();

// Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.
await context.credentials.create('example.com', {
id: credentialId,
userHandle,
privateKey,
publicKey,
});
await context.credentials.install();


const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com/login');
// The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.

You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with credentials.get(), and seed it into later tests — see Credentials for details.

🗃️ Web Storage

New WebStorage API, available via page.localStorage and page.sessionStorage, reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:

await page.localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const token = await page.localStorage.getItem('token');
const items = await page.sessionStorage.items();

New APIs

Network

  • apiResponse.securityDetails() and apiResponse.serverAddr() mirror the browser-side response.securityDetails() and response.serverAddr().

Updates `jsdom` from 28.0.0 to 29.1.1
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v29.1.1

  • Fixed 'border-radius' computed style serialization. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed computed style computation when using 'background-origin' and 'background-clip' CSS properties. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Significantly optimized initial calls to getComputedStyle(), before the cache warms up. (@​asamuzaK)

v29.1.0

  • Added basic support for the ratio CSS type. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() sometimes returning outdated results after CSS was modified. (@​asamuzaK)

v29.0.2

  • Significantly improved and sped up getComputedStyle(). Computed value rules are now applied across a broader set of properties, and include fixes related to inheritance, defaulting keywords, custom properties, and color-related values such as currentcolor and system colors. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed CSS 'background' and 'border' shorthand parsing. (@​asamuzaK)

v29.0.1

  • Fixed CSS parsing of 'border', 'background', and their sub-shorthands containing keywords or var(). (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() to return a more functional CSSStyleDeclaration object, including indexed access support, which regressed in v29.0.0.

v29.0.0

Breaking changes:

  • Node.js v22.13.0+ is now the minimum supported v22 version (was v22.12.0+).

Other changes:

  • Overhauled the CSSOM implementation, replacing the @acemir/cssom and cssstyle dependencies with fresh internal implementations built on webidl2js wrappers and the css-tree parser. Serialization, parsing, and API behavior is improved in various ways, especially around edge cases.
  • Added CSSCounterStyleRule and CSSNamespaceRule to jsdom Windows.
  • Added cssMediaRule.matches and cssSupportsRule.matches getters.
  • Added proper media query parsing in MediaList, using css-tree instead of naive comma-splitting. Invalid queries become "not all" per spec.
  • Added cssKeyframeRule.keyText getter/setter validation.
  • Added cssStyleRule.selectorText setter validation: invalid selectors are now rejected.
  • Added styleSheet.ownerNode, styleSheet.href, and styleSheet.title.
  • Added bad port blocking per the fetch specification, preventing fetches to commonly-abused ports.
  • Improved Document initialization performance by lazily initializing the CSS selector engine, avoiding ~0.5 ms of overhead per Document. (@​thypon)
  • Fixed a memory leak when stylesheets were removed from the document.
  • Fixed CSSStyleDeclaration modifications to properly trigger custom element reactions.
  • Fixed nested @media rule parsing.
  • Fixed CSSStyleSheet's "disallow modification" flag not being checked in all mutation methods.
  • Fixed XMLHttpRequest's response getter returning parsed JSON during the LOADING state instead of null.
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() crashing in XHTML documents when stylesheets contained at-rules such as @page or @font-face.
  • Fixed a potential hang in synchronous XMLHttpRequest caused by a race condition with the worker thread's idle timeout.

v28.1.0

  • Added blob.text(), blob.arrayBuffer(), and blob.bytes() methods.
  • Improved getComputedStyle() to account for CSS specificity when multiple rules apply. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Improved synchronous XMLHttpRequest performance by using a persistent worker thread, avoiding ~400ms of setup overhead on every synchronous request after the first one.
  • Improved performance of node.getRootNode(), node.isConnected, and event.dispatchEvent() by caching the root node of document-connected trees.
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() to correctly handle !important priority. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed document.getElementById() to return the first element in tree order when multiple elements share the same ID.
  • Fixed <svg> elements to no longer incorrectly proxy event handlers to the Window.
  • Fixed FileReader event timing and fileReader.result state to more closely follow the spec.

Updates `supabase` from 2.107.0 to 2.108.0
Release notes

Sourced from supabase's releases.

v2.108.0

Supabase CLI v2.108.0 — 2026-06-25

A major release completing the TypeScript port of core commands, fixing edge functions offline support, and adding several new configuration options.

Highlights

  • Edge functions fully functional offline — The Go edge-runtime is now bundled with the CLI, enabling both supabase start and functions serve to work without external dependencies. Cold-start errors are handled gracefully with automatic retries. (#5682, #5678, #5677)
  • Core database and storage commands now TypeScript-native — db diff, db pull, db dump, db query, function operations, and storage management are fully ported with behavior matching the Go CLI exactly. (#5620, #5586, #5561, #5652, #5680, #5634, #5667, #5651)

New features

  • --reveal flag for API key commands — Display unmasked API keys for easier testing and integration. (#5633)
  • issue form command — Create and manage issue forms directly from the CLI. (#5459)
  • Local SMTP configuration — Configure email delivery for local development via [local_smtp] in config.toml. (#5333)
  • Email templates from file paths — Auth email templates are now pushed from content_path in config, no longer embedded in TOML. (#5686)
  • SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY in environment output — branches get-env now includes the publishable key. (#5655)
  • Docker registry fallbacks — Container image pulls now retry across multiple registries in restricted networks. (#5660)

Improvements

  • Better diagnostics for supabase start failures — Error messages are clearer and more actionable when containers or services fail. (#5616)
  • Storage bulk delete respects rate limits — Requests are chunked to stay within API caps. (#5629)
  • Typegen with podman fallback — Automatically uses podman if Docker is unavailable. (#5658)
  • Config merge during push — remotes.* blocks are now properly merged instead of overwritten. (#5618)
  • Test database plaintext connections — Local test connections skip SSL for simpler debugging. (#5644)
  • SQL test file include resolution — \ir includes now resolve relative to the test file's directory. (#5619)
  • Auth identity synchronization — Fixed hybrid stitch/stamp identity handling. (#5607)
  • $SUPABASE_HOME honored everywhere — Environment variable is respected across all code paths. (#5624)
  • start command structured output — Container information now appears in JSON/machine output. (#5687)
  • Synchronized container image pulls — CLI waits for all images before starting containers, reducing race conditions. (#5681)
  • Private npm dependencies in function builds — Auth tokens are now forwarded to the bundler. (#5645)
  • Persistent verify_jwt configuration — Setting is no longer lost during config push. (#5348)

TypeScript port progress

  • Now served by the TypeScript shell: db diff, db pull, db dump, db query, db schema declarative, functions deploy, functions list, functions new, functions serve, seed buckets, storage ls, storage cp, storage mv, storage rm. Full behavior parity with the Go CLI. (#5620, #5586, #5561, #5652, #5680, #5634, #5667, #5651)

Plus dependency and container image updates, and internal improvements.

Full changelog: https://github.com/supabase/cli/compare/v2.107.0...v2.108.0

One branch = one deploy, per the deploy-cost rule. Overnight full-auto run (~120 verified agents across 7 workflows).

### Dead code pruned (knip, per-file verified)
- 34 dead files + 81 dead exports deleted, 85 de-exported; dead deps removed (`@capacitor/*` untouched — native runtime); 9 knip false-positives kept with documented reasons (fs-read fixtures, script imports, a webpack `index.tsx` shadow).

- **eslint: 2,158 → 0 warnings**; `lint` script now `--max-warnings 0`; ratchet baseline locked at zero. 48-agent design-token migration: `bg-white` → cream/glass surfaces, raw inputs/buttons → ui wrappers (new `ui/NativeSelect` for native-select surfaces), text-px → type scale, banned colors → tokens, `any` → real types. `no-raw-input` scoped to text-like inputs (checkbox/radio/range/file/color have no wrapper — rule now matches its own rationale); 16 stale suppressions deleted.

- **Players were 100% locked out of Lift Lab** (`resolveLiftingAccess` had no athlete-self branch; failures swallowed). Fixed + tested.

Updates `actions/github-script` from 7.1.0 to 9.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from actions/github-script's releases.

v9.0.0

New features:

  • getOctokit factory function — Available directly in the script context. Create additional authenticated Octokit clients with different tokens for multi-token workflows, GitHub App tokens, and cross-org access. See Creating additional clients with getOctokit for details and examples.
  • Orchestration ID in user-agent — The ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID environment variable is automatically appended to the user-agent string for request tracing.

Breaking changes:

  • require('@actions/github') no longer works in scripts. The upgrade to @actions/github v9 (ESM-only) means require('@actions/github') will fail at runtime. If you previously used patterns like const { getOctokit } = require('@actions/github') to create secondary clients, use the new injected getOctokit function instead — it's available directly in the script context with no imports needed.
  • getOctokit is now an injected function parameter. Scripts that declare const getOctokit = ... or let getOctokit = ... will get a SyntaxError because JavaScript does not allow const/let redeclaration of function parameters. Use the injected getOctokit directly, or use var getOctokit = ... if you need to redeclare it.
  • If your script accesses other @actions/github internals beyond the standard github/octokit client, you may need to update those references for v9 compatibility.

Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action's releases.

v4.36.2

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943

No user facing changes.

v4.36.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

v4.35.5

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

v4.35.4

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

v4.35.3

  • Configurations for private registries that use Cloudsmith or GCP OIDC are now accepted. #3850
  • Best-effort connection tests for private registries now use GET requests instead of HEAD for better compatibility with various registry implementations. For NuGet feeds, the test is now always performed against the service index. #3853
  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.3. #3865

v4.35.2

## One-train consolidation of the 2026-07-03 admin-dashboard fixes

Prod admin dashboard (`/admin`, `/admin/golf`) has been erroring since the Bridge v2 + DB-hardening deploys. This PR consolidates every open fix onto **one branch so main gets exactly one Vercel deploy** (supersedes #736, #737, #738, #739; includes #734 via the train2 merge).

### What was actually broken (root-caused)

1. **`get_admin_rounds_rollup` 42501 Forbidden on `/admin/golf`** — every `get_admin_*_rollup` RPC gates on `users.role='admin'`; baseball onboarding's service-role `users` upsert clobbered the super-admin's row down to `coach`. The role was restored live at 2026-07-03 04:18Z; this train makes the demotion impossible to reintroduce (`ensureUserRowPreservingAdmin`, from #736).
2. **`/golf/dashboard` RSC crash** (digest 3173807121, "Functions cannot be passed to Client Components") — icon component types crossed the RSC boundary via `EmptyState` (from #737).
3. **PR #739's branch was build-broken** — `shouldPersistAdminTables` was a sync export from a `'use server'` file. Completed here: moved to `src/lib/telemetry-gate.ts`, all 4 importers repointed, writer tests use the `ADMIN_EVENTS_FORCE_CAPTURE=1` hatch, new gate unit tests.

### Contents

- **P0 (#736)**: baseball onboarding can no longer demote admins; honest Bridge panel fallback with real retry.
- **P1 (#737)**: stop passing icon component types across the RSC boundary.
- **P2 (#738)**: baseball #651 settings-OS columns + catching `event_type` reconcile migration (already applied to prod, in-repo as source of truth).
- **Telemetry (#739 + completion)**: prod-only incident feed (`shouldPersistAdminTables` in its own module), Next control-flow filter, demo-sessions force-dynamic, retention pg_cron mirror.
- **train2**: disable dependabot auto-rebase (rebase pushes billed preview builds), docs regen (#734).
- **Gate hygiene**: lint ratchet re-locked 2275→2158; telemetry writer tests fixed for the prod gate.

### Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors
- lint-ratchet: green, baseline re-locked
- Unit suite: **4287 passed, 0 failed** (39 skipped)
- 3-lens adversarial review (build/RSC, DB/auth, telemetry) over the full consolidated diff: see PR comment

body:
Prod runtime error on /golf/dashboard + /golf/dashboard/coachhelm: `Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components` with payload `{$$typeof, render: function, displayName}` — a lucide **forwardRef component type** crossing the server→client boundary.

`EmptyState` is `'use client'` (framer-motion) and takes `icon?: LucideIcon` (a component TYPE). Four server components passed icons that way — worst is the golf `(dashboard)` group's `not-found.tsx`, so **every `notFound()` under the dashboard** (deleted round/player/qualifier ids) crashed to the generic RSC error instead of the branded 404. That's why the error shows on multiple dashboard routes at low volume since 06-22 (10 hits / 6 users).

Fix: `EmptyState.icon` now also accepts a rendered **element** (serializable); the chip sizes element icons via `[&>svg]` so they render identically. The four server call sites (`not-found`, `travel`, `stats/team` ×2) pass `icon={<Icon strokeWidth={1.75} />}`. Client callers passing component types are untouched.

Verify after deploy: hit /golf/dashboard/rounds/<bad-id> → branded 404, and digest 3173807121 stops appearing in runtime logs.

body:
## Root cause (H1 confirmed, H2 ruled out)

Every `get_admin_*_rollup` SECURITY-DEFINER function gates on `users.role='admin'`. The Bridge app layer gates on the `SUPER_ADMIN_USER_IDS` env allowlist. Those two agreed until **baseball onboarding's users upsert** (`{ onConflict: 'id' }`, service-role client, no `ignoreDuplicates`) clobbered the allowlisted super-admin's row from `admin` → `coach`. After that, `requireSuperAdmin()` passed and every panel's RPC died with 42501. H2 (session not reaching the RPC) ruled out: `fetchAdminRollupA` uses the request-scoped server client, and the RPC succeeds with only a `sub` claim in a simulated call.

## Already done live (no deploy needed)
- `users.role` restored to `admin` for admin@helmsportslabs.com (04:18Z).
- Verified: simulated authenticated calls to `get_admin_dashboard_rollup` / `get_admin_rounds_rollup` return data; exactly one `role='admin'` row and it IS the allowlist entry — the two admin models agree again.

## This PR (prevents recurrence + honest UX)
- `ensureUserRowPreservingAdmin()` at both baseball onboarding users-row writes: insert-if-missing, player↔coach conversion allowed, an existing `admin` is NEVER overwritten. (Golf onboarding already used `ignoreDuplicates` and could not demote.)
- `PanelBoundary`/`PanelStale`: the fallback claimed "showing last known data" while rendering none. Copy now says "temporarily unavailable" and ships a real retry (`router.refresh()` + boundary remount).
- `panel-boundary.test.tsx`: asserts the honest copy, the retry path, and that the misleading claim never returns (7/7 green).

Chosen model per sweep option 2: `users.role='admin'` stays the DB source of truth, env allowlist stays the app-layer second factor, and onboarding can no longer un-sync them — only one super-admin exists, so an `is_super_admin()` table indirection adds surface without adding safety today.

## Owner ask (verbatim, from tonight's live review)

> I need to see every single thing golf is doing… every team should have their own page dedicated to activity and errors… more insight… more green.

## What shipped, per lane

**Data layer** (`feat/bridge-v2-data`)
- `@/lib/admin/data/activity.ts` — `fetchGolfActivity()`, cursor-paginated across rounds, signups, sign-ins, insights, messages, events, demo sessions, documents, and errors.
- `@/lib/admin/data/team-detail.ts` — `fetchTeamDetail()`, fail-soft per-section (team, coaches, roster, daily activity, errors, CoachHelm usage).
- `@/lib/admin/data/briefing.ts` — `fetchBriefing()`, severity-ordered attention/watch items (max 6) for the dashboard strip.
- `@/lib/admin/data/team-scope.ts` — shared team-id → user-id/conversation-id resolution used by every scoped query.

**Activity tab** (`feat/bridge-v2-activity`)
- New `/admin/activity` page: full cross-team "everything golf is doing" feed, kind filter chips, team filter, cursor-based load-more (no offset pagination), day-grouped rows, native Fairway styling.

**Team + user depth** (`feat/bridge-v2-teams`)
- New `/admin/teams/[id]` page: coaches, roster, 30-day activity trend, recent errors, CoachHelm usage — every team now has its own dedicated activity+errors page as asked.
- New `/admin/users/[id]` `EngagementPanel` — per-user round/insight/review counts and recent activity, wired into the existing user detail page.
- `TeamHealthTable` rows now link through to the new team pages.

**Green identity pass** (`feat/bridge-v2-green`)
- Briefing strip on `/admin` (severity-ordered attention/watch chips, all six lanes of Fairway signal wired to real data).
- Graphite numerals + green delta chips on `KpiTile`/`StatTile`; helm-green hairline rules under section headers; 2px green left edge on key panels; green-primary charts. Red reserved for genuine errors (kept as-is on `/admin/errors`, `/admin/deploys`, `/admin/jobs`).

## Query-discipline statement

Every new query is scoped and single-purpose — no legacy `/golf/admin` monolith reuse:
- Cursor pagination by timestamp (`created_at`/`entered_at`), not offset — used in `activity.ts`, `team-detail.ts`.
- Counts via `.select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })` everywhere a number (not rows) is needed — `team-page-extras.ts`, `user-engagement.ts`, `briefing.ts`.
- Every list query carries a `LIMIT` (`.limit()`/`.range()`); no fetch-everything-then-compute-in-JS.
- No N+1: batched `.in('id', […])` / `.in('user_id', […])` lookups (e.g. document uploader names, team→user-id resolution) instead of per-row fetches.
- Legacy `src/app/golf/admin/**` was read only as a feature map, never imported from or reused as UI.

## No legacy UI

All new surfaces are native Bridge/Fairway components (`Surface`, `StatusPill`, `StatTile`, `KpiTile`, `TrendChart`, `PanelStates`, `FilterPill`, `Button`) — nothing carried over from `src/app/golf/admin/**` styling.

## Everything clicks

- Activity feed rows → `href` from `ActivityItem` (round/team/user/error targets).
- `TeamHealthTable` team names → `/admin/teams/[id]`.
- User references → `/admin/users/[id]`.
- Errors → existing `/admin/errors/[fingerprint]` detail route.

## indexNotes (no migrations run — for the data-lane owner / next migration batch)

Candidate indexes based on the actual filter/sort predicates in the new queries (all currently unindexed hot paths per code inspection, no migration applied per machine rules):
- `golf_rounds (team_id, status, created_at desc)` — hit by activity feed, team detail, briefing, and user engagement round counts.
- `golf_rounds (player_id, created_at desc)` — user engagement panel.
- `admin_events (event_type, created_at desc)` and `admin_events (team_id, event_type, created_at desc)` — activity feed logins/errors, team detail error list, briefing critical-error strip.
- `admin_events (event_type, severity, created_at desc)` — briefing's error/critical filter.
- `golf_coach_insights (team_id, created_at desc)` and `golf_coach_insights (player_id, created_at desc)` / `(coach_id, created_at desc)` — activity feed + user/team engagement.
- `golf_messages (conversation_id, created_at desc)` — activity feed message events.
- `golf_events (team_id, created_at desc)` — activity feed event_created items.
- `golf_documents (team_id, created_at desc)` — activity feed document uploads.
- `golf_demo_sessions (entered_at desc)` — activity feed demo sessions (no team scoping possible; table has no team_id/user_id).
- `golf_team_coach_staff (coach_id)` / `(team_id)` — team detail + user engagement coach→team resolution.
- `golf_coachhelm_llm_calls (coach_id, created_at desc)` and `golf_coachhelm_llm_budget (coach_id, date)` — team detail CoachHelm usage panel.

## Gate results

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors.
- `npm run lint` (full repo) — 0 errors, 2278 warnings, well under the 6000 ratchet ceiling; **0 errors, 0 warnings** on every file this PR touches (verified with a targeted `eslint` pass over the exact touched-file diff vs. base).

All 3 failures are in `src/lib/baseball/__tests__/program-type-nav-variants.test.ts` (baseball nav-variant ordering) and are pre-existing: reproduced identically (same assertion diffs) on `origin/fix/bridge-mobile-login-landing` via an isolated worktree before merging any Bridge V2 lane. Unrelated to this PR's admin/golf changes.

## What & why

**Requirement:** reopening the app (or leaving it idle) for **>5 minutes** must require signing in again, instead of the app silently auto-loading the persisted session.

## Root cause
- The Supabase **middleware refreshed the session on every request with no idle check** — that's the "auto-loads you in".
- The existing client timeout was **30 min** with a **fail-open bug**: the `last_activity` cookie expired *at* the timeout, so a reopen after the window found no cookie and treated it as "just active" → never logged out.

## Fix (two layers, one shared marker)
- **`session-idle-shared.ts`** (new): `sb_last_activity` cookie, **5-min** window, **30-day** cookie life (so a real reopen is always "present + stale", never fail-open), pure helpers.
- **Middleware** (`updateSession`): server-side enforcement on authenticated `golf`/`baseball`/`lifting` page requests — `signOut({scope:'local'})` + redirect to `/{sport}/login?message=session_expired`, clearing `sb-*-auth-token` (union of request + response cookie names) and the marker. **Absent/fresh marker → allow** (a brand-new login is never bounced).
- **Client hook** (`useSessionActivity`): 30 → 5 min, writes the shared cookie on real interaction, checks on mount **before** refreshing the marker, and re-checks on `visibilitychange`/`pageshow` (mobile reopen from bfcache fires no network request).

`/api` and `/admin` are intentionally out of scope (admin has its own 3-layer gate).

## Verification
- ✅ Typecheck (0 errors), ESLint (0), **32 unit tests** incl. new coverage locking the 5-min window + the fail-open-on-absent guarantee.
- ✅ **Security review** (fresh-context agent): no mass-logout / redirect-loop / bypass; cookie-clear mechanics verified against `@supabase/ssr` + Next edge-runtime cookie internals.

**Manual QA to run on the preview:**
1. Log in → wait >5 min with the tab closed → open a dashboard URL → should land on the login page with "Session expired".
2. Log in → keep tab open & idle >5 min → auto-logout via the interval.
3. iOS Safari: background >5 min → foreground → logout via `visibilitychange`/`pageshow`.
4. Active use (clicking/typing) must **not** log you out.

## Follow-ups (not blocking)
- **M1:** hoist `SessionActivityProvider` to all authenticated surfaces (onboarding/welcome/**lifting** shells currently rely on the middleware catch-on-next-navigation).
- **M2:** add a middleware idle-branch integration test (request → redirect + `Set-Cookie` assertions).

> Done out-of-band today: cleared my shared `login_attempts` lockout row — 10 failed attempts from `::1` (local dev testing) had locked the shared prod account. Brute-force policy unchanged.

body:
## What broke tonight

Commit `cbdc9f040` shipped the Helm Bridge `/admin` console to prod. Nick hit it on his phone right after deploy and found four things wrong on the Overview (390px viewport), plus the login flow didn't route super-admins into the console at all. This PR combines two disjoint fix lanes (`fix/bridge-login-landing` + `fix/bridge-mobile-overview`) into one branch — no file overlap between them, both merged clean, no conflicts.

## Nick's screenshot findings → fixes

1. **Horizontal overflow** on incident titles/URLs and the "Sentry not configured" helper line. `truncate` (nowrap+ellipsis) only clips when every ancestor has a definite width, which isn't true in these flex/grid layouts. Swapped to `break-words [overflow-wrap:anywhere]` + `min-w-0` on the ancestors, across `TriageQueue`, the errors list, the fingerprint detail page, and the auth-tab lockouts/sign-in feed — every surface rendering a raw error string, URL, or fingerprint.

2. **KPI grid orphaning** — `StatTile`'s starved ("Not enough data yet") branch rendered its eyebrow label as a bare sibling *above* a separately-bordered `InsufficientData` box, instead of one panel like the ready state. Fixed by giving both states the same `bg-surface-sunken rounded-fw-md p-4` chrome, adding `h-full` to the panel + `KpiTile`'s `Link` (paired with `items-stretch` on the grid) so every cell in a phone-width 2-col row shares a height, and dropping the icon in this dense embedding so a starved tile doesn't dominate the viewport.

3. **Stray blue focus rings** — `KpiTile`'s `Link` used `focus-visible:outline-2` with no color/style, so the browser's default blue ring painted through (iOS Safari can leave a tapped link `:focus-visible` across a client refresh). Replaced with the same `outline-accent-500` token every other Fairway interactive element already uses (calendar, data-table, date-picker) — a real fix, not a new affordance.

4. **React #418 hydration mismatch — root cause confirmed**: `TriageQueue.tsx` and `SessionsPanel.tsx` are Client Components calling `new Date(...).toLocaleTimeString()`/`toLocaleString()` directly in render. That resolves against the *runtime's* default timezone — Vercel's serverless functions run UTC, Nick's iPhone resolves its own local zone — so the same instant produces two different strings: one baked into SSR HTML, a different one computed client-side during hydration. Deterministic, not a timing race, and it fires on every load where the triage queue has any item. Added `LocalTime` (small `'use client'` component) that renders a fixed placeholder through SSR and the client's first pass, then swaps to the locale string post-mount (`suppressHydrationWarning` as belt-and-suspenders, same pattern as `ReminderBadge.tsx`). Plain Server Components using the same calls (`AdminStatusBanner`, `PanelStates`, the errors/auth/fingerprint pages) were left alone — they render once server-side and aren't re-executed client-side, so they can't mismatch.

5. **Login didn't land super-admins in `/admin`** — a super-admin account can be team-less (no `golf_coaches`/`golf_players` row), which routed it into onboarding instead of the console. `loginActionImpl` now checks `isSuperAdminUserId` (pure env-var parse + Set lookup, same allowlist middleware/`requireSuperAdmin` already use — zero extra DB cost for ordinary users) *before* the coach/player resolution, and returns `redirectTo: '/admin'`. A caller-supplied `returnTo` still wins — this is only the default when none is present.

## The `returnTo` security note (same-origin-only)

`isSafeInternalPath` (shared by login, welcome, and the client fast-path) now also allows `/admin` and `/admin/**` alongside the existing `/golf/` and `/baseball/` prefixes, via `isAdminPath` — a pure string check with **no auth decision of its own**. This lets the middleware's `?returnTo=/admin<path>` redirect (for logged-out visitors hitting `/admin`) survive the login round-trip. It does **not** widen who can reach `/admin`: the actual gate is still the existing 3-layer check (middleware → `requireSuperAdmin` → RLS), which runs downstream of this redirect regardless of how the user arrived at the URL. Absolute URLs, protocol-relative (`//evil.com`), backslash tricks, and embedded whitespace/control chars are all still rejected — covered by new tests in `safe-redirect.test.ts`.

## Zero-behavior-change statement for ordinary users

- Ordinary players/coaches: `isSuperAdminUserId` returns `false` for every non-allowlisted id (fails closed on missing/empty env too — tested), so the login action falls straight through to the exact same onboarding/team redirect logic as before. No new query, no new branch taken.
- Every mobile-overview fix is scoped to `src/app/admin/**` and the shared `StatTile`/`KpiTile` primitives' *admin-density* rendering path — the “ready” KPI branch and every non-admin consumer of `StatTile` keep their existing markup aside from the additive `h-full`.
- The 3-layer admin gate (middleware → `requireSuperAdmin` → RLS) is untouched by both lanes.

## Gate results

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean, 0 errors
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing repo-wide warning count under the `--max-warnings 6000` ratchet; **0 errors and 0 warnings** on all 15 touched files individually)
- `npx vitest run src/app/admin src/lib/admin src/lib/utils/__tests__/safe-redirect.test.ts` — **128 test files / 848 tests passed**, including `coverage-contract.foundation.test.ts`
- `npx vitest run src/app/golf/actions/__tests__/coverage-contract.b5.test.ts` — 4/4 passed

No migrations. No baseball/lifting/crm app code touched. Not merged — this PR combines both lanes for Ship-stage review.

- **Page's one job:** convert a first-time visitor (coach or player) into a demo view or a team join — the whole scroll is one continuous argument for "the program, seen clearly."
- **Primary action:** "See it in action" (kelly green, real link → `/golf/demo`) appears in the nav, the hero, and the final CTA — always reachable, never a dead button.
- **Visual hierarchy:** M1 hero photo-dark cinema → M2 ecru editorial claim → M3 deep-pine pinned product-cinema (the effort-signal moment) → M4 sport-fork diptych → M5 ecru→pine intelligence proof → M6 warm player moment → M7 ecru honesty band → M8 photo-inset final ask → M9 pine footer.
- **Scan pattern:** vertical, one deliberate beat per moment — no competing motion within a section (CLAUDE.md's "one signature move" discipline); glass grammar (3 grades) and the ecru/pine/clay/kelly-green/brass palette repeat every ~900px so the eye never resets.
- **What got demoted:** the old page's dark-hero-only, zero-signup landing is gone; email-capture-first CTA is replaced by real routed CTAs (demo page, invite-code join); golf-only nav/footer links are now sport-balanced.

## Owned files
`src/components/marketing/first-light/**` (new — CSS, fonts, scroll primitives, 9 moment stubs, barrel, CONTRACTS.md), `public/marketing/first-light/photos/*.jpg` (temp graded-gradient placeholders — see CONTRACTS.md), `src/app/page.tsx` (rewritten composition, contract-preserving).

CONTRACTS.md is the ownership map for the 6 lanes building on this scaffold (`landing-hero+nav`, `landing-editorial`, `landing-cinema`, `landing-portals+cta`) — read it before touching a `moments/M*.tsx` file.

## Design-bar checklist
- [x] Palette: ecru `#F5F1E6` / pine `#143527` / clay `#B0703C` / kelly green `#16A34A` (only saturated accent) / brass `#B08D57` — CSS vars in `first-light.css`
- [x] Fraunces (serif/display) via `next/font/google`, no italic anywhere (feedback_helm_no_italic_accent_word)
- [x] No centered-white-card-on-cream; no generic gray borders/harsh shadows
- [x] Motion: transform/opacity only; `position: sticky` for M3's pin; house ease `[0.16,1,0.3,1]`
- [x] `prefers-reduced-motion` → fully static (verified: zero console errors, incl. zero hydration mismatches — see notes below)
- [x] Mobile 390px → calm, non-wrapping layout (nav collapses to brand + one CTA)
- [x] ≤2 backdrop-blur layers per viewport; WKWebView `@supports` fallback in place
- [x] Every CTA has a real handler (`/golf/demo`, `/golf/join`, `/products#...`, real footer links)

## Verify results
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors
- `npx eslint` (all changed files): 0 errors, 0 warnings
- Live-verified on port 3010 with Playwright, full-page scroll top-to-bottom at 1440×900 and 390×844, plus `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulation — zero console errors in every mode. Frames saved to the workflow scratchpad.
- Found and fixed 6 real bugs surfaced only by live scroll-interaction testing (not caught by tsc/eslint):
  1. Tailwind can't apply an opacity modifier to a `var()` arbitrary color (`text-[var(--x)]/60` silently drops) — swapped to `rgba(var(--x-rgb), N)` everywhere.
  2. `m.*` components need a `LazyMotion` ancestor or every animation prop no-ops — added the one shared `LazyMotion` to `LenisRoot`.
  3. A `whileInView` mask-reveal that observes its own transformed/clipped child deadlocks (self-clipping paradox) — `MaskedReveal` now observes the untransformed wrapper and propagates via variants.
  4. Motion v12's native `ScrollTimeline` acceleration for `target`+`offset` `useScroll` doesn't reliably update through a cross-component `useTransform` chain — `useScrollProgress` is now a hand-rolled, always-reactive scroll listener.
  5. `<main overflow-x-hidden>` implicitly promotes `overflow-y` to `auto` (CSS spec), turning `<main>` into its own scroll container and breaking every `position: sticky` descendant — switched to `overflow-x-clip`.
  6. A plain `.fl-glass-2 { position: relative }` rule beat a consumer's `absolute` utility on source-order — now zero-specificity via `:where()`.
  7. Structural reduced-motion branching with framer-motion's own `useReducedMotion()` throws a real hydration mismatch for actual reduced-motion users — added an SSR-safe `usePrefersReducedMotion` (`useSyncExternalStore`) for the two primitives that branch DOM structure.

body:
Stacked on #679.

## LAYOUT BRIEF
- **Job:** let college/JUCO staff read a saved, source-cited postgame action review and turn each item into a real object (timeline note, practice-planner backlog item, resolved/dismissed) without leaving the page.
- **Primary action:** Generate/Regenerate review for the target game (header CTA, mirrored in the no-review empty state).
- **Hierarchy:** 1st = the review header card (title, score, source-status, confidence GradeStamp — "is this trustworthy?"); 2nd = the five action sections (Workload → Timeline → Practice Focus → Staff Decisions → Video), each item's source citation always visible; 3rd = per-item Resolve/Dismiss/Convert row (secondary, revealed after the citation).
- **Scan pattern:** masthead → game picker (which game am I reviewing) → header card (trust check) → section-by-section item cards (title + priority + citation, then action).
- **Demoted:** the standalone confidence-percent badge (folded into the GradeStamp), the amber import-warning text callout (now a quiet InkBadge stamp, not a colored box).

## What changed
`postgame/page.tsx` + `PostgameReviewClient.tsx` rebuilt onto the Living-Annual kit (`SectionMasthead`, `PaperCard`, `InkBadge`, `GradeStamp`, `HairlineRule`, `Eyebrow`, `StatReadout`, `EditorsLetter`, `Reveal`, `LiveDot`, `pressableClass`). Presentation only:

- **Preserved verbatim:** `getPostgameReview` read-model, `generatePostgameReview` / `convertPostgameItemToTimeline` / `convertPostgameItemToPractice` / `setPostgameItemDisposition` server actions, `SourceTrustBadge`, all `toast`/`router` UX feedback.
- **All 3 gate layers stay:** middleware `STAFF_CAPABILITY_ROUTES`, `getPostgameReview()`'s `authorized` flag, and RLS — page.tsx's coach-type / organization_id redirects and the read-model call are byte-identical.
- **All 6 empty branches stay, same forbidden-vs-setup split:** error / forbidden / setup / no-games / no-review / zero-items — each now an `<EditorsLetter>` (never `<EmptyState>`/yellow box) with its original copy intact, `unauthorizedReason` still driving the forbidden-vs-setup fork.
- Class B surface (no existing fork) — rewrote the client in place, page wrapped in `fairwayScope('min-h-full')` on both return paths (matches the `command-center` precedent: no `isRedesignEnabled` fork, the shell gates the subtree).

### Judgment calls
- Spec note said "game-picker pills → `InkBadge`/`ToolRailStack` + `LiveDot`"; `ToolRailStack` is a 20-80 tool-grade stack and doesn't fit a horizontal game list, so pills compose `InkBadge` (label) + `LiveDot` (has-review) inside a `pressableClass` tab button instead.
- The "forbidden" empty branch needed custom copy (not the fixed `EmptyIssue variant="generic"` preset), so it renders via `<EditorsLetter>` directly with an `InkBadge label="Restricted"` in the action slot as the "lock" treatment — matching the pattern already used elsewhere in this migration (roster's `aggregatesWarning`, scout-packets' `bg-amber-50` banner) for states needing bespoke copy.
- Added a "Complete setup" CTA (`Link` to `/baseball/dashboard/program`) to the setup empty state — a presentation-only addition, parity with command-center's equivalent branch.

## Design-bar self-audit
- [x] Deeper cream via `PaperCard`, never a white card.
- [x] `font-annual` (Space Grotesk) scale throughout; no Inter/Roboto.
- [x] Green rules (`HairlineRule ink="team"`) + green leaders/status (`InkBadge tone="team"`); numerals are graphite `StatReadout`/`GradeStamp`, never washed out.
- [x] Macro-whitespace: `space-y-8` sections, `p-6/p-7` cards.
- [x] Double-bezel card architecture via `PaperCard` (letterpress inset, registration tick on the review header).
- [x] `Reveal` for entrance (no bespoke framer-motion/LazyMotion — removed the old hand-rolled `fadeIn`).
- [x] `EditorsLetter` for all 6 empty/error states — grepped the diff for `bg-warning`/`amber`/`yellow`: zero hits (only doctrine comments).
- [x] a11y: `role="tablist"`/`role="tab"`/`aria-selected` kept on the game picker; focus-visible rings via `pressableClass`; `ariaLabel`s on `StatReadout`s.
- [x] Mobile: all badge/action rows are `flex-wrap`; no fixed-width overflow.
- [x] Banned list clear: no Inter/Roboto, no drop shadows (`PaperCard`'s letterpress inset only), no 1px gray borders, no `ease-in-out`/linear easing (kit's `EASE_PRESS`/`EASE_GLIDE` only).

## Verify
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → 0 errors.
- `npx eslint "src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/postgame/page.tsx" "src/components/baseball/postgame/PostgameReviewClient.tsx"` → 0 errors, 0 warnings (one `helm/no-raw-button` warning resolved with a documented disable comment, matching `RiskFeedStrip.tsx`'s precedent for the same pattern).

body:
## Root cause

Two compounding bugs in the Discover data path, both confirmed against the actual shooter-fleet screenshots already sitting in `scratchpad/visual-verify/` (`coach-recruiting__discover__desktop.png` = the 4-card no-chrome skeleton; `coach-recruiting__discover-peek-panel__desktop.png` = Command Center, not the peek panel) and Fable's verdict doc (`FABLE_VERDICTS.md`) reviewing the same run.

**1. `useBaseballAuth()` ran its full 4-round-trip session verification twice, sequentially, on every hard navigation into `(dashboard)`.**

`DashboardSessionGuard` ((dashboard)/layout.tsx) calls `useBaseballAuth(null)` to gate the team-context recovery redirect. Only once that settles does it mount `BaseballShellLayout`, which calls `useBaseballAuth(requiredRole)` *again* to gate the shared shell chrome. Both calls independently run `auth.getUser()` + 3 parallel profile queries — with no dedup, unlike the sibling hooks `useAuth()` (use-auth.ts) and `useBaseballNavContext()`, which both already implement exactly this caching pattern for exactly this reason. Every dashboard page load paid for the verification twice before any chrome could render, visible as an extended "4-card skeleton, no chrome" (`GenericPageSkeleton` via `<PageLoading/>`). Under the shooter fleet's concurrent-session load this plausibly pushed some captures past the wait budget entirely — the permanent-skeleton capture.

The hook also had **no try/catch** around `verifyServerSession()` — any unexpected throw would strand `loading` at `true` forever. `use-auth.ts`'s own doc comment explicitly documents having fixed this exact failure mode once already for the sibling hook; `useBaseballAuth` never got the same treatment.

**2. `getActiveProgramType()` in `server-route-guards.ts` was missing a fallback that was already shipped for the identical bug elsewhere.**

`requireRecruitingCoachRoute()` (which gates Discover/Pipeline/Watchlist/Compare) only read `baseball_teams.program_type`, with no fallback to `team_type`. `program_type` is nullable and left unset on some teams — `nav-context.ts` documents this exact scenario and already falls back to `team_type` for the sidebar's nav resolution. The route guard was never given the same fix, so a team in that state can fail the program-type half of the guard's OR-check and — for a coach whose `coach_type` doesn't independently satisfy the other half — hard-redirect to `/baseball/dashboard/command-center`. That's the second capture: the "peek panel" screenshot landed on Command Center instead of Discover.

## Fix

1. `useBaseballAuth`: short-lived (5s) module-scope cache + in-flight dedup keyed by `requiredRole`, so back-to-back mounts within the same navigation share one server round trip (every fresh navigation still fully revalidates — preserves #416's "always revalidate the server" intent). Wrapped `verifyServerSession()` in try/catch/finally so `loading` always resolves and an unexpected failure routes to an honest recovery surface (`/baseball/login`) instead of hanging forever.
2. `getActiveProgramType()`: mirrors `nav-context.ts`'s already-shipped fix — fall back to `team_type` when `program_type` is null, wrapped in try/catch so a transient read failure can't take down the whole route render.

## Repro evidence

Playwright repro against the running prod build (127.0.0.1:3100, coach `njrini99@gmail.com`): Discover consistently resolves within ~5-6s in isolation (skeleton → full content + sidebar), confirming the page is NOT infinite-hang under normal single-session conditions — but the ~5-6s of full-page, chrome-less skeleton on every cold entry into the dashboard is a real, confirmed, doubled-round-trip cost, and is exactly what a shooter under fleet load (many concurrent sessions) would plausibly time out on.

## Test plan

- New `src/hooks/__tests__/use-baseball-auth.test.tsx`:
  - Dedupes two back-to-back mounts (same `requiredRole`) into a single `auth.getUser()` call.
  - Never strands `loading=true` on a thrown verification error — resolves and redirects to `/baseball/login`.
- New cases in `server-route-guards.test.ts`:
  - `requireRecruitingCoachRoute` allows a college coach when `program_type` is null but `team_type` is set (the exact "left unset" scenario nav-context.ts documents).
  - `requireShowcaseOrgRoute` falls back to `team_type` when `coach_type` alone wouldn't satisfy the gate.
  - Still redirects when neither coach_type nor the (fallback-resolved) program_type is allowed.
- `npx eslint` on all 4 touched files: 0 errors, 0 new warnings.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean, full project.
- `npx vitest run` (targeted): 32/32 passing across all 4 workspace projects (business/integration/rls/unit). Confirmed the one pre-existing unrelated failure in `program-type-nav-variants.test.ts` (nav-registry ordering) fails identically on the unmodified base branch — not a regression from this change.

## Root cause

`src/app/baseball/(public)/team/[id]/page.tsx` and `src/app/baseball/(public)/program/[id]/page.tsx` sit in the `(public)` route group but both called `notFound()` unconditionally for **any** logged-out visitor, and again for any authenticated user who wasn't a college/juco coach:

```ts
const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
if (!user) {
  notFound(); // Block unauthenticated access
}
```

So shared team/program links 404'd for recruits' parents, fans, and HS coaches — anyone without a college/juco coach session.

Digging one level deeper: even a pure code fix couldn't have worked, because every underlying table these pages read (`organizations`, `baseball_teams`, `baseball_team_coach_staff`, `baseball_coaches`) only grants `SELECT` `TO authenticated` via RLS. A logged-out (anon) Supabase client gets zero rows back from any of them regardless of what the page code does.

## Fix

Both pages now branch on `isPublicViewer = !user`:

- **Logged-out visitors** get a SAFE public view: team/org name, division/conference, location, logo, about, and coaching staff (`full_name` + `role` + `avatar` only — no bio, no email, no phone). The Roster section renders a tasteful "Sign in to view roster" card (`IconLock`, explanatory copy, a `returnTo`-aware `/baseball/login` link) instead of any roster data.
- **Authenticated college/juco (recruiting) coaches** keep the exact current behavior — same data source (direct authenticated-only table reads), same roster-visibility rules, same fields.
- **Any other authenticated user** (player, HS/showcase coach, etc.) keeps the pre-existing block, unchanged. This PR only widens access for **logged-out** visitors, per the product decision — it does not change who's authorized once someone is signed in.

### DB (gated — NOT applied)

`supabase/migrations/20260702110000_baseball_public_team_program_profile_views.sql` adds three new narrow, column-allowlisted views that the anon branch reads through instead of the base tables:

- `organizations_public_profile`
- `baseball_teams_public_profile` (excludes `join_code` — the team invite secret — and `created_by`)
- `baseball_team_coach_staff_public` (pre-joined staff identity; excludes `email`/`phone`/`bio`)

These are the **only** `anon` `SELECT` grants added anywhere — deliberately scoped to non-PII columns only, following the same view-as-security-boundary pattern already established by `public.baseball_coaches_public` (`REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated` then `GRANT SELECT` only, `security_invoker = false`). Base-table RLS is untouched; base tables stay authenticated-only. **db_gated** — an operator must apply this before the anon code paths return real data. Until then, those code paths query views that don't exist yet, so anon requests will fail closed exactly as they 404 today — no regression risk from shipping code ahead of the migration.

### Bonus fix (found while restructuring, same class of bug as PR #656)

`program/[id]/page.tsx`'s staff query selected `first_name`/`last_name` from `baseball_coaches` — a table that has never had those columns (only `full_name`). Every staff fetch on that page 400'd and silently rendered an empty Coaching Staff section. This was called out as a known, explicitly out-of-scope follow-up in the PR #656 regression test comment; since I was already rewriting this exact query block to add the anon/authed branch split, I fixed it in place (switched to `full_name`, matching the sibling `team/[id]` page's already-fixed pattern; also dropped the unused `email` field that was being fetched but never rendered).

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors
- [x] `npx eslint` on both changed page files — 0 errors, 0 *new* warnings (each file's `helm/no-arbitrary-bg-white` warning count matches its pre-existing baseline exactly: team page 9, program page 8)
- [x] `npx vitest run` on the two regression-guard test files — 72/72 passing:
  - Updated `src/lib/baseball/__tests__/public-team-profile-staff-query.test.ts` (PR #656 guard, now covers both pages + a new PII-column guard)
  - New `src/lib/baseball/__tests__/public-profile-anon-gating.test.ts` — static guards against the unconditional logged-out `notFound()` reappearing, and against `join_code`/PII leaking into the anon-safe read paths
- [ ] Manual: needs the migration applied + a live team/program id to verify end-to-end (DB is gated, so this PR ships the read paths only)
- [ ] CI: full typecheck/build/RLS suite (authoritative gate)

## Root cause

The demo team (Rini University Baseball) is seeded by
`scripts/seed-rini-baseball-demo.ts`, which computes every date relative
to whenever it was last run. Real calendar time keeps moving, so the
"upcoming" game/practice/meeting drifted into the past (screenshots
showed the anchor game dated Jun 28, already gone by), readiness
check-ins read as weeks stale, and a few premium surfaces the base seed
never populated at all (development plans, documents, coach<->player
messaging) had no content to demo.

## Fix

New idempotent companion script: `scripts/reseed-rini-demo-freshness.ts`.

1. **Re-dates anchor events/games** — practice (tomorrow), meeting (+2
   days), game vs Coastal State (+3 days), plus the 2 "next" scheduled
   games — so "this week" always has a future game + practice + meeting.
2. **Seeds 2 development plans** (4 goals each) — Marcus Rodriguez
   (rinin376's player row) gets an `in_progress` plan with one completed
   goal + two in-progress + one not-started, so the player-facing "My
   Development" goal-checkbox/progress-ring UI has real content. Jake
   Thompson gets a `sent` plan for coach-side list/detail variety.
3. **Seeds 4 team documents** — playbook, schedule, travel policy,
   conditioning manual. Real `baseball_documents` +
   `baseball_document_versions` rows backed by tiny placeholder `.txt`
   files uploaded through the exact same `documents` storage bucket +
   `baseball-documents/<teamId>/<file>` path convention
   `uploadBaseballDocumentAction` uses — not fake metadata pointing at
   nothing.
4. **Seeds 1 coach → player conversation** with 4 messages (natural
   back-and-forth, most recent unread) so Messages has content.
5. **Re-dates recent lift sessions + readiness** — both the live
   `helm_lifting_*` tables and the legacy `baseball_readiness_checkins`
   table a couple of surfaces still read — so the readiness / "today's
   lift" panels read as current instead of drifting stale.

### Idempotency / safety

- Rows the base seed already owns (events, games, readiness check-ins,
  lift sessions/program-assignments/results/assignments) are updated
  **in place** via partial-column `.update().eq('id', id)` on the SAME
  deterministic ids the base seed minted — never a fresh insert, never a
  delete-then-insert. (Initially tried `.upsert()` with a partial
  payload; Postgres validates an INSERT's column list against NOT-NULL
  constraints even when it will resolve via `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, so
  that failed on these wide tables — switched to plain `.update()`.)
- New rows (dev plans, documents, conversation/messages) are keyed under
  a dedicated `baseball-demo-reseed-v1` id namespace — that namespace is
  the stable dedupe key / ownership marker, so re-running just upserts
  the same rows again.
- Scoped entirely to the demo team (`2acc63ce…`) / org / the two demo
  users. Golf is never touched.

## What was actually written (ran against prod with `--confirm`)

| Table | Rows |
|---|---|
| `baseball_events` (updated) | 3 |
| `baseball_games` (updated) | 2 |
| `baseball_developmental_plans` | 2 |
| `baseball_documents` | 4 |
| `baseball_document_versions` | 4 |
| storage objects (`documents` bucket) | 4 |
| `baseball_conversations` | 1 |
| `baseball_conversation_participants` | 2 |
| `baseball_messages` | 4 |
| `baseball_readiness_checkins` (updated) | 14 |
| `helm_lifting_readiness_checkins` (updated) | 14 |
| `helm_lifting_program_assignments` (updated) | 4 |
| `helm_lifting_sessions` (updated) | 56 |
| `baseball_lift_results` (updated) | 14 |
| `baseball_lift_assignments` (updated) | 28 |

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck ...` targeted check on the file — 0 errors (the `scripts/` dir is excluded from the project tsconfig)
- [x] `npx vitest run src/contracts/baseball/demo-stats-smoke.contract.test.ts` — 9/9 passed (unaffected; base seed file untouched)

## Root cause

`/baseball/dashboard/calendar` computed its "N upcoming events" headline and its per-type badges (Practice/Meeting/Game) from **two different filters over the same events array**:

- `upcomingEvents` = `events.filter(e => start_time >= now).length` — excludes past events.
- `eventTypeCounts` = `events.reduce(...)` over the **raw, unfiltered** array — every event the team has ever had, including past ones.

Confirmed against live data: the seeded demo events for "Rini University Baseball" (1 practice 6/26, 1 meeting 6/27, 1 game 6/28) are genuinely in the past relative to DB `now()` (2026-07-02), so `upcomingEvents` correctly reported `0` while `eventTypeCounts` — which never filtered by date — still summed all three. Two numbers, same dataset, contradictory story.

Separately, on mobile (390px) the badge row used `overflow-x-auto` with a hidden scrollbar (no visible affordance to scroll), which clipped `"1 Game"` mid-word at the viewport edge. And the mobile swipeable day view's `next/dynamic` Suspense fallback reused a generic 3-block skeleton (`ViewLoadingSkeleton`) shared across all four calendar views — during the load window it renders as two blank, disconnected gray panels with nothing that reads as "a calendar is loading here," which is what the visual-verify capture (`coach-ops__calendar__mobile.png`) caught.

## Fix

1. **One source of truth for the summary strip** (`page.tsx`): both `upcomingEvents` and `eventTypeCounts` now derive from the same filtered list. "Upcoming" is defined as start time at or after **local midnight today** (not the exact `now` instant), so an event earlier today doesn't drop out of the count mid-day. The strip is now gated on `upcomingEvents > 0` instead of `events.length > 0`, so a team with only past events doesn't render `"0 upcoming events ·"` with nothing after the separator.
2. **Badge row wraps instead of scrolling** (`CalendarFairway.tsx` + the legacy `page.tsx` fallback render): `overflow-x-auto` → `flex-wrap` with `gap-x/gap-y`, so on 390px the row wraps to a second line instead of clipping off-screen with no visible way to reach the rest.
3. **Mobile day-view loading state** (`PremiumCalendarClient.tsx`): `CalendarDayViewSwipeable`'s dynamic-import fallback now uses a dedicated `DayViewSwipeableLoadingSkeleton` shaped like the real component (compact date header + event-card rows) instead of the generic skeleton. Also added a `useEffect` that preloads that chunk as soon as `showMobileUI` resolves true, ahead of the auto-switch effect that flips `view` to `'day'` — shrinks (often eliminates) the loading window in the first place.

## Scope note

While tracing this I found that `useCalendarRangeEvents` (the shared client-side range-fetch + realtime hook `PremiumCalendarClient` uses) is hardcoded to query the `golf_events` table and subscribe to `golf_events` realtime changes — even when mounted from baseball's `CalendarFairway`/`BaseballCalendarWrapper`. In practice this doesn't cause visible breakage today because `page.tsx`'s server fetch is unbounded (no date-range filter, so `initialEvents` already contains every event for the team) and the hook falls back to `initialEvents` whenever its own fetch returns 0 rows — which it always will for a baseball team_id against `golf_events`. But it does mean baseball's calendar never gets realtime pushes, and would silently show a stale/incomplete calendar the day the server fetch is ever range-limited. This is a real, separate table-prefix defect (`golf_events` used for a baseball surface) that's larger than this PR's scope — parameterizing a hook shared with golf's calendar — so I did not touch it here. Flagging as a follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx eslint` on the 3 changed files: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` (full project): 0 errors
- [x] `npx vitest run` on `use-calendar-range-events` + `BaseballCalendarWrapper.rsvp-routing` suites: 56/56 passing
- [x] Manual repro against `127.0.0.1:3100` (coach login, 390×844 viewport) — confirmed via direct SQL that the seeded events are genuinely in the past, ruling out a timezone/date-boundary bug in the count itself; the badges were the actual bug
- [ ] Recommend a follow-up visual-verify pass on this branch's preview to confirm the wrapped badge row and shaped mobile skeleton match the design bar in a real capture

body:
## Root cause

`CreateDevPlanModal`'s "Select Player" field fetches the roster with:

```ts
.from('baseball_team_members')
.select(`player:baseball_players (...)`)
.eq('team_id', teamId)
.is('left_at', null)   // <- this column does not exist
```

`baseball_team_members` has no `left_at` column (see the generated
schema in `src/lib/types/database.ts` — the table only has `status:
team_member_status | null`, not a departure timestamp). Every fetch
therefore errored at the Postgrest layer, `data` stayed `null`, and
the picker unconditionally rendered:

> No players in roster. Add players to your team first.

...even though the same coach's `/baseball/dashboard/roster` shows a
full roster (14 players in the reported repro). The picker had drifted
into re-implementing its own roster query instead of reading from the
same source the Roster page uses, and referenced a column that never
existed.

Grepping for the same broken pattern (`left_at` against
`baseball_team_members`) turned up one more instance:
`src/app/baseball/(public)/player/[id]/page.tsx` selected `left_at`
inside a nested `baseball_team_members` embed on the main player
query. A bad column reference inside a nested select makes the whole
query error, and this page treats any query error as `notFound()` —
so this one bug was 404ing the public recruiting profile page
(`/baseball/player/[id]`) for every player, unconditionally.

## Fix

- `CreateDevPlanModal.tsx`: drop the `.is('left_at', null)` filter.
  Query now matches the canonical roster read model (`getRoster` in
  `src/lib/baseball/read-models/roster.ts`) — all current
  `baseball_team_members` rows for the team, no status filter — so the
  picker always shows exactly what the Roster page shows.
- `player/[id]/page.tsx`: drop `left_at` from the nested
  `baseball_team_members` select so the public profile query no longer
  errors on a nonexistent column.
- Searched for any other player-picker with the same broken pattern
  (grep for the empty-roster copy string and for every client-side
  `baseball_team_members` fetch used by a `'use client'` component).
  No other instance found — `LiftBuilderClient`'s identical-looking
  empty-roster copy is driven by a separate, already-correct
  server-side `getGroupAvailability` read model, not a client refetch.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `src/components/coach/__tests__/CreateDevPlanModal.test.tsx`:
  - asserts the picker maps every roster row the query returns into a
    selectable player card (regression guard for "roster has players
    but picker says empty")
  - asserts the query is scoped with `.eq('team_id', ...)` and never
    calls `.is('left_at', ...)` again
  - asserts the true empty state only renders when the team genuinely
    has zero roster rows
- [x] `npx eslint` on both changed files — 0 errors, same 7 pre-existing
  `helm/no-raw-input` warnings on `CreateDevPlanModal.tsx` (unrelated
  lines, present before this change too)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — full project, exit 0, no errors on either
  changed file
