## Root cause

`/baseball/dashboard/documents` always rendered "Documents could not load / Some data could not be loaded. Try refreshing." — reproduced on fresh nav and hard reload, **even with zero documents in the table**.

`getTeamDocuments(teamId, isCoach)` (and its siblings `getDocument`, `getVersionHistory`, `uploadNewVersion`) all queried `baseball_documents` / `baseball_document_versions` with a PostgREST embed:

```ts
.select(`
  *,
  uploader:uploaded_by(
    full_name,
    email
  )
`)
```

`uploaded_by` is a FK to `public.users(id)`. Confirmed against the **live** schema (via Supabase SQL and a direct signed-in-coach repro against the real project — coach `njrini99@gmail.com` / team "Rini University Baseball"):

```
column_name             | data_type
id                       | uuid
email                    | text
role                     | USER-DEFINED
created_at               | timestamptz
updated_at               | timestamptz
notification_preferences | jsonb
last_seen                | timestamptz
```

`public.users` has **no `full_name` column**. PostgREST validates embedded columns against the schema cache before executing, so the query fails unconditionally with:

```json
{"code":"42703","message":"column users_1.full_name does not exist"}
```

— regardless of how many document rows exist, which is exactly the "always errors, even fresh/empty" symptom.

As a sanity check I also hit golf's `golf_documents` with the identical embed pattern using the service-role key: it fails too, with a different error (`PGRST200 — Could not find a relationship`), because `golf_documents.uploaded_by` was migrated to FK `auth.users(id)` at some point and `auth` isn't in PostgREST's exposed-schema list. So the "golf documents previously worked" comparison is **stale** — golf has independently drifted into the same class of bug. Out of scope for this PR (baseball-only bug report), but worth a follow-up issue.

## Fix

No DB migration needed — this is a query-shape bug, not a missing column. `full_name`/`email` genuinely exist on `baseball_coaches` (keyed by the same `public.users.id` via `baseball_coaches.user_id`), and document upload/create already requires the `can_manage_documents` capability, so every `uploaded_by` is a coach.

- Dropped the broken `uploader:uploaded_by(full_name, email)` embed from all 4 call sites (`getTeamDocuments`, `getDocument` incl. nested versions, `uploadNewVersion`'s inserted-version select, `getVersionHistory`).
- Added `resolveUploaders(supabase, userIds)`: one batched follow-up `baseball_coaches` query (`.in('user_id', ids)`) that builds a `Map<user_id, {full_name, email}>`.
- Each call site attaches `uploader` from that map after the main query, with unmatched/removed uploaders degrading to `uploader: null` instead of failing the whole page.

## Test plan

- New `src/app/baseball/actions/__tests__/documents.test.ts`:
  - Regression guard on all 4 call sites: none of the `select(...)` calls ever contain `uploader:uploaded_by` again.
  - `getTeamDocuments` loads cleanly with zero rows (the exact previously-broken case) and with rows, resolving `uploader` from `baseball_coaches` or degrading to `null` when unmatched.
  - `getDocument` resolves `uploader` on the document and on each nested version.
  - `getVersionHistory` resolves `uploader` per version.
- `npx vitest run src/app/baseball/actions/__tests__/` — 58 files / 604 tests pass (no regressions in the surrounding baseball actions suite).
- `npx eslint` on both changed files — 0 errors/warnings.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean on both changed files.
- Live repro against the real Supabase project (read-only; no writes/migrations) confirmed the exact `42703` error pre-fix and a clean empty-array response post-fix-shape (no documents currently exist for the demo team, so uploader-resolution itself is covered by the mocked unit tests rather than a live row).

## Notes

- `db_gated`: **not applicable** — no migration required, fix is entirely code-side.
- Related but out-of-scope: `src/app/golf/actions/documents.ts` has the same broken-embed pattern against `golf_documents`/`golf_document_versions` (FK now points at `auth.users`, which PostgREST can't embed). Worth its own ticket.

## Root cause

The legacy dark sidebar's `<aside>` is `flex flex-col h-dvh`, with the
scrollable `<nav>` sandwiched between a fixed-height logo header and a
non-growing bottom block (Pro badge / user info / Sign out — plus
Settings for players). The `<nav>` had no explicit `min-h-0` and only
16px of bottom padding.

Flex items default their automatic minimum size to their *content* size
unless the browser correctly infers 0 from `overflow: auto`. That
inference is spec-correct in evergreen Chromium/Firefox, but is a known
soft spot in older/embedded WebKit (notably Capacitor's iOS WKWebView,
which this app ships to). Where it doesn't infer correctly, the nav
sizes to its full content instead of the remaining column space, so the
non-growing bottom block visually pins over the tail of the item list —
the last item(s) render partially clipped ("Discover" cut off
mid-word) with no visual cue that the list is even scrollable.

## Fix

`src/components/layout/sidebar.tsx`, surgical/presentation-only:

- `<nav>`: add explicit `min-h-0` so it always fills only the remaining
  flex-column space (never grows past it) and scrolls its own overflow.
- `<nav>`: bump bottom padding `py-4` → `pt-4 pb-8` so the last item has
  real breathing room at the scroll end instead of ending flush against
  the bottom block's top border.
- `<nav>`: add `WebkitOverflowScrolling: 'touch'` + `overscrollBehavior:
  'contain'` inline styles — native momentum scroll on touch, and stops
  an exhausted nav scroll from chaining into the page scroll. Mirrors
  the same pattern already used on `<main>` in `BaseballDashboardShell`.
- Logo header + bottom (Settings/Sign-out) block: add `shrink-0` so
  neither can be compressed by the flex layout on short viewports,
  which would otherwise risk the opposite failure (footer content or
  nav items overlapping).

No nav grouping/IA changes — this is scroll/padding only, kept minimal
to avoid touching the same file area as the parallel
`feat/baseball-nav-8tab` grouping work.

## Test plan

      (127.0.0.1:3100, coach login) by inspecting the live sidebar's
      computed flex geometry (`clientHeight` vs `scrollHeight`,
      footer/nav boundary) to confirm the fix targets the right
      container and the right CSS properties

## Root cause

`getCommandCenter()` (`src/lib/baseball/read-models/command-center.ts`) selected `baseball_player_aggregates` as a **nested PostgREST embed** under a `baseball_team_members` query:

```ts
supabase.from('baseball_team_members').select(`
  player_id, jersey_number, position, status, joined_at,
  baseball_players!inner ( ... ),
  baseball_player_aggregates ( ... )   // <-- the problem
`)
```

`baseball_player_aggregates` has foreign keys to `baseball_players` and `baseball_teams` — **but not to `baseball_team_members`**. PostgREST needs a direct FK to resolve a nested embed, so this query failed on every single call with:

```
PGRST200: Could not find a relationship between 'baseball_team_members' and
'baseball_player_aggregates' in the schema cache
```

Reproduced live against prod Supabase (team "Rini University Baseball") with a throwaway script hitting the exact query — confirmed the exact PGRST200 error above, then confirmed the fix resolves cleanly (14 members / 14 aggregates joined correctly).

That failure set `membersRes.error`, which the read model turns into `error: 'The roster pulse could not be loaded.'` and empty `rosterPulse`/`rosterPlayers` arrays. Since `summary.rosterSize`, `summary.playersWithData` etc. are all derived from `rosterPulse.length`, every hero KPI (ROSTER / ON THE RECORD / OPEN RISKS / TODAY) rendered 0, and the "Signals are catching up — The roster pulse could not be loaded" error card appeared.

Daily Contracts on the same page stayed correct (ROSTER=14) because `getCoachDailyContracts()` queries `baseball_team_members` **without** the aggregates embed — it was never affected by this bug.

## Fix

- Split the query into two: fetch `baseball_team_members` (with the working `baseball_players!inner` embed) and `baseball_player_aggregates` separately, then join them in JS by `player_id` — the same pattern already used by `roster.ts` and `coach-daily-contracts.ts`.
- Degrades gracefully now: if the aggregates query alone fails, the roster still renders (with honest `noData: true` rows) instead of blanking the whole pulse.
- Wired the previously-declared-but-unused `loadState` prop into `CommandCenterFairway` so a genuine load failure (`loadState === 'error'`) renders the KPI figures as an em-dash placeholder (`ghost` on `RuledStatLine`) instead of a fabricated confirmed zero — real error is now visually distinguishable from an honest empty roster.
- Reworded the error card title from "Signals are catching up." (implies an AI-signals-specific problem) to "Some data couldn't load." since the underlying failure can be roster/events/insights, not just the risk feed.

## Files changed

- `src/lib/baseball/read-models/command-center.ts` — split query, JS join, resilient aggregates handling
- `src/components/baseball/command-center/CommandCenterFairway.tsx` — wire `loadState`, ghost KPIs on real error, error copy
- `src/components/baseball/living-annual/molecules/KPIContentsStrip.tsx` — add `ghost` passthrough to `KPIContentsItem`/`RuledStatLine`

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduced the PGRST200 error live via a throwaway node script against prod Supabase, then confirmed the split-query fix returns 0 errors (14 members / 14 aggregates for the Rini demo team)
- [x] `npx eslint` on the 3 changed files — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean, no new errors
- [x] `npx vitest run` on `src/lib/baseball/read-models`, `src/components/baseball/living-annual`, `src/components/baseball/command-center` — 370/370 passed
- [x] No DB migration needed — fix is query-shape only, no schema change

## Summary

Stage-0 of the BaseballHelm UI sweep: the shared micro-interaction vocabulary for "The Living Annual" design system. Nick's mandate — micro-interactions everywhere, but **systematized**, never re-invented per page. Presentation-only, no data/action changes.

Three new primitives + three new `motion.ts` tokens:

| Primitive | What it is | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `<Reveal>` | Generic entrance wrapper — mount-based fade/rise/unblur (reuses the existing `inkSettles` variant), `staggerIndex` cascade | So a card grid / roster wall settles on the SAME curve as hero numerals, one prop, no bespoke variants wiring |
| `<HoverReveal>` | Row/card hover-reveal wrapper, with a **touch fallback** | A bare `group-hover:opacity-100` strands touch users with an invisible-but-tappable control |
| `pressableClass()` | CSS-only press-down + lane-ink hover tint (`cn()` helper, server-safe) | Bespoke tappable surfaces (rows/cards/chips) that aren't a `<Button>` (which already owns its own `active:scale` system) |

**New `motion.ts` tokens** (additive, nothing renamed/removed): `EASE_PRESS` `[0.4,0,0.2,1]` (quick press curve, distinct from the two settle curves), `PACE` (generic duration ladder — `fast`/`base`/`slow`/`cinematic`, pinned to existing `DUR` entries so nothing forks), `STAGGER_STEP` (extracted from `inkColumn`'s hardcoded 0.06, now a shared constant).

## Design-bar checklist

- [x] Presentation-only — no data/action changes
- [x] `'use client'` where hooks are used (`Reveal`, `HoverReveal`); `pressable.ts` is a pure helper, server-safe
- [x] No new deps — framer-motion + `AnimatedNumber` already in the repo
- [x] No banned patterns — no Inter/Roboto, no harsh drop shadows, no linear/generic ease-in-out (custom cubic-beziers throughout, matching the kit's existing `EASE_GLIDE`/`EASE_SOFT` family)
- [x] `prefers-reduced-motion` first-class (`Reveal` renders final state instantly; `HoverReveal`/`pressableClass` are CSS-only, not gated — chrome visibility isn't a motion principle)
- [x] Matches kit naming/idiom — extended the existing flat `motion.ts` (already the kit's token source of truth) instead of introducing a competing `motion/` directory

## Two things worth flagging

1. **`whileInView` → mount-based instead.** The original brief asked for `IntersectionObserver`/`whileInView` for `<Reveal>`. `src/components/ui/reveal.tsx` already tried that and reverted it: the baseball dashboard shell scrolls an inner `<main>`, so `IntersectionObserver` against the document viewport never fires for content below the fold — pages got stuck at `opacity: 0`. `<Reveal>` reuses `inkSettles` on mount + a `staggerIndex` cascade instead, documented inline and in the spec doc.
2. **No `StatRoll` built.** `<StatReadout>` (already in the kit) already IS the mount-roll + update-roll `tabular-nums` stat wrapper. A second component would just be a second name for the same behavior — documented this instead of duplicating.

## Reference implementation

`StatsCenterClient.tsx` (already-migrated "Radar-Gun Stat Wall," §6 P1 #5) — each `PlayerRowPlate` row now wraps in `<Reveal staggerIndex={i}>` so the roster wall settles top-to-bottom on load (capped at row 10). `PlayerRowPlate` itself was updated to use `pressableClass` (replacing a hand-rolled neutral hover with a lane-ink tint + real press feedback) and a `<HoverReveal>` trailing chevron affordance.

## Docs

- `docs/baseball/design-system-living-annual.md` — new §7.1 "Interaction layer (Stage-0 addendum)": tokens, when-to-use-which table, code snippets, the `whileInView`/`StatRoll` rationale.
- `src/components/baseball/living-annual/README.md` — new "Interaction layer (Stage-0)" section + updated component table + Helpers list.

## Exports (barrel: `@/components/baseball/living-annual`)

`Reveal`, `RevealProps`, `HoverReveal`, `HoverRevealProps`, `pressableClass`, `PressableOptions`, `PressableInk`, plus `EASE_PRESS`, `PACE`, `STAGGER_STEP` from `motion.ts`.

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors (repo-wide)
- [x] `eslint` on all changed/new files — clean
- [x] New unit tests: `pressable.test.ts` (6 tests, pure), `Reveal.test.tsx` (7 tests, verifies mount-based animate + stagger delay math + reduced-motion final state via a framer-motion mock matching the existing `HeroInsightCard.test.tsx` pattern), `HoverReveal.test.tsx` (7 tests, touch-fallback + focus-within classes)

## Summary

**Repo-prod parity commit — nothing in this PR needs to be applied.** All DB work described here is already live in prod (owner reviewed and applied each migration directly tonight, full verification battery green). This PR authors the 5 migration files that didn't yet exist on any branch, so repo history matches what's actually running.

Also commits `docs/audits/DB_READINESS_PACKET_2026-07-02.md` (previously untracked) with an **APPLIED** addendum at the top listing all 8 applied migrations and the 3 owner amendments.

## What changed since the first version of this PR

The original commit took a dual-write + code-change approach to reconciling `baseball_stat_sources`/`catching_events`/`baserunning_events` before the owner's own live-DB review established that all 6 #651-affected tables (plus the practice-effectiveness table) were completely empty — so no backfill or dual-write was ever needed. That approach (including the `stat-event-imports.ts` code change) is **reverted** in this commit. `stat-event-imports.ts` is untouched relative to `batch/baseball-fixes`.

## Files (5 new, matching the applied state exactly)

1. **`20260702095900_baseball_651_column_reconcile.sql`** — #651 across all 6 affected tables in one migration (not the two-tier split an earlier draft proposed). ## Summary

Phase 2 half-built completion: **teams-manage**. The Showcase coach "Teams" page (`/baseball/dashboard/teams`) could only create a team and generate an invite, both via raw client-side Supabase writes with silently swallowed errors and `Math.random()`-derived invite codes.

- New `src/app/baseball/actions/teams.ts` server actions, all `withBaseballAction`-wrapped and `can_manage_settings`-gated (except `leaveTeamAsCoach`, which only requires being staff — see note below):
  - `createTeam` — first-write flow (`requireActiveContext: false`), uses the admin/service-role client for the team + primary-staff-row two-step insert (mirrors `completeCoachOnboarding`; the staff-row INSERT's RLS check requires an existing primary staff row, a chicken-and-egg problem for the very first staff row on a brand-new team).
  - `updateTeam` — whitelisted-field update (name/description/colors only).
  - `deleteTeam` — primary-coach-only, blocked while the team has an active roster.
  - `leaveTeamAsCoach` — non-primary coach removes their own staff row; primary coach is rejected.
  - `createTeamInvitation` / `revokeTeamInvitation` — new `baseball_team_invitations` rows, with insert-collision retry.
- `TeamsClient.tsx`: Edit modal, Delete confirm (surfaces the roster-not-empty error), Leave Team control for non-primary coaches, Revoke control on the invite chip. Every failure path now shows a `toast.error` — no more silent no-ops. Extracted a shared `TeamFormModal` + `ColorField` so the create/edit forms aren't duplicated (also keeps the design-token lint warnings for this file at 4, down from 7 on `main`, rather than doubling them).
- Hardened `generateInviteCode()` to `crypto.randomBytes` (CSPRNG) instead of `Math.random()` — the char alphabet has exactly 32 entries so `byte % 32` has zero modulo bias. Every call site still pairs this with an insert/update retry-on-collision loop (`isUniqueViolation`) rather than trusting uniqueness up front.

## DB (gated — not applied)

`leaveTeamAsCoach` is written defensively (checks `.select()` on the delete and returns an explicit error if RLS filtered it to 0 rows) because the **live** `baseball_team_coach_staff` DELETE policy only allows the primary coach or `can_invite_staff` holders — there's no "delete your own row" clause. A non-primary coach without `can_invite_staff` will get a clear in-app error today ("ask the primary coach to remove your staff access") rather than a silent no-op, but true self-service leave needs this policy addition:

```sql
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "baseball_team_coach_staff_delete" ON public.baseball_team_coach_staff;
CREATE POLICY "baseball_team_coach_staff_delete" ON public.baseball_team_coach_staff
  FOR DELETE TO authenticated
  USING (
    public.is_baseball_primary_coach(team_id)
    OR public.has_baseball_staff_capability(team_id, 'can_invite_staff')
    OR coach_id = public.get_my_coach_id()
  );
```

Not applied per instructions — code-only PR.

## Test plan

`dev-plans-goal-schema`).

`CreateDevPlanModal` generated a `crypto.randomUUID()` per goal for React
`key`s but **dropped it on insert** (wrote only `title`/`description`/
`target_date`/`completed`). `parseGoals()` then minted a **brand-new random

  backward compatibility (existing player-side imports unchanged).

## Summary
- `PlayerLiftSessionClient` reads lift sessions from `helm_lifting_sessions` (per the W2-G rewire) and hands out helm-space ids, but `startLiftSession` / `logSetResult` / `completeLiftSession` still looked up `baseball_lift_sessions` by that id — so every player-self set log threw "Session not found" (100% reproducible).
- The coach Live Weight Room (`LiveWeightRoom.tsx`, via `getLiveWeightRoomData`) still hands out **legacy** `baseball_lift_sessions` ids to these same three actions, so a legacy-only fix would have broken that surface instead. Fixed with a per-call table-space resolver (`resolveLiftSessionSpace`) rather than assuming one space.
- PR detection (which still targets the legacy `baseball_strength_prs`/`baseball_strength_maxes` tables, both FK'd to `baseball_lift_sessions`/`baseball_lift_exercises`) is bridged via `legacy_baseball_id` on the helm session/session_exercise rows that `publishLiftDay`'s Helm bridge already sets — skips gracefully (no PR fabricated, matches the existing swallow-errors contract) when no legacy mirror exists.
- Also fixed a latent `onConflict` bug: the helm-space upsert used the 3-column form (`session_exercise_id,athlete_id,set_number`) copied from `src/app/lifting/actions/*`, but the real DB constraint on `helm_lifting_set_results` (migration `20260625000020`, `uq_helm_lifting_set`) is `UNIQUE(session_exercise_id, set_number)` — the 3-column form would 400 on every upsert.

## Root cause (confirmed)
Reader/writer table-space mismatch from an incomplete rewire: read models (`player-lift.ts`) moved to `helm_lifting_*`; write actions (`lifting-v11.ts`) were never updated, and are also called from a second surface (coach Live Weight Room) that's still on the legacy table space.

## Changes
- `src/app/baseball/actions/lifting-v11.ts`
  - Added `resolveLiftSessionSpace` + `resolveAthletePlayerId` helpers.
  - `startLiftSession`, `logSetResult`, `completeLiftSession` now resolve the session's table space per call and branch reads/writes accordingly (helm vs legacy), instead of assuming legacy space.
  - `logSetResult`'s helm-space upsert corrected to the real 2-column `onConflict`.
  - `completeLiftSession`'s PR sweep + H2 stats (top set / RPE average) now source from whichever table the session's sets actually live in, and the PR sweep maps to legacy ids via `legacy_baseball_id` instead of a second legacy-only query.

## Summary

Narrow slice of Phase 2 spec #13 (journey-vocab): reconciles the player's 6-value self-reported journey status with the canonical 5-stage coach pipeline vocabulary, and removes a dead UI branch.

- The player "My Journey" status update (`updateInterestStatus`) previously mutated `baseball_recruiting_interests` directly from the browser client (`src/hooks/use-journey.ts`) with **no server-side validation and no ownership check** — any authenticated player could rewrite any interest row by id, and any string value was accepted.
- `JourneySchool.coach_name` was hardcoded to `null` forever (never joined from the coach side), so `{school.coach_name && (...)}` in `journey/page.tsx` was permanently dead code.

## Changes

- `src/lib/validation/action-schemas.ts` — new `RecruitingSchemas.updateStatus` Zod enum for the player's 6-value journey vocab (`interested`/`researching`/`contacted`/`visited`/`offered`/`committed`), documented as intentionally distinct from `WatchlistSchemas.updateStatus`'s 5-value coach `pipeline_stage` enum (the only 5 valid `PipelineStage` values per `CLAUDE.md`). These are different domain concepts (player self-report vs coach classification) and are never written to the same column — no schema unification attempted here.
- `src/app/baseball/actions/interests.ts` — promoted `updateInterestStatus` to a real `'use server'` action: `withBaseballAction`, Zod-validated, ownership-checked against `ctx.activePlayerId` (fetch-then-compare, mirroring `verifyWatchlistOwnership`'s pattern on the coach side), security-event logged, `revalidatePath`'d — matching the existing `addToInterests`/`removeFromInterests` pattern in the same file.
- `src/hooks/use-journey.ts` — removed the old unvalidated client-side `updateInterestStatus` export and the dead `coach_name` field/assignment on `JourneySchool`.
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/journey/page.tsx` — imports `updateInterestStatus` from the server action module instead of the hook; removed the now-unreachable `coach_name` JSX branch.
- `src/app/baseball/actions/__tests__/interests.test.ts` — added coverage: valid status update persists + revalidates, invalid vocab value rejected before any write, cross-player ownership rejected before any write.

## DB (gated — not applied)

No schema change required for this slice — `baseball_recruiting_interests.status` remains free text server-side-validated by the new Zod enum. If a future pass wants the same guarantee at the DB layer, the proposed (not applied) migration would be:

```sql
-- Backfill any out-of-vocab rows first, then:
ALTER TABLE baseball_recruiting_interests
  ADD CONSTRAINT baseball_recruiting_interests_status_check
  CHECK (status IN ('interested','researching','contacted','visited','offered','committed'));
```

## Out of scope (left for the full #13 epic)

- Cross-linking player interest status with the coach's `baseball_watchlists.pipeline_stage` (side-by-side "coach's status" badge), engagement-event `status_change` rows, and the `use-journey.ts` engagement-matching-by-name bug — these require a product decision doc per the spec and are materially larger than this fix.

- **Root cause (loop: camps):** `CreateCampModal.tsx` inserted new camps with `status: 'active'` via a raw client-side `supabase.from('baseball_camps')` write, but the `baseball_camps_select` RLS policy only grants non-owner (player) reads when `status = 'published'`. ## Summary

Fixes the video-clip broken loop (Phase-1 spec #7): clips stored `clip_start_time`/`clip_end_time` as inert metadata while every playback surface pointed at the full-length parent video URL, so a "clip" always played the entire source video.

- `VideoPlayer` (`src/components/features/video-player.tsx`) now accepts optional `clipStart`/`clipEnd`. On `loadedmetadata` it seeks to `clipStart`; on `timeupdate` it clamps playback into `[clipStart, clipEnd]` and auto-pauses at the bound (undefined props → unchanged full-video behavior).
- Video detail page (`videos/[id]/page.tsx` → `video-detail-client.tsx`) now threads `video.clip_start_time`/`clip_end_time` into `VideoPlayer`.
- Library modal (`VideoLibraryClient.tsx`) `VideoModalProps.video` now carries `is_clip`/`clip_start_time`/`clip_end_time`, forwarded into `VideoPlayer`, and both call sites (Library view + Player view) pass those fields through.
- Clip creation moves off a raw client-side `supabase.from('baseball_videos').insert(...)` (CLAUDE.md mutation rule) into a new `createVideoClip` server action (`src/app/baseball/actions/videos.ts`), wrapped in `withBaseballAction` with `requiredPlayerAccess: 'can_upload_video'`. It re-loads the parent video scoped to the caller's own `player_id` (never trusts a client-supplied `parentVideoId`) and re-validates the requested bounds against the parent's stored duration via the existing `validateClipRange` helper before writing. `VideoClipper.tsx` now calls this action instead of inserting directly.

**Scope guard (per spec):** does not touch the separate "coach clip-creation entry point / team-video ownership" access-control gap — flagged as follow-up, out of scope here.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx eslint` on all 6 changed files — 0 errors, 3 pre-existing `helm/no-arbitrary-bg-white` warnings in `VideoClipper.tsx` at lines untouched by this diff (unrelated JSX predating this change)
- [ ] Full `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` (CI, per task instructions — not run locally here)
- [ ] Manual: create a clip start=10s/end=20s on a >30s source video; open the clip on its detail page and via the library modal → playback should seek to 10s and auto-pause at 20s instead of playing the full parent video
- [ ] Manual: attempt to save a clip with out-of-range bounds → server action returns a validation error instead of writing an invalid row

## DB (gated — not applied)
No schema changes. All touched columns (`clip_start_time`, `clip_end_time`, `is_clip`, `parent_video_id`, `duration`) already exist on `baseball_videos`.

## Summary
- The legacy `/baseball/dashboard/stats/upload` wizard (Map-Columns + Match-Players steps) let coaches override column mappings and player matches client-side, but `uploadStatsCSV` discarded both and always re-derived matches via auto-detection server-side — silently dropping the coach's corrections.
- `uploadStatsCSVAction`/`uploadStatsCSV` now accept optional `columnMappings?: Record<string, string | null>` and `playerMatches?: PlayerMatch[]`. When supplied, stat-field columns resolve from the coach's explicit mapping (not `findColumnMapping` auto-detect) and player assignment resolves from the coach's `PlayerMatch` array (honoring explicit "skip" as a deliberate do-not-insert), falling back to auto-detection only when a given CSV name/field isn't covered. This mirrors the explicit-first/auto-detect-fallback pattern already used in `actions/imports.ts`.
- `StatsUploadClient.tsx` now serializes its `columnMappings` state to the `Record<csvColumn, mappedField>` shape and passes it plus the (post manual-override) `playerMatches` state to `uploadStatsCSV`.
- Also stamps `row_count`/`processed_count`/`completed_at` on insert + update — the columns `UploadHistory.tsx` actually reads (both already exist on `baseball_stat_uploads` per the `20260624000010_baseball_stat_uploads_reconcile.sql` migration; the action was previously only writing the legacy `total_rows`/`matched_rows` columns, so history always showed 0 processed rows).
- Out of scope (per spec): the raw-CSV persistence gap in `resolveUnmatchedPlayers` for the legacy path — that's a separate, larger fix already documented inline in `stats.ts`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Manual: explicitly "skip" a player in the Match step → no row inserted for that name, and it's not reported as unmatched

## Summary
- All three verdict buttons on a Practice Effectiveness review card ("Worked", "Needs More Time", "Not Enough Data") called `dispose('resolved')` — they all wrote byte-identical `disposition='resolved'` with no field distinguishing the coach's actual conclusion.
- Adds an orthogonal, nullable `verdict` column so each button persists a distinct outcome while `disposition` continues to represent workflow state only.
- Extends `setReviewDisposition` to accept an optional `verdict`, forced to `null` unless `disposition === 'resolved'` (so dismiss/reopen/convert can never leave a stale verdict behind).
- Extends the `runPracticeEffectiveness` engine's existing disposition carry-forward (#476 fix) to also carry forward `verdict` on re-runs, so re-measuring never clobbers a coach's recorded verdict — mirrors the exact pattern already used for `disposition`.
- Wires each of the three buttons to `dispose('resolved', <verdict>)` and renders a small badge with the persisted verdict on resolved cards.

## DB (gated — not applied)
New migration `supabase/migrations/20260701030000_baseball_practice_effectiveness_verdict.sql` (idempotent, additive only):
```sql
ALTER TABLE "public"."baseball_practice_effectiveness_reviews"
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "verdict" text NULL;

-- guarded CHECK add:
ALTER TABLE "public"."baseball_practice_effectiveness_reviews"
    ADD CONSTRAINT "baseball_practice_effectiveness_reviews_verdict_check"
    CHECK ("verdict" IN ('worked', 'needs_more_time', 'not_enough_data'));

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_baseball_practice_effectiveness_reviews_team_verdict"
    ON "public"."baseball_practice_effectiveness_reviews" ("team_id", "verdict");
```

## Summary
- Program logo upload (`/baseball/dashboard/program`) has always failed because the `logos` storage bucket and its `storage.objects` RLS policies never existed in any migration — the client code was already correctly wired to it.
- Adds public `logos` bucket (2 MB cap, matching client-side size guard; jpeg/png/webp/svg) + 3 owner-scoped INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies, mirroring the existing `course-images` bucket pattern.
- Hardening: upload/update errors now surface the real Supabase error message in the toast (was a generic swallowed message); previous logo object is best-effort cleaned up on re-upload so retries don't orphan storage objects.

## DB (gated — not applied)
New migration `supabase/migrations/20260701031000_baseball_program_logo_storage.sql`:
```sql
INSERT INTO storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
VALUES ('logos', 'logos', true, 2097152, ARRAY['image/jpeg','image/png','image/webp','image/svg+xml'])
ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE
  SET public = EXCLUDED.public, file_size_limit = EXCLUDED.file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types = EXCLUDED.allowed_mime_types;

CREATE POLICY "logos_authenticated_insert" ON storage.objects
  FOR INSERT TO authenticated WITH CHECK (bucket_id = 'logos');

CREATE POLICY "logos_owner_update" ON storage.objects
  FOR UPDATE TO authenticated
  USING (bucket_id = 'logos' AND owner = auth.uid())
  WITH CHECK (bucket_id = 'logos' AND owner = auth.uid());

CREATE POLICY "logos_owner_delete" ON storage.objects
  FOR DELETE TO authenticated USING (bucket_id = 'logos' AND owner = auth.uid());
```
This migration is NOT applied to any database by this PR — it needs to be run (`supabase db push` or equivalent) before program logo upload will work end-to-end.

## Test plan
- [ ] Confirm `select id, public, file_size_limit from storage.buckets where id='logos'` returns 1 row after migration apply
- [ ] `pg_policies` shows 3 `logos_%` policies on `storage.objects`

- [ ] Coach uploads <2MB image at `/baseball/dashboard/program` → "Logo updated successfully" toast, `organizations.logo_url` updated, public URL returns 200

## Summary

- `usePlayerRecruitingGate` (`src/hooks/use-route-protection.ts`) previously redirected only *unactivated* non-college players; activated non-college players who reached the coach-only `/baseball/dashboard/college-interest` page fell through every render branch in `CollegeInterestClient.tsx` to `return null`, with no redirect ever firing → permanent blank page.
- Gate now redirects **any** non-college player (activated or not) to `/baseball/dashboard/journey`, since this page has no player-facing rendering path at all. College players are still left to the component's own "not available" locked state (unchanged).
- `CollegeInterestClient.tsx`: the terminal `return null;` for the redirect-in-flight case is replaced with `return <PageLoading />;` (already imported) so there's no flash-of-blank while the client-side redirect resolves.

Confirmed by code trace (see `docs/audits/BASEBALLHELM_HONEST_FEATURE_READ.md`, loop #4): `CollegeInterestClient.tsx` is coach-only (queries `baseball_team_coach_staff` by coach id, zero player data path), but `usePlayerRecruitingGate()` only redirected on `!isActivated`, and a nav-registry entry sent players here directly.

## What & why
Team/player pitching totals were adding innings-pitched with `+`. In baseball notation `.1`/`.2` are **outs** (thirds of an inning), so `6.1 + 6.2` gave `12.3` instead of the correct `13.0` (39 outs). Any summed IP — and the ERA/WHIP/K9 derived from it — was wrong whenever multiple partial innings were involved.

## Fix
New shared helper `src/lib/baseball/innings.ts`:
- `ipToOuts` / `outsToIp` — convert between notation and outs
- `ipToInnings` — TRUE decimal innings (`outs / 3`) for rate denominators
- `sumInningsPitched(ips[])` — sum via outs (`[6.1, 6.2] → 13.0`)

Wired into every IP-summing site:
- `BoxScoreView.tsx` — team pitching totals + team ERA/WHIP
- `BoxScoreEntry.tsx` — pitching totals footer
- `PlayerGameLog.tsx` — pitching totals footer ERA/WHIP
- `read-models/stats-center.ts` — `addPitching` accumulation + `finalizePitching` (ERA/WHIP/K9/BB9/HR9/H9 now divide by true innings)

Rate stats now divide by true innings (`outs / 3`), not the base-10 notation value.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Shared `sumInningsPitched` helper that converts to outs and back (`6.1 + 6.2 → 13.0`)
- [x] Unit tests cover partial-inning sums and resulting ERA/WHIP/K9 (`innings.test.ts`, 8 cases, green)
- [x] Box Score view, game log footer, and Stats Center pitching splits all use the helper

## Testing
`vitest run src/lib/baseball/innings.test.ts` → 8 passed.

## What & why

`recalculatePlayerAggregates` (`src/app/baseball/actions/stats.ts`) only persisted `career_avg`, but My Stats `StatsOverviewCards` reads `career_obp` / `career_slg` / `career_ops` — columns that never existed on the live `baseball_player_aggregates` table. Players with CSV/practice upload data saw AVG populated but OBP/SLG/OPS permanently show `---`, despite having the counting stats.

- **New pure helper** `src/lib/baseball/aggregates/career-slash-line.ts` — `computeCareerSlashLine()` sums counting stats and applies standard formulas:
  - OBP = (H + BB + HBP) / (AB + BB + HBP + SF)
  - SLG = total bases / AB, total bases = H + 2B + 2·3B + 3·HR
  - OPS = OBP + SLG

## What & why

`EffectivenessReviewRow` in `StaffDecisionRoomClient.tsx` treated any non-`improved` direction as a regression, so `'no_change'` (metric held steady) and `null` (insufficient sample) rendered as a red **"Moved the wrong way"** badge. Coaches were misled into thinking neutral or inconclusive practice-effectiveness reviews had hurt performance.

The read model (`effectiveness.ts`) already maps DB directions to the honest union `'improved' | 'regressed' | 'no_change' | null` — the UI just wasn't honoring all four.

## Fix

Added an `effectivenessPresentation()` helper (mirroring the existing `verdictPresentation()` pattern in the same file) that maps each direction to distinct copy, tone, and glyph:

| direction | tone | copy | glyph |
|-----------|------|------|-------|
| `improved` | success | Associated improvement | trending up |
| `regressed` | danger | Moved the wrong way | trending down |
| `no_change` | secondary | Held steady | minus |
| `null` | secondary | Not enough data | help |

Only `regressed` uses danger styling now.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `improved`, `regressed`, `no_change`, and `null` each have distinct badge copy/tone.
- [x] `no_change`/`null` never use danger styling (both render `secondary`).
- [x] UI matches the mapped directions from the effectiveness read model.

## What & Why

Fixes #478.

Legacy `analyzePlayer` in `src/app/baseball/actions/insights.ts` emitted separate hit-milestone and HR-milestone insights, but **both** used `insight_type: 'development_milestone'`. Reconciliation keys insights by `` `${playerId}::${insight_type}` `` (lines 142-143), so when a player crossed both thresholds in one run (e.g. 50 hits **and** 10 HR), only one milestone survived — the other was dropped or blocked the first from refreshing. Coaches could miss an achievement entirely.

## Fix

- Hit-milestone branch now uses `insight_type: 'milestone_hits'`.
- HR-milestone branch now uses `insight_type: 'milestone_hr'`.
- Added both literals to the `BaseballInsightType` union in `src/lib/types/index.ts` so types stay correct.

Distinct types make the reconcile key naturally unique per milestone kind, so each is inserted/refreshed independently.

No DB migration required: `baseball_coach_insights.insight_type` is plain `text` with no CHECK constraint (verified in `20260527000000_prod_public_baseline.sql`). The substring-tolerant `templateForInsightType` in `practice-intelligence.ts` still resolves safely (default template).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Use distinct `insight_type` values (`milestone_hits`, `milestone_hr`).
- [x] Player with both milestones at once generates two persistable insights (different reconcile keys → two inserts).
- [x] Re-running generation updates each milestone independently without overwriting the other (each keyed row refreshes in place).

**Lane A · A2** (item-2 plan). The operational Signal Inbox has written **0 rows** in prod — a total silent no-op — for two live-verified reasons:

1. `uq_baseball_signal_dedupe` was `UNIQUE(team_id,dedupe_key)` **`DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED`**. The app upserts `.onConflict('team_id,dedupe_key')`; Postgres only infers **immediate, non-partial** unique indexes as `ON CONFLICT` arbiters, so both the DEFERRABLE constraint and the partial `baseball_signals_dedupe_open_uidx` were ineligible → every upsert failed.
2. `baseball_signals_disposition_check` had a stray `'open'` and was **missing** `'new'/'sample_too_small'/'converted'` that the app writes.

**Migration `20260701010000` (already applied to prod — table empty, no data risk):** rebuild `uq_baseball_signal_dedupe` as an **immediate** unique (drop+re-add, since `ALTER CONSTRAINT … NOT DEFERRABLE` is FK-only), drop the redundant partial index, widen the CHECK to the 7 `BaseballSignalDisposition` values. Verified live: constraint now `condeferrable=false`, partial index gone, CHECK = 7 values.

**App:** `operational-signals.ts` + `engine-run.ts` swallowed the upsert error and returned `success:true` — now they surface `success:false`/`emptyResult` (preserving the already-saved insight count) so a future failure is visible, not silent.

Closes #464

## Problem
Player onboarding completed via a client `.update()` scoped by `user_id`; if no row existed yet (failed seed / retry / alt auth path) it matched 0 rows, returned no error, and silently never set `onboarding_completed` → bounce loop.

## Fix
Route completion through the existing, tested `completePlayerOnboarding` server action (admin-client **upsert on `user_id`**, server-side identity via `auth.getUser()`). All **6 measurables** (`height_feet`, `bats`, `throws`, `pitch_velo`, `exit_velo`, `sixty_time`) are threaded through `PlayerOnboardingInput` into that upsert — a first attempt dropped them, but they have **no other write path** (verified: `updateMyPlayerProfile`'s whitelist omits them), so dropping them would have been a data-loss regression on core recruiting metrics read by discover/match-calculator/public profile. `profile_completion_percent` rescored to only credit fields actually persisted.

## Verification
- Page-wiring test click-drives the wizard and asserts `completePlayerOnboarding` is called with all 6 measurables; existing 24-test suite + new all-6-persist test green. `tsc`/eslint clean. Non-destructive.
title: fix(baseball): complete player onboarding via idempotent upsert without dropping measurables (#464)

Closes #492

## #486 (crit) — published lifts never reached players
`publishLiftDay` materialized sessions only into the legacy `baseball_lift_*` tables; the player Lift Home / Today surfaces read `helm_lifting_sessions`. A first attempt bridged them with `.upsert({ onConflict: 'legacy_baseball_id' })`, but that column has only a **partial** unique index (`WHERE legacy_baseball_id IS NOT NULL`, migration 20260625000020) — PostgREST can't target it, so every publish threw and was swallowed by a bare catch (100% silent no-op).

**Fix:** manual **SELECT-by-`legacy_baseball_id` → UPDATE-if-found / INSERT-if-absent** for both `helm_lifting_sessions` and `helm_lifting_session_exercises`, mirroring the working `createLiftAssignment` precedent. Bridge failures now go through `logServerError` (never silently swallowed).

## #492 (high) — edited prescriptions didn't appear on re-publish
Session-exercise step now **updates in place** (stage-and-swap, non-destructive) instead of skipping when a session already has rows.

## Verification
- New 415-line integration test (`publish-lift-day-helm-bridge.integration.test.ts`) asserts publish→round-trip + stage-and-swap + error-logging; 18/18 pass.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean, `src/app/baseball/actions` 464 tests green. Single file (+ test). Non-destructive.
- Concurrency race on program-assignment find-or-create documented inline (follow-up).
title: fix(baseball): materialize published lifts into helm_lifting_sessions via manual upsert (#486, #492)

## Summary
The only baseball coach-note composer (`PlayerProfileClient`) hardcoded `scope: 'staff_public'`, so coaches could **never** create the `player_visible` notes that Player Today + the player timeline are built to show. The server-side privacy model already supports it (`coach-notes.ts` emits `player_only` timeline events for `player_visible`; `player-today.ts` reads `player_visible`) — the authoring UI just couldn't produce them.

Added a **Visibility** selector offering **Staff only** (`staff_public`) and **Visible to player** (`player_visible`), passing the chosen scope to `createCoachNote`.

## Files (1)
- `src/components/baseball/player-profile/PlayerProfileClient.tsx`

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Composer exposes the permitted scopes (`staff_public` + `player_visible`).
- [x] Creating a `player_visible` note appears on Player Today + the player timeline as `player_only` (existing server path).
- [x] `staff_public` notes remain absent from player surfaces.

## Adversarial notes
Both offered scopes are authorable by **any** staff (`canAuthorScope` → `true` without a capability requirement), so a coach can't pick a scope the server would reject. The capability-gated scopes (`coach_group`/`strength`/`academic`/`hidden_from_player`) are intentionally **not** offered here — they'd need the coach's capability map client-side; that's a follow-up, not required by #511. The server still enforces `canAuthorScope` regardless.

## Verification
- `npx eslint …/PlayerProfileClient.tsx` — 0 warnings (used `NativeSelect`, not a raw button)
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint:ratchet` — OK, no regressions

Closes #511
title: fix(baseball): let coaches choose note visibility (staff vs player) (#511)

## Summary
`mapItem` hardcodes `disposition: 'new'` for every emitted item, and the item persistence uses `.upsert(itemRows, { onConflict: 'review_id,dedupe_key', ignoreDuplicates: false })`. So re-running a postgame review **overwrote every conflicting row's `disposition` back to `'new'`**, re-opening items a coach had already `converted_to_timeline` / `converted_to_task` / `dismissed` — directly contradicting the file's own comment ("never clobber a coach conversion") and the non-destructive re-run contract.

Now, before the upsert, prior dispositions are fetched by `dedupe_key` and any **non-`'new'`** disposition is preserved in the payload. Re-runs still refresh title/detail/content and re-open genuinely-new items, but coach actions survive.

## Files (1)
- `src/app/baseball/actions/postgame.ts`

## Adversarial notes
- The stale-reconcile step (soft-dismiss `'new'` items no longer emitted) is unaffected — it only touches `disposition = 'new'` rows, and preserved conversions are no longer `'new'`.
- Genuinely new / re-emitted-still-new items keep `'new'` (no prior row, or prior was `'new'`).

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint:ratchet` — OK, no regressions

Closes #477
title: fix(baseball): preserve postgame item disposition across review re-runs (#477)

Batched — both live on the roster/lineup surface.

## #490 — swap the displaced player
`LineupBuilder.handleDrop` cleared the source slot to `null` and then overwrote the target, so dropping a player onto an **occupied** slot in a slot→slot move left the source empty and dumped the incumbent out of the lineup. Now it **swaps**: the target's current player moves into the source slot. Dragging in from the bench still returns the incumbent to the available pool (they no longer occupy a slot). Also guards the case where the target slot doesn't exist.

## #489 — don't fake save success
The roster lineup `onSave` awaited `saveLineup(...)` and then unconditionally toasted **"Lineup saved successfully"**. But `saveLineup` returns `{ success: false, error }` (it does not throw) for validation failures — duplicate batting orders, > 9 players, missing coach. Now it checks `result.success` and surfaces `result.error` on failure.

## Files (2)
- `src/components/coach/lineup/LineupBuilder.tsx`
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/roster/RosterClient.tsx`

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` — clean

Closes #490
Closes #489

## Summary
`/baseball/dashboard/activate` performed a **raw client-side** `baseball_players.update({ recruiting_activated: true })`, bypassing `activateRecruitingExposure` — the server action gated on the team's `recruiting_exposure_enabled` toggle (`requiredPlayerAccess`). A program that turned recruiting exposure **off** in Settings could still be activated from this page if RLS allowed the write, so the toggle wasn't load-bearing on the surface players actually use.

Now `handleActivate` calls `activateRecruitingExposure()` and handles its error envelope. The `withBaseballAction` wrapper **throws a sanitized error** when exposure is disabled (or the caller is a college player), so activation fails with a user-visible message and the row stays unchanged.

body:
One **camps-registration** surface, three related defects (all share `camps/page.tsx`, so batched per the clean-slate plan).

## #442 — atomic capacity (high)
Player registration was a **raw client-side insert** gated only by a UI `isFull` check; `registerForCamp` never read `capacity`, so concurrent sign-ups could overbook.
- **New migration** `20260701000442_...`: `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC `baseball_register_for_camp(p_camp_id)` — locks the camp row (`FOR UPDATE`), counts active registrations, and rejects over-capacity joins **inside one transaction**. Two simultaneous registrations for the last spot serialize; the second sees the updated count and gets `full`.
- Player is resolved from `auth.uid()` (**no IDOR** — you can only register yourself). `REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC` + `GRANT EXECUTE TO authenticated, service_role` only.
- `registerForCamp` now calls the RPC and maps results; `handleRegister` goes through the server action and updates the UI **only on success** (surfacing `This camp is full`).
- Also fixes a **latent bug**: the old action inserted a non-existent `registered_at` column (would have failed at runtime).

## #443 — accurate counts (high)
Card counts / `isFull` counted **cancelled** registrations, so a camp stayed "full" after drop-outs. A shared helper counts only active (non-cancelled) rows, applied via one `loadCamps` loader that replaces **5 copies** of the raw embedded-count query.

## #447 — dates
Camp dates were parsed with `new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')` (UTC midnight) → prior day in US timezones. Shared `formatCampDate` anchors date-only values at **local noon**, reused by list + detail pages.

## Files (6)
- `supabase/migrations/20260701000442_baseball_camp_register_atomic.sql` (new RPC)
- `src/lib/baseball/camp-utils.ts` (new: `formatCampDate`, `activeCampCountsByCamp`) + `.test.ts`
- `src/app/baseball/actions/camps.ts` (register → RPC)
- `camps/page.tsx` (loader + counts + register-via-action + dates)
- `camps/[id]/page.tsx` (shared date formatter)

## Adversarial review
- **Atomicity:** `FOR UPDATE` on the camp row serializes concurrent registrations; the active count is read under the lock, so the last spot can't be double-booked.
- **Auth:** anon can't call it (grant + `auth.uid()` null → `unauthorized`); `SECURITY DEFINER` only performs the capacity-checked registration for the calling player.
- **Authoritative vs display:** the RPC is the source of truth for capacity regardless of RLS; the client count is a UX hint with the same RLS visibility as the original embedded count (no regression).
- Capacity `NULL` = unlimited (check skipped); cancelled→re-register reactivates the existing row.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run src/lib/baseball/camp-utils.test.ts` — pass (count-drop + noon-anchor)
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint:ratchet` — OK, no regressions

Closes #442
Closes #443
Closes #447
title: fix(baseball): enforce camp capacity atomically + accurate counts + dates (#442, #443, #447)

body:
## The leak
Greptile's Usage dashboard shows it bills **bots as developers**:
- `dependabot[bot]` → 44 credits
- `github-actions[bot]` → 34 credits

That's **~78 credits/month** reviewing automated dependency bumps and workflow commits that never need AI review — a big chunk of what tripped the flex limit (alongside 184 from the human account).

## Why the existing setting didn't catch it
`ignoreKeywords: "dependabot"` matches PR **titles**, but Dependabot titles are "bump X from Y to Z" — they don't contain the word "dependabot". The correct mechanism is **`excludeAuthors`**.

## Fix
`excludeAuthors: ["dependabot[bot]", "github-actions[bot]", "renovate[bot]", "greptile[bot]"]` — Greptile skips these authors' PRs entirely, so they stop draining the 50/dev credit pool.

Combined with `triggerOnUpdates: false` (#562), future credit burn drops sharply: no bot reviews + no re-review-on-every-push.

Config-only.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: chore(greptile): excludeAuthors bots — stop billing Dependabot/Actions reviews

body:
One-line change: stop Greptile re-reviewing on every push.

Greptile includes **50 review credits / active dev / billing period**; beyond that it's $1/review flex, and the flex cap (once hit) skips all reviews until reset. On an active PR stack, `triggerOnUpdates: true` re-reviews on every commit and drains the 50 fast — a likely cause of hitting the monthly limit.

With `false`, Greptile reviews on **PR open** and on explicit **`@greptileai review`** comments, but not on every push. Biggest single credit saver for a busy repo.

Config-only.

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #549 (drop legacy no-capability RLS policies). #549 deliberately deferred `baseball_team_lineups` and `baseball_lineup_positions` because their correct capability, `can_manage_lineups`, referenced a column that doesn't exist on `baseball_team_coach_staff` — gating on it then would have risked a runtime error instead of closing the bypass. This PR fixes the root cause and then closes the deferred bypass.

Refs NN-1, NN-2 (`docs/CLEANSLATE_JOB_LIST.md`).

Two coupled migrations, one PR (the column-add must apply before the lineups RLS — enforced by filename ordering):

### `supabase/migrations/20260701002000_baseball_staff_capability_columns.sql` (NN-1)

`has_baseball_staff_capability()`'s `RETURN CASE` references 17 `can_*`/`is_head_coach` fields; `baseball_team_coach_staff` only has 11 of the corresponding columns. Reconciled live:

- **Existing (11):** `can_invite_staff`, `can_manage_calendar`, `can_manage_imports`, `can_manage_lifting`, `can_manage_practice`, `can_manage_roster`, `can_manage_settings`, `can_manage_stats`, `can_message_team`, `can_view_academics`, `can_view_medical`
- **Missing (6, added by this migration):** `can_manage_lineups`, `can_view_readiness`, `can_modify_availability`, `can_view_private_notes`, `can_message_players`, `can_export_reports`

Confirmed live that referencing a missing one errors immediately rather than resolving false:

```sql
SELECT CASE 'can_manage_lineups'::text
  WHEN 'can_manage_lineups' THEN t.can_manage_lineups
  ELSE false
END FROM public.baseball_team_coach_staff t LIMIT 1;
-- ERROR: 42703: column t.can_manage_lineups does not exist
```

PL/pgSQL type-checks the whole `RETURN CASE ... END` as one unit the first time it executes, so any call to `has_baseball_staff_capability()` that reaches the CASE (an active, non-head-coach staff row found) risks hitting this.

This is also a **live, user-facing bug today**, not just a latent RLS landmine: `src/components/baseball/staff/StaffSettingsClient.tsx` (backed by `src/lib/baseball/capability-groups.ts`) already renders toggles for all 6 of these capabilities. Any coach trying to grant a teammate "Manage lineups", "View readiness", "Modify availability", "View private notes", "Message players", or "Export reports" today is writing to a column that doesn't exist.

Columns are `NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, backfilled `true` for `is_head_coach OR is_primary` — mirroring the exact precedent set by `can_manage_documents` (`20260630180100_baseball_documents_capability.sql`). This isn't cosmetic: verified live that `has_baseball_staff_capability()` only short-circuits to `true` for `is_head_coach`, **not** `is_primary`, so a primary-but-not-head coach needs the concrete column value to pass the RLS check these columns will gate. Verified live: 5/5 current `baseball_team_coach_staff` rows are `is_primary = true` (3/5 also `is_head_coach`), and none use the `capabilities` jsonb bag — so this backfill preserves 100% of current staff write access; it grants nothing new to anyone who didn't already have it via `is_head_coach`/`is_primary`.

### `supabase/migrations/20260701003000_baseball_lineups_rls_capability.sql` (NN-2)

Mirrors #549's pattern for the two deferred tables, now that `can_manage_lineups` is safe to use:

- **`baseball_team_lineups`**: drop `"Coaches can manage their team lineups"` (ALL, no cap/status check). Add `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` on `has_baseball_staff_capability(team_id, 'can_manage_lineups')`, plus a staff `SELECT` (`is_baseball_team_staff(team_id)`) since the legacy ALL was the coaches' *only* read path — the remaining `"Players can view their team lineups"` SELECT is player-only and is left untouched.
- **`baseball_lineup_positions`**: has no `team_id` of its own — scoped via the parent lineup. Drop `"Coaches can manage lineup positions"` (ALL, no cap/status check). Add `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` gated by `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM baseball_team_lineups l WHERE l.id = lineup_id AND has_baseball_staff_capability(l.team_id, 'can_manage_lineups'))`, plus a staff `SELECT` via the same `EXISTS` pattern with `is_baseball_team_staff(l.team_id)`. The existing `"Players can view lineup positions"` SELECT is untouched.

Both: `to_regclass()`-guarded, `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS` → `CREATE POLICY`, `TO authenticated` only, no anon grants, re-runnable.

## Adversarial self-review

- **Coach reads:** the dropped ALL policy on both tables was also the coaches' only read path (the surviving SELECT policies are player-only). Both new staff SELECT policies close that gap — verified this before finalizing, since a naive drop-and-replace-writes-only would have silently broken lineup viewing for every coach.
- **Head-coach writes:** `has_baseball_staff_capability()` short-circuits to `true` for `is_head_coach` regardless of the specific capability column, so head coaches keep write access with zero dependency on NN-1's backfill.
- **Primary-but-not-head-coach writes:** depends entirely on NN-1's backfill (no short-circuit for `is_primary` in the SQL helper). Verified live that 5/5 current staff rows are `is_primary = true`, so this is a confirmed no-op for every staff member who can write today — nobody loses access.
- **`baseball_lineup_positions` subquery correctness:** the capability check resolves entirely through `lineup_id -> baseball_team_lineups.team_id -> baseball_team_coach_staff`; it never touches `baseball_players` or the row's own `player_id` column, so it resolves identically regardless of any player row's existence.
- **Table grants:** confirmed live that `authenticated` already holds `SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE` (plus TRIGGER/REFERENCES/TRUNCATE) on both tables and `anon` holds nothing — new policies take effect with no additional GRANTs, no anon exposure introduced.
- **Type regen:** ran `db:types` manually against live prod to check for drift — since neither migration is applied yet, the live schema (and therefore generated types) is unchanged; nothing to commit there. Types will pick up the new columns naturally once this migration is actually applied.

## Verification

All findings (exact policy names/`cmd`/`qual`/`with_check`, column lists, function body via `pg_get_functiondef`, table grants, live row counts) were pulled via the read-only Supabase MCP `execute_sql` tool. No `apply_migration` call was made; this PR is migration-file-only.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run test:rls` locally / in CI against a database with both migrations applied, in order
- [ ] Manually verify: a coach can toggle "Manage lineups" / "View readiness" / "Modify availability" / "View private notes" / "Message players" / "Export reports" on a teammate in Staff Settings without error
- [ ] Manually verify: a staff member without `can_manage_lineups` cannot INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE `baseball_team_lineups` or `baseball_lineup_positions` rows for their team via direct PostgREST
- [ ] Manually verify: a `suspended`/`removed` staff row cannot write to either table
- [ ] Manually verify: lineup build/publish flow in `src/app/baseball/actions/lineups.ts` still works end-to-end for a head coach and for a primary (non-head) coach
title: fix(baseball): add missing staff capability columns + gate lineups RLS

## Summary
The player Privacy Settings form rendered ~18 `show_*` toggles and wrote the entire settings object to `baseball_player_settings` through the **untyped** client. But that table only has four privacy columns — `profile_visibility`, `show_academics`, `show_contact_info`, `show_dream_schools`. Every save therefore hit a PostgREST "unknown column" error and toasted **"Failed to save privacy settings"** — the feature was **completely broken** (high severity).

## Fix (2 files)
- **`PrivacySettingsForm.tsx`** — reduced to the 3 editable boolean columns that exist (Contact Info, Academics, Dream Schools), mapped correctly, and persisted via the **typed** client (`supabase.from('baseball_player_settings')`) so an unknown column is now a *compile* error. Kept the existing non-destructive select→update/insert (no DELETE-then-INSERT, no upsert-constraint assumption).
- **`privacy/page.tsx`** — load only the real columns; removed the fabricated `show_full_name/…= true` defaults for non-existent fields.

`profile_visibility` is intentionally **not** written here — it gates public-profile access (`public-profile-access.ts`) and is managed elsewhere.

## Spec / product note
The `12_profile` V1 spec defines only *coach-controlled* visibility of data to players — there's no spec basis for the 18 player toggles, so they were unbacked UI. I removed them rather than leave dead controls. **Surfacing a decision:** if granular player privacy controls (per-field videos/stats/location/etc.) are desired, that's a separate additive migration to add those columns + wire the read side — happy to follow up.

## Adversarial notes
Client-side write is RLS-scoped to the player's own settings row (unchanged pattern). No destructive write. Only 3 booleans are written; `profile_visibility` and notification columns are preserved. Form types are consumed only by this page (verified), so the interface change is contained.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` — clean (typed client now guards the payload)
- `npm run lint:ratchet` — OK, no regressions

Closes #470
title: fix(baseball): make privacy settings save the real schema columns (#470)

## Summary
The Decision Room staff read-model computed `canManageStaff = is_head_coach || can_invite_staff || can_manage_settings`. But **every** staff mutation in `actions/staff.ts` (`inviteStaff`, `updateStaffCapabilities`, `removeStaff`, …) is gated on `requiredCapability: 'can_invite_staff'`. A coach with only `can_manage_settings` therefore saw the invite/edit UI (client-gated on `canManageStaff`) and then hit server-side rejections.

Aligned the read-model to the **server authority model** (`src/lib/baseball/capabilities.ts`): primary and head coaches hold ALL caps; everyone else needs the specific `can_invite_staff` flag.

- **Drop** `can_manage_settings` → removes the false-positive (UI shown, mutation fails).
- **Add** `is_primary` → removes a symmetric false-negative (a primary coach not flagged `is_head_coach` still has full authority server-side, so they should see the UI).

## Files (1)
- `src/lib/baseball/read-models/decision-room/staff-settings.ts`

## Adversarial notes
This is a read-model that only decides whether to **show** management UI — the real authority is still enforced by `withBaseballAction({ requiredCapability: 'can_invite_staff' })` on every mutation, so this can't grant access; it only stops advertising actions that would fail. Verified head/primary → all caps in `capabilities.ts` (lines 15-16), so keeping those two in the gate matches the server.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint:ratchet` — OK, no regressions

Closes #505
title: fix(baseball): gate Staff Settings management on can_invite_staff, not settings (#505)

## Problem (net-new, found during the Wave-1 RLS audit)
`baseball_box_score_batting` and `baseball_box_score_pitching` gate **INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE** on `is_baseball_team_coach_v2(team_id)` only — that helper checks team membership and nothing else: **no capability flag, no active/suspended/removed status check.** Any `baseball_team_coach_staff` row for the team (any capability, any status) can insert/update/delete game batting & pitching lines via a direct PostgREST call.

This is the identical bypass shape #549 closes on `baseball_player_stats` / `baseball_player_season_stats`; these two box-score tables were simply outside #549's assigned table list (flagged by the RLS-cleanup agent).

## Fix
`supabase/migrations/20260701001000_baseball_box_score_batting_pitching_rls.sql` — replace the `is_baseball_team_coach_v2` write policies with `has_baseball_staff_capability(team_id, 'can_manage_stats')` (the exact capability the sibling stat tables use in #549). That function enforces `COALESCE(status,'active')='active'` internally and short-circuits `true` for head coaches, so this closes **both** the capability and the status bypass in one move.

## Scope
- **SELECT policies untouched** — read-path unaffected; only WRITES tightened (same scope decision as #549).
- ADDITIVE / re-runnable (`DROP POLICY IF EXISTS` → `CREATE`, `to_regclass()`-guarded). No anon grants.
- **Written, not applied** — no `apply_migration` call; needs manual prod apply after merge.
- Depends on nothing; complements #549. `baseball_team_lineups`/`baseball_lineup_positions` remain deferred (blocked by the missing `can_manage_lineups` column — NN-1).
title: fix(baseball): capability+status-gate box-score batting/pitching writes (sibling of #549)

## Summary
`handleWatchlist` and `handleAddAllToWatchlist` mutated local `watchlistIds` immediately after awaiting `addToWatchlist` / `removeFromWatchlist`. Those actions return `{ success: false, ... }` **without throwing** on rejection (unauthenticated, missing `can_manage_stats`, validation), so the `try/catch` never caught it and the star still flipped — diverging the UI from what's actually watchlisted. Now the state update is gated on `result.success`.

## Files (1)
- `src/components/coach/discover/DiscoverView.tsx`

## Adversarial notes
No optimistic pre-flip exists, so gating on `success` is sufficient — there's no stale state to roll back. On failure the star simply doesn't move (silent no-op rather than false success); DiscoverView has no toast infra and adding it is out of scope for this fix.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` — clean

## Why
While wiring more context into Greptile, I verified the config against Greptile's live docs and found the **existing `.greptile/` setup was using field/file names Greptile doesn't read**:
- `config.json` used `review`/`ignore`/`additional_context`/`instructions_file` — none are real fields. The real schema is `strictness`/`commentTypes`/`ignorePatterns`/`ignoreKeywords`/`instructions`/`rules[]`.
- Greptile auto-reads exactly **three** files from a `.greptile/` folder: `config.json`, `rules.md`, `files.json`. A file named `instructions.md` **is not read**.

Net: our custom rules were being ignored; Greptile fell back to dashboard defaults (which is why it still posted reviews). This migrates to the correct schema and makes Greptile a **product-aware reviewer that also suggests enhancements**.

## Changes
**Correct schema**
- `config.json` rewritten to real fields + a structured `rules[]` set (service-role scope, RLS-on-new-table + no cross-team `USING(true)`, no destructive writes, pipeline-stage enum, no client-side LLM, no historical-migration edits, sport-prefixed tables, server-action auth, calendar-timezone, idempotent imports).
- `git mv instructions.md → rules.md` (hard-rule numbering preserved so existing doc citations stay valid). Added a note explaining the `.greptile/` file model and that **Greptile auto-indexes the code** (docs are for *intent*, not code description).

**Ultra-aware context**
- New `.greptile/files.json` — 22 scoped context pointers (business docs load every review; sport brains + research scoped per surface).
- New **"Suggest enhancements"** mode in `rules.md`: non-blocking, business-grounded suggestions (finish a workflow, remove coach/player friction, close a competitor-parity gap, add a missing test/telemetry lane).
- **Cascading per-surface rules**: `src/app/golf`, `src/app/baseball`, `src/lib/coachhelm`, `supabase` `.greptile/rules.md` (calendar folded in as *one example*, not a focus — per your note).

**Closes the baseball context gap** (CLAUDE.md said Baseball had "no deep reference")
- `memory/context/baseballhelm-{database,features,workflows}.md` + `docs/business/07-baseballhelm-context.md`.

## Notable finding surfaced by the baseball mining
- **Pipeline-stage bug (triple-confirmed):** `src/lib/recruiting/stages.ts` declares 7 stages (`contacted`, `campus_visit`) but `baseball_pipeline_stage` enum has only 5 → dragging a card to those columns writes an invalid enum value Postgres rejects, and that drag path skips `assertCoachCanRecruitPlayer`.
- **Possible RLS gap (needs prod verification):** `baseball_players_select` policy is `USING (true)` in the baseline migration (later migration `20260630180000_baseball_scope_player_ids_rls` may address it — unverified against prod).

Docs/config only. No source code, no golf files touched.

## Summary
`isUpcoming(dateStr)` parsed a date-only departure (`YYYY-MM-DD`) as **UTC midnight** and compared it to a UTC "today" (`new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]`), while `formatDate` anchored the same value at **local noon** (`+ 'T12:00:00'`). Now `isUpcoming` uses the same local-noon anchor and compares against local midnight today, so Upcoming/Past matches the date shown.

## Summary RLS is applied across BaseballHelm (441 policies, verified live 2026-07-01), but ~9 tables still carry a pre-capability-model baseline `FOR ALL` policy with **no capability check and no staff-status check**. Postgres ORs multiple PERMISSIVE policies together on the same command, so on every affected table the old ALL policy silently overrides the newer, correctly capability-gated per-command policies — any team staff row (any capability, and on several tables any active/suspended/removed status) can write via a direct PostgREST call, bypassing both the capability model and the app-layer gate in `src/lib/baseball/capabilities.ts`. This PR drops the legacy ALL policy on 5 tables and adds the missing capability-gated per-command policy/policies so every write path is capability-gated + status-gated (`has_baseball_staff_capability()` itself enforces `COALESCE(status,'active') = 'active'`, so this closes the status bypass and the capability bypass together). Closes #405, #394, #501 (RLS scope). Migration: `supabase/migrations/20260701000000_baseball_rls_legacy_policy_cleanup.sql` — **written, not applied**. All findings below were verified live against `pg_policies` / `information_schema` via the read-only Supabase MCP `execute_sql` tool; no `apply_migration` call was made. ## Tables covered | Table | Legacy policy dropped | Capability chosen | Why | |---|---|---|---| | `baseball_player_stats` | `Coaches can manage player stats` (ALL, plain staff-row EXISTS, no cap/status) | `can_manage_stats` (new DELETE only) | INSERT/UPDATE were already correctly gated on this capability; there was no DELETE policy at all | | `baseball_staff_invitations` | `baseball_staff_invitations_manage` (ALL, gated by `baseball_can_invite_staff()` — checks is_head_coach/can_invite_staff but never status) | `can_invite_staff` (new DELETE only) | INSERT/UPDATE were already correctly gated on this capability; there was no DELETE policy at all | | `baseball_player_season_stats` | `Coaches can manage season stats` (ALL, gated by `is_baseball_team_coach_v2()` — team membership only, no cap/status) | `can_manage_stats` (new INSERT+UPDATE+DELETE) | No per-command write policies existed at all; sibling table `baseball_player_stats` uses this exact capability for the same stat-entry workflow | | `baseball_box_score_uploads` | `Coaches can manage their uploads` (ALL, gated on raw `coach_id` ownership only — no team/cap/status check) | `can_manage_imports` (new SELECT+INSERT+UPDATE+DELETE) | Matches the sibling `baseball_stat_uploads` table, which is **already** correctly gated on this exact capability for its INSERT/UPDATE. **Note:** this table had *no* SELECT policy at all before this PR — dropping the ALL policy without adding one would have removed read access entirely and broken the box-score review flow in `src/app/baseball/actions/games.ts`, so a SELECT policy (`is_baseball_team_staff(team_id)`, matching the sibling's `baseball_stat_uploads_select` pattern) was added alongside the write policies. This is the one place this PR adds a SELECT policy rather than leaving SELECT untouched. | | `baseball_team_invitations` | `Coaches can manage their team invitations` (ALL, bare tcs+coaches join, no cap/status) | `can_manage_roster` (new INSERT+UPDATE+DELETE) | See "capability I was unsure about" below. The existing `Anyone can view active invitations by code` SELECT policy is untouched. | ## Deferred (needs a capability decision / schema fix first) **`baseball_team_lineups` and `baseball_lineup_positions` are NOT touched by this PR.** The correct capability is clearly `can_manage_lineups` — confirmed via `src/app/baseball/actions/lineups.ts` (`requireBaseballCapability(teamId, 'can_manage_lineups')`, lines 68/77/148/216) and `src/lib/baseball/capabilities.ts`. But it cannot be safely used in a new RLS `WITH CHECK` today: `has_baseball_staff_capability()`'s CASE branch for `can_manage_lineups` references `baseball_team_coach_staff.can_manage_lineups` — **a column that does not exist on that table.** Confirmed live: ```sql SELECT CASE 'can_manage_lineups'::text WHEN 'can_manage_lineups' THEN t.can_manage_lineups ELSE false END FROM public.baseball_team_coach_staff t LIMIT 1; -- ERROR: 42703: column t.can_manage_lineups does not exist ``` `information_schema.columns` confirms the table has 11 `can_*` boolean columns and `can_manage_lineups` isn't one of them, even though the app-layer capability list (`BASEBALL_CAPABILITY_KEYS`) and the SQL function's CASE both reference it. Because PL/pgSQL type-checks the whole `RETURN CASE ... END` expression as one unit the first time that code path executes, gating these two tables on `can_manage_lineups` risks a hard runtime error on every non-head-coach lineup write, rather than a clean deny. Shipping that would trade a silent security bypass for a broken feature — worse, not better. **Recommendation:** file a follow-up migration adding `can_manage_lineups boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` to `baseball_team_coach_staff` (mirroring how `can_manage_documents` was added in `20260630180100_baseball_documents_capability.sql`, backfilled from `is_head_coach`/`is_primary`), then gate `baseball_team_lineups` / `baseball_lineup_positions` in a second, small migration once the column exists and is backfilled. ## Capability I was less certain about `baseball_team_invitations` → `can_manage_roster`. This table issues **player** join codes (roster growth), distinct from `baseball_staff_invitations` (staff invites, already correctly gated on `can_invite_staff`). There's no existing app-layer capability check to mirror for this table — `InviteModal.tsx` and `TeamsClient.tsx` both insert directly via the browser Supabase client with no capability gate at all client-side, so RLS is the *only* enforcement point here. `can_manage_roster` is the closest existing "who controls my roster" capability and is a defensible choice, but if there's a more specific intended capability for join-code generation I didn't find evidence of it — flagging in case there's context I'm missing. ## Verification - All current-state findings (exact policy names, `cmd`, `qual`, `with_check`, table columns, function bodies, table grants) were pulled live via `mcp__supabase__execute_sql` (read-only) — no writes made to the database. - Confirmed `authenticated` already holds `SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE` (plus TRIGGER/REFERENCES/TRUNCATE) at the table-grant level on all 5 tables, and `anon` holds nothing — so the new DELETE/INSERT/UPDATE policies take effect without any new GRANTs, and no anon exposure is introduced. - Did not run `apply_migration`; this PR is migration-file-only. ## Test plan - [ ] `npm run test:rls` locally / in CI against a database with this migration applied - [ ] Manually verify: a staff member with `can_manage_stats = false` cannot INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE `baseball_player_stats` or `baseball_player_season_stats` rows for their team - [ ] Manually verify: a `suspended`/`removed` staff row cannot write to any of the 5 tables above via direct PostgREST - [ ] Manually verify: the box-score upload → review flow in `src/app/baseball/actions/games.ts` still works end-to-end (read path depends on the newly-added SELECT policy) - [ ] Manually verify: join-code generation (`InviteModal.tsx`) still works for a coach who holds `can_manage_roster`

The box-score upload read policy needs a status-aware check before merging. - The new write policies use the capability helper that rejects inactive staff. - The new upload SELECT policy uses a staff-membership helper that does not reject suspended or removed staff. - Direct PostgREST reads can expose raw upload and parsed player data. supabase/migrations/20260701000000_baseball_rls_legacy_policy_cleanup.sql

1.2.0

body:
Security + robustness hardening across the CI workflows. Validated locally with `actionlint` (exit 0). ### 🔴 P0 — supply-chain RCE in the security gate `review-gate.yml`'s actionlint step ran `bash <(curl -fsSL …/rhysd/actionlint/main/scripts/download-actionlint.bash)` — a piped install from a **mutable branch** (`main`) executed *inside the workflow that gates every PR*. Now pinned to the immutable tag **v1.7.12**. ### 🟠 Pinned floating downloads (`releases/latest` → tag) - **ast-grep** → `0.44.0` (asset name unchanged) - **hadolint** → `v2.14.0` — also fixes a latent break: `latest` moved the asset from `hadolint-Linux-x86_64` to lowercase `hadolint-linux-x86_64`, so the old capital-L URL 404s on current releases. ### 🟠 Missing hardening added - **`migration-lockdown.yml`** (had none): `permissions: contents: read`, PR concurrency cancellation, job timeout. - **`codeql.yml`**: PR-scoped concurrency, 20-min timeout, and removed the dead `swift → macos-latest` runner ternary (swift isn't in the matrix). - **Timeouts** on all 11 `review-gate` jobs + all 12 `ci` jobs (previously a hung job could burn up to GitHub's 6-hour default). ### Deferred (follow-up) - Pin bare `pip install` / `npm install -g` linter installs to versions (low supply-chain risk, adds maintenance; not done to avoid churn). - SHA-pin any remaining floating-tag third-party actions (`gitleaks-action` is already SHA-pinned). Part of the "max out the GitHub setup" pass. `gitleaks` was already SHA-pinned; no `${{ github.event.* }}` untrusted input is interpolated into any `run:` block in the touched files. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR hardens the GitHub Actions CI and review workflows. The main changes are: - Pinned workflow downloads and checkout actions. - Added timeouts across CI and review-gate jobs. - Added least-privilege permissions and concurrency controls. - Moved the Supabase RLS job into the CI aggregate gate.

Confidence Score: 5/5

This looks safe to merge. - No blocking issues found in the changed code.

Important Files Changed
