Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.57.0 to 1.61.1
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.61.1

Bug Fixes

  • #41365 [Bug]: Expect.Extend matcher with same name as default matcher in same expect instance overrides default matchers implementation to custom matcher
  • #41351 [Bug]: Playwright UI mode: apiRequestContext._wrapApiCall reports unexpected number of bytes (same test passes in headed mode)
  • #41360 [Bug]: Trace viewer: message times in websockets are downscaled by 1000
  • #41311 [Bug]: [Regression]: Sync loader throws "context.conditions?.includes is not a function" on Node 22.15
  • #41371 [Regression]: Sync ESM loader (registerHooks) fails to resolve extensionless .ts subpath imports across pnpm workspace symlinks

v1.61.0

🔑 WebAuthn passkeys

New Credentials virtual authenticator, available via browserContext.credentials, lets tests register passkeys and answer navigator.credentials.create() / navigator.credentials.get() ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers:

const context = await browser.newContext();

// Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.
await context.credentials.create('example.com', {
id: credentialId,
userHandle,
privateKey,
publicKey,
});
await context.credentials.install();


const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com/login');
// The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.

You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with credentials.get(), and seed it into later tests — see Credentials for details.

🗃️ Web Storage

New WebStorage API, available via page.localStorage and page.sessionStorage, reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:

await page.localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const token = await page.localStorage.getItem('token');
const items = await page.sessionStorage.items();

New APIs

Network

  • apiResponse.securityDetails() and apiResponse.serverAddr() mirror the browser-side response.securityDetails() and response.serverAddr().

Release notes

eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7.1.1 (April 17, 2026)

Note: 7.1.0 accidentally removed the component-hook-factories rule, causing errors for users who referenced it in their ESLint config. This is now fixed.

  • Add deprecated no-op component-hook-factories rule for backwards compatibility. (@​mofeiZ in #36307)

eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7.1.0 (April 16, 2026)

This release adds ESLint v10 support, improves performance by skipping compilation for non-React files, and includes compiler lint improvements including better set-state-in-effect detection, improved ref validation, and more helpful error reporting.

  • Add ESLint v10 support. (@​azat-io in #35720)
  • Skip compilation for non-React files to improve performance. (@​josephsavona in #35589)

  • Improved ref validation for non-mutating functions and event handler props. (@​josephsavona in #35893, @​kolvian in #35062)

## Summary The detailed-stats **admin path** (`getDetailedStats` reads on the service-role client to bypass `golf_shots` RLS + the 8s `authenticated` timeout — the #339/#340 root fix) was *still* emitting `57014 canceling statement due to statement timeout` → round-level fallback on heavier / background reads (5 occurrences over 06‑22→06‑23, all `user_id: null` = CoachHelm engine/cron fetches, not user-facing). **Root cause:** `service_role` had no explicit `statement_timeout` (`rolconfig` null), so it didn't get the unbounded behavior the fix assumed. This sets an explicit, bounded **30s** — matching the convention heavy DB functions already use (`SET statement_timeout TO '30s'`), generous over the ~1k-row shot read, still bounding runaways. ## State - Applied to prod via Supabase MCP (`service_role.rolconfig` now `statement_timeout=30s`). This file is source-of-truth / for other envs. - **Honesty note:** I could not fully confirm from the SQL console that the pooled PostgREST path picks up the new value on `SET ROLE` (the console session has an explicit 2min that masks all role GUCs). It's the Supabase-documented approach and harmless if a no-op; I'll confirm by watching whether the background fallback warnings stop, and escalate to a function/RPC-level `SET` if they persist. ## Not bugs (verified while investigating) - **Ben's stats:** zero errors in `error_logs`; he has 0 rounds/shots → empty by data, not a failure. - **SG standards change (scratch/D1–D3 removal):** safe — `sg_baseline_scale()` defaults any removed key to `1.000`; all teams resolve to a valid scale (1.000 / 1.083). No nulls, no errors. - **"Functions cannot be passed to Client Components":** transient build skew from the 06‑22 deploy churn; zero occurrences since the clean 02:13 deploy. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This migration attempts to fix recurring `57014 canceling statement due to statement timeout` errors on the `getDetailedStats` admin/service-role path by giving `service_role` an explicit 30s `statement_timeout` via `ALTER ROLE … SET`. The PR honestly acknowledges uncertainty about whether the PostgREST `SET LOCAL ROLE` path will pick up the new value. - **Single DDL statement:** `ALTER ROLE service_role SET statement_timeout = '30s'` — idempotent and non-destructive, matching the 30s convention used by other heavy functions in this codebase. - **Likely ineffective for PostgREST:** PostgreSQL only applies `ALTER ROLE … SET` GUC defaults at session login time. PostgREST connects as `authenticator` (which sets `statement_timeout=8s`) and then issues `SET LOCAL ROLE service_role` per request; the role's own GUC defaults are not re-loaded on `SET ROLE`, so the 8s timeout from `authenticator` stays active. - **Missing migration safety comments:** The project pattern requires `-- VERIFIED:` and `-- ROLLBACK:` comments in every migration file; both are absent here.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Safe to merge without data risk, but almost certainly won't stop the background-fetch timeouts it was written to fix. The DDL itself is non-destructive and idempotent, so merging won't break anything. The concern is that it probably doesn't fix the problem: PostgreSQL's `ALTER ROLE … SET` defaults only load at connection time (when the session logs in directly as that role), and PostgREST's `SET LOCAL ROLE service_role` within an `authenticator` session does not trigger a GUC reload. The 8s `authenticator` timeout will most likely remain in effect, meaning the `57014` fallbacks on heavy background reads will continue unchanged after this lands. supabase/migrations/20260623000000_service_role_statement_timeout.sql — needs `-- VERIFIED:` and `-- ROLLBACK:` comments, and a follow-up RPC-level `SET` to guarantee the timeout actually applies in the PostgREST path.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | supabase/migrations/20260623000000_service_role_statement_timeout.sql | Single `ALTER ROLE service_role SET statement_timeout = '30s'` DDL — idempotent and harmless, but likely a no-op for PostgREST connections (which use `SET LOCAL ROLE` mid-session); also missing required `-- VERIFIED:` and `-- ROLLBACK:` migration comments. |

## Root cause Coaches see blank shot-level stats (SG, driving distance, miss bias, proximity, scrambling, 3-putts) — the round-level fallback. `getDetailedStats` already authorizes the read via `verifyPlayerAccess` (viewer is the player, or a coach in the player's team org — the exact rule the `golf_shots` RLS policies encode), but the shot read was still issued on the **user-scoped** client. A coach therefore re-pays that rule **per row** via the `is_golf_team_coach()` RLS function across ~1k `golf_shots`. Under DB load that exceeds the `authenticated` role's **8s statement_timeout** and degrades to round-level stats. ## Fix (root, not recovery) Issue the read on the **service-role client** after the access check: identical authorization, **no per-row RLS, no statement_timeout** → full stats in ~100ms instead of timing out at 8s. Same trust model as the existing `getDetailedStatsAsAdmin`. This **supersedes** the admin-retry shipped in #339 (`7a92be20`), which recovered the stats only *after* eating the 8s timeout. That retry now remains purely as a safety net. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Fixes the coach RLS timeout by issuing the shot-level query on the service-role client (`createAdminClient`) after `verifyPlayerAccess` has already confirmed authorization, eliminating the per-row `is_golf_team_coach()` RLS overhead that caused the 8 s `statement_timeout` for coaches. - `getDetailedStats` now creates a service-role client after the access check and passes it to `queryDetailedStatsWithClient`, mirroring the existing `getDetailedStatsAsAdmin` pattern. - The in-function admin-retry from #339 remains as a secondary safety net, but the root cause is now addressed upstream so it should never trigger on the normal path.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge — the authorization gate (verifyPlayerAccess) remains on the user-scoped client and is unchanged; only the downstream shot query moves to the service-role client, matching the pre-existing getDetailedStatsAsAdmin pattern. The one-line change is well-scoped: the admin client is created only after a successful verifyPlayerAccess check, and the same as-unknown-as cast is already in production use. The minor observation is that allowAdminRetry still defaults to true, meaning a redundant second admin client would be created if the primary admin query ever failed with a timeout code — not a real defect today but worth tightening. The single changed file src/app/golf/actions/stats-data.ts warrants a quick look around the allowAdminRetry default to confirm the redundant retry path is acceptable.

body:
## Problem Coach **Ben Potter** (Guilford Men's Golf) reported "most of the stats are not showing up". Screenshots show a player's detailed view with strokes-gained, driving distance, miss bias, proximity, putts/GIR, 3-putts, scrambling and approach detail all blank ("— / 0 of 1"), while round-level fields (scoring, GIR, fairways, putts/round) render. ## Root cause This is the round-level fallback in `queryDetailedStatsWithClient`. A **coach viewing a player's** shot-level stats reads ~1k `golf_shots` rows through the per-row `golf_shots` RLS policies (`is_golf_team_coach()` evaluated per row). Under DB load this exceeds the `authenticated` role's **8s statement_timeout** (57014), so the query degrades to round-level stats — blanking everything shot-derived. Verified: the same query runs in ~63ms as service_role (no RLS), and prod `error_logs` show 57014 timeouts in Ben's exact session window. A player viewing their *own* stats is cheap (own-row RLS) and unaffected — which is why only the coach hits it. **Not** caused by the PGA/LPGA SG baseline change — Ben's stored data (rounds, shots, caches, standings) is fully intact and was never touched by that migration (his `sg_baseline` was already NULL). ## Fix On a 57014 timeout, retry the **same** query once on the service-role admin client (no RLS, no statement_timeout) and return full stats instead of the round-level fallback. Authorization is already enforced upstream by `getDetailedStats → verifyPlayerAccess`, so this widens no data access (same pattern as the existing `getDetailedStatsAsAdmin`). Recursion-guarded via `allowAdminRetry=false` on the retry. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes blank shot-derived stats for coaches viewing a player's detailed stats page by retrying the timed-out shot query on the service-role admin client (no RLS, no `statement_timeout`) instead of silently degrading to round-level stats. The root cause — per-row `golf_shots` RLS policy (`is_golf_team_coach()`) evaluated for every shot row under DB load — was confirmed via `error_logs` showing 57014 timeouts in the affected session window. - Adds an `allowAdminRetry: boolean = true` parameter to `queryDetailedStatsWithClient`; on a 57014 timeout, retries the same query once using `createAdminClient()` (bypasses RLS) with `allowAdminRetry=false` to prevent recursion. - If the admin retry also fails, Sentry is paged and execution falls through to the existing round-level fallback, so users always see at least headline numbers.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The fix is well-scoped and safe to merge. Authorization is enforced before this function is reached, the admin retry is guarded against recursion, and the round-level fallback is preserved when the retry also fails. The retry logic is sound and the recursion guard works correctly. The one gap is that `getDetailedStatsAsAdmin` inherits `allowAdminRetry=true` by default, so it could theoretically spawn an unnecessary admin-client retry if it ever hit a 57014. Only `src/app/golf/actions/stats-data.ts` changed. The `getDetailedStatsAsAdmin` call site at line 1119 should explicitly pass `false` to match the recursion-guard contract.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/app/golf/actions/stats-data.ts | Adds `allowAdminRetry` parameter with default `true` to `queryDetailedStatsWithClient`; `getDetailedStatsAsAdmin` does not explicitly pass `false`, so it inherits `true` and could trigger an unnecessary admin-client retry on statement_timeout. |

Passing `false` explicitly makes the intent clear and matches the guarded recursion contract described in the parameter comment.

Consolidated stabilization + features branch. Fast-forward-clean onto `main` (no conflicts). Bundles the visual-QA UI pass, the goal-tracking rebuild, the CoachHelm **stale-data remediation**, the PGA/LPGA-only strokes-gained switch, and the dev/qualifier features. ## ⚠️ Deploy requirements (read before merging) Four migrations land on this branch. **Two are already applied to prod** (the UI-era ones); **two are NOT yet applied** and must run via the deploy pipeline (`supabase db push`) **with or before** the app deploy, because the new code reads/writes the columns/functions they add: | Migration | Applied to prod? | What it does | |-----------|------------------|--------------| | `20260621230000_focus_areas_timeframe` | ✅ applied | focus-area measurable-target timeframe | | `20260621231000_qualifier_round_courses` | ✅ applied | qualifier per-round course assignment | | `20260622130000_pga_lpga_only_sg_baselines` | ❌ **pending** | rewrites `sg_baseline_scale()` to PGA(1.0)/LPGA(1.083) only; reverts teams off removed baselines + recomputes. Idempotent. | | `20260622140000_causal_relationships_is_active` | ❌ **pending** | additive `is_active` column + partial index for the causal stale-data fix | Both pending migrations are additive/idempotent. If the code deploys *before* them, the causal panel degrades to honest-empty (read catches the error → `[]`) rather than showing stale data — but the standard pipeline ordering avoids that window. ## CoachHelm stale-data remediation (headline) Fixes the recurring "tabs show old stuff" bug. The rule enforced everywhere: when the engine fires (round-submit, "Analyze Team", crons) it must **retire rows that no longer apply**, and the read must **default to fresh/active**. A full audit of all 25 persisted CoachHelm outputs (adversarially verified) found three holes; the other 22 are correct or are immutable-by-design ledgers. - **`golf_patterns_v2`** (two-sided): `savePatterns()` soft-supersedes the player's now-absent active patterns (`is_active=false`, preserves coach-set lifecycle, **never deletes**); `getTeamPatterns()` defaults `is_active=true`. - **`golf_causal_relationships`** (two-sided, + migration): `CausalEngine.saveRelationships()` soft-supersedes relationships that stop firing (retires all on an empty run), reactivates survivors; `fetchPlayerRowsDeduped` defaults active-only with an `includeInactive` opt-out. - **`golf_insight_drill_attachments`** (read-side): the drill readers now gate on parent-insight visibility via `applyInsightVisibility`, so drills of archived/dismissed/stale-v2 insights stop surfacing on My-Development. Guard tests added for all three (supersede-not-delete, player scoping, id-exclusion, visibility gating). ## Goal tracking (player + coach) - **Accurate in-progress tracking**: progress is measured over the goal **window** (rounds since `started_at`, via `golf_round_stats_cache`) instead of the all-time career average that diluted improvement. SG = per-round mean; rate stats pooled; metrics whose TS/DB band boundaries diverge deliberately fall back to the standing. - **Auto-fill**: choosing a stat suggests a target from the player's standing. - **Elite display**: "Your One Thing" hero, trajectory sparkline, gap-to-target, origin-aware provenance, validated-win state. `window_days` persisted; resume-to-active clears the stale outcome stamp. ## Strokes-gained baselines → PGA / LPGA only Removed NCAA D1/D2/D3 + scratch baselines per direction. `sg_baseline_scale()` resolves PGA(1.0) or LPGA(1.083) only; baseline auto-derives from gender; the `SgBaselineSelector` UI is gone (replaced with an auto-from-gender note); affected teams recompute in the migration. ## UI stabilization + features (original pass) Brand-green (`#16A34A`) buttons; round-review flyovers → framed 3-up cards; light in-round shot-tracking chrome; `PlayerIdentity` primitive unified across roster/CoachHelm/Messages/Qualifiers; pattern actionability surfaced; DiagnosisPanel/Sheet root-cause insight; landing→login fade; focus-area timeframe + autofill; qualifier per-round courses; CSV/loading-skeleton polish. ## Verification tsc 0 · ESLint 0 · **8,515 unit tests pass** · `next build` green at HEAD. `database.ts` regenerated from prod by the pre-commit hook (no drift — the two pending migrations' columns appear once applied; the new code uses the `as any` escape hatch so it compiles meanwhile). Also in this prep pass: added the missing `auth.getUser()` guard to `getQualifierRoundCourses` (the one outstanding CodeRabbit hard-gate blocker from the prior review). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

Large UI stabilization pass (brand-green buttons, round-review 3-up card grid, in-round shot tracking redesign, roster/messages/qualifiers identity unification) combined with three features: development focus-area timeframes, multi-round qualifier course assignment (Feature G), and goal progress wiring (P1-07) that connects the previously-frozen progress bars to live standings. - **Goal progress driver** (`goal-progress.ts`): `evaluateAndPersistGoals` and `runGoalProgressForPlayers` use `createAdminClient()` inside an `src/app/**/actions/**` file with no auth guard, exposing both as callable server actions that can write to `golf_goals` for any player ID without ownership verification (hard rules #4 and #5). - **Migrations `20260622130000` and `20260622140000`**: missing required `-- VERIFIED:` and `-- ROLLBACK:` annotations; the SG-baseline migration is higher-risk than a pure additive change because it drops/re-adds a CHECK constraint and runs `recompute_team_sg` in a per-team loop. - **Feature G (qualifier round courses)**: `getQualifierRoundCourses` auth gate added (addressing prior review comment); `setQualifierRoundCourses` correctly uses upsert + targeted delete; `is_active` soft-supersession pattern applied to both causal relationships and patterns to fix the recurring "old stuff" stale-data bug.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge after the goal-progress action file is refactored to remove the admin-client-without-ownership-check path. The goal progress driver introduces two exported server actions that use the service-role client with no auth or ownership verification. Any authenticated client can invoke them with an arbitrary player ID, writing to that player's goal state. The rest of the PR — qualifier course assignment, is_active soft-supersession, timeframe fields, UI stabilization — follows the project's patterns correctly. The two new migrations without VERIFIED/ROLLBACK annotations add procedural risk but are otherwise structurally sound. src/app/golf/actions/v3/goal-progress.ts is the primary concern; the two callers (my-development/page.tsx and development/page.tsx) are safe in isolation but rely on the action not being callable with a fabricated player ID from a client component.

Security Review

 - **Privilege escalation via admin client in server action** (`src/app/golf/actions/v3/goal-progress.ts`): `evaluateAndPersistGoals` and `runGoalProgressForPlayers` use `createAdminClient()` (service-role key, RLS bypassed) with no auth or ownership check. Because the file is `'use server'`, both functions are invocable from any client component with an arbitrary `playerId`, allowing an authenticated user to overwrite another player's goal `current_value`, `snapshots`, and `state`. Hard rule #4 restricts the admin client to `src/lib/supabase/admin*` / `src/app/api/**/admin/**`; this file is in `src/app/golf/actions/v3/`.

## Wave E — hot-file serialized chains (final audit batch) Closes the 2026-06-20 GolfHelm E2E tab-audit remediation. This batch groups the audit's **hot-file serialization chains** — clusters that all touch the same high-traffic files (`golf.ts`, `tasks.ts`, `dashboard-data.ts`, the calendar page + range hook, settings, the dashboard shell, the command palette) — into one collision-safe commit so they can't race the parallel autonomous PRs (#328–#331). ~50 files. ### Tasks — single source of truth on the M:N join - `golf_tasks.assigned_to` is never written; assignment lives in `golf_task_assignments`. The player **Hub/home pending-task list now keys on the player's own assignment status** (`status in (pending, in_progress)`), so it reflects reality and clears when the player completes a task. - create / complete write the join consistently; `TaskCard` / `TasksList` / `tasks/page` reflect per-player status; `use-task-realtime` subscribes to assignment changes. - **NEW** `/api/cron/task-reminders` route + `vercel.json` cron for due-task reminders. ### Calendar — pagination + range-driven realtime - `calendar/page` and `use-calendar-range-events` paginate past the PostgREST 1000-row cap via `fetchAllRowsResult().range()` — a busy ±3-month window exceeded a bare `.limit()`, silently dropping events (audit **F102**). - series fields (`parent_event_id`, `recurrence_rule`, `status`) reach the client so the scope picker renders; cancelled events are kept (rendered distinctly, **#19**). - a failed events fetch **THROWS to the route error boundary** (retryable) instead of a cheerful empty calendar (**#20**); client range fetches surface a retryable error + `retryRange`. - navigating outside the loaded window refetches that range and merges (**#9**). ### Other chains - **qualifiers:** `use-qualifier-realtime` + `QualifierLeaderboardRealtime` live refresh. - **settings:** `FairwaySettingsGeneral` + `notification-preferences` wired. - **roster/team:** active-team scoping on roster / team / team-hub pages + pickers. - **onboarding:** coach/player flows + `onboarding.ts`. - **coachhelm:** v2 `orchestrator` + v3 `notifications/types` scaffold; `insights`, `announcements`, `course-library`, `whats-new`, `FairwayDashboardShell`, `CommandPalette`. ### Docs - `CALENDAR_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md §2.4` corrected — availability polling is **backend-only (no UI caller)**, not "✅ COMPLETE" (audit **F040**). ### Gate - `tsc --noEmit` **rc=0** · eslint **0 errors** on changed files · full unit suite **2533 passed / 39 skipped / 0 failed** · `lint:ratchet` **rc=0** (warnings 2347→2346, locked in). - Behavioral green-repro (demo coach + rinin376) to run on this PR's Vercel preview before merge. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

Wave E consolidates a large batch of hot-file audit fixes: the tasks subsystem is unified on the `golf_task_assignments` M:N join (replacing the never-written `golf_tasks.assigned_to` column), calendar range fetches are paginated past the PostgREST 1000-row cap, a new hourly task-reminder cron is wired up with correct admin-client threading, and several smaller fixes land for qualifiers, event lifecycle, and roster team-scoping. - **Tasks unification**: `use-task-realtime`, `dashboard-data`, `TaskCard/TasksList`, and `task-reminders` all now key on `golf_task_assignments` for assignment and completion state; the old broken FK joins on `users!assigned_to` and `users!created_by` are replaced by the correct `resolveTaskRecipients` path. - **Calendar pagination**: `use-calendar-range-events` switches from a bare `.limit(500)` to `fetchAllRowsResult` with a stable secondary `.order('id')`, and the calendar page now throws to the error boundary on fetch failure instead of silently showing an empty calendar. - **Cron & reminders**: `/api/cron/task-reminders` uses `createAdminClient` and threads it through the full send/mark-sent chain; `vercel.json` schedules it hourly alongside the existing event-reminder cron.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge after verifying the Hub pending-task query is team-scoped; all other changes are well-guarded fixes to previously broken paths. The new taskDetails query in getPlayerDashboardData fetches golf_tasks by raw task_id with no team_id constraint, while the equivalent player-view path in use-task-realtime explicitly guards with row.task.team_id === teamId. A player who held assignments on a previous team will see those tasks on their Hub/home page until the filter is added. Every other changed path — calendar pagination, cron client threading, qualifier auto-advance, and the tasks realtime rewrite — looks correct and well-reasoned. src/app/golf/actions/dashboard-data.ts — the taskDetails follow-up query at line 932 needs .eq('team_id', teamId) to match the scoping applied in use-task-realtime's player view.

Comments Outside Diff (2)

 1. `src/hooks/golf/use-task-realtime.ts`, line 360-378 ([link](https://github.com/njrini99-code/helmv3/blob/a7747f87b932ce0dffaf12680590c546aa8a3d13/src/hooks/golf/use-task-realtime.ts#L360-L378)) **Global `golf_task_assignments` subscription triggers refetch for all clients** The subscription has no `filter` because `golf_task_assignments` has no `team_id` column. As a result, every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the assignments table — from any team on the platform — fires `fetchTasks()` for every connected client viewing the tasks tab. With N teams each having M active sessions, a single player completing a task fans out to N×M simultaneous `fetchTasks()` calls. The PR acknowledges this in the comment, but at scale this will cause a noticeable query storm on the Supabase project. Consider adding a `team_id` column to `golf_task_assignments` (or a denormalized view) so the subscription can be scoped with `filter: \`team_id=eq.${teamId}\``. 2. `src/app/golf/actions/task-reminders.ts`, line 106-128 ([link](https://github.com/njrini99-code/helmv3/blob/a7747f87b932ce0dffaf12680590c546aa8a3d13/src/app/golf/actions/task-reminders.ts#L106-L128)) **`assigned_by` is selected for access verification but never checked** The comment says "Verify the user has access to this task" and `assigned_by` is fetched, but nothing is compared against the current user — access control is delegated entirely to the Supabase RLS policy. `cancelTaskReminder` doesn't even do the existence check; both functions rely on RLS as the sole gate. If that's the intended model, the misleading comment and the unused `assigned_by` column in the `select` should be cleaned up. The explicit check that existed in the old code has been removed without a correct replacement — adding `task.assigned_by === coachId` after resolving the coach's domain id (already done in `getUpcomingReminders`) would make the guard explicit and RLS-independent.

## Wave B — batch 1 (5 autonomous MEDIUM clusters) Second remediation wave from the 2026-06-20 GolfHelm E2E tab audit. File-disjoint, autonomous tier (LOW/MEDIUM). Plan: `docs/audits/GOLFHELM_REMEDIATION_PLAN_2026-06-20.md`; ledger: `docs/audits/_e2e_tab_audit_2026-06-20/REMEDIATION_LEDGER.csv`. ### Closes (10 findings) | Cluster | Findings | Fix | |---|---|---| | B19 | F059 | Coaching Intelligence Settings gated in server layout (non-coach → FeatureUnavailable; no infinite skeleton) | | B21+B22 | F054, F055, F056, F111 | Insights stats match list RLS scope; error state on failed read; removed fake trend arrow; unified focus-area promotion | | B26 | F085 | Round-review "vs team" resolves player's active team via `golf_team_members` | | B27 | F087, F088 | Rounds list filters `status='active'`; paginates past the 1000-row cap (`fetchAllRowsResult`) | | B31 | F052, F114 | Genome non-coach → `/golf/dashboard` (was 404); qualifying error home → `/golf/dashboard/qualifiers` | ### Gate - `tsc --noEmit` clean · eslint clean on changed files · vitest **95 passed / 6 skipped**. - Behavioral green-repro (demo coach + rinin376) to be run on this PR's **Vercel preview** before merge. ### Notes - F056 leaves the now-dead `onAction('create_focus_area')` branches in other consumers intact (out of scope, harmless); the action type stays in the union. - B26/B27 honesty guards preserved (no-team → no team comparison; >=5-round threshold untouched). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

Wave B batch 1 remediation across five independent clusters: a server-side coach gate on the Coaching Intelligence settings layout, insight stats aligned to the list's RLS scope, a round-review "vs team" resolver that now looks up the player's active team via `golf_team_members`, rounds pagination past the 1000-row PostgREST cap, and two redirect fixes for non-coach deep-links. - **B19 / settings gate**: `coaching-intelligence/layout.tsx` becomes an async server component that blocks players with `FeatureUnavailable` and redirects unlinked users to login, preventing the infinite skeleton on direct access. - **B21+B22 / insights**: `getInsightsStats` drops the `coach_id` column filter in favour of RLS parity with the list query; `InsightsPageContent` gains a `loadError` state with a dedicated `InsightsErrorState` banner so a failed fetch is never mistaken for an empty feed; the fabricated trend arrow is removed from the Active StatCard. - **B26 / round-review**: `getStatAverages` now auto-resolves `resolvedTeamId` via a `golf_team_members` admin lookup when the caller doesn't supply one, making the \"vs team\" comparison live. - **B27 / rounds list**: both the coach team query and the player query migrate from `.limit(50)` to `fetchAllRowsResult` with a stable secondary `id` sort, and the team-member filter adds `status='active'`. - **B31 / redirects**: non-coach genome page goes to `/golf/dashboard`; qualifying error home goes to `/golf/dashboard/qualifiers`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; all five fix clusters are well-scoped and the logic is sound for the common case. The round-review `.maybeSingle()` call doesn't check the returned error, so a player on multiple active teams silently loses the "vs team" comparison with no log entry. The `coachId` parameter in `getInsightsStats` is now only used as a non-empty guard while the query relies entirely on RLS, creating a misleading API contract that could trip up future callers. Both are edge-case quality issues, not present defects on the normal path. src/app/golf/actions/round-review-system.ts and src/app/golf/actions/insight-management.ts warrant a second look; all other changed files are straightforward.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/app/golf/actions/round-review-system.ts | Adds active-team auto-resolution via golf_team_members when teamId is not supplied; .maybeSingle() error is not checked, silently suppressing team comparison on multi-team edge case. | | src/app/golf/actions/insight-management.ts | Drops coach_id filter from getInsightsStats to align with list RLS scope; coachId param now only guards against empty string, which is a semantic drift from its implied role. | | src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/insights/InsightsPageContent.tsx | Adds loadError state and InsightsErrorState component to distinguish a failed fetch from a genuinely empty feed; removes fabricated trend arrow from StatCard. | | src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/rounds/page.tsx | Replaces hard .limit(50) with fetchAllRowsResult pagination and adds status='active' filter on team member lookup; secondary sort by id ensures stable page boundaries. | | src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/settings/coaching-intelligence/layout.tsx | Promotes layout to async server component; gates non-coaches with FeatureUnavailable (player) or login redirect (unlinked), preventing infinite skeleton on direct deep-links. | | src/components/golf/coachhelm/insight-card/InsightCard.tsx | Unifies promote path for coaches to always use PromoteToFocusAreaButton (V2), removing the resolved-branch that previously hard-navigated via the legacy action. | | src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/coachhelm/genome/[playerId]/page.tsx | Redirects non-coaches to /golf/dashboard instead of a non-existent /forbidden route; straightforward fix. | | src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/coachhelm/qualifying/[id]/error.tsx | Corrects homePath from /dashboard/coachhelm to /dashboard/qualifiers; one-line fix. | | src/components/fairway/pages/rounds/FairwayRoundsLibrary.tsx | Removes the 50-row cap caveat from meta string now that server paginates past the PostgREST limit; comment and capNote variable cleaned up. |

## Wave A — DB / security hardening First wave of the GolfHelm E2E tab-audit remediation. Audit: `docs/audits/GOLFHELM_E2E_TAB_AUDIT_2026-06-20.md` · Plan: `GOLFHELM_REMEDIATION_PLAN_2026-06-20.md` · Ledger: `docs/audits/_e2e_tab_audit_2026-06-20/REMEDIATION_LEDGER.csv`. > **These migrations are already applied to production** (2026-06-21) and verified. This PR records them in the repo, runs the pgTAP regression test in CI, and submits the audit/plan/ledger artifacts. ### Closes (7 findings — all verified live) | Finding | Severity | Fix | |---|---|---| | F004 | CRITICAL | conversations RPC IDOR → `auth.uid()`, revoke anon/PUBLIC EXECUTE | | F071 | HIGH | exclude soft-deleted messages from preview/unread | | F003 | CRITICAL | `golf_documents` player SELECT honors `is_public` | | F005 | CRITICAL | player-self UPDATE policy on `golf_player_focus_areas` | | F086 / F113 | MEDIUM | revoke anon GRANT ALL on `golf_round_reviews` + `golf_patterns_v2` | | F120 | LOW | `progress_notes` default → `{"entries":[]}` | ### Verification - Live re-query of all 9 catalog/grant checks (post-apply, persisted) — all green. - **IDOR functional test:** impersonated player gets only their own conversations; a bogus `p_user_id` is ignored (returns the caller's rows). - Security advisor: **0 new issues** on any touched object. - `supabase/tests/rls/wave_a_db_security.sql` — 17 pgTAP assertions (CI regression guard against re-granting anon / reopening the IDOR). ### Migration filenames match recorded prod versions `20260621041824…049` — no `db push` drift. ### Follow-ups (not in this PR) - F003 code companion (documents read action `is_public` guard for non-coaches) → Wave B (cluster B8). - Pre-existing hardening surfaced by the advisor: `golf_teams` join-code enumeration, `v_crm_coaches_by_school` SECURITY DEFINER view, broader ~90-table anon-grant residue → recommend separate tickets. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

Wave A closes seven audit findings (F004 IDOR, F071 soft-delete leak, F003 document visibility, F005 focus-area self-update, F086/F113 anon grants, F120 default shape) across five forward-only migrations and adds a 17-assertion pgTAP regression suite to guard against re-opening them. - **A1 (`20260621041824`)**: Replaces `p_user_id`-scoped SECURITY DEFINER RPC with `auth.uid()` scope, filters soft-deleted messages from preview/unread, and revokes anon/PUBLIC EXECUTE. The previously flagged `SET search_path TO 'public'` (should be `''`) and missing VERIFIED/ROLLBACK comments remain open. - **A3 (`20260621041839`)**: Adds a player-self UPDATE policy on `golf_player_focus_areas` but omits the `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS` guard that A2 correctly uses; this breaks idempotency on any re-apply and diverges from the project's `IF NOT EXISTS / IF EXISTS everywhere` migration safety rule. - **A6/A8 (`20260621041844`, `20260621041849`)**: Clean REVOKE-only and ALTER COLUMN DEFAULT; no issues beyond the already-flagged missing VERIFIED/ROLLBACK headers.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge. All five migrations are restrictive or additive — no grants widened, no RLS loosened — so the deployed security posture is sound. The IDOR fix correctly re-scopes to auth.uid() inside a SECURITY DEFINER function, the anon EXECUTE/table-grant revocations are clean, and the focus-area self-update policy is correctly predicated. The missing DROP POLICY IF EXISTS guard in A3 is a migration hygiene gap that affects re-apply idempotency but introduces no runtime security regression. supabase/migrations/20260621041839_focus_areas_player_self_update.sql — missing DROP POLICY IF EXISTS guard. supabase/migrations/20260621041824_harden_get_golf_conversations_rpc.sql — previously flagged SET search_path issue still open.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | supabase/migrations/20260621041824_harden_get_golf_conversations_rpc.sql | IDOR fix for get_golf_conversations_with_details: re-scopes to auth.uid(), filters soft-deleted messages, revokes anon/PUBLIC EXECUTE. Previously flagged: SET search_path TO 'public' should be '' per rule 6, and VERIFIED/ROLLBACK comments are absent. | | supabase/migrations/20260621041833_golf_documents_select_is_public.sql | Replaces golf_documents_select_team policy to gate player SELECT on is_public=true. Uses the correct DROP POLICY IF EXISTS guard. VERIFIED/ROLLBACK comments absent (flagged separately). | | supabase/migrations/20260621041839_focus_areas_player_self_update.sql | Adds player-self UPDATE policy on golf_player_focus_areas. Missing DROP POLICY IF EXISTS guard (unlike A2 which correctly prefixes the guard); breaks idempotency and violates the IF NOT EXISTS / IF EXISTS everywhere migration safety rule. | | supabase/migrations/20260621041844_relock_anon_grants_reviews_patterns.sql | Simple REVOKE ALL from anon/PUBLIC on golf_round_reviews and golf_patterns_v2. Safe, minimal, no guard needed for REVOKE. | | supabase/migrations/20260621041849_focus_areas_progress_notes_default.sql | Changes progress_notes column default to {"entries":[]}. Correctly notes that existing rows are not rewritten and the read path must tolerate both shapes; Wave B code companion is tracked. | | supabase/tests/rls/wave_a_db_security.sql | 17 pgTAP regression assertions covering IDOR, anon grants, is_public gate, policy existence, and progress_notes default. Previously flagged: header timestamp range references 20260618 not 20260621, and A3 assertion tests only policy existence not the auth.uid() predicate body. |

Note: if you make any changes to this PR yourself, they will take precedence over the rebase. --- [//]: # (dependabot-end) Bumps [hono](https://github.com/honojs/hono) from 4.12.23 to 4.12.27.
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.27

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

hono/jsx does not isolate context per request

Affects: hono/jsx, hono/jsx-renderer. During SSR, context was stored process-wide instead of per request, so useContext()/useRequestContext() read after an await in an async component could return another concurrent request's value — leading to cross-request data disclosure or authorization checks against the wrong request. GHSA-hvrm-45r6-mjfj

Server-Side XSS via JSX escaping bypass in cx()

Affects: hono/css. cx() marked its composed class name as already-escaped without escaping the input, so untrusted input passed as a class name could break out of the JSX class attribute during SSR and inject markup (XSS). GHSA-w62v-xxxg-mg59

API Gateway v1 adapter can drop a repeated request header value

Affects: hono/aws-lambda. The API Gateway v1 (and VPC Lattice) adapter de-duplicated repeated header values by substring instead of exact match, dropping a value that is a substring of another (e.g. 203.0.113.1 dropped when 203.0.113.10 is present) — affecting logic such as X-Forwarded-For-based IP restriction. GHSA-xgm2-5f3f-mvvc

Users of hono/jsx/hono/jsx-renderer, hono/css (cx()), or the hono/aws-lambda API Gateway v1 / VPC Lattice adapters are encouraged to upgrade.

What's Changed

v4.12.25

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

CORS Middleware reflects any Origin with credentials when origin defaults to the wildcard

Affects: hono/cors. Fixes the wildcard origin reflecting the request Origin and sending Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true when credentials: true is set without an explicit origin, where any site a logged-in user visited could make credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses from cookie-authenticated endpoints. GHSA-88fw-hqm2-52qc

Body Limit Middleware can be bypassed on AWS Lambda by understating Content-Length

Affects: hono/body-limit on AWS Lambda (hono/aws-lambda, hono/lambda-edge). Fixes the request being built with the client-declared Content-Length while the body is delivered fully buffered, where a client could declare a small Content-Length with a much larger body and slip past the configured size limit. GHSA-rv63-4mwf-qqc2

Path traversal in serve-static on Windows via encoded backslash (%5C)

Affects: serveStatic on Windows (Node, Bun, Deno adapters). Fixes the path guard allowing a lone backslash, where an encoded backslash (%5C) decoded to \ was treated as a separator by the Windows path resolver, letting a single URL segment escape into a middleware-guarded subtree. GHSA-wwfh-h76j-fc44

## What Send cold outreach **directly through the real Workspace mailbox** (Gmail API, domain-wide delegation) instead of Resend — optimized for Primary-inbox placement. **Inert until the service-account env is configured** (the existing compose-tab flow is unchanged otherwise), so merging carries no runtime risk. ## Core - `src/lib/crm/gmail-send.ts` — DWD service-account auth (jose), true `text/plain` **quoted-printable** MIME, base64url `raw`. `server-only`. - `src/app/golf/actions/crm-gmail-send.ts` — one-click per-coach send + paced **"Send next 10"** batch (head/primary decision-maker, one per school, `new_lead`, valid+verified email, not recently contacted, not suppressed). Admin-gated. ## Hardened via 3-way adversarial review (auth / security / deliverability) - **CRLF header-injection blocked** — header values sanitized (the non-ASCII-only guard let CR/LF through → `Bcc:` injection). - **Suppression bypass fixed** — `.maybeSingle()` errored on multi-row (`UNIQUE(email,reason)`) addresses → reported not-suppressed; now `.limit(1)`. - **Daily cap on single sends** too (not just batch); **contact-log-based double-send guard** closes the re-send window if a status flip silently fails. - Auth verified spec-correct (JWT claims, scope-in-payload, token exchange, PKCS#8, base64url `raw`). ## Anti-spam toolkit - **Email verification at send** (`deep-email-validator`: MX/syntax/disposable, no SMTP) — skips + marks dead addresses → kills bounces. - **Spam-score linter** — armed template shows *Inbox-safe / Tidy copy / Spammy* + the exact issues. - **SPF/DKIM/DMARC self-check** (DNS) — "email auth" chip on the bar. - **Auto warm-up ramp** (5→15→30→cap over 3 weeks) + **jittered pacing** (~2–6s). ## Also - "Last contacted" date now visible in the coaches table (md+) and school-group rows. - `docs/setup/GMAIL_SEND_SETUP.md` (Google Cloud + Workspace setup + deliverability guide); `.env.example` `GMAIL_*` vars. ## Verification - typecheck: 0 errors · lint-ratchet: clean (2347) · production build: ✓ · QP encoder unit-tested (ASCII/UTF-8/wrap/round-trip). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a Gmail API direct-send path for CRM cold outreach using Google Workspace domain-wide delegation (DWD), replacing/augmenting the existing Gmail compose-tab flow. The feature is gated behind three environment variables and is inert until configured. - **New send paths**: `src/lib/crm/gmail-send.ts` mints short-lived DWD access tokens via `jose`, builds RFC 2045 quoted-printable MIME, and sends via the Gmail API; `src/app/golf/actions/crm-gmail-send.ts` exposes per-coach single send + paced batch (up to 15 emails/call) with suppression checks, email verification, daily cap, and auto warm-up ramp. - **Anti-spam toolkit**: `email-verify.ts` (MX/syntax/disposable via `deep-email-validator`), `spam-score.ts` (authoring-time linter), `domain-auth-check.ts` (DNS SPF/DKIM/DMARC presence check), plus jittered pacing and a 3-week cap ramp to protect deliverability. - **UI updates**: `CoachTable` and school-group rows now surface a \"Last Contact\" column; `TodayQueue` and `CoachDetailPanel` add a direct-send mode button; `page.tsx` wires the new server actions, batch trigger, and domain-auth chip.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The feature is correctly gated behind env vars and is inert until configured, so there is no runtime impact on the existing compose-tab flow. The two issues in the new send path — DEFAULT_DAILY_CAP not handling empty-string or non-numeric env values, and a concurrent token-cache race — can both fire once the Gmail env is configured. The DEFAULT_DAILY_CAP = Number(process.env.GMAIL_DAILY_CAP ?? '50') line is the sharpest edge: an empty-string env var (common from cleared CI secrets) produces 0, silently blocking all outreach, while a non-numeric value produces NaN, which makes the single-send daily-cap check always pass. Both outcomes are wrong and the breakage is invisible. The token-cache race is lower-stakes but real once the batch path is in use. The QP trailing-whitespace deviation is minor. src/app/golf/actions/crm-gmail-send.ts (daily-cap env-var parsing) and src/lib/crm/gmail-send.ts (token cache and QP encoder) deserve a second look before the Gmail env is configured in production.

JWT minting and header sanitization look correct; token cache has a concurrent-refresh race and the QP encoder has a trailing-whitespace edge case before soft-wrap boundaries. | | src/app/golf/actions/crm-gmail-send.ts | Server action wiring suppression, daily cap, warm-up ramp, and batch logic. DEFAULT_DAILY_CAP uses ?? instead of ||, making empty-string or non-numeric env values silently zero or NaN — blocking all sends or bypassing the cap in the single-send path. | | src/lib/crm/email-verify.ts | Thin wrapper around deep-email-validator with explicit fail-open on transient DNS errors; design tradeoffs are well-documented and correct. | | src/lib/crm/spam-score.ts | Pure dependency-free heuristic scorer; no side effects, correct level thresholds, advisory only. | | src/lib/crm/domain-auth-check.ts | DNS TXT presence check for SPF/DKIM/DMARC. The Today queue was filling with assistant coaches. It picked the highest-level *eligible* coach per school, but most head coaches are already contacted/enrolled (failing the new_lead + 7-day filter), so it fell back to the assistant. Verified on prod: 88 schools queued an assistant, 50 of which actually have a head coach that was just filtered out. Fix: never target `assistant_coach`/`volunteer` — pick the best head/director/associate (or explicit `is_primary_contact`) per school; drop the school if its only eligible contact is an assistant. New composition verified: 786 head / 30 director / 24 primary-flagged / 1 associate — **zero assistants/volunteers**. `tsc` 0 · build green · lint unchanged.

Now: - `crm-templates.ts` server actions (admin-gated): create / update / delete / duplicate / set-default + **sendTestTemplate** (send-to-self), single-default-per-category invariant - `TemplateManager.tsx`: full surface with a **format selector** (text = Gmail-Primary plain / plain = branded shell / html = verbatim), clickable merge-tag inserts, **live preview** against a sample coach, duplicate/delete/set-default, "send test to myself" - `TemplatePicker`: create now persists `format` + `merge_tags`; composer chips render the template's tokens - A **Templates** tab in the Automate group ### Resend max-out (free features, every in-app sender) - **Batch send**: the bulk route is now a single `/emails/batch` call (was N serial fetches) with per-message `reply_to` + RFC 8058 `List-Unsubscribe` one-click + idempotency key + tags - Bulk route returns `details[]` → the "Show details" panel goes live; writes structured `metadata` jsonb - Sequence cron: same deliverability envelope + canonical merge (NOT auto-registered — sends stay human-triggered by design; comment corrected) - Webhooks: bounce/complaint now write `crm_email_suppressions` (previously dead enums); inbound gated on reply type - Shared libs retire 5 duplicated merge-tag copies, extract the unsubscribe HMAC, and centralize deliverability headers - `.env.example` documents every Resend/email env var ### Review fixes (adversarial pass) - **Send route now also skips the suppression list**, not just `crm_coaches.email_status` — an unlinked bounce / Audiences unsubscribe would otherwise still get emailed - **Webhook uses the real `contact.updated` + unsubscribed-flag** event (the prior `email.unsubscribed`/`contact.unsubscribed` aren't real Resend events); Greptile Summary

This PR completes the CRM email template lifecycle (create/update/delete/duplicate/set-default/test-send) and maximises Resend's free-tier features: batch sends replace N serial fetches, RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe headers are added to every outbound send, bounce/complaint/audience-unsubscribe events now write `crm_email_suppressions`, and five duplicated merge-tag implementations are consolidated into one shared module. - **Template lifecycle**: new `crm-templates.ts` server actions (admin-gated) + `TemplateManager.tsx` UI surface the full CRUD flow with a format selector (`text`/`plain`/`html`), live merge-tag preview, and a test-send-to-self action. - **Batch send**: `send-email/route.ts` now issues a single `/emails/batch` call with per-message `reply_to`, `List-Unsubscribe` headers, idempotency key, and Resend tags; the route also checks `crm_email_suppressions` before including a recipient — not only `crm_coaches.email_status` — closing the gap for unlinked bounces. - **Shared libs**: `merge-tags.ts`, `outreach-headers.ts`, and `unsubscribe-token.ts` are extracted as single sources of truth used by the bulk route, sequence cron, and Gmail-compose path alike; a DB migration adds the missing `crm_contact_log.metadata` jsonb column the sequence cron was already trying to write.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Safe to merge for all paths except the test-send feature, which will silently stop delivering after the first preview of the day for a given admin. The batch-send refactor, suppression-list integration, shared merge-tag libs, and webhook hardening are all correct and well-considered. The one concrete defect is in the test-send flow: the Resend idempotency key is keyed on midnight-of-today plus the synthetic test-userId recipient id, so every template preview from the same admin on the same day shares the same key. Resend returns the cached first-batch response without re-sending, the route still counts it as delivered, and the UI confirms success — the admin has no signal that the email was dropped. This directly undermines the template-preview workflow introduced by this PR. src/app/api/admin/crm/send-email/route.ts — the idempotency key construction at line 279 needs to differentiate test sends from production batch sends.

## What Full overhaul of the GolfHelm admin CRM (`/golf/admin/crm`) — cold-outreach workflow for the NCAA coach prospect book. Built as 10 verified increments; build green, typecheck 0 source errors, lint ratchet no regressions. ### Workflow / IA - Condensed 11 flat side-tabs into grouped IA (**Work / Automate / Admin**) with a unified **Outreach** hub. - New **/Today** queue as the default landing — the queue *is* the product. - Mobile-first: bottom-nav, phone-usable composer, 44px touch targets, full-screen modals, bottom-sheet detail panel. Designed so Ben & Leah can work it from a phone (one shared login; `assigned_to` labels split the book without separate accounts). - Cmd+K command palette. ### Engagement model (the big correctness fix) - **Replies are the only "hot" signal.** On `.edu`, Mimecast/Proofpoint/Safe-Links bots auto-click every link, so the old click-weighted matview flagged coaches "hot" off a single gateway bot click. Inverted the `crm_coach_engagement` matview: clicks score **zero** (kept for display), a human reply → hot, decayed opens → warm. Sending path already moved to fit-based scoring. - Verified on prod after migration: **hot=0** (no more bot-click inflation), warm=34, cold=2,284 across 2,318 rows. ### Outreach mechanics - **"Open in Gmail"** manual send — arm a template as a filter, click per-coach to open a merged Gmail compose in your own inbox (ToS-clean, unlimited manual volume, outside the 40 automated/day). - Segment resolver mirrors **all** column filters (no accidental over-send). - Sequence cockpit shows per-step **reply** metrics, not bot opens/clicks. - Dedup/merge tool (re-parents history, archives — never deletes). ### Deliverability - Resend hardening: `reply_to`, `List-Unsubscribe` + one-click POST, campaign/division tags, idempotency keys, one-click unsubscribe route (HMAC). ## DB migrations (already applied to prod + verified) - `crm_coaches.assigned_to` (text) + filtered index — manual work-division labels. - `crm_coach_engagement` matview rebuild (clicks→0, reply→hot) + **REVOKE** of Supabase's auto-granted anon/authenticated access so the matview ACL stays `{postgres, service_role}` (read only via service-role admin client). RPC `refresh_crm_coach_engagement()` verified working. ## Verification - `tsc --noEmit`: 0 source errors - `next build`: green - `lint-ratchet`: OK, no regressions - Prod DB: migrations applied + ACL/row-counts/RPC verified 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR is a comprehensive CRM overhaul for the GolfHelm admin prospect book: it restructures navigation into grouped sections, adds a TodayQueue landing page, mobile-first layout, Cmd+K palette, per-operator assignee labels, a "Open in Gmail" manual-send path, dedup/merge tooling, and inverts the engagement matview so replies are the only "hot" signal (fixing bot-click inflation from `.edu` security gateways). - **Engagement model fix**: the `crm_coach_engagement` matview is rebuilt to score clicks as zero and treat a human reply as the sole "hot" promotion — the old click-weighted model was flagging coaches "hot" off gateway bot clicks on every `.edu` link. - **Server-side segment mirroring**: `enrollSegmentInSequence` now mirrors the remaining `crm_coaches`-column filters server-side, closing the gap where saved segments with `search`/`hasNotes`/`followUpDue` filters were only applied client-side and could over-enroll the wrong cohort. - **Deliverability hardening**: Resend sends now include `reply_to`, `List-Unsubscribe`, campaign/division tags, and idempotency keys; one-click unsubscribe is routed via HMAC.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The engagement matview inversion and deliverability hardening are solid, but the manual-send path has a silent failure mode that skips the frequency cap, and the server-side segment fix has an incomplete ILIKE escape that can still over-enroll coaches with underscore-containing search terms. Three separate correctness gaps exist in the most change-dense paths: the ILIKE `_` wildcard is unescaped in `enrollSegmentInSequence`, meaning the server-side segment fix can still produce an over-wide enrollment for certain saved searches; `logManualGmailTouch` failures are fully silent so the frequency cap is not applied on DB errors; and the coach-ID reply-attribution fallback in `getSequencePerformance` credits all unresolved replies to the earliest enrolled step, making later steps look worse than they are. src/app/golf/actions/crm-sequences.ts (ILIKE escape + reply attribution), src/app/golf/admin/crm/page.tsx (manual-send fire-and-forget)

body:
## The recurring Xcode Cloud failure Every archive failed with `a resolved file is required when automatic dependency resolution is disabled ... dependencies were added: 'capacitor-swift-pm'`, and `ci_post_clone.sh` exited 74 at the resolve phase. ## Root cause [swiftlang/swift-package-manager#6914](https://github.com/apple/swift-package-manager/issues/6914): **Xcode Cloud enables `IDEPackageOnlyUseVersionsFromResolvedFile` by default**, which forbids SwiftPM from resolving any dependency not already pinned in the committed `Package.resolved`. But `cap sync` rewrites `CapApp-SPM/Package.swift` every build → the resolved file's `originHash` drifts → the resolver must run to re-pin `capacitor-swift-pm`. With the flag on, both our phase-6 regenerate **and** Xcode Cloud's own build-step resolution hard-fail. The 3 prior fixes (#250/#251/#261) added retries, diagnostics, and the regenerate step — but never cleared this flag, so the regenerate could never succeed. ## Fix Clear the flag in `ci_post_clone.sh` **before any xcodebuild runs** (persists in the user domain for the whole build, incl. the Archive step): ``` defaults write com.apple.dt.Xcode IDEPackageOnlyUseVersionsFromResolvedFile -bool NO defaults write com.apple.dt.Xcode IDEDisableAutomaticPackageResolution -bool NO ``` iOS-CI-only — no app/runtime change. `bash -n` + shellcheck clean. Validated by the next Xcode Cloud build on `main` after merge.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes the recurring Xcode Cloud `IDEPackageOnlyUseVersionsFromResolvedFile` failure by writing two Xcode user-defaults (`IDEPackageOnlyUseVersionsFromResolvedFile` and `IDEDisableAutomaticPackageResolution`) to `NO` at the very start of `ci_post_clone.sh`, before any `xcodebuild` invocation. The root cause (Xcode Cloud enabling the "resolved-file-only" lock by default, which conflicts with `cap sync` rewriting `Package.swift` every build) is well-diagnosed and the fix is correctly targeted. - The two `defaults write` calls are placed before all other phases, ensuring the flags are cleared for the `xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies` call in phase 6 and for the subsequent Archive step. - Both commands use `|| true`, which silently swallows any failure from `defaults`; if either write fails undetected, the build will still hit the original SPM error at phase 6 with no improved diagnostics.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge — the change is iOS CI-only and does not touch any app or runtime code; the worst case is that the fix doesn't take effect if `defaults write` silently fails. The root-cause analysis is solid and the fix is correctly placed before any `xcodebuild` call. The only concern is the `|| true` pattern, which means a failure of `defaults write` goes completely unlogged — if that happens, the build will still fail at phase 6 with the same cryptic SPM error and no hint that the fix itself didn't apply. It's a diagnostics gap rather than incorrect logic, so the change is still worth merging. Only `ios/App/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh` is changed; the `|| true` on both `defaults write` lines is the one area worth a second look.

Important Files Changed

## Per-recruit documents in Recruiting HQ Coaches can upload and organize documents — **notes, schedules, transcripts, film** — **per prospect**, inside the recruit's edit drawer. (Requested by a coach who wanted per-player notes/schedules.) ### Security-first design Recruiting material is coach-confidential, so this does **not** reuse `golf_documents` — its `golf_documents_select_team` policy lets *any team player* read every row. Instead: - **`golf_recruit_documents`** table — coach-only RLS (`is_golf_team_coach` + admin read), **no player policy at all** (RLS default-deny blocks players). A same-team trigger keeps `team_id` honest (mirrors `golf_event_documents_assert_same_team`). - **Private `recruit-documents` storage bucket** (25 MB, mime allowlist) with team-scoped, coach-only `storage.objects` policies via `is_golf_team_coach((storage.foldername(name))[1]::uuid)`. Path = `{teamId}/{recruitId}/{uuid}.ext`. Downloads use 1-hour **signed URLs** (bucket is never public). ### Server (`src/app/golf/actions/recruit-documents.ts`) `getRecruitDocuments` · `uploadRecruitDocument` · `deleteRecruitDocument` · `getRecruitDocumentUrl`. `team_id` is derived from the recruit's own row (never the active-team cookie). Category vocabulary lives in a plain module (`recruit-documents-categories.ts`) — a `'use server'` file may only export async functions. ### UI A **Documents** section in the recruit edit drawer (edit mode only — uploads need a saved recruit id), wired into **both** the Fairway redesign (`FairwayRecruitDocuments`, the prod path) and the legacy drawer (`RecruitDocuments`). Upload (title + category + file), list (type icon, category pill, size/date, Open), two-step delete. ### Verification - `tsc` clean · `eslint` 0 warnings on new files · **2431 unit tests** green - RLS proven **coach-only** (4 policies, no player policy); same-team trigger proven to reject cross-team writes - **Full browser CRUD pass** as the demo coach against the prod DB: upload → list → delete, with the storage object + DB row both created and purged (no orphans) ### Migration / deploy note `supabase/migrations/20260614020000_recruit_documents.sql` is **already applied to prod** (additive — new table, bucket, policies; nothing existing modified; dormant until this code ships). `src/lib/types/database.ts` was regenerated to include the new table. **Not merged** — merging to `main` auto-deploys to prod, so that's your call.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a coach-only per-recruit document system (upload, list, delete, signed-URL open) to Recruiting HQ — both the Fairway redesign path and the legacy drawer. A dedicated `golf_recruit_documents` table with strict coach-only RLS and a private `recruit-documents` storage bucket keep recruiting material separate from the team-visible `golf_documents` table. - **New server actions** (`recruit-documents.ts`): MIME validation closes the empty-`file.type` bypass noted in the previous review round; insert-failure rollback correctly removes the orphaned storage object; delete correctly logs storage errors but still returns success to the coach. - **`deleteRecruit` storage purge** (`recruiting.ts`): pre-collects storage paths before the FK cascade, but the collection query's error return is never checked — a silent failure here causes every file for the deleted recruit to be orphaned after the cascade completes. - **Migration** (`20260614020000_recruit_documents.sql`): additive, already applied to prod; `VERIFIED`/`ROLLBACK` comments are present; RLS is enabled immediately with four coach-only policies; the DB select policy grants admin read while no storage policy does (mismatch flagged in a prior thread).

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge with one fix: the document path-collection error in deleteRecruit is silently swallowed, leaving storage objects orphaned whenever that query fails during a recruit deletion. The new recruit-document actions are well-constructed — auth-before-DB, rollback-on-failure, and proper error logging throughout. The one concrete defect is in the existing deleteRecruit action in recruiting.ts: the pre-cascade query that collects storage paths never checks its own error return, so a query failure quietly zeroes out the path list and all storage objects survive after the cascade wipes their DB rows. src/app/golf/actions/recruiting.ts — the deleteRecruit storage-path collection needs its error destructured and handled before proceeding.

Auth-before-DB pattern followed, rollback-on-insert-failure handled, delete logs storage errors. The previously flagged admin/storage policy mismatch (DB select allows admins, storage select does not) is the main outstanding concern per the outside-diff comments. | | supabase/migrations/20260614020000_recruit_documents.sql | Well-structured additive migration: VERIFIED/ROLLBACK comments present, IF NOT EXISTS guards used, RLS enabled immediately, FK indexes created. The DB select policy grants admin read while no storage policy does — mismatch already noted in a prior review thread. | | src/components/fairway/pages/recruiting/FairwayRecruitDocuments.tsx | New Fairway-design document shelf component. Uses signed URLs, two-step delete confirmation, Capacitor-safe openExternalUrl, and correct server-action imports. | | src/components/golf/recruiting/RecruitDocuments.tsx | Legacy-drawer parity component. Logic mirrors FairwayRecruitDocuments; uses legacy UI primitives consistent with the existing RecruitFormSheet style. | | src/app/golf/actions/recruit-documents-categories.ts | Plain module exporting the category const array and type outside the 'use server' boundary — correct workaround for Next.js action proxy constraints. | | src/lib/types/database.ts | Auto-generated; adds golf_recruit_documents Row/Insert/Update types with correct FK relationships. | | src/components/fairway/pages/recruiting/FairwayRecruitFormSheet.tsx | Adds FairwayRecruitDocuments into the edit-mode section of the sheet, guarded by isEditing && recruit. | | src/components/golf/recruiting/RecruitFormSheet.tsx | Adds RecruitDocuments into the legacy edit-mode drawer, matching the Fairway integration pattern. | | memory/registry.yml | Adds recruiting feature entry to the registry with correct action/component/db paths. | | src/components/fairway/pages/recruiting/index.ts | Barrel export for FairwayRecruitDocuments added. |

Comments Outside Diff (2)

 1. `src/app/golf/actions/recruit-documents.ts`, line 377-414 ([link](https://github.com/njrini99-code/helmv3/blob/4ccd4cc369f5efec557803c1c028d7434b6c5166/src/app/golf/actions/recruit-documents.ts#L377-L414)) **Admin DB policy and storage policy are mismatched — admins can list documents but cannot open them** `golf_recruit_documents_select_coach` (the DB RLS) includes `OR public.is_admin()`, so an admin user's call to `getRecruitDocuments` returns rows. However, `recruit_documents_coach_select` on `storage.objects` only allows `is_golf_team_coach(...)` — admins are not included. Supabase `createSignedUrl` enforces storage RLS on the calling user's session, so `getRecruitDocumentUrl` will return an error for any admin who is not also a coach for that team. The UI will happily display the document list and then fail silently on "Open." If admins are never expected to access the recruiting documents UI, remove `OR public.is_admin()` from the DB select policy to match the storage layer. If admins need file access, add an admin exception to `recruit_documents_coach_select` as well. 2. `src/app/golf/actions/recruiting.ts`, line 428-431 ([link](https://github.com/njrini99-code/helmv3/blob/10dd815c36104daf6f05f4d3756eb468abe21eba/src/app/golf/actions/recruiting.ts#L428-L431)) **Silent path-collection error causes orphaned storage objects on recruit delete** The `error` return from the `golf_recruit_documents` query is never destructured or checked. If the query fails (transient network error, unexpected RLS edge-case), `docRows` is `null`, `paths` is `[]`, and the `if (paths.length > 0)` branch is skipped. When `deleteRecruit` then succeeds and the FK cascade removes the document rows, every storage object under `recruit-documents/{recruitId}/` is orphaned permanently. The `deleteRecruitDocument` action in `recruit-documents.ts` is careful to log storage errors — the same discipline is missing here.

body:
## Problem The premium coverflow course picker shipped in #290 **full-page-crashed** `helmsportslabs.com/golf/dashboard/rounds/new` with **React minified error #310** ("Rendered more hooks than during the previous render"). Because the picker is the New Round landing screen, the crash took down the entire page. ## Root causes (two independent defects) **1. The #310 crash — framer scroll hooks on a conditionally-rendered container** The coverflow drove its transforms with `useScroll({ container: trackRef })` + `useTransform`. framer-motion requires the scroll-container ref to be **hydrated at hook-call time** ([motion.dev](https://motion.dev/troubleshooting/use-scroll-ref)). The track `
` is only rendered in the carousel branch — *after* the `loading` / empty-state early returns — so under concurrent React the hook count diverged between renders → #310. **Fix:** re-authored the coverflow **imperatively** — one rAF scroll handler writes `perspective()/scale()/rotateY()`/opacity straight to each slide's element. The only framer usage left is the `m.div` entrance + `AnimatePresence` stage swap + `useReducedMotion`, all proven safe under the dashboard `LazyMotion` provider. **2. Runaway refetch loop** `useToast()` returns a fresh object (new `showToast` identity) on every render, so `refreshCourses` (`useCallback([showToast])`) was rebuilt every render, and the course-load effect (`useEffect([open, refreshCourses])`) re-fired every render — thrashing `loadingCourses` and refetching the library in an unbounded loop. **Fix:** keep the latest `showToast` in a ref so the data callbacks stay referentially stable; the load effect now runs only when `open` changes. ## Test Adds `src/test/golf/components/FairwayCoursePicker.test.tsx` — a jsdom regression gate that renders the picker open, lets `listCourses` resolve (the loading→loaded re-render that crashed prod), and asserts the carousel + empty state mount with no render crash. This test **fails on the old code** (skeleton-stuck from the refetch loop) and passes on the fix. ## Verification - `tsc --noEmit` clean - `eslint` 0 errors (3 pre-existing `bg-white` warnings on the dark header, unchanged) - full golf suite: **771 passing**, 0 failing 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes two independent production bugs introduced in #290: a React minified error #310 crash caused by framer-motion `useScroll`/`useTransform` hooks being called on a conditionally-rendered container, and an unbounded refetch loop caused by `useToast()` returning a new `showToast` identity on every render, which destabilised `useCallback` deps and re-fired the course-load effect on every render. - **Coverflow rewritten imperatively**: `useScroll`/`useTransform`/`CoverflowSlide` replaced with a single `requestAnimationFrame` scroll handler that writes `perspective()/scale()/rotateY()/opacity` directly to inner slide elements via `slideRefs`, eliminating the hook-hydration requirement entirely. - **Refetch loop fixed via ref pattern**: `showToast` is now captured in a `showToastRef` (updated synchronously on every render), and all data callbacks use `showToastRef.current` with empty dependency arrays, making `refreshCourses` referentially stable so the load effect only fires when `open` changes. - **Regression test added**: `FairwayCoursePicker.test.tsx` renders the picker open, resolves the async `listCourses` mock, and asserts both carousel and empty-state mount without errors.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge — both root causes are correctly addressed, the new code compiles clean, and the regression test gates the exact re-render path that crashed prod. The two production bugs (hooks crash and refetch loop) are correctly fixed. The imperative paint approach is sound and the showToastRef pattern is well-established. The live region removal is a genuine accessibility regression against the component’s own stated ARIA APG compliance, and the mid-render ref reset is fragile under concurrent React — neither blocks the critical crash fix from shipping. FairwayCoursePicker.tsx — the CoursesStage coverflow section (lines 439–514) around the slideRefs reset and the removed live region.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/components/fairway/pages/rounds-new/FairwayCoursePicker.tsx | Replaces framer-motion useScroll/useTransform coverflow with an imperative rAF+getBoundingClientRect approach and stabilises useCallback deps via showToastRef; two P2 issues: aria-live region removed (a11y regression) and slideRefs.current reset during render rather than in useLayoutEffect. | | src/test/golf/components/FairwayCoursePicker.test.tsx | New regression test renders the picker open, resolves the listCourses mock (the exact re-render that triggered the prod crash), and asserts carousel + empty-state mount without errors; correctly wraps in LazyMotion and reproduces the unstable useToast identity via vi.fn(). |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[scroll event on track] --> B{rafRef.current != null?} B -- yes --> C[skip: rAF already queued] B -- no --> D[requestAnimationFrame] D --> E[rafRef.current = null] E --> F[paint] F --> G[getBoundingClientRect on track] G --> H{reduceMotion?} H -- no --> I[for each slideRef: compute signed offset] I --> J[write transform + opacity to inner div] H -- yes --> K[skip transforms] J --> L[compute scrollLeft / maxScroll] K --> L L --> M[setScrollable / setCanLeft / setCanRight] M --> N[write scaleX to progressRef] N --> O[React re-render if state changed] P[useLayoutEffect after commit] --> F Q[window resize] --> F ``` Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["fix(golf): stop the new-round course pic..."](https://github.com/njrini99-code/helmv3/commit/d68e83d983d1f1eb99d7c0c351f2dea25351b327) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=37445672) > Greptile also left **2 inline comments** on this PR.

## What Rebuilds the new-round **course chooser** as its own full-screen, cinematic screen with an **image-forward coverflow carousel** and a first-class **"Add a course"** tile — replacing the plain list that read as "AI slop." Lives only inside the New-round flow (redesign shell); flag-off falls back to the existing `TeePickerDrawer`. This is the visual/motion follow-up to #285/#286/#288/#289 (Cloud Course Library). Backend, data flow, and snapshot safety are unchanged. ## Why it's premium now (research-led) Researched the current bar (Material 3 carousel, Apple Cover Flow, ARIA APG, motion.dev, web.dev perf, iOS Safari constraints) and rebuilt against it: - **Coverflow** — centered card is full-size/opacity; neighbours scale down, dim, and tilt (subtle rotateY + translateZ + perspective) by distance from centre. The round still freezes its own par/yards into `golf_holes` from the client `holes`; the cloud course/tee are provenance only. ## Still deferred (not in this PR) - Removing the legacy `golf_player_courses` quick-pick/saved entirely (would remove existing players' personal tiles) — kept as fallback by design. - The legacy `golf_player_courses` bulk data migration (deferred earlier). ## Gate tsc 0 · eslint 0 (changed files) · **45 course-library + 2428 unit tests green** · `next build` exit 0. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
