body:
Backend-first replacement for the player-scoped saved-courses system, in two pure-backend phases (no UI, no user-facing change yet). A **course = a facility** (e.g. *Pinehurst No. 2*) that owns **many tee sets**. Built off a 7-agent pre-implementation audit → `docs/audits/COURSE_LIBRARY_AUDIT_2026-06-13.md`. The audit's key finding — round data is an immutable snapshot, so course/tee edits never rewrite historical analytics — is what makes this safe. --- ## Phase 1 — backend foundation (migrations applied to prod additively + verified) **New tables (RLS enabled, anon fully revoked):** `golf_course_tees`, `golf_course_tee_holes`, `golf_team_saved_courses`, `golf_course_edit_history`, `golf_course_tee_edit_history`. Free-form tee `category` (**not** a binary-gender enum), open-contribution + last-edited audit + soft-delete. **Additive columns:** `golf_courses` (normalized_name/slug/address/website/image_url/source/audit/deleted_at/updated_at, backfilled) + `golf_rounds.tee_id` (nullable; rounds **still** snapshot into `golf_holes`). **Dedup spine:** `golf_normalize_name()` collapses `Pinehurst No. 2` / `#2` / `Number 2` / `No.2` → `pinehurst 2`, word-anchored so it can't strip `No` out of *Northwood*. (Hard unique guard + dedup deferred to the gated final phase.) **Tests:** 37-assertion pgTAP (`supabase/tests/rls/golf_course_library.sql`). ## Phase 2 — data access layer (`src/app/golf/actions/course-library.ts` + `src/lib/golf/course-library.ts`) Server-action surface: list/search courses, course detail (+tees), tee+holes, edit history, team-saved library · create/update/soft-delete+restore course · create/update/soft-delete+restore tee · save/unsave/default-tee/pin (coach-gated). **Invariants enforced:** - **Snapshot safety** — zero references to `golf_rounds`/`golf_holes`/`golf_shots`; editing a tee never rewrites round history. - **No destructive writes** — soft-delete everywhere; hole edits are **stage-and-swap** (upsert → delete-surplus), unlike legacy `courses.ts` which delete-then-reinserts. - **Attribution** — every write stamps `*_by_user_id` + appends append-only edit-history. No hardcoded user/team IDs (auth + cookie). - **Dedup-aware create** — returns the existing course instead of inserting a duplicate. **Hardened per adversarial code review (3 findings fixed + locked by tests):** 1. `updateTee({holes:[]})` no longer wipes the hole set (rejects empty replacement). 2. `listCourses` sanitizes PostgREST metacharacters — a comma in `.or(...)` could've injected conditions bypassing the `deleted_at` guard. 3. `createCourse` handles `23505` on insert (race-loser returns the winner as a dedup hit) → self-heals when the gated unique guard lands. **Tests:** pure-helper dedup matrix + tee-completeness + diff + mappers; action tests for auth guard, dedup-no-duplicate-insert, attribution+history+revalidate, coach-gate, injection-sanitize, empty-holes destructive guard. --- ### Gate ✅ tsc clean · ✅ eslint clean · ✅ **2396 unit tests pass** · ✅ `next build` succeeds · ✅ all 37 pgTAP predicates validated against prod · ✅ security advisor clean for new objects. ### Known scope boundaries (next phases) `getTeamSavedCourses` returns `[]` for players (coach-only team resolution for now) · legacy `courses.ts` create doesn't set `normalized_name` so transition-era courses aren't dedup-matched yet (closed by Phase 3/4 rewire + gated dedup) · **next:** new-round `tee_id` integration → cinematic carousel UI (5 screenshots) → gated dedup + `golf_player_courses` migration + unique guard → E2E. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Phase 3 — round integration (added) Wires `golf_rounds.tee_id` through the submission path so a round can reference a tee set, **without** changing the par/yardage snapshot. - **Migration `20260613170000`** (applied to prod + verified): patches `submit_round_atomic` + `save_partial_round_atomic` to persist `tee_id`. Both apply columns from jsonb via an explicit list, so they ignored the new key. The migration is a drift-free `DO` block — reads each function's **live** `pg_get_functiondef`, injects one line after the `tees_played` assignment, recreates it; idempotent + self-asserting (raises if the anchor is missing). Verified post-apply: `tee_id` assigned exactly once each, anchor + neighbors + the `golf_holes` snapshot INSERT all intact. - **`golf.ts`**: `teeId?` on the round input; when present, `course_id` is derived from the tee (authoritative over fuzzy name match) and `tee_id` flows into `roundData` (RPC + fallback). Optional → zero behavior change when absent (**all 266 existing golf-action tests pass**). - **`getTeeRoundDefaults(teeId)`** in the DAL: loads a tee + holes shaped as new-round defaults for the Phase-4 picker; null for soft-deleted tees. The visible tee-picker UI + form wiring land in **Phase 4** (the carousel); this is the backend so a selected tee flows end-to-end the moment the UI sends it. **Gate (Phase 3):** tsc · eslint · 34 course-library + 266 golf-action tests · `next build` · RPC defs verified post-apply. --- ## Phase 4 — UI + image upload (added) The image-forward library UI and the upload pipeline behind it. Players browse/search the cloud library; coaches manage tees + the team-saved set. **UI (`src/components/golf/courses/`)** - **CourseImage** — `next/image` when a photo exists; otherwise a deterministic **scenic vista placeholder** (sky → hills → fairway → green palette) + course monogram, so an empty library still looks intentional rather than broken. Real photos come from upload only (no scraping — copyright + the free-public-only data policy). - **CourseCard** — `featured` (overlaid title on a scrimmed photo) + `standard` (photo-top, text-below) variants, drawn from the 5 reference cards. - **CourseLibraryClient** — hero + **Saved** + **All** sections + normalized search (reuses `normalizeName`, so `#2` finds `No. 2`). - **CourseDetailDrawer** — hero photo upload, tee list, add/edit tee, edit course, coach save-to-team. - **CourseFormDrawer / TeeFormDrawer** — create/edit course + tee with a per-hole editor. - **TeePickerDrawer** — 2-step course → tee picker for the new-round flow; returns `TeeRoundDefaults`. - **`/dashboard/courses`** page (`force-dynamic`) + a **Courses** entry in `GolfSidebar` (coach + player nav). **Image upload** - **`course-images`** public bucket (5 MB, image mimes only) — `20260613180000_course_images_storage.sql`. **Least-privilege:** no broad SELECT policy (public URL serves the object; the app stores that URL in `golf_courses.image_url` and never lists the bucket) — clears the `public_bucket_allows_listing` advisory. Any authenticated user may upload (open contribution); only the uploader may replace/delete their object. - **Client-direct Storage upload** (`upload-course-image.ts`) sidesteps the 2 MB server-action body limit (5 MB images can't round-trip through a server action). The server only ever receives a URL — and `setCourseImageUrl` **validates that URL was minted in our own bucket** (`isCourseImagePublicUrl`) before persisting, so `image_url` can't be pointed at an arbitrary external host. **Round integration** - New-round **"Browse course library"** opens the picker; a picked tee pre-fills the setup form's pars/yards and records `golf_rounds.tee_id`. The round **still snapshots its own holes** — the tee only seeds defaults. **Snapshot safety** preserved throughout: the DAL never touches `golf_rounds`/`golf_holes`/`golf_shots`. **Also fixed (Greptile P1 on Phase 2):** `loadTeamSaved` fetched the backing courses/tees with **no `deleted_at` filter** — a soft-deleted course lingered in every team's saved library. Both backing queries now scope to active rows; regression test locks it (failed before the fix). **Gate (Phase 4):** tsc 0 errors · eslint 0 errors (2921 warnings, < 6000 cap) · **41 course-library + full unit suite green** · `next build` exit 0 · storage advisor clean. --- ## Phase 5 — enforce dedup (UNIQUE normalized_name + trigger) Turns the catalog's dedup spine from advisory into **enforced**, and resolves the open design question on the legacy data. **DB (`20260613190000`, applied to prod + verified live):** - A `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE OF name` trigger sets `normalized_name = golf_normalize_name(name)`, so **every** write path (the new DAL, legacy `courses.ts`, anything future) gets a correct dedup key automatically — the client-side set becomes belt-and-suspenders. - Swaps the Phase-1 **non-unique** partial index for a **UNIQUE** partial index on `normalized_name WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND normalized_name <> ''`. A soft-deleted course leaves the index so its name can be reused; degenerate stopword-only names (normalize to `''`) are excluded so they can't collide on an empty key. - A pre-flight `RAISE` aborts harmlessly if an active duplicate group ever exists (prod has **0**). `SECURITY INVOKER`; `authenticated` already holds EXECUTE on `golf_normalize_name` (anon does not). Verified live: trigger normalized `No.`/`#`, the unique index **blocked** the colliding insert, test self-rolled-back (no prod rows added). **Adversarial verification:** a 4-lens workflow (idempotency/replay · write-path breakage · data-truth/snapshot · RLS/grants) returned **0 refutations**. Snapshot-safe: touches only `golf_courses`; all 191 rounds key off `golf_rounds.course_name` **string** (0 by `course_id`), so no `normalized_name` change can move a historical stat. **Legacy data migration — DEFERRED (decision):** the 35 `golf_player_courses` rows are free-text, name-only (no `course_id`), zero-overlap with the catalog, and include junk ("bob"). Backfilling free-text personal entries into a **shared** multi-team catalog is high-cost / low-recoverability, so the library **starts clean** and grows from real contribution; the legacy player-saved-courses feature is left fully intact and running. (Migrate later, if ever, alongside the round-flow rewrite.) **Code hardening** — the new constraint can now raise `23505` on rename/restore; the paths that can trip it now surface it instead of failing opaquely: - DAL `updateCourse`: `23505` → "Another course already uses that name". - DAL `restoreCourse`: `23505` on un-soft-delete → "rename the active one first". - legacy `courses.ts updateCourse`: captured the previously-**swallowed** UPDATE error (it returned `success:true` on a silently-failed rename); `23505` → friendly message, else logged + surfaced. **Gate (Phase 5):** tsc 0 errors · eslint 0 errors · **43 course-library + 2407 unit green** · `next build` exit 0 · prod migration applied + verified · no new security advisory.

Greptile Summary

This PR delivers the Cloud Course Library backend (Phases 1–3): five new tables with RLS, additive columns on `golf_courses` and `golf_rounds`, a normalized-name dedup helper, a full server-action DAL with soft-delete + edit-history, and `tee_id` wiring through the round-submission RPCs — all with no destructive writes and zero changes to historical round data. - **Phase 1 (migration):** Additive schema — `golf_course_tees`, `golf_course_tee_holes`, `golf_team_saved_courses`, and two edit-history tables — with RLS enabled and anon access fully revoked. A second migration fixes the `golf_normalize_name` regex word-boundary bug and re-backfills `normalized_name`. - **Phase 2 (DAL):** `src/app/golf/actions/course-library.ts` exposes list/detail/create/update/soft-delete for courses and tees plus team-saved management, with injection sanitization, dedup-aware create, and stage-and-swap hole edits. A security gap exists: `createCourse` and `updateCourse` both accept `imageUrl` directly, bypassing the `isCourseImagePublicUrl` bucket-origin check that `setCourseImageUrl` enforces. - **Phase 3 (round wiring):** `golf.ts` threads `teeId` through `submitGolfRoundComprehensive`, but the tee lookup for `course_id` derivation omits a `deleted_at` filter, allowing a soft-deleted tee's `course_id` to be used and a stale `tee_id` FK to be persisted in `golf_rounds`.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The schema and pure helpers are solid, but two issues in the write paths need resolution before merge. Both `createCourse`/`updateCourse` accept an unchecked `imageUrl` that bypasses the bucket-origin guard deliberately built into `setCourseImageUrl`, allowing any authenticated user to store arbitrary external URLs in the global course catalog and have them rendered for all platform users. Separately, the new tee-lookup in `submitGolfRoundComprehensive` omits a `deleted_at` filter, so a soft-deleted tee can be used to set a round's `course_id` and leave a stale `tee_id` FK in `golf_rounds`. `src/app/golf/actions/course-library.ts` (imageUrl bypass in `createCourse` and `updateCourse`) and `src/app/golf/actions/golf.ts` (tee lookup missing soft-delete filter).

Security Review

 - **Arbitrary image URL injection** (`src/app/golf/actions/course-library.ts`): `createCourse` and `updateCourse` accept `imageUrl` from callers without the `isCourseImagePublicUrl` bucket-origin check that `setCourseImageUrl` enforces. An authenticated user can store any external URL in the global `golf_courses.image_url`, which `CourseImage.tsx` renders via `` for all platform users (tracking pixel / untrusted content injection).

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/app/golf/actions/course-library.ts | 994-line server-action DAL for the course library. Two issues: (1) `createCourse`/`updateCourse` accept `imageUrl` without the `isCourseImagePublicUrl` origin guard — a security bypass; (2) `setCourseDeleted`/`setTeeDeleted` skip existence checks, silently returning success on unknown IDs. | | src/app/golf/actions/golf.ts | Adds `teeId` to round submission; the tee lookup for `course_id` resolution is missing `.is('deleted_at', null)`, so a soft-deleted tee's `course_id` can be stored on a round and the `tee_id` FK points to a tombstoned record. | | supabase/migrations/20260613160000_course_library_phase1.sql | Phase 1 foundation migration creating five new tables, two additive ALTER TABLEs, RLS policies, and grants. Issues already flagged in previous threads. | | supabase/migrations/20260613170000_course_library_round_tee_id.sql | Drift-free DO block patching `submit_round_atomic` and `save_partial_round_atomic` via `pg_get_functiondef`. Idempotent with explicit anchor assertion. No new issues found. | | src/lib/golf/course-library.ts | Pure helpers (normalization, mappers, completeness, diff). Well-tested, no I/O, no issues found. | | src/lib/golf/upload-course-image.ts | Client-side upload helper — validates MIME and size, then uploads directly to Supabase storage. No issues found. | | supabase/migrations/20260613160100_course_library_normalize_fix.sql | Fixes `golf_normalize_name` regex with `\m`/`\M` word-boundary anchors and re-backfills `normalized_name`. Idempotent. No issues found. | | src/app/golf/actions/__tests__/course-library.test.ts | Action-level tests covering auth guard, dedup, attribution, coach gate, injection sanitization, empty-holes guard, and soft-delete filtering. ## What Makes it **unmistakable which team you're viewing**, and makes the switch feel premium — directly addressing "there should be some kind of indicator that you're on women's or men's… a color change of the gradient." When a dual-team head / director-of-golf is active, the shell adopts a per-team accent (chosen direction: **indicator + faint wash**): - **Active pill segment** fills with the team accent — Men's = helm green, Women's = a refined violet — plus an on-accent dot. - A **faint top wash** (low-alpha team tint, masked into transparency) bleeds down ~220px behind the glass top bar, then dissolves into the warm cream. - A **2px underline** under the glass top bar in the team accent. - Switching is an **instant optimistic flip** (pill + accent change immediately, before the RSC refresh) with a 280–520ms cross-fade; reverts on failure. Scoped to the toggle affordances only — the rest of the UI stays green-forward, respecting the design system's "never a colored gradient." Players + single-team coaches are **completely unthemed**. ## Design note Men's = locked helm green; Women's = a refined violet (≈#7C3AED), matched in weight to primary-600 so white text clears AA. Deliberately *not* the pink/blue cliché. ## Files - `src/styles/design-tokens.css` — `--fw-color-team-mens` / `--fw-color-team-womens`. - `src/lib/golf/team-theme.ts` (+ test) — `normalizeTeamGender` / `teamGenderLabel` / `teamAccentVar`. - `AppShell.tsx` + `FairwayTopBar.tsx` — generic `accentColor` prop → wash + underline (cross-fading, motion-reduce safe). - `TeamSwitcher.tsx` (+ test) — accent-filled active segment, optimistic flip, `onOptimisticSwitch`. - `FairwayDashboardShell.tsx` — derives active gender, holds it optimistically, feeds the shell. ## Verification Ran a headless visual test against a dev server as a (temporarily seeded, then torn down) dual-team demo coach — **13/13**: - pill renders · optimistic flip fires · **wash hue 149.6 (green) → 292.9 (violet)** · underline changes · `golf_active_team` cookie flips both ways · roster re-scopes · no page errors. - `tsc` clean · `eslint` 0 errors (no new warnings) · **production build OK** · full unit suite **2372 passed** (+team-theme 9, +2 TeamSwitcher). Screenshots (men's green → one click → women's violet, data re-scoped) shared in-thread. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

Adds a premium active-team indicator for dual-program head coaches: an accent-filled pill segment, a faint top wash, and a 2 px top-bar underline, all cross-fading on team switch with an optimistic flip (instant visual feedback before the RSC refresh, revert on failure). The team-theme utility (`normalizeTeamGender` / `teamGenderLabel` / `teamAccentVar`) is a clean extraction from TeamSwitcher, well-tested, and the `AppShell`/`FairwayTopBar` `accentColor` prop is properly opt-in — single-team coaches and players are entirely unaffected. - **Optimistic state wiring** (`FairwayDashboardShell`): `optimisticGender` state is seeded from and re-synced to `serverGender` via `useEffect`; `onOptimisticSwitch` callback propagates the instant gender flip into the shell before the server round-trip, with a correct revert path on failure. - **Design tokens** (`design-tokens.css`): two new `--fw-color-team-*` tokens scoped to the toggle affordances only; violet lightness matched to `primary-600` for WCAG AA white-text compliance. - **One logic gap**: `optimisticGender ?? serverGender` silently falls through when `optimisticGender` is `null` (non-gendered team selected in dropdown mode), leaving the previous team's accent visible during the optimistic window — see inline comment."

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge for the primary pill-mode use case; one logic gap in the dropdown fallback path can show a stale accent during the optimistic window when switching to a non-gendered team. The core feature — optimistic pill flip, accent wash, top-bar underline, correct revert-on-failure — is sound and well-tested. The gap is isolated to FairwayDashboardShell line 350: null ?? serverGender falls through when the target team has no gender, so the old accent lingers for up to 520 ms before the RSC refresh corrects it. This only affects the dropdown fallback path (>2 teams or missing/duplicate genders), not the primary men's/women's pill flow. src/app/golf/(dashboard)/FairwayDashboardShell.tsx — the `optimisticGender ?? serverGender` expression on line 350 needs a sentinel-based fix before the feature reaches coaches with non-gendered teams in dropdown mode.

## What Makes the "two org rows for one school" bug **impossible going forward**. While testing the team toggle against University of Lynchburg, we found its men's and women's teams lived under **two separate `organizations` rows** whose names differed only by a trailing space (`"University of Lynchburg "` vs `"University of Lynchburg"`). The per-org unique index (`golf_teams_org_gender_uidx`) only enforces one team *per gender within* an org — it can't catch a school fragmented across two orgs, so no coach was a dual-team head and the toggle could never appear. (The split data itself was consolidated separately on 2026-06-13.) ## Fix (durable, two layers) **1. DB backstop — migration `20260613150000`** (already applied to prod + verified): - Trims any whitespace already stored (idempotent; 0 rows). - `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX organizations_normalized_name_uidx ON organizations (lower(btrim(name))) WHERE name IS NOT NULL` — one org per school name, **case- and whitespace-insensitive**, for **every** insert path (onboarding, admin, future code). **2. App layer — `onboarding.ts`:** - Trims `orgName` before insert (and in the team-name fallback). - Catches the `23505` and returns a friendly *"An organization named X already exists — ask your program's head coach to add you"* instead of a raw error or a silent duplicate. Deliberately does **not** auto-join an existing org by name (that would let anyone attach to any program by typing its name) — a clear error is the safe behavior. ## Verification - **Migration applied to prod + proven:** index present (`lower(btrim(name)) WHERE name IS NOT NULL`); a trial `"University of Lynchburg "` insert is **rejected** (proven via a self-rolling-back `DO` block — nothing persisted); still exactly 1 Lynchburg org; post-fix scan shows **0** whitespace names and **0** normalized-name collisions across all orgs. - `tsc` clean · `eslint` clean · `docs:check` clean · onboarding suite **48 passed** (incl. +2: trims the name; friendly 23505 error without proceeding to create coach/team). ## Note on `database.ts` The pre-commit `db:types` hook reconciled `src/lib/types/database.ts` against applied prod schema — alphabetizes the now-applied `golf_pga_standards.tour` column (drops the stale "ahead of prod" comment) and adds the `is_golf_team_head_coach` function type from the team-toggle migration. Benign; no types removed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR adds two defensive layers against duplicate-school organization rows: a DB-level partial unique index on `lower(btrim(name))` and an app-layer trim + `23505` catch in `completeCoachOnboarding`. The migration is idempotent and the new Zod/action logic is well-tested. - **Migration** (`20260613150000`): normalizes any existing whitespace in org names, then creates `organizations_normalized_name_uidx` — a case- and whitespace-insensitive unique guard that covers every insert path, not just the onboarding action. - **`onboarding.ts`**: trims `orgName` before the DB insert, uses the trimmed name in the team-name fallback, and catches `23505` to return a human-readable error instead of a raw failure — correctly stopping before coach/team rows are created. - **`database.ts`**: benign type-sync reconciliation (alphabetizes `tour` column, adds `is_golf_team_head_coach` function signature, drops a stale \"ahead of prod\" comment).

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge after addressing the whitespace-only orgName schema gap in onboarding.ts. The migration and 23505 error-handling path are solid. The gap is in the Zod schema: an all-whitespace orgName passes min(1) validation, then gets trimmed to an empty string by the action, which would be inserted as a malformed organization name. Adding .trim() to the schema field before .min(1) closes this hole completely. Everything else looks correct. src/app/golf/actions/onboarding.ts — specifically the coachOnboardingSchema orgName field and the 23505 constraint-name check.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/app/golf/actions/onboarding.ts | Trims orgName before insert and catches 23505 with a friendly message; all-whitespace orgName still slips past Zod validation and is inserted as an empty-string org name. | | supabase/migrations/20260613150000_organizations_unique_normalized_name.sql | Adds a partial unique index on lower(btrim(name)) with a preceding idempotent UPDATE; migration is safe to re-run and correctly handles the Lynchburg trailing-space scenario. | | src/app/golf/actions/__tests__/program-onboarding.test.ts | Adds two new tests: one verifying name trimming on insert and team-name fallback, another verifying the 23505 path returns a friendly error and halts without creating a coach row. | | src/lib/types/database.ts | Routine db:types reconciliation — alphabetizes the tour column in golf_pga_standards, drops a stale "ahead of prod" comment, and adds the is_golf_team_head_coach function type. |

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. `src/app/golf/actions/onboarding.ts`, line 18 ([link](https://github.com/njrini99-code/helmv3/blob/bf4246f9b95d8fea9688a0ae61be2bc70444fa0c/src/app/golf/actions/onboarding.ts#L18)) An all-whitespace `orgName` (e.g. `" "`) passes the Zod `min(1)` check because its length is > 0, but `.trim()` at line 114 reduces it to `""`. That empty string is then inserted as the organization name — the first such insert succeeds because `lower(btrim(""))` = `""` doesn't conflict with any existing row, leaving a malformed organization in the database. Adding `.trim()` as a Zod transform before `.min(1)` causes the schema to reject whitespace-only names with the same "Organization name is required" message, and the trimmed value flows through as `validatedData.orgName` so the explicit `.trim()` on line 114 becomes a harmless no-op.

## What Scopes the GolfHelm **conversation rail** to the coach's **active team** so a dual-team head / director-of-golf sees only the active team's DMs — not the union of both teams. Single-team coaches and players are **completely unaffected**. This is **follow-up #2** from the team-toggle build (#281), where the rail was documented as commingling both teams' DMs for a dual-team head. ## Root cause The rail is fetched **client-side** by `useGolfConversations()` → RPC `get_golf_conversations_with_details(p_user_id)`, which scopes **only by participant membership** and never projects/filters `team_id`. A dual-team head participates in conversations stamped with **both** teams' `team_id` (every golf conversation is stamped with the active team at creation — `createConversation` requires `team_id` for golf), so the rail returned the **union**. Flipping the `TeamSwitcher` re-resolved the active team everywhere *except* the rail (keyed on `user` only). ## Fix — no migration, no RLS change New server action **`getGolfActiveTeamConversationIds()`** (`src/app/actions/messages.ts`): - returns the active team's participant-conversation ids, **or `null` = "do not scope"**. - cookie-aware via `resolveCoachTeamIdWithCookie` (mirrors `announcements.ts`); a forged cookie is validated + falls back to the staffed/default team inside the resolver. The client hook filters **both** the RPC rows and the team-chat supplement by the allow-set. ### No-op contract (9 unit tests) Returns `null` — i.e. byte-for-byte the prior rail — for: - players (no `golf_coaches` row), - coaches staffed on **0 or 1** team, - unresolved active team / any unexpected error (**fail-open**, never blanks the rail). Only a coach staffed on **>1 team** is ever scoped. Gated on team **count** (not `canSwitch`) so a dual-team **assistant** is scoped too. ## Decisions baked in - **Gate = team count > 1** (scopes dual-team assistants, not just heads). - **No-cookie first load = default-scope** to the resolver's primary/oldest team (consistent with announcements/tasks), not union. ## Out of scope (flagged, not fixed here) - Direct thread access by `conversation_id` (`useGolfMessages`) is **not** team-gated — a stale deep-link to the other team's thread remains openable. Rail-only per the ticket. - Cross-team DMs stay **pinned to their creation-time team** (a conversation has exactly one `team_id`). ## Verification - `tsc` clean · `eslint` clean · **production build OK** (the `'use server'` boundary — the module is imported by the client hook) - full unit suite **2373 passed** / 39 skipped - new action test **9/9** - Live 2-team toggle itself was separately verified **9/9 against production** (the switcher flips the `golf_active_team` cookie both ways). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR scopes the golf conversation rail to a coach's active team by introducing a new server action (`getGolfActiveTeamConversationIds`) that returns the allow-set of conversation IDs for the active team, with a `null` sentinel meaning "do not scope." Single-team coaches and players are unaffected; only coaches staffed on more than one team receive a filtered rail, and the filter re-resolves on every fetch via the `golf_active_team` cookie. - **New server action** (`src/app/actions/messages.ts`): four sequential DB queries determine whether scoping applies, resolve the active team from the cookie, and return the intersection of the user's participant conversations and the active team's conversations. Returns `null` (no-op) for unauthenticated users, players, and single-team coaches, and `null` on any unhandled exception. - **Hook integration** (`src/hooks/golf/use-golf-messages.ts`): `fetchConversations` calls the action after the RPC and uses the resulting `Set` to filter both the RPC rows and the team-chat supplement, with a try/catch that falls back to `null` on exceptions. - **9 unit tests** cover the no-op contract (unauthenticated, player, 0- and 1-team coach, unresolved team) and the scoping path for both head and assistant coaches, but the failure mode where a Supabase query returns `{ data: null, error }` is not exercised by the mock.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge for single-team coaches and players; multi-team coaches can see a blank rail if either of the two inner Supabase queries returns an error response rather than throwing. The action's JSDoc explicitly guarantees fail-open behaviour ("never blank the rail"), but the two queries that build the allow-set (`golf_conversation_participants` and `golf_conversations`) only destructure `data` and discard `error`. A real Supabase error response sets `data` to `null` without throwing, so the outer `try/catch` does not fire. For the participants query this leads to `partIds = []` and an early `return []`; for the conversations query it leads to `return []`. An empty array is not `null`, the client-side `Set` constructed from it is truthy, and every conversation is filtered out. The test suite misses this path because the mock never populates the `error` field. The scope of impact is narrow (multi-team coaches only, only when a DB query fails), and the fix is small. src/app/actions/messages.ts — the two inner Supabase queries need `error` checks with `return null` on failure; the corresponding test in `golf-active-team-conversations.test.ts` should add a case where the mock returns `{ data: null, error: new Error(...) }` to cover this path.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/app/actions/messages.ts | Adds `getGolfActiveTeamConversationIds` server action; the two inner Supabase queries ignore `error`, so a DB failure returns `[]` instead of `null`, breaking the stated fail-open contract and silently blanking the rail for multi-team coaches. | | src/hooks/golf/use-golf-messages.ts | Integrates the new scoping action into `useGolfConversations`; filtering logic for both RPC rows and the team-chat supplement is correct; scoping call is sequential to the RPC when it could run in parallel. | | src/app/golf/actions/__tests__/golf-active-team-conversations.test.ts | 9 well-structured tests covering the no-op contract and happy-path scoping; the mock returns `{ data: null }` for missing table seeds, which does not replicate a real Supabase error response (`{ data: null, error: ... }`), leaving the P1 failure mode untested. | | src/app/golf/actions/messages.ts | Trivial re-export addition of `getGolfActiveTeamConversationIds`; no logic changes. |

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Hook as useGolfConversations (client) participant SA as getGolfActiveTeamConversationIds (server action) participant DB as Supabase DB Hook->>DB: rpc get_golf_conversations_with_details(user_id) DB-->>Hook: rawData (all participant convs, both teams) Hook->>SA: getGolfActiveTeamConversationIds() SA->>DB: auth.getUser() DB-->>SA: user SA->>DB: golf_coaches .eq(user_id) DB-->>SA: coach (or null → return null) SA->>DB: getCoachTeamSwitchContext(coach.id) DB-->>SA: ctx.teams alt "teams.length <= 1" SA-->>Hook: null (no scoping) else "teams.length > 1" SA->>DB: resolveCoachTeamIdWithCookie (reads cookie) DB-->>SA: activeTeamId SA->>DB: golf_conversation_participants .eq(user_id) DB-->>SA: partIds SA->>DB: golf_conversations .eq(team_id, activeTeamId) .in(partIds) DB-->>SA: teamConvs SA-->>Hook: string[] (allow-set) end Hook->>Hook: filter rawData by allow-set Hook->>Hook: filter team-chat supplement by allow-set Hook->>Hook: merge + sort → setConversations ```

## Men's / Women's Team Toggle — complete build

Consolidates #266 (switcher) + #267 (LPGA standards) + #268 (program onboarding) and finishes the feature **end-to-end across backend scoping, RLS, onboarding/data-model, and UI**, per a 4-agent audit. Supersedes #266/#267/#268.

### The core fix
The toggle existed but was **~⅓ wired** — only ~28 of ~85 coach actions honored the active team; several **threw** on a real 2-team program. This PR makes active-team resolution authoritative everywhere and hardens the security model.

### Phase A — data model + authz core (migrations)
- Restored `golf_pga_standards.tour` to `database.ts` (the 3-way merge silently dropped #267's column → build break).
- `UNIQUE(organization_id, gender)` partial index — one men's + one women's per program.
- New `is_golf_team_head_coach()` predicate; repointed `team_chs_settings_write_team` + `golf_team_coach_staff_insert` to it — **fixes the program head being locked out of managing their own second/women's team** (was gated on `is_primary`, which a head holds on only one team).
- `validateCoachTeamAccess` is now **staff-strict** (dropped the broad org fallback; legacy-only zero-staff escape) — the cookie read-boundary now equals the write-boundary.
- `addSecondTeam`: catches the 23505 dup-gender race + asserts org before the privileged staff insert. `createTeam`: gender-aware.

### Phase B — every coach surface honors the active team
Re-scoped ~20 action files to `resolveCoachTeamIdWithCookie`. Fixed the P0 multi-team **throws** (Team Stats, Recruiting, qualifier create) and the cookie-blind reads (insights, patterns, intelligence, stats, travel, development, round-reviews, command-palette, calendar-feeds, whats-new…). Authorization sites (`documents`, `announcements`, `communication`, `travel`, round-view in `golf.ts`/`insights.ts`) corrected to **staff-strict** `validateCoachTeamAccess` so a director-of-golf staffed on both teams keeps access to either regardless of the toggle.

### Phase C — staff-scoped RLS wall (migrations) + logout
- Staff-scoped `golf_players` (`user_is_coach_of_golf_player`) and `golf_rounds_update_team` — **was org-scoped**, so an assistant on the men's team could read the women's roster / update their rounds. Now: a coach sees a team only if staffed on it; a head staffed on both sees both (per the agreed posture).
- `REVOKE` anon `EXECUTE` on team predicates.
- `clearActiveTeam()` on all 6 sign-out paths (hygiene — staff-strict reads already closed the carry-over hole).

### Phase D / E
- Recruiting HQ → `force-dynamic`; `loadPlayerCohort` lists memberships (never throws on anomaly, classifies women's if any active team is women's).
- Staff-strict "wall" regression test + cohort anomaly coverage. **Full unit suite green (2364 passed); `tsc` clean.**

---
## ⚠️ Prod migrations — apply IN THIS ORDER before/with deploy (NOT yet applied)
1. `20260610160000_program_onboarding_backfill.sql` (#268) — creates head_coach+is_primary staff rows for existing coaches. **Must run first** (the staff-scoped RLS + switcher gate depend on it).
2. `20260610170000_seed_lpga_standards.sql` (#267) — adds `golf_pga_standards.tour` + LPGA seed. (After applying, regenerate `database.ts` from prod — the `tour` column is currently hand-added ahead of prod.)
3. `20260612120000_team_toggle_data_model.sql` — UNIQUE(org,gender) + head-coach predicate + repointed policies.
4. `20260612130000_team_toggle_rls_staff_scope.sql` — staff-scope golf_players/golf_rounds + anon REVOKE.

## Decisions captured
- **Team wall = staff-scoped** (director on both sees both; assistant on one cannot cross).
- Plan/runbook: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-12-team-toggle-complete.md`.

## Follow-ups (documented, not blocking)
- Messages conversation rail commingles both teams' DMs for a dual-team head — add a team filter/badges (a UX choice, not a bug).
- Optional CI grep-guard forbidding new `eq('organization_id', …)` coach-team lookups in actions (skipped now — brittle vs. legit by-id+org authz patterns).
- Full 2-team E2E fixture matrix (unit + RLS coverage shipped; browser/iOS QA is human).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
## What & why During the 308-coach demo blast, a production deploy landed at the traffic peak (**21:13 UTC**). The cold Vercel CDN edge couldn't serve large JS chunks (one is **477 KB**) fast enough under ~**224 concurrent demo opens in 30 min**, so chunk fetches **timed out → ChunkLoadError → a downstream React Suspense/#310/#419 cascade**, leaving coaches "stuck loading" for ~13 minutes. **This was NOT a code defect.** Production `error_logs` show every error confined to a single 13-min window on a now-replaced deployment; the current deployment serves the demo dashboard cleanly (verified: `/golf/demo` → `/golf/dashboard` 200, all 63 chunks warm). React #310 here = *"Rendered more hooks than during the previous render,"* a downstream artifact of partial chunk loads (hit ~10% of loads, not 100%), not a render-loop bug. The real user-facing gap: `StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript` reloaded **exactly once** on a chunk error, then its `sessionStorage` guard left the user stuck if that reload also hit the still-cold window. ## Changes - **`StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript.tsx`** — replace the one-shot reload guard with up to **3 cooldown-spaced (12 s) retries** so a user rides out a brief cold edge instead of getting stuck. The attempt cap is **encoded in the URL param**, so it survives the reload even with no `sessionStorage` — which also closes a latent **infinite-reload loop the original had in Safari private mode** (`getItem` null + `setItem` throws → reloaded every time). Debounced to one reload per page load; hard cap guarantees ≤3 reloads ever. - **`scripts/warm-edge.ts`** — pre-campaign **go/no-go**: auto-logs in via `/golf/demo`, pulls the dashboard's actual chunk set, fetches them over several rounds, and PASS/FAILs on whether they're warm. Run after a deploy, before a blast. ## The real prevention Never deploy to prod while a campaign is actively sending; if a deploy just landed, run `npx tsx scripts/warm-edge.ts` until it PASSes before blasting. ## Verification - `npm run typecheck` ✅ `eslint` ✅ embedded recovery script `node --check` ✅ - `warm-edge.ts` live run: deployment `dpl_6bTVZ`, 63/63 chunks 200, warmed to ~70 ms by round 2 → **PASS** 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR addresses the CDN cold-edge chunk-load failures that caused a 13-minute outage during the 308-coach demo blast by replacing the one-shot `sessionStorage` reload guard with a URL-param-based counter (up to 3 retries, 12 s cooldown each), and adds a `scripts/warm-edge.ts` pre-campaign tool that auto-logs in, extracts the dashboard's actual JS chunk set, fetches them across multiple rounds, and exits non-zero if any chunk is still slow. - **`StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript.tsx`**: Retry count now lives in `?__deployment_refresh=N` so it survives reloads in Safari private mode (where `sessionStorage.setItem` throws), closing the original infinite-reload regression; `reloadScheduled` debounces the burst of simultaneous chunk errors on a cold load. - **`scripts/warm-edge.ts`**: Cookie-jar login flow, regex-based chunk extraction from dashboard HTML, and parallel-fetch rounds with a PASS/FAIL exit code intended to gate campaign sends after a deploy.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The browser-side recovery logic is safe to merge; the pre-blast warm-edge script has a hang risk under unresponsive network conditions that should be addressed before it is relied upon in the campaign runbook. The browser-side recovery logic is well-reasoned and the Safari private mode fix is a genuine improvement. The warm-edge.ts script has no fetch timeout — any stalled chunk fetch will block the process forever, which is directly contrary to its purpose as a go/no-go gate before sending a blast. The false-PASS risk from ROUNDS=0 or an empty env var compounds this. scripts/warm-edge.ts needs a fetch timeout and an input guard on ROUNDS before being used as the pre-campaign gate.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | scripts/warm-edge.ts | New pre-campaign CDN warm-up script; auto-logs in via /golf/demo, extracts JS chunk URLs from the dashboard HTML, fetches them across multiple rounds, and exits 0 only when all chunks respond quickly. Two issues: no fetch timeout so the script can hang indefinitely on a stalled connection, and ROUNDS=0/empty causes a false PASS without running any warming rounds. | | src/components/providers/StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript.tsx | Replaces the one-shot sessionStorage guard with a URL-param-based counter (max 3 retries, 12 s cooldown) that survives reloads and fixes the Safari-private-mode infinite-reload regression. The cooldown timestamp stored in sessionStorage is a future moment rather than the actual fire time, which can slightly under-space retries on slow devices but is bounded by the URL cap. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User Browser participant S as StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript participant CDN as Vercel CDN Edge participant SS as sessionStorage participant URL as window.location U->>CDN: Load page (cold edge) CDN-->>U: ChunkLoadError (timeout) U->>S: error / unhandledrejection event S->>URL: currentReloadCount() reads ?__deployment_refresh URL-->>S: count (0, 1, or 2) S->>S: "count >= MAX_RELOADS (3)? bail" S->>S: "reloadScheduled=true (debounce)" S->>SS: read RELOAD_KEY lastAt S->>S: compute wait (0ms on first, ~12s on retries) S->>SS: write Date.now()+wait S->>U: clearStaleState() (caches + SW) S->>S: setTimeout(wait) S->>URL: "location.replace(?__deployment_refresh=count+1)" URL-->>U: Page reloads with updated param Note over U,CDN: Repeat up to MAX_RELOADS=3 times ``` Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["fix(resilience): cooldown-spaced chunk-e..."](https://github.com/njrini99-code/helmv3/commit/ab2aac075cbc9fa717aa435cd971dbc0b527efa8) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=37117988) > Greptile also left **3 inline comments** on this PR.

Found by the CRM send-readiness audit. Two send-breaking bugs in the in-app CRM demo blast: 1. **Tracking broken** — TemplatePicker pre-substituted {email}/{first_name} with one preview coach before the route saw the body, so every recipient CTA ?ref={email} pointed to the same coach (admin_events attribution collapsed). Greptile Summary

This PR fixes two send-breaking bugs in the CRM blast flow: `TemplatePicker` no longer pre-substitutes merge tokens before the route sees the body (fixing per-recipient `?ref=` tracking), and `BulkEmailModal` now chunks large recipient lists into ≤100-recipient batches sent sequentially (fixing the HTTP 400 that silently dropped everything above 100). - **TemplatePicker** removes `replaceMergeTags` and passes raw template tokens to the modal; preview substitution is kept client-side in `BulkEmailModal` using the first coach as a sample. - **BulkEmailModal** introduces a `BATCH_SIZE = 100` loop that accumulates `aggSent/aggSkipped/aggFailed` across batches, handles hard-stop conditions (429 daily cap, 401/403 session expiry) with a user-visible stop message, and updates a live progress bar per batch.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Safe to merge for the tracking fix; the batching logic has a counting gap that produces wrong numbers in the result card when the daily cap is hit mid-run. The merge-token fix is clean and correct. The batching loop works, but when a hard-stop condition fires mid-run, the current batch and all remaining unprocessed batches are silently excluded from the aggFailed total, so the operator sees fewer failures than actually occurred. BulkEmailModal.tsx — specifically the hard-stop branch inside the batch loop

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/app/golf/admin/crm/components/BulkEmailModal.tsx | Adds batch-chunking (<=100/POST) for the Helm send path and accumulates per-batch results; hard-stop branches (429/401/403) exit the loop without adding the current or remaining batches to aggFailed, causing the result card to under-report failures. | | src/app/golf/admin/crm/components/TemplatePicker.tsx | Removes client-side replaceMergeTags pre-substitution so raw tokens are passed to the route; the coachData prop is now unused but still declared, and the footer hint about merge tags contradicts the new behavior. |

Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. ## Shared demo coach account + auto-auth link + login tracing A single demo login emailed to ~300 prospective coaches, dropping them into a fully-populated "Demo University Golf" team to explore. ### What's in this PR (code) - **`/golf/demo?ref=` auto-auth route** (`src/app/golf/demo/route.ts`) — one reusable link signs the shared demo coach in server-side (creds from env, can ONLY ever auth the demo account) and redirects to the dashboard. No password typing; reusable by unlimited people; captures `ref`. - **Login tracing** (`auth.ts` + `golf-sign-in-form.tsx`) — `loginAction` now records `ref` + IP + geo (`x-vercel-ip-*`) + user-agent + `is_demo` into the existing `admin_events` table (`event_type='login'`). Backward-compatible (optional `ref` param); the form threads `?ref=` through like `returnTo`. - **`scripts/seed-demo-team-ops.ts`** — idempotent seeder for calendar/tasks/messages/announcements/docs/travel/qualifiers, strictly scoped to the demo team. - **`scripts/demo-login-report.sql`** — query to see who logged in. ### Already applied to prod (data, no deploy needed) - Shared demo coach **`demo@golfhelmdemo.com` / `Demo2026`** created on Demo University Golf (onboarding complete, philosophy + CoachHelm settings seeded) — **password login works on the live site right now.** - Team-ops seeded: 12 events / 84 attendance, 8 tasks, 15 messages, 4 announcements, 4 docs, 2 trips, 2 qualifiers. Team already had 7 players, 78 rounds, 173 fresh insights. ### Requires this deploy + Vercel env to activate The **auto-auth link** and the **rich login tracing** only work once this branch is deployed AND these env vars are set in Vercel (Production): - `DEMO_ACCOUNT_EMAIL=demo@golfhelmdemo.com` - `DEMO_COACH_PASSWORD=Demo2026` (must match the provisioned password) Until then: the password login works, but logins log only `{ip}` (old code) and `/golf/demo` won't exist. ### Tracking Mail-merge a per-coach `?ref=` into each emailed link (`…/golf/demo?ref=coach-stanford`) to identify who logged in. Pairs with Resend click tracking (who clicked the email) for two layers: click vs actually-explored. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a shared demo coach account feature: a one-click auto-auth route (`/golf/demo`), enriched login tracing (geo, user-agent, `ref`, `is_demo`) stored in `admin_events`, an idempotent team-ops seeder script, and a reporting SQL query. - **`/golf/demo` auto-auth route** signs in the shared demo account server-side using env-var credentials and redirects to the dashboard, with `?ref=` tracing so per-prospect email links identify who clicked. - **`loginAction` in `auth.ts`** now captures `userAgent`, country, city, `ref`, and `is_demo` on every successful login; `is_demo` is computed server-side against `DEMO_ACCOUNT_EMAIL` and cannot be spoofed by the client. - **`golf-sign-in-form.tsx`** threads `?ref=` through `sessionStorage` so the value survives any redirect cycle before being forwarded to `loginAction`.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The auto-auth route works as designed for the demo flow, but has two behavioral issues that should be fixed before wide distribution: it will bump any already-authenticated user off their own session, and it accepts unlimited traffic with no per-IP gate protecting the Supabase Auth quota. Two issues in route.ts affect real deployed behavior: the unconditional signInWithPassword call will silently replace an active real-coach session with the demo session, and the absent rate-limit guard means a bot can exhaust Supabase Auth quotas and break the demo link for legitimate prospects exactly when the email blast lands. A third issue in golf-sign-in-form.tsx means a stale ref in sessionStorage can misattribute a subsequent login to the wrong prospect, corrupting the tracking data the feature is built around. src/app/golf/demo/route.ts needs rate limiting and a session-presence check before calling signInWithPassword. src/components/auth/golf-sign-in-form.tsx needs the stale-ref clearing logic tightened.

Security Review

 - **`/golf/demo` — no rate limiting before Supabase auth call**: the endpoint has no per-IP or per-request rate limit. A bot can flood it with requests, exhausting Supabase Auth quotas for legitimate visitors. `loginAction` already has this protection; the same guard is absent here. - **`/golf/demo` — overwrites any active session unconditionally**: any authenticated user (including real coaches) who hits this URL will have their session silently replaced with the shared demo session. The account credentials are locked to the demo user by env var, so no privilege escalation is possible, but a real coach will be unexpectedly logged out. - **`?ref=` reflected into `admin_events` metadata**: the ref value is sanitized (control chars stripped, capped at 80 chars) before storage, which is adequate. No injection risk identified.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/app/golf/demo/route.ts | New auto-auth endpoint that signs in the shared demo account and redirects. Missing IP rate limiting (unlike loginAction), no existing-session check before overwriting, and sanitizeRef is duplicated from auth.ts. | | src/app/golf/actions/auth.ts | Adds userAgent, geo, ref, and is_demo fields to login tracing; is_demo computed server-side only. Backward-compatible change; sanitizeRef strips control chars correctly. | | src/components/auth/golf-sign-in-form.tsx | Threads ?ref= through sessionStorage to loginAction. Stale ref can persist on failed logins and fire on a subsequent successful login without a ref param, silently corrupting attribution. | | scripts/seed-demo-team-ops.ts | Idempotent seeder for demo team ops data; deletes FK children before parents, batches inserts, supports --dry-run. Non-production script with no runtime impact. | | scripts/demo-login-report.sql | Read-only reporting query against admin_events for is_demo=true logins. No issues. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant P as Prospect (email link) participant D as /golf/demo Route participant SA as Supabase Auth participant L as logLogin (admin_events) participant DB as /golf/dashboard P->>D: "GET /golf/demo?ref=coach-stanford" D->>D: sanitizeRef(ref) D->>D: read DEMO_COACH_PASSWORD env alt password missing D-->>P: 302 to /golf/login end D->>SA: signInWithPassword(DEMO_ACCOUNT_EMAIL, password) alt auth error D-->>P: 302 to /golf/login end SA-->>D: session + user D->>L: "logLogin(userId, email, {ip, userAgent, ref, is_demo:true})" Note right of L: fire-and-forget D-->>P: 302 to /golf/dashboard (with session cookies) P->>DB: GET /golf/dashboard ``` Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["feat(demo): shared demo coach login + au..."](https://github.com/njrini99-code/helmv3/commit/c4879e1a0b3430ace52e3dc492d98b98df8094a3) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=37013419) > Greptile also left **4 inline comments** on this PR.

This PR follows up on reviews from #257/#259, fixing two verified authorization bugs (class-sync ownership hole, reschedule-notification CHECK violation) plus two CodeQL nits. The ownership guards prevent teammates from overwriting or deleting each other's class calendar events, and the SQL migration extends the `notification_type` CHECK to allow `event_updated:` patterns that reschedule notifications already write. - **`removeClassFromCalendar` ownership check** (`calendar-sync.ts`): new guard looks up the class row via the user-role client before allowing the admin-client delete, but the `golf_player_classes` SELECT RLS only permits the row's owner and their coaches to read it — a regular teammate's query returns `null` for a real row, which the orphan-path logic incorrectly treats as \"safe to clean up.\" - **`syncClassToCalendar` ownership check** (`calendar-sync.ts`): correctly fails-closed (null → reject), so this path is safe. - **Notification constraint migration** and **cron-route CodeQL nit** are clean with no issues identified.

This PR remediates 32 confirmed defects from the June 2026 calendar audit across six parallel workstreams — root-delete/cascade protection, per-row delta series edits, hourly reminders, additive-only attendee edits, TZ-correct RSVP deadlines, self-RSVP RLS, conflict detection, range-driven fetching, ICS feed access, and email fan-out. - **Series integrity (P0 fixes):** `promoteSeriesRoot` correctly promotes the earliest surviving child before any delete that would trigger `ON DELETE CASCADE`; the per-row delta edit shifts each occurrence by the same wall-time difference rather than collapsing all rows to a single timestamp. - **Cron and notifications:** `event-reminders` is now hourly (`0 * * * *`), paginated past the PostgREST 1 000-row cap, deadline-guarded, and fans out push + email before writing the idempotency row — so partial failures retry on the next tick without double-counting successes. - **DB migrations (already applied):** `end >= start` CHECK constraint + 3 corrupt-row repairs; `attendance_status` column (dual-axis with RSVP `status`); `golf_event_attendance_insert_self` policy; TRUNCATE revoke on calendar tables.

## Summary
Makes the Strokes Gained **baseline a per-team coach setting**. A coach picks which reference their team's SG is measured against — **PGA Tour, Women's, Scratch, NCAA D1/D2/D3** — in Coaching Intelligence settings. Because SG is **stored, not computed on read**, changing the setting recomputes the team's stored SG so every surface (StandingBar, stats, CoachHelm) reflects the choice automatically.

This started as the women's-team SG fix (men's Broadie baseline over-penalized women's longer approaches, reading −12 to −29/round) and generalized into a selectable baseline. Each baseline maps to a single telescoping-preserving expected-strokes scale factor; **men's/PGA Tour = 1.0 = provably identical computation**.

## Changes

### DB (migrations applied to prod via MCP; files included as source)
- `golf_teams.gender` column (`20260607160000`), women's teams flagged.
- `sg_expected_strokes` gains optional `p_scale` (`20260607170000`).
- **Per-team baseline** (`20260607200000`):
  - `golf_team_settings.sg_baseline text` + check constraint.
  - `sg_baseline_scale(key)` → uniform expected-strokes scale factor.
  - `sg_scale_for_player(player)` → team's explicit setting, else gender default.
  - both SG writers (`recalculate_round_strokes_gained` = authoritative, `calculate_round_strokes_gained` = BEFORE-completion trigger) derive scale from the player (replaces the hardcoded gender CASE).
  - `recompute_team_sg(team)` — SECURITY DEFINER, **service_role-only** (REVOKE anon/authenticated): recomputes all completed rounds + refreshes player cache/standing.

### App
- `sg-benchmarks.ts`: `SgBaselineKey`, `SG_BASELINE_OPTIONS`, `sgBaselineScale`, `defaultSgBaseline`, `effectiveSgBaseline` — scales kept in sync with the DB.
- `team-sg-baseline.ts` server action: get/set baseline, recompute via the service-role RPC (admin client), revalidate SG paths.
- `SgBaselineSelector` client component, wired into **both** the legacy and Fairway Coaching Intelligence settings pages (gated on `teamId`).

Defaults preserve current behavior (women's → Women's 1.083, men's → PGA Tour 1.0); no backfill needed on apply.

## Verified on prod
- **Bidirectional toggle**: Women's team set to `pga_tour` → Grace Saunders SG **−7.45 → −12.91**; reverted to default → back to **−7.45**. Auto-switches on select.
- Women's per-round SG residual: **−6.0 → −0.20** (men's band −0.32).
- cache↔standing parity: **0 drift** across all players with standing rows.
- Men's SG unchanged (Nick Rini / Jackson Hale −3.70, Tyler Hayes −3.21).
- `tsc` 0 errors · `lint` 0 errors · 18 targeted tests green · `next build` success (coaching-intelligence route compiles).

## Methodology note
Scale factors derived via the codebase's documented scoring-ratio scaling — defensible approximations, not per-tour ShotLink anchors. If true per-distance data is sourced later, only the factor/curve needs updating (mechanism is in place).

## helm-review daily — 2026-06-07

Autonomous daily review of **Sentry · DB error tables · Vercel runtime logs**. Ships the durable, env-independent, high-confidence fixes found; everything else is triaged in the daily brief below (no code change, with rationale).

**Two fixes:**
1. `golf_rounds` auto-save `permission denied` (PG 42501) — the prod user-facing bug found in the error tables.
2. RLS test fixture using an invalid `insight_type` — **was turning the required `Supabase lint + RLS tests` check red on `main` for every PR** (found while taking this PR green).

---

### Fix 1 — `golf_rounds` auto-save `permission denied` (PG 42501)

**Symptom (production):** `savePartialRound.updateExisting` failed with `permission denied for table golf_rounds` → players saw *"Auto-save server error: Failed to save round. Please try again."* and the client circuit-breaker tripped. **92 failures, 2026-06-02 → 06-06** (39 client-visible on `helmsportslabs.com`), real users (e.g. `clynde@guilford.edu`).

**Root cause:** `authenticated` holds only a **column-level** UPDATE allowlist on `golf_rounds` (baseline `20260527000000`, extended by `20260603040000`), not a table-level grant. Postgres checks per-column UPDATE privilege for **every** column in an UPDATE's `SET` list regardless of whether the value changes, so once the table gained columns outside the allowlist (`strokes_gained_*`, `coachhelm_*`, `ai_recap*`) and any UPDATE path touched one, the whole statement was rejected with 42501. The allowlist has now drifted out of sync with the schema **twice**.

Verified live against prod DB:
```
has_table_privilege(authenticated, golf_rounds, UPDATE)              = false
has_column_privilege(authenticated, golf_rounds, strokes_gained_total, UPDATE) = false
has_column_privilege(authenticated, golf_rounds, total_score,         UPDATE) = true   (in allowlist)
has_table_privilege(authenticated, golf_rounds, SELECT)              = true   (RETURNING * works)
```

**Fix:** `GRANT UPDATE ON TABLE public.golf_rounds TO authenticated` — table-wide, ending the allowlist drift. Same pattern already adopted for this exact class of bug on `golf_round_reviews` (`20260602190000`) and `golf_coach_insights` (`20260528011000`).

**Security:** unchanged at the row level. RLS (`golf_rounds_update` + coach/team UPDATE policies) still scopes *which rows* `authenticated` may modify; this only widens *which columns*, on rows the role can already update. `SELECT`/`INSERT`/`DELETE` already table-wide. Idempotent.

> ⚠️ **Action required after merge:** the grant only takes effect once applied to prod (`supabase db push` / migration apply). The error is currently quiescent (last seen 06-06 01:32) but the schema fragility remains, so apply at the next migration window.

### Fix 2 — RLS fixture `insight_type` drift (unblocks the required check)

`supabase/tests/rls/golf_coach_insights_cross_tenant_select.sql` seeded `insight_type = 'value_derived'`, which is **not** in `golf_coach_insights_insight_type_check` (a placeholder that only ever existed in unit-test mocks, never emitted by production generators). The seed `INSERT` failed with a check-constraint violation, aborting the pgTAP plan (*"planned 6 tests but ran 0"*) and turning the **required** `Supabase lint + RLS tests` check **red on `main`** — confirmed failing on `main` HEAD (`19fd32a5`, 2026-06-06T19:37Z), i.e. blocking *all* PRs, not just this one. Swapped to `'putting'` (constraint-valid, matches the row's category); the test asserts cross-tenant isolation so the type value is immaterial.

---

## Daily brief — triage of everything else (no code change)

| # | Signal | Last seen | Env | Disposition |
|---|--------|-----------|-----|-------------|
| 1 | **`golf_rounds` 42501 auto-save** | 06-06 01:32 | **prod** | ✅ **Fix 1** |
| 2 | **RLS `Supabase lint + RLS tests` red on main** (`value_derived`) | 06-06 19:37 | CI | ✅ **Fix 2** |
| 3 | `is9Hole is not defined` — `stats_data.queryDetailedStatsWithClient` | 06-07 02:47 | local dev | **Not a canonical bug.** Symbol absent from origin/main + HEAD + worktree — stale local `next dev` build chunk. Restart dev server. |
| 4 | `Rendered more hooks` (useMemo) | 06-06 15:23 | local dev | HeadlessChrome `.helmdev` automation on `/stats` & `/my-insights` (redesign WIP). Not pinned to a canonical component. |
| 5 | `device_tokens` RLS INSERT — `registerDeviceToken` | 06-06 18:50 | prod | 2 ev. `upsert(onConflict:'token')` can't reassign a token owned by another user (shared device / account switch). Recommend conflict handling, not an autonomous push-auth change. |
| 6 | `fetchShotDriversByCategory` / stats `57014` timeout | 06-06 01:32 | server | 11 ev; query perf, fails gracefully. Needs EXPLAIN/index — not an unprofiled autonomous change. |
| 7 | React **#418** hydration `/dashboard` | 06-02 | prod | 12 ev, stopped 5d ago; non-fatal. Monitor. |
| 8 | React **#310** `/dashboard/stats` | 06-06 18:20 | prod | 1 ev singleton. Monitor. |
| 9 | `Loading chunk … failed` / `Load failed` | 06-06 | prod | Deploy-churn (13 prod deploys/14h). Not code bugs. |
| 10 | causality `unknown metric` (Sentry 2K) | ongoing | cron | Known **deferred** v3 causality registry drift (~45 metric IDs). Needs domain mapping. |
| 11 | 49ffe06d generator burst (ParType/PuttDistance/synthesis/starvation) | 05-26/27 | cron | ~10k ev but **stopped 11d ago**, one player, routine telemetry. Excluded. |

**Sentry MCP:** not queryable this run (interactive OAuth required, unattended). Used DB `error_logs` + `admin_events` (richer than the Sentry prod filter) + Vercel runtime logs.

**Vercel production runtime (3d, error/fatal):** effectively clean — 1 non-fatal `AuthApiError` on `GET /sw.js` (200). No platform-level 500s/timeouts/OOM.

## Production Review Fixes — PR #216

This branch contains PR #216's three nightly fixes plus the production-review remediation on top.

### Addressed

**🔴 #1 Push inputs not validated** — Added Zod schemas to `push-notifications.ts`; `token`/`platform`/`deviceName` are validated (`safeParse`) before any DB op. Invalid payloads return `{ success: false, error }` instead of hitting Supabase.

**🔴 #4 Unauthorized push registration swallowed** — `registerDeviceToken` (and `unregisterDeviceToken`) now **return** a typed retryable failure on unauthorized:
```ts
{ success: false, error: 'Unauthorized', code: 'UNAUTHORIZED_RETRYABLE', retryable: true }
```
instead of throwing. The `registration` listener in `push-registration.ts` now retries the retryable case with backoff (1/2/4/8s) and logs non-retryable failures once. This fails the iOS login-confirm cookie race soft instead of paging Sentry.

**🟢 #6 CodeRabbit config warnings** — Converted the unrecognized `yaml_language_server:` key to the standard `# yaml-language-server:` schema comment and removed the unrecognized `enable_free_tier_features` key.

body: ## Root cause `generateAndStoreRoundReview()` was refactored to a single `upsert(..., { onConflict: 'round_id' })` = `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (round_id) DO UPDATE`. Postgres requires the **UPDATE** privilege for that statement *even when the row is freshly inserted*. The `authenticated` role had INSERT but **not UPDATE** on `golf_round_reviews`, so **every** review generation (player and coach) failed at the table-privilege check with `permission denied for table golf_round_reviews` → the page showed **"Failed to save review"**. This is a silent regression from the old select-then-insert/update pattern (INSERT-only happy path worked) to the upsert. Confirmed in prod logs (two `ERROR: permission denied for table golf_round_reviews`). ## Fixes (already applied to prod via MCP; committed here for source-of-truth) 1. **`20260602190000`** — `GRANT UPDATE ON golf_round_reviews TO authenticated`. RLS still scopes writes to own rows (`Players can update their own reviews`) / coach's team (`round_reviews_write_coach`). Mirrors the earlier `20260528011000` fix for `golf_coach_insights`. 2. **`20260602191000`** — `round_reviews_insert_coach` policy. The review page authorizes coaches (`player_or_coach`) and auto-generates when uncached, but only a *player* INSERT policy existed, so coaches hit "Failed to save review" on any uncached player round. New policy is scoped identically to the existing coach SELECT/UPDATE policies (active membership + `is_golf_team_coach`). ## Also `scripts/refresh-demo-nick-rini.ts` — one-off, env + `--dry-run` gated. Rebuilds the demo player's complete shot ledgers from a Guilford source and re-dates the demo team into the rolling 30-day analytics window. Not wired into any runtime path. ## Verification (live prod) - **Player** rinin376: round review generates; flyover reconstructs all shots (H1 double = 6 strokes), momentum is per-hole (finishes +12, matches scorecard), putting consistent (35 putts everywhere), SG captions agree with arrows. - **Coach** njrini99: opening an uncached player round now generates successfully (no "Failed to save review"). ## Follow-up (noted, not in this PR) `anon` has stray INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on `golf_round_reviews` (RLS-blocked, but should be revoked for defense-in-depth). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---
title: fix(round-review): grant UPDATE + coach INSERT on golf_round_reviews

body: ## What Supabase security-advisor remediation. The DDL is **already applied to production** via Supabase MCP (migration version `20260602165152`); this PR mirrors it into the repo for parity (idempotent), so prod and `supabase/migrations/` stay in sync. ### (1) `function_search_path_mutable` (lint 0011) — 21 functions Pinned `search_path = public, pg_temp`. Verified behavior-preserving by reading every body: all cross-schema refs were already qualified (`auth.uid()`, `extensions.hypopg_reset()`), all unqualified refs are public objects — including the `::citext` cast in `write_suppression_on_unsubscribe` (citext lives in `public`, so an empty search_path would have broken it). Advisor now reports **0 of the 21** still mutable. ### (2) `anon_security_definer_function_executable` (lint 0028) — 17 admin/telemetry functions These SECURITY DEFINER functions were executable by `anon` via the default `PUBLIC` grant, so they could be invoked **unauthenticated** through PostgREST — e.g. `POST /rest/v1/rpc/get_users_with_auth` with the public anon key returned `users` + `auth.users` PII. Revoked `PUBLIC`/`anon` EXECUTE and granted `authenticated` + `service_role`, so both app call paths keep working (user-session admin actions — which already gate on `role='admin'` — and service-role admin actions). Verified: `anon=false`, `authenticated=true`, `service_role=true`. ## Deferred (documented in the migration header) A logged-in **non-admin** can still call some of these directly (authenticated retains EXECUTE). Closing that needs per-function work: revoke `authenticated` on the service-role-only functions, and add an inline `is_admin()` gate to user-session ones like `get_users_with_auth`. Their callers use dynamic `rpc(name)`, so each client must be traced before changing grants/bodies — deferred to avoid breaking the admin dashboard. ## Note `src/lib/types/database.ts` is included — a generated-types sync (adds the `preferences` column already present in prod from migration `20260528041553`). Compile-time only; unrelated to the grant changes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

## What On mobile/tablet (≤1024px), the Fairway shell's glass top bar — and every in-page sticky sub-header (CoachHelm Signals toolbar, etc.) — scrolled away instead of pinning. Verified live on production at iPhone width during post-deploy visual QA. ## Root cause Two `@media (max-width:1024px)` rules in `globals.css` set `overflow-x: hidden` on `/` as an iPhone side-scroll guard. Per CSS Overflow 3, `overflow-x: hidden` forces the other axis (`overflow-y`) to compute from `visible` → `auto`, turning `` into a **scroll container**. The Fairway shell scrolls the *document* (`min-h-dvh`), so `position: sticky; top:0` resolved against that non-scrolling `` box and never pinned. Confirmed empirically in the live browser: header `rectTop == -scrollY` at every offset with `hidden`; `rectTop == 0` once `overflow-x` was set to `clip` (or `visible`). ## Fix `overflow-x: clip` (with `overflow-x: hidden` kept first as a pre-iOS-16 / Chrome-<90 fallback). `clip` clips the side-scroll **without** creating a scroll container (it leaves `overflow-y: visible`), so sticky works. ## Flag-OFF safety Legacy `GolfDashboardShell` (flag-OFF) uses an inner `overflow-y-auto` `
` under a `flex h-dvh` root — `` never scrolls there, so this is a visual/behavioral **no-op** for flag-OFF. `clip` and `hidden` are visually identical. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---
title: fix(mobile): keep Fairway glass top bar sticky (overflow-x: clip)

No dead buttons, no double drawers. - **Live scoring stays immersive** — `rounds/new` and `rounds/continue/[id]` render *without* the shell chrome, so the round controls don't fight the nav bar. ## iOS audit — all facets - ✅ **Notch / status bar** — top bar pads `env(safe-area-inset-top)`; `viewport-fit: cover` is set in `layout.tsx`, so `env()` actually resolves in WKWebView. - ✅ **Home indicator** — content now pads `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`; mobile drawer already pads top+bottom safe areas. - ✅ **Capacitor build** — change is **web-only** (no `ios/**`, no `capacitor.config.ts`, no plugins), so `cap sync` + `xcodebuild` are unaffected. body: ## What & why Coach **Ben Potter** reported he couldn't add new players — the signup **"Access Code Required"** gate said the code *"does not match the requested format."* This is a **regression** from the signup access-code gate added **2026-03-06** (`5266fde`). Before that gate existed, players signed up freely and joined via the invite link (`processGolfTeamInvitation`) — that's how all 6 current members of his "Men's Golf" team joined (membership created minutes-to-days *after* signup). The gate now blocks new players two ways: 1. **Digits-only input.** The access-code `` used `inputMode="numeric"` + `pattern="[0-9]*"`, so an alphanumeric team join code (Ben's is `PXGF5L`) is rejected by the browser's native validation — *"does not match the requested format."* On mobile the keyboard was a number-pad that can't type letters at all. 2. **Gate ignored team codes + the join never completed.** The gate only accepted the global `SIGNUP_ACCESS_CODE`. And `/golf/join/[code]` already redirects un-onboarded players to `/golf/player?joinCode=CODE` expecting onboarding to finish the join — but `completePlayerOnboarding` never consumed `joinCode` (the *"optionally auto-joins"* comment was stale). So invited players were never added to the team. ## The fix — no env / Vercel change - **signup input** — `inputMode="text"`, `pattern="[A-Za-z0-9]*"`, auto-uppercase; prefill the code from the invite link and carry a typed code through to onboarding. - **`validateAccessCode`** — accept the global code **or any existing team `join_code`** (admin lookup, case/whitespace-insensitive, best-effort: a missing service-role key can never crash the gate). - **`golf-sign-up-form`** — forward the join code into onboarding instead of dropping it. - **`completePlayerOnboarding`** — restore the auto-join via `processGolfTeamInvitation` (best-effort; never blocks onboarding). - **test** — new `access-code` regression suite (10 cases). Every team's own code now lets a player in **and** joins them to that team — both via the invite link and by typing the code. ## Verification Validated end-to-end against **production** data — Ben Potter / team "Men's Golf" / `join_code = PXGF5L`: - `PXGF5L` passes the new `[A-Za-z0-9]*` input pattern (it failed the old `[0-9]*` — his exact error). - It exists in `golf_teams.join_code`, so `validateAccessCode('PXGF5L')` → true; lowercase/spaced variants resolve too. Local: `tsc --noEmit` ✅ · full unit suite (1339 passing) ✅ · new access-code test (10/10) ✅ · eslint ✅ (no new findings; only pre-existing W0 warnings). ## Test plan - [ ] Logged out, open `/golf/join/PXGF5L` → land on signup with the code prefilled → Continue → create account → onboarding → auto-added to "Men's Golf". - [ ] Or: go to `/golf/signup`, type `PXGF5L` → Continue → same result. - [ ] Global access code still works for non-invited signups. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

Arbitrary z-index `z-[N]` → tier classes (1/2/9→z-base, 19→z-raised, 60→z-modal, 70→z-toast, 100→z-toolbar, 9999→z-tooltip). ## Hand-handled edge cases (regex would have broken these) - `ConfirmClassesModal.tsx`: the `\`${cls.color}15\`` hex-alpha concat would yield invalid `var(...)15` CSS → rewrote to `color-mix(in srgb, … 8%, transparent)`; standalone fallbacks use a `DEFAULT_CLASS_COLOR` token const. - `stat-card-sparkline.tsx`: `sparkColor` feeds a **canvas** renderer (`ctx.strokeStyle`), which cannot resolve `var()` → added a runtime `resolveToken()` reading the CSS custom property off `:root`, with SSR-safe fallback. - Updated the (skipped) sparkline color test assertions to the new token values. ## Banned-pattern grep — before → after (owned paths) | pattern | before | after | |---|---|---| | #16A34A | 10 | 0 | | #16a34a | 9 | 0 | | #DC2626 | 2 | 0 | | rounded-[Npx] | 11 | 0 | | z-[N] | 17 | 0 | ## Regression test Added `scripts/__tests__/sweep-clean-components.test.mjs` (node:test) — scans the four owned trees, excludes the 3 reserved chart subdirs, asserts ZERO of the five banned patterns. Verified it fails on a seeded violation and passes clean. ## Local gate - `npm run typecheck` → exit 0 - `npm run lint` → exit 0 (0 errors, 5309 warnings < 6000 ceiling; remaining banned-color/radius warnings are `emerald-*`/`green-N` className tokens and files outside this agent's scope) - `node --test scripts/__tests__/sweep-clean-components.test.mjs` → 3/3 pass - Full `next build` intentionally excluded per admin-override policy (env-blocked in CI; tsc is the compile gate). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---
